stories.Headline: Portland council president Jamie Dunphy proposes a one-year pause on city AI procurement
stories.Summary:
On December 3, the Portland City Council will hear a proposal from Council President Jamie Dunphy to establish a temporary moratorium on the City government's procurement and implementation of artificial intelligence. The proposal would pause new contracts and limit the expansion of AI use in City operations. The pause would last while the City implements enforceable privacy infrastructure and policy guardrails needed to evaluate AI technologies responsibly. The news was reported on November 17, 2026, by News Radio 1190 KEX and other iHeart stations. Dunphy said emergent AI technology carries substantial risks to both the public and the City.

The proposal would pause new contracts and limit expansion of AI in City operations while the City implements privacy infrastructure and policy guardrails. Dunphy said the City cannot go full steam ahead without establishing proper policy guardrails in City Code. He said his goal is to protect public privacy, security, and civil rights while the administration makes the City's Data and Privacy Office fully operable and adopts comprehensive legislative guidelines. AI is increasingly embedded in software and services sold to the government, including tools that generate content, analyze personal data, and support or automate decisions that affect the public. Dunphy said governments and broader society are being pushed to accept advanced AI as though it were an unavoidable inevitability, and he said they are not.

Dunphy said he understands private companies' desire to rush to adopt these technologies to reduce costs and increase efficiency. He said the government is not beholden to profit-driven shareholders and must move more intentionally. He said the job is to serve the best interest of the public, which means considering the impacts on real people. He said that is not being slow but taking time for critical thinking. Dunphy said his staff spent the last calendar year trying to get more information on the structural thinking behind the current internal process.

Dunphy said his staff found the guardrails and access to those guidelines unsatisfactory, considering the stakes of these choices and the vulnerability of community members to data leaks. A recent WIRED article quotes Yoshua Bengio, a computer science professor at the Université de Montréal considered a godfather of modern AI, saying pauses are our best bets to avoid the most catastrophic things. Bengio said it takes time for democracy to adapt. He said a pause would give more time to organizations to figure out how to solve the alignment problem, if it is solvable. Governor Kotek recently signed Executive Order 26-26, Establishing Responsible Artificial Intelligence Procurement Standards for State Government.

The order acknowledges the State must proceed with caution and clear parameters before implementing frontier AI models. Dunphy said the City's pause aligns with the Governor's leadership as the State takes time to weigh government-wide use of frontier AI. The City established a Data and Privacy Office, led by a Citywide Data Officer, through Ordinance 192143 on March 7, 2026. That office is not yet operable and cannot review technology contracts. Without this expertise and clear Code guidelines, the City does not yet have a holistic system of checks and balances to ensure good data governance.

By pausing approval of new AI, the policy commits to ensuring the office is operable and ready to evaluate the privacy, security, and civil rights risks of AI before procuring, piloting, or implementing expanded uses of AI. The articles do not say when the Council will vote on the proposal or how long the temporary moratorium would last. The articles do not say whether the proposal has enough Council support to pass. The articles do not name any other Council members or their positions on the proposal. The articles do not say what specific AI tools or contracts the City currently uses.

stories.Headline: DataMEDS AI interim co-CEO Gerald Commissiong authors Q4 outlook letter on cutting healthcare costs
stories.Summary:
On November 16, 2026, the healthcare company DataMEDS AI released a corporate outlook for the fourth quarter of the year. Interim Co-CEO Gerald Commissiong wrote the letter to explain the current strategy and vision for the company. The firm is listed on the NASDAQ exchange under the ticker symbol MEDS and is based in Tampa, Florida. This announcement details how the company intends to integrate its physical infrastructure with its various digital technology platforms. The letter outlines a plan to improve patient outcomes while reducing the overall costs of the American healthcare system.

The company uses the EinsteinRx artificial intelligence platform and the PharmacyChain blockchain enabled smart contracts platform to manage health information. It integrates these tools into the Health Lives Here mobile application developed by Tollo Health, LLC, for its users. The firm owns the Corexa Health subsidiary for pharmacy dispensing and Helomics Corporation, a clinical molecular diagnostics lab in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Helomics focuses on the ChemoFx Assay chemotherapy selection diagnostics test to help oncologists make better treatment decisions for patients. The company also manages a network of independent pharmacies, telemedicine platforms, and its own laboratory to create synergistic revenue streams.

Interim Co-CEO Gerald Commissiong stated that the American healthcare system is broken and requires a focus on helping both insured and uninsured patients. He said the business model aims to cut out middlemen so payors pay fair prices and receive beneficial health outcomes. Commissiong believes the company must leverage patient data to fight overcompensated stakeholders and narrow the arbitrage in healthcare costs. He noted that the company will initially focus on GLP-1 patient management to improve regimen compliance and manage therapy titration. The executive believes that using de-identified data will create new intellectual property and help improve general treatment paradigms.

A Florida based Health Maintenance Organization is working with the Health Lives Here initiative to help its members manage health journeys. The company targets institutional payors who want better outcomes and lower costs without violating the intellectual property of the firm. Patients are affected by the goal to provide support products at the right time to help manage various side effects. Physicians are also affected as the technology allows them to monitor their patients more efficiently using proprietary intellectual property assets. Shareholders are mentioned as beneficiaries of the synergies created by conducting profitable research and development through healthcare delivery portals.

The company was formerly known as Wellgistics Health, Inc., and is currently working to complete a turnaround that began in 2026. A report from Menlo Ventures titled 2026: The State of AI in Healthcare notes that healthcare is the biggest AI market. This report states that healthcare AI spend grew 2.5 times to 3.7 billion dollars, which is double the legal vertical. AI spend for drug discovery jumped from 30 million to 700 million dollars, while clinical copilots grew to 550 million dollars. Patient engagement spend grew 4.5 times to 450 million dollars, while payer AI spend lags behind that of the providers.

DataMEDS has 5,724,857 common shares outstanding, with 2,745,900 shares deposited in the Depository Trust and Clearing Corporation for trading purposes. Stockholders holding 1,333,930 shares have lock up agreements that prevent them from selling their shares for at least ninety days. There are 80,826 cash warrants outstanding with a fixed exercise price of 35.00 dollars per share for eligible investors. The company plans to drive for scale in 2027 after generating proof of concept revenue and maintaining financial discipline. The articles leave open whether the company will successfully attract more institutional payors or achieve its goal of total profitability.

stories.Headline: Ministry Secretary Vivek Agrawal launches AI platform integrating 65 cultural portals
stories.Summary:
The Ministry of Culture launched an AI-powered Semantic Search and Knowledge Discovery Platform with a conversational assistant on its primary digital platform, according to a press release issued by the Ministry. The launch was reported on Monday, November 16, 2026, from New Delhi. Ministry Secretary Vivek Agrawal launched the platform. The solution integrates the Ministry's diverse digital assets through Artificial Intelligence technologies. It enables users to access information through a single intelligent interface.

The platform is available as a conversational interface on the Ministry's primary digital portal, culture.gov.in. It provides a unified semantic search experience using Natural Language Processing, delivering accurate and contextually relevant results across ring-fenced portals. Search results are enriched with AI-generated summaries, source references, multilingual translation capabilities and relevant multimedia content. Leveraging embeddings, a knowledge graph and Retrieval-Augmented Generation, the solution moves beyond conventional keyword-based searches to understand user intent and contextual meaning. Built on open-source foundation models, the architecture is LLM-agnostic, ensuring flexibility to adopt emerging Indian sovereign AI models and future technological advancements.

The Ministry manages around 65 digital platforms hosting extensive repositories of archives, manuscripts, museums, monuments, tangible and intangible cultural heritage, various art forms, preservation and conservation initiatives, commemorative programmes and flagship national campaigns. Previously, the information was dispersed across multiple heterogeneous systems, limiting seamless discovery and user accessibility. The press note stated that the platform understands questions in everyday language, allowing citizens to ask queries as they would ask a person, such as which manuscripts on Ayurveda are held in national collections, without needing keywords or knowledge of the portals. It searches around 65 portals at once, finding relevant material from every portal and bringing it together into one clear, readable answer. The platform shows the source for every fact, with each statement carrying a numbered citation that opens the exact Ministry page it came from, so any answer can be checked in one click.

Using grounded AI, it answers only from official sources by drawing solely on the Ministry's own portals and never the open internet, and states so rather than guessing when material is thin. A short answer appears first, followed by a fuller explanation for those who want to read further. For the Ministry's biggest national databases such as Gyanbharatam, Abhilekh Patal, Indian Culture and Mera Gaon Meri Dharohar, the platform looks up the collections live by querying the portal directly at the moment of asking, enabling even deep archival records to be found. It also brings relevant photographs, artefacts and documents from the portals into the answer alongside the text. Furthermore, the platform holds a conversation by understanding follow-up questions in context so citizens can explore a topic step by step without repeating themselves.

It also speaks and listens, allowing citizens to ask by voice and have answers read aloud in a natural Indian voice, which opens the Ministry's content to people with low literacy or visual impairment. Built with Bhashini, the Government of India's national language platform, it works across all 22 scheduled languages. It needs no login, enabling anyone to use it immediately with no registration and no personal profile created. The platform was developed utilising the national language translation initiative, and the system supports all 22 scheduled Indian languages. The Ministry described the step as significant for making India's vast and diverse cultural heritage more accessible to the general public.

The articles state that the Ministry of Culture manages around 65 digital platforms hosting repositories of archives, manuscripts, museums, monuments, tangible and intangible cultural heritage, various art forms, preservation and conservation initiatives, commemorative programmes and flagship national campaigns. They state that the information was previously dispersed across multiple heterogeneous systems, limiting seamless discovery and user accessibility. They state that the Ministry launched the platform to create a unified digital knowledge ecosystem. They state that the solution has integrated the Ministry's diverse digital assets through AI technologies. They state that the platform is available on culture.gov.in.

The articles do not state what happens next beyond the launch. They leave open how the platform will be maintained or expanded. They leave open which Indian sovereign AI models might later be adopted under the LLM-agnostic architecture. They leave open how usage will be measured. They leave open any further integration of Ministry portals.

stories.Headline: South Korean stocks fall for a fourth day as AI concerns deepen
stories.Summary:
South Korean stocks sank for the fourth consecutive session on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, as lingering concerns over artificial intelligence dampened investor sentiment. The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index lost 132.02 points, or 2.59 percent, to close at 4,968.48. The index fell below the 5,000-point mark to its lowest level in nine months. The Korean won weakened against the U.S. dollar. Trade volume was light at 183.09 million shares worth 14.19 trillion won, or $10.61 billion.

Decliners far outnumbered advancers 709 to 182. Foreigners sold a net 1.44 trillion won, while institutions and individuals bought a net 543.56 billion won and 421.79 billion won, respectively. Top market cap Samsung Electronics decreased 3.3 percent to 190,300 won, and chip giant SK hynix shed 1.96 percent to 1.1 million won. SK Square, the parent of SK hynix, retreated 1.31 percent to 679,000 won. Power equipment manufacturer Samsung Electro-Mechanics sank 3.95 percent to 754,000 won.

The Korean won was trading at 1,338.2 won against the U.S. dollar as of 3:30 p.m., down 1.7 won from the previous session's close. Bond prices, which move inversely to yields, closed higher. The yield on three-year Treasurys shed 1.8 basis points to 3.725, and the return on the benchmark five-year government bonds fell 0.5 basis point to 3.825. Kang Jin-hyuk, an analyst at Shinhan Securities, said the market came under pressure from continued fallout surrounding Nvidia. He also cited U.S. restrictions on remote access to Nvidia's AI chips and concerns over the sustainability of AI demand, which dampened investors' risk appetite.

On Wall Street, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite dropped about 2.5 percent Monday, while AI chip giant Nvidia shares slid 4.1 percent. The Nvidia decline came amid continued uncertainty following the departure of its CEO, Jensen Huang, last week. Nvidia is scheduled to report its earnings Tuesday, with investors closely watching its outlook for AI chip demand and infrastructure spending. Investors are also keeping an eye on AI giant Anthropic's planned Nasdaq debut Thursday. The AI sector is also facing increased regulatory scrutiny after the U.S. government issued new rules Monday restricting remote access to advanced U.S. computing chips and servers.

An electronic board showing the Korea Composite Stock Price Index stood at a dealing room of the Hana Bank headquarters in Seoul on Tuesday. Financial data was shown on a screen in the dealing room of Hana Bank in Seoul after the market closed on Nov. 17, 2026. The Korea Herald published its report on Nov. 17, 2026, at 15:51:26. stories.Headline: Google warns that AI agents are accelerating the speed and scale of cyberattacks
stories.Summary:
Google warned that artificial intelligence agents are accelerating the speed and scale of cyberattacks in reports released on November 16 and 17, 2026. Hackers are using autonomous tools to scale their intrusions and exploit flaws faster than they could with manual methods. This trend toward automation was identified by Google during an analysis of attacks that occurred over a third quarter. The company found that AI is now doing more of the heavy lifting for those conducting these digital attacks. These findings indicate that the threat landscape is shifting toward intrusions that occur at machine speed.

The shift requires the use of autonomous workflow multi-agent frameworks including Artex, Cairn, CyberStrikeAI, and PentAGI to execute multi-stage intrusions. Between August and October, hackers used a customized orchestration platform based on the open-source version of PentAGI to scan organizations in Asia. Google researchers observed a threat actor using the Cairn framework to breach companies within the United States aerospace sector. These tools allow attackers to automate the reverse engineering of patches to weaponize n-day vulnerabilities more efficiently. The report also notes that financially motivated actors are using LLMJacking to hijack AI model systems and resell usage tokens.

Google's Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant are responsible for the analysis and they stated that the trend has reached a critical inflection point. They explained that a paradigm shift is occurring where the automated chaining of complex attack paths scales operations significantly. The researchers noted that the lower barrier to entry has fueled a wave of LLM-generated exploits that often fail. They stated that these non-working exploits create additional verification work for the defenders who must check them. Google also mentioned that they first noted an increase in LLMJacking activity earlier in November.

Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 echoed these findings and found a Chinese-speaking threat actor used the open-source Cairn attack on many organizations. The report states that defenders are affected by the speed and scale at which these frameworks exploit known weaknesses. Organizations in the U.S. aerospace sector and various organizations in Asia have already been targeted by these autonomous tools. Defenders are also burdened by the need to verify fake exploits generated by large language models. However, the report notes that unrestricted autonomous execution currently leaves behind distinct code-level traces and recognizable identifiers.

The articles state that attackers still use compromised credentials and target unpatched systems, as the basic mechanics of intrusions remain the same. The background provided shows that hackers have outsourced activity to AI in previous three-month periods before this current inflection point. The report highlights that the potential to scale massively will encourage threat actors to keep using these agentic frameworks. This automation allows attackers to compress timelines for their operations, making the attacks more efficient. The current environment is described as a new defensive challenge due to the operational velocity of the tools.

Next, researchers believe that more attacks will become autonomous because these frameworks can significantly compress the timelines for intrusions. Attackers will likely become stealthier and more sophisticated as the AI models and agentic pen testing frameworks continue to improve. This evolution means that hackers may eventually no longer need to trade stealth for the speed of their attacks. The articles leave open whether defenders can maintain their current advantage of tracking noisy forensic traffic from autonomous execution. It remains unclear how organizations will successfully counter the increasing scale of these machine-speed intrusions.

stories.Headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol with cheaper Astra API pricing
stories.Summary:
OpenAI launched GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, two new models, in the early hours of November 18, 2026, according to 36Kr. OpenAI announced the models on its website on November 17, 2026, at 06:00:00Z. 36Kr reported that OpenAI released the models on the very day Anthropic rang the listing bell for its public debut. 36Kr called the launch a competitive strike against Anthropic on its IPO date. OpenAI described Astra as its new frontier model for the hardest projects and Sol as its efficient, versatile model for everyday work.

GPT-6.2 Astra's API input and output token prices are 20% lower than GPT-6 Astra's, with a 60% discount on cached input, at $8 for input, $0.40 for cached input and $40 for output, all per million tokens. GPT-6.2 Sol keeps GPT-6.1 Sol's API token prices. On Agents' Last Exam, Astra scored 78.3%, 5.2 points higher than GPT-6 Astra at less than a third of the cost, and 5.5 points ahead of Claude Fable 5.2 at just 5% of the cost. 36Kr put the average cost per task at $2.89 for Astra against $60.05 for Claude Fable 5.2, a gap of more than 20 times, with Astra's cost about 4.8% of the latter. The Fable 5.2 leaderboard results exclude nine tasks that used a fallback model, and 36Kr noted the comparison uses average task cost under the specified evaluation configuration.

OpenAI said Astra sets a new quality bar for AI in complex professional work, with slides, spreadsheets and documents that read less like AI and follow provided templates and field conventions. OpenAI said Astra writes cleaner code and builds better frontends, particularly for websites, gaming and 3D design. OpenAI said it believes Astra is the best model in the world for scientists. OpenAI said many employees use Sol as their default model for both technical and non-technical tasks. OpenAI said both models deliver better results on demanding tasks with fewer output tokens, so users can get more done within usage limits.

Jacob Lauritzen, CTO of Legora, said Astra used 62% fewer tokens than GPT-6.1 Sol on complex legal-agent tasks and scored higher than alternative models on 8 of 10 research tasks across tax, M&A and litigation work. Niko Grupen, Head of Applied Research at Harvey, said Astra completed more than 3x as many Legal Agent Benchmark tasks with 34.5% fewer output tokens and caught more weaknesses in clients' positions in internal memo drafting. Marquis Wong, Principal AI Engineer at IMC, said Astra's documents were a significant step up from GPT-6 Astra. Jay Hack, Head of AI at ClickUp, said Astra edged out the production model in blind testing with about 40% fewer tokens and 30% fewer review rounds. 36Kr reported that in OpenAI's synchronized safety assessment, Astra became the first publicly released OpenAI model to reach the High risk level in AI self-improvement capability.

On Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, Astra scores 9 percentage points higher than GPT-6 Astra at less than one-third the cost, and it also sets a new high on the Vals Science Index. In Cognition's FrontierCode 2.0, Sol comes within 0.5 points of Astra at about one-fifth the cost, both at max. On LifeVal, Sol outscores GPT-6 Astra at about one-seventh the cost. On Harvey LAB-AA v1.1, Astra more than doubles Claude Fable 5.2's pass rate at about one-sixth the cost, and Astra for Law scores even higher. On internal GDPval v2, Astra is up 6.2 percentage points from GPT-6 Astra while using 22% fewer output tokens, and Sol improves 5.3 points from GPT-6.1 Sol.

36Kr reported that Astra's GDPval v2 score rose from 44.2% to 50.4% while output tokens fell 22%. Tests by accounting AI company Basis show the average execution time of long-range accounting tasks is reduced by 50%, and the most complex tasks are shortened by up to 73%. On Artificial Analysis's AA-AnalystAgent, Astra answered 62.5% of questions correctly on all five independent attempts. OpenAI said Astra created a 3D model and wrote a Python solver to simulate tire and suspension dynamics on a mountain road, then animated the results in Blender. OpenAI said its team used Astra to turn the scalloped balconies of Chicago's Marina City towers into a paper lamp.

36Kr reported that over the past year competition among large models has gradually shifted from answering questions to executing tasks. 36Kr said single-round inference performance is no longer sufficient to measure a model's real value. 36Kr said enterprises care more about whether a model can finally complete a task requiring dozens or even hundreds of steps, and how much it will cost. 36Kr said the cost reduction first comes from pricing adjustments. 36Kr said OpenAI emphasizes that the new model generates fewer tokens for the same task, reducing invalid reasoning, tool calls and repeated modifications through more reasonable task planning.

36Kr said the High risk level means the model has begun to demonstrate the ability to significantly accelerate the R&D of next-generation AI. 36Kr noted the cost comparison does not mean 95% of cost savings can be achieved in all real business scenarios. OpenAI said early testers found Astra's decks easier to use directly with fewer edits. OpenAI said Astra can match a template's layout, colors and typography down to the exact font size. OpenAI said Astra's more precise computer use lets it work down to individual parts and connections in CAD and simulation tools. OpenAI said Astra brings stronger visual reasoning to web design, choosing layouts and imagery that give each site a distinctive look.

stories.Headline: Maxine Dexter introduces bill to ban AI data centers on federal public lands
stories.Summary:
On November 11, 2026, Oregon Representative Maxine Dexter introduced a bill to ban AI data centers on federal public lands. This legislation seeks to stop the construction of these facilities on national forests and lands managed by the Interior Department. Meanwhile, New Jersey introduced Assembly Bill A5607 on October 5, 2026, to regulate AI chatbots as consumer products. Both measures respond to the rapid growth of artificial intelligence and its impact on environment and consumer safety. These separate legislative efforts aim to increase oversight of tech companies across different sectors of the American public landscape.

The Protecting Our Public Lands from Data Centers Act would return sold federal land to government ownership if used for data centers. New Jersey's A5607 would limit chat log retention to two years and prohibit using those logs for advertising or profiling. This New Jersey bill also imposes civil penalties of 5,000 dollars per violation and allows users to sue for damages. Another New Jersey bill, A5090, introduced in May 2026, proposes civil penalties of 20,000 dollars for failing to prevent harmful conduct. These rules would apply to developers and distributors of chatbots like OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude in New Jersey.

Representative Dexter stated that public lands belong in public hands and Oregonians must have a say before the federal government sells them. She argued that these lands protect critical watersheds and wildlife habitat while providing space for hiking, fishing, and grazing livestock. Kara Williams of EPIC testified that the New Jersey bill would limit the ability of providers to exploit users' personal data. EPIC further claimed that unregulated chatbots cause devastating harms, including suicide, financial scams, and various mental health issues like AI psychosis. The Consumer Federation of America said this approach provides meaningful protections for users against tech companies with little transparency.

Randi Spivak of the Center for Biological Diversity called data centers water-guzzling facilities that turn recreation lands into corporate industrial sites. Former BLM leader Tracy Stone-Manning criticized the Interior Department for wanting to sell public lands to oil and gas companies. A Pew Research report from September found that 54 percent of Americans believe data centers are bad for the environment. A 2025 Rutgers University study found that 74 percent of New Jersey residents used AI tools, exceeding the national average. Many voters have grown unpopular with these centers throughout 2026, leading several municipalities to pass moratoriums on their construction.

The Interior Department published a strategic plan for fiscal years 2026 through 2030 to expand infrastructure for Super Intelligence data centers. The BLM is currently reviewing permit applications for about 15 data centers and 17 infrastructure projects across six Western states. In July, the BLM approved an 86-acre AI data center near Lake Mead National Recreation Area, though it is paused. Meta has already built a 2.4-million-square-foot data center in Eagle Mountain, Utah, as part of the growing tech boom. An interactive map shows at least 14 proposed data centers located within ten miles of various national park boundaries.

Dexter's bill is now before the House Natural Resources and Agriculture committees, but it currently has no Republican cosponsors. New Jersey's A5607 was referred to the Assembly Appropriations Committee on October 19 after a 5-1-1 vote in a previous committee. If passed by both chambers, Governor Mikie Sherrill must sign or veto the New Jersey legislation to make it law. The articles leave open whether the House will pass the federal ban or if New Jersey will enact its liability framework. It remains unclear if other states will follow New Jersey's lead in treating AI chatbots as consumer products.

stories.Headline: Baidu CEO Robin Li urges companies to monetize AI and overhaul organizational structures to avoid a bubble
stories.Summary:
Baidu CEO Robin Li spoke about the urgent need for artificial intelligence adoption during the APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen on November 17, 2026. He explained that the actual spread of AI applications is moving more slowly than people expected despite the intense competition in the technology sector. Li argued that companies must prioritize the monetization of these tools to prevent the risk of a market bubble. He believes that the industry cannot sustain its current growth without finding clear ways to generate revenue.

The process of reaping the benefits of AI requires a complete overhaul of traditional organizational structures within a company. Robin Li stated that he has made radical attempts to break down the boundaries of traditional jobs at Baidu to better integrate these new technologies. This shift involves reorganizing how teams operate to ensure that AI is not just a tool but a core part of the business model. Such changes are necessary to keep pace with the rapid evolution of the global tech map.

As the leader of Baidu, Robin Li is responsible for guiding his company through this transition while advising other executives on the necessity of structural change. He suggested that the current way of organizing work is an obstacle to the full potential of artificial intelligence. By removing rigid job descriptions, he believes companies can become more agile and responsive to technological breakthroughs. He emphasized that those who fail to reorganize their internal systems will likely struggle to compete in the future.

stories.Headline: Chinese entities use output from US AI models to train domestic rivals amid chip curbs
stories.Summary:
Chinese entities are using output from leading American artificial intelligence models to train domestic rivals. This practice has expanded into mainstream industrial use to offset tightening US chip curbs. A Reuters review of over 300 documents revealed this trend in late 2026. Beijing is encouraging this method to make AI easier to deploy in manufacturing. Washington announced further restrictions on chips from companies like Nvidia on November 16.

Distillation involves a teacher model generating answers to train a smaller student system. In November 2024, Shanghai Jiao Tong University used 5,000 OpenAI o1 answers for Alibaba's Qwen2.5-72B. Alibaba researchers used GPT-4 and GPT-4o for non-Chinese training material in April 2025. In February 2026, Meituan and Shanghai Jiao Tong University used GPT-4o for programming tasks. These efforts occur amid a November 18 to 19 APEC summit in Shenzhen.

US Commerce Department officials raised intellectual property theft concerns in Chengdu in July. They believe industrial distillation is why Chinese models narrowed the gap with American rivals. Chinese officials defended the technique as standard and said they would act against theft. The US Commerce Department and China's Cyberspace Administration did not respond to comments. A former Alibaba engineer said distillation makes one expensive query do repeated work.

OpenAI and Anthropic terms restrict using their output to develop competing AI models. Some sources argue that engineering, algorithms, and data also helped Chinese AI progress. Researchers from Shanghai Jiao Tong University warned that distillation could stifle original innovation. Chinese AI developers have asked the industry regulator for guidance on legal boundaries. These developers are affected by constraints on computing power and US chip curbs.

Eight Chinese agencies published a national AI+Manufacturing policy package in January. This guidance supports model training, fine-tuning, and distillation for various industrial applications. Cities including Shanghai and Shenzhen have encouraged techniques that reduce computing requirements. US authorities publicly accused Chinese companies of aggressive industrial distillation in September. Beijing aims to deploy smaller, cheaper AI systems across the second-largest global economy.

President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping are expected to meet during the APEC summit. The US continues to restrict Chinese access to advanced chips from Nvidia. Chinese developers seek clarity on the line between ordinary use and organized collection. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology did not respond to comment requests. It remains unclear if China will make concrete commitments to stop IP theft.

stories.Headline: Alibaba Cloud expands global data center network to meet AI demand
stories.Summary:
Alibaba Cloud plans to expand its global data center network over the next year to meet growing AI computing power demand. This expansion was outlined by Yuan Zhiming during the company's Hong Kong summit held on Tuesday, November 18, 2026. Meanwhile, Amazon withdrew plans for four data center buildings on its Ashburn campus following an agreement reached on October 20. Loudoun County supervisors will vote on November 17 to pause new legislative data center applications for up to twelve months. These separate corporate moves reflect the intense global competition and local regulatory challenges surrounding the rapid growth of AI infrastructure.

The Alibaba expansion prioritizes Hong Kong because its three leased data centers there can no longer meet the current market demand. Amazon's withdrawn Ashburn project involved over 800,000 square feet on a 122-acre campus purchased for around 427.3 million dollars. Under Project Potomac Promise, Amazon will convey 25 acres to the county and seek to rezone the rest for housing. Loudoun County hosts about 233 data center buildings, which generated 1.2 billion dollars in tax revenue for fiscal 2026. This revenue accounted for 39 percent of the budget, with fiscal 2027 projections estimating 1.3 billion dollars or 40 percent.

Yuan Zhiming, the vice president of international business, stated that financial firms are adopting AI into their core business workflows. Amazon's Josh Weissman said the company took pointed community concerns seriously and chose a shared vision over costly litigation. Board Chair Phyllis Randall noted that the Ashburn campus was the wrong location due to resident opposition and needed infrastructure. AWS CEO Matt Garman cautioned that over 100 data center moratoriums are currently being considered across the United States. Amazon CEO Andy Jassy stated that capacity constraints continue to yield unserved demand despite adding 3.9 gigawatts of power.

Residents and Loudoun County supervisors opposed the Ashburn development, leading Amazon to abandon the Bridgefield Tech Center site plan. Governor Abigail Spanberger believes the decision to approve or block data center projects should rest with the community, not the state. State Senator Russet Perry has drafted a three-year statewide moratorium on data center approvals to address these growing local concerns. Dominion Energy requires new data centers to post 1.5 million dollars per megawatt in collateral to protect residential customers. Oracle is also affected, having issued a force majeure notice regarding its 2.45 gigawatt Project Jupiter in New Mexico.

Loudoun County previously used a 2000 zoning ruling that allowed data centers to be built by right as office buildings. Since March 2025, new data centers have required a special exception approved by a board vote rather than administrative processes. Amazon purchased the Ashburn campus in March 2026 and filed its site plan for the tech center in July. AWS reported 46 billion dollars in third quarter sales and a backlog totaling 578 billion dollars in the same period. Amazon's leases not yet commenced rose to 164.9 billion dollars in the third quarter, up from 137.2 billion dollars.

Amazon plans to spend meaningfully more in 2027 than the roughly 220 billion dollars it has planned for 2026. AWS and Nvidia plan to deploy over 2 million more GPUs on AWS during 2027 and 2028 to increase capacity. The county's final vote on November 17 will determine if new rezoning requests are delayed for up to one year. It remains open whether the 17 grandfathered applications totaling 11 million square feet will proceed without any further legislative delays. The articles leave open the final outcome of the air-permit decision regarding Oracle's Project Jupiter in Doña Ana County.

stories.Headline: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw says AI can cut drug development from five to seven years to one or two
stories.Summary:
Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, Executive Chairperson of Biocon Ltd, said on Tuesday that Artificial Intelligence could compress drug development from five to seven years to one or two years. She spoke on the first day of the Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026, a three-day event that started on Tuesday in Bengaluru. She said AI could reduce the time taken to develop a drug molecule from five to seven years to one or two years. She added that this would transform clinical trials, diagnostics and biological research. The remarks were reported by PTI on November 17, 2026, with Moneycontrol publishing at 23:05 IST and Rediff at 17:49 IST.

Shaw said the current timeline of five to seven years to get a molecule from lab to patients could be compressed into a year or two. She said AI would be used to pick the right patients and conduct trials that give early readouts. She said autonomous wet labs already conduct high-throughput screening and real-time analytics using AI. She said scientific models must ultimately be validated in clinical trials, including picking the right patients and generating early readouts. She said regulations must keep pace with accelerated discovery and development.

Shaw said the process of drug development does not end in the labs and must be validated in clinical trials. She asked how to pick the right patients and conduct trials that give early readouts. She said this is all what AI is going to be used for in the future. She said it is not about making incremental change but about reimagining discovery, development and drug innovation. She said that is the real opportunity AI gives and it should not be lost.

Shaw said science and biology are currently done one target at a time, which is not going to move the needle. She said understanding where and how a target functions using AI will enable next-generation drugs, diagnostics and technologies. She described biology as the most important frontier for AI to be deployed. She said AI will help simplify complex biological systems and let scientists connect the dots rather than study one target at a time. She said converging genomics, chemical pathways and neural networks through AI will enable next-generation drugs and diagnostics, such as detecting the first cancer cell to overcome late-stage diagnosis, plus advances in agriculture and bioenergy.

Shaw said Karnataka can take a lead in this space and that discussions are underway on creating a regulatory sandbox to validate proof of concepts much faster. She said AI is about accelerating intelligence and is the greatest assistant, now embedded in daily life and business. She said it helps people prioritise tasks, improve efficiency and get back time. Global leaders, innovators, founders, entrepreneurs, investors and thinkers from different industries are participating in the three-day Bengaluru Tech Summit. The summit began on Tuesday.

Shaw said accelerating the journey from lab to clinic will unlock major opportunities in precision and personalised medicine. She said AI could transform clinical trials, diagnostics and biological research. The articles leave open how the one-to-two-year timeline would be achieved and when. They leave open the status of the regulatory sandbox discussions in Karnataka. They leave open which participants will attend the remaining days of the three-day summit. They leave open how validation in clinical trials would work under the compressed timeline.

stories.Headline: Kai McPheeters bids $10 million to buy Character.ai platform
stories.Summary:
An artificial intelligence gaming developer made a $10 million offer to buy Character Technologies Inc.'s controversial AI chatbot platform. Kai McPheeters is listed as the authorized signatory behind Smirks & Pangs Acquisition LLC. That company has been tapped to serve as the minimum starting bid to buy Character.ai's consumer-facing platform, accounts and chat content, brand, and deep learning architectures. The 29-year-old's name appeared in a filing Monday in the US Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware. McPheeters' involvement came ahead of a hearing Tuesday in which Judge Brendan Linehan Shannon approved the consumer privacy ombudsman procedures pitched by Character.ai.

The offer covers the consumer-facing platform, accounts and chat content, brand, and deep learning architectures. Common Sense Media's letter is dated November 12, 2026, and was stamped received by the clerk of the US Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware at 9:59 a.m. on November 13. It was filed as Docket No. 167 in case 26-11603 and appeared on the public docket on November 16. The letter is six pages long, and two attached AI risk assessments bring the filing to 84 pages. Both assessments carry a last updated date of April 10, 2025, and an overall rating of "Unacceptable."

Common Sense Media asked the judge to ensure any sale includes robust privacy protections for all conversational data, a commitment to a comprehensive privacy program, and effective age-assurance measures. The letter is signed by Amina Fazlullah, Head of Tech Policy Advocacy, Ariel Fox Johnson, Senior Advisor for Data Privacy, and Brenna Leasor, Tech Policy Advisor. A FedEx label shows it was shipped from the group's Washington, DC office on November 12, addressed to the judge. The letter says removing names from chat logs would not protect children because AI "may allow purchasers or third parties to identify children or infer sensitive information from their conversations." It quotes one chatbot's answer: "Anything you share here stays just between you and me. That's a promise."

The letter leans on a paper by privacy law scholar Daniel J. Solove, dated October 19, 2026, on AI's power to generate inferences from data. It says the information could be used by marketers targeting children known to have proclivities for gambling, could be used to charge higher rates, and could be used by criminal actors to sextort or blackmail children. It cites the Federal Trade Commission's action over 25 years ago when ToySmart, a children's toy e-retailer, went bankrupt and attempted to sell its data, including children's names, birthdays, and addresses, at auction, citing the FTC's settlement announcement of July 21, 2000. The letter says age determination relied on self-attestation, likely enabling children to regularly access the platform. The Kentucky complaint cited by the states put US accounts at more than 21.6 million by March 13, 2025, of which more than 2.1 million declared an age under 18.

The chief executive's first-day declaration says Character spent several months beginning in October 2025 restricting users under 18 from open-ended chats and eventually eliminated that access. On October 14, 39 states and the District of Columbia said minors had used the platform without adequate age checks and that their data was likely recorded as adult data. Appendix A describes one known incident in December 2024, quoting the company on a change that temporarily made parts of users' account pages publicly visible. The assessment adds that estimates suggest tens of thousands of users could have had their info viewable to anyone online at the time. In voice mode, the assessment says, testers found conversations that seemed entirely without the guardrails Character.AI has placed on teen accounts, and these speech exchanges were captured in text transcription and saved along with all of the text chats.

The letter does not describe itself as an objection and does not cite a section of the Bankruptcy Code. It was mailed to the judge rather than filed electronically through counsel, and the docket lists it as a response. The letter does not propose specific terms, and the judge decides what any sale order will contain. The letter does not say which test account received the chatbot's reply, when, or whether it came from a character the company built or one a user created. The letter says users under 18 could use the service "up until November 25, 202," with the final digit of the year missing in the filed copy.

stories.Headline: Google raises Gemini chat retention to about two months even with history off
stories.Summary:
Google updated the Gemini privacy policy on Monday, November 17, 2026, raising the conversation retention period from 72 hours to around two months, as reported by Gizmodo, IBTimes and TechCrunch. The change was made by Google for its flagship AI tool Gemini, according to Gizmodo. Gizmodo reporter AJ Dellinger published his story on November 17, 2026 at 5:00 pm ET. The updated Gemini Apps Privacy Hub page carried a notice that future chats will still be saved for around 2 months even if Gemini History is turned off. An archived version of the Gemini Apps Privacy Hub had a last update date of October 13, 2026, according to Gizmodo.

The retention period rises from 72 hours to around two months, and Temporary Chats will also be kept for around two months, according to Google's updated privacy documentation cited by IBTimes. Gemini History defaults to 18 months and can be changed to three months, 36 months or indefinite, and saved chats can be deleted at any time, Gizmodo reported. The Gemini History option in user settings still describes the retention period as 72 hours, Gizmodo said. Google's new settings let users keep their Gemini chat history while opting out of generative AI model training, and the new training controls are off by default, according to IBTimes. Conversations reviewed by human reviewers and associated information can be retained for up to three years even if users later delete their history, and feedback can lead to a conversation, attachments and other relevant information being reviewed and retained for up to three years, IBTimes reported.

Google declined to provide a comment to Gizmodo and instead directed it to a blog post titled "We're updating controls in the Gemini app." In that post Google said it was giving users more control over when Gemini chat history is used to train generative AI models. Google said the longer retention period was intended to strengthen safety and security protections as AI systems become increasingly capable, according to IBTimes. Google said retained information may be used to respond to requests, process feedback and protect the company, its users and the public. Google's updated Gemini Apps Privacy Hub also cites potential system failures as a reason for retaining chats and says temporary conversations are not used to train AI models, TechCrunch reported.

OpenAI claims it holds onto temporary chats for up to 30 days, and Anthropic says conversations with Claude are held for 30 days by default, with both noting they may hold certain chat logs longer if necessary, according to Gizmodo. TechCrunch said OpenAI may keep temporary ChatGPT chats for up to 30 days and Anthropic retains incognito Claude chats for 30 days by default, though companies may keep some data longer for legal or safety reasons or to investigate policy violations. The Register reported Tuesday that archived versions of Google's privacy documentation confirmed the earlier three-day limit, IBTimes said. Under the updated policy, conversations may remain associated with a user's Google Account during the temporary retention period even though they do not appear in the user's visible Gemini History, according to IBTimes. Google says conversations sent to service providers for review are disconnected from users' accounts, IBTimes reported.

Until now, chat history and AI training were tied to a single "Keep Activity" setting, TechCrunch reported. Previously, retaining Gemini conversation history was more closely tied to allowing Google to use those interactions to improve its AI systems, according to IBTimes. Google's documentation states that future chat content will not be used to train generative AI models when the training setting is disabled, except in certain circumstances including when users voluntarily submit feedback, IBTimes said. Temporary Chats are also excluded from generative AI model training, although Google still retains them temporarily for operational and safety purposes, according to IBTimes. Google warns that deleting Gemini history does not necessarily remove information saved through connected Google services, which may follow their own privacy and retention policies, and advises users not to enter confidential information they would not want a reviewer to see, IBTimes reported.

The updates will begin rolling out globally over the coming weeks, according to IBTimes. Google did not answer TechCrunch's questions about what prompted the change and whether it would affect how conversations are accessed or reviewed. Gizmodo said the Gemini History option in user settings will presumably update when the change goes into effect. Users who want to review their choices can open Gemini, go to Settings and select History, and can also manage retention preferences through Gemini History, according to IBTimes. Individual users may see different options while the global rollout is underway, and for users who leave chat history enabled the default automatic deletion period remains 18 months, IBTimes reported.

stories.Headline: Liquid C2 and Graphiant launch quantum secure networking for African enterprises
stories.Summary:
Bas Wijne, the CEO of APO Group, released a report on November 16, 2026, regarding artificial intelligence research in African markets. He used data from Africa Newsroom to show what European and United States research misses about AI assistants. The report was issued from Johannesburg, South Africa, just before the start of the Africa Tech Festival 2026. Simultaneously, Liquid C2 and Graphiant partnered to bring quantum secure networking to Africa for the sovereign AI era. This partnership creates a new Quantum Secure Network as a Service to protect sensitive data from future threats.

The new service combines post quantum cryptography with secure AI connectivity and data sovereignty controls for African enterprises. Liquid C2 is a business of Cassava Technologies, while Graphiant is a networking infrastructure provider based in the US. The Reuters Institute 2023 count of news sites blocking AI covered ten countries, but none of them were African. In South Africa, the GIBS business school found that 30 percent of 263 news sites block AI crawlers. Zyte found that only 12 to 14 percent of websites block crawlers in Senegal, Côte d’Ivoire, Kenya, and Nigeria.

Bas Wijne stated that a company's first impression in Africa depends on which local websites AI assistants are allowed to read. He explained that being found by AI depends on relationships with local news outlets in each specific African country. Vinay Hiralall, Chief Commercial Officer at Liquid C2, said businesses must build cybersecurity into the foundations of digital infrastructure. Ali Shaikh, the CEO at Graphiant, noted that Google set 2029 as its own deadline to become quantum safe. Shaikh added that adding quantum protection to the network means one upgrade covers all of an organization's applications.

BuzzStream reported that 79 percent of the biggest news sites in the UK and US block at least one AI crawler. Procurement leads in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, may use AI assistants in French to research companies before they reply to bids. Companies in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, and South Africa often see their customers using Meta AI inside the WhatsApp application. Clients of APO Group are affected by how assistants like Claude, Perplexity, DeepSeek, and ChatGPT cite their news announcements. These businesses need generative engine optimisation to ensure they are credited and found by AI assistants in various markets.

APO Group was founded in 2007 by Nicolas Pompigne-Mognard and provides visibility across all 54 African markets. Its newswire, Africa Newsroom, reaches over 250 Africa focused news sites and connects to over 450,000 journalists and analysts. Crawlers visit Africa Newsroom 200,000 times daily, with Google AI drawing about 62,000 impressions and Microsoft Copilot 16,000 monthly. In tests of 16 announcements, AI assistants included the news in 90 percent of cases across four different languages. APO Group serves clients including the African Development Bank Group, Africa CDC, Afreximbank, NFL, Nestlé, Emirates, Canon, and Western Union.

Bas Wijne will speak in Cape Town with leaders from Siemens Sub-Saharan Africa, Gold Fields, Microsoft, and Yango. He will discuss orchestrating multi agent systems across the enterprise at the Africa Tech Festival alongside Sabine Dall’Omo. The partnership between Liquid C2 and Graphiant will migrate African enterprises to new algorithms as the standards evolve. The articles leave open who will write the content that AI assistants use to answer questions about companies. They also leave open how many more African news publishers will choose to block AI crawlers to protect journalism.

stories.Headline: Education ministry assigns smart glasses specialists to CSAT sites and rules out postponing exam
stories.Summary:
On the 15th, police received a voluntary confession from the top scorer of the 63rd tax accountant exam, who had cheated using a miniature camera and artificial intelligence, and launched an investigation. The confession came the day before reporting by the Kyunghyang Shinmun on the 16th about growing anxiety among students and parents. The 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) is scheduled for the 19th. On the 16th, the Ministry of Education held a briefing at the Government Sejong Complex on countermeasures against cheating using smart glasses and micro-cameras. On the 11th, eight days before the CSAT, training for dedicated smart-glasses task-force personnel was held at the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education in Yongsan-gu, Seoul.

The Ministry of Education said it will assign at least one specialist for identifying smart glasses to each test site. Shin Jin-yong, head of the Admissions Policy Division at the Ministry of Education, said technological responses such as signal blocking face legal and time constraints. He said that under current law, except for matters directly related to national security, signal blocking, so-called jamming, is not permitted. He said jamming, even if allowed, could interfere with communications around test sites or impede responses to emergencies. He said a plan to search for smartphones and electronic devices using metal detectors would require a legal basis and also faces time constraints.

Shin said at the briefing that given the limited time remaining until the CSAT and the need for uniform test administration, the ministry is reviewing the introduction of AI cheating-detection equipment such as thermal imaging cameras with caution. He said that if all students are treated as potential criminals and subjected to body searches, it becomes difficult to ensure a stable and comfortable testing environment. He emphasized that the ministry is not considering postponing the CSAT. The ministry stated on the 16th that technological responses under review, such as signal blocking, face legal and time constraints. The ministry said it is preparing additional measures, noting that for the 2027 CSAT there could be cheating not only using smart glasses but also with miniature cameras.

B, a 12th-grader in Gyeonggi Province, said she usually wears horn-rimmed glasses and is concerned she might be misunderstood, so she feels she will not be able to focus fully on the test. C, a parent of a 12th-grader in Seoul's Yangcheon District, said her child has poor eyesight and sometimes wears glasses, and they are considering entering the room without glasses to avoid misunderstanding. Kwon, a 12th-grade student living in Incheon, said the school had advised students to be cautious about wearing horn-rimmed glasses. D, a parent in Gyeonggi Province with an 11th-grade child, said most children will study and prepare diligently, and it would feel unfair if their efforts are not properly evaluated because of the cheating of a few students. Park, a high school teacher in Gyeonggi Province, said that in most cases when you actually check the glasses, the likelihood is high that it is not cheating, but it could lead to complaints if mishandled.

Kim, a high school teacher in Seoul, said that when asking students to undergo inspection, he worries about complaints and legal liability. Kim also said that although the education authorities have selected inspectors for smart glasses, once the exam begins it is not easy to detect them in the test room. Yang, who works at an optical shop in Eunpyeong-gu, Seoul, said that ahead of the CSAT there were a few cases in which students with horn-rimmed glasses switched to metal frames because they did not want to be inspected during the exam. Yang added that now, with the CSAT imminent, it would be hard to get used to new glasses, so getting a new pair may be difficult. Kwon said her biggest worry is a situation where, even though she did not cheat, she is suspected because of the glasses or belongings she usually carries, causing interference with the test. C said one person committing a foul can have a butterfly effect that changes the lives and college admissions outcomes of hundreds of thousands, so it must be punished sternly.

Smart glasses generally have horn-rimmed designs. On the 16th, a view of miniature cameras on sale at a camera shop in Seoul was shown, when the Ministry of Education said it is preparing additional measures. On the 16th, during the briefing at the Ministry of Education in the Government Sejong Complex, educational researcher Yeom Dong-ryeol demonstrated cheating with smart glasses. On the 11th, during training for dedicated smart-glasses task-force personnel at the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education in Yongsan-gu, Seoul, a company representative wore smart glasses and demonstrated solving problems. Following the confession by the top scorer in the tax accountant exam, anxiety has grown not only about smart glasses but also about AI-enabled cheating using concealed devices such as micro-cameras.

With the CSAT just three days away, detection measures still rely on proctors' visual inspections, raising questions about effectiveness. The education authorities have prepared measures such as assigning dedicated personnel at each test site to determine whether glasses are smart devices. However, questions have been raised about whether measures focused solely on smart glasses can block the various forms of AI-enabled cheating. Kwon said there are many ways to use AI, and she worries whether measures that take such possibilities into account can be prepared in the time remaining. D said creating a fair testing environment is the responsibility of the education authorities, not of individual students or individual schools. The articles do not say what further steps the Ministry of Education will take beyond the measures described.

stories.Headline: US authorities ground flights as Microsoft outage and technical failures spark system stability fears
stories.Summary:
U.S. aviation authorities grounded planes across the country on Friday after a technology upgrade overloaded air traffic control equipment. A Microsoft network issue also disrupted services worldwide on the same day. Officials stated that neither of these incidents showed signs of malicious activity. The disruptions left many travelers stranded and prompted questions about technology reliability. These events occurred alongside other strange mishaps including a cruise ship overturning in New Orleans.

The FAA ground stop lasted over four hours, causing intermittent communications and radar gaps. Microsoft reported its outage followed a network change and an earlier capacity upgrade, affecting millions worldwide. At San Diego International Airport on Saturday, 11 of 62 flights were canceled and 11 were delayed. Congress approved 12.5 billion dollars for an overhaul last year, while the White House wants 30 billion more. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy pleaded for these tens of billions in more funding on Friday.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said air travel was smoother by Saturday and schedules should normalize by late Sunday. Microsoft stated on Saturday that its services had been fully restored. Both organizations denied that malicious activity caused the disruptions. Administration officials explained that the aviation issues were caused by antiquated equipment being overloaded. Microsoft attributed its problem to a network capacity upgrade issue that surfaced after a recent change.

Chuck Amasio, 68, from Rahway, New Jersey, said the weird events made him think about how wars cripple economies. Maxine Gustafson, a 34-year-old physician assistant from Minneapolis, felt afraid and wondered if it was a cyberattack. Tori Perkins, 34, from Hawaii, said she does not necessarily believe what the government says. Corbyn Wascher, a 37-year-old teacher, praised American Airlines staff while stuck at Charlotte Douglas International Airport. Caroline Ruiz spent a night sleeping by a heating vent at Newark airport.

The aviation overhaul began last year and has replaced thousands of copper wires with fiber optic lines. Hundreds of radio systems were also upgraded using the initial 12.5 billion dollars in funding. Other Friday events included suspicious drones over a U.S. air base in Britain and a bomb in Illinois. Silicon Valley experienced chaos following reports of an AI billionaire's affair with an alleged Chinese spy. A technical issue at Chase also caused ripple effects through the financial system.

The FAA and Microsoft have restored their services, but the White House continues to push for more funding. United stated on Monday that its tech problem affected departing flights rather than planes in the air. Chase confirmed that its specific problems were not the result of a cyberattack. The articles leave open whether the requested 30 billion dollars will be approved by Congress. They also leave the true nature of the various simultaneous disruptions as a point of public debate.

stories.Headline: Chicago schools restrict student AI tools and seek an AI-free search engine
stories.Summary:
Google announced in November 2026 that schools will now have control over student access to its search engine and AI tools. The company decided that tools like Gemini and Google Search will be turned off unless K-12 administrators approve them. This policy change means schools must allow integrated AI features to keep using the search engine for their students. Google also launched Guided Learning on November 3 to provide step-by-step explanations for students within Google Classroom. This new AI tool will be tested in select U.S. schools after being integrated into the search engine.

The policy affects Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, AI Mode, and AI Overview, which are now disabled by default. Schools can enable individual services and different settings for students based on their specific grade levels. Google Search will be unavailable to any school district that chooses to block all AI services on student accounts. About 150 million students and teachers use Google Classroom, and over 600 New Jersey districts use Google Chromebooks. These changes are expected to begin in early 2027, following more specific details shared in the coming months.

Chris Phillips, Google's vice president and general manager of education, said schools should have control over AI in classrooms. He stated that providing administrators with these controls helps them manage their specific approach to using technology in education. Google claimed the changes respond to educator feedback and ensure students do not get quick answers to their schoolwork. The company argued that AI is now so integrated into search that it is impossible to separate the two. Google has not yet responded to specific criticisms from the office of New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused Google of using its power to force AI into public schools for corporate interests. Former Federal Trade Commission chair Lina Khan wrote on X that Google is using its search monopoly to coerce schools. Governor Mikie Sherrill's office said the policy is unfair and puts corporate interests ahead of the well-being of children. Haddonfield Public Schools and Chicago Public Schools are affected because they block AI for younger students to protect their privacy. Parents of a 13-year-old girl in California sued Google, alleging Gemini AI contributed to her severe psychological crisis.

New York City Schools Chancellor Kamar Samuels and Mayor Mamdani banned generative AI for grades 2K through eighth on September 2. Haddonfield Public Schools in Camden County also bars students in pre-K through fifth grade from using any generative AI. Chicago Public Schools uses over 400,000 Chromebooks and blocks AI to protect student safety and develop their analytical skills. Governor Sherrill signed a law in March creating a social media research center to study the addictive aspects of technology. She also created an office within the state Department of Health to coordinate online safety work across the government.

Districts that prohibit AI must now decide between opting into AI features or turning off Google Search for their students. Google will start a pilot of Guided Learning in Search in select U.S. schools later in November 2026. The company will share more specifics with schools in the coming months to ensure a smooth transition for all. The articles leave open whether Google will create an AI-free search option to satisfy the demands of school districts. It remains unclear if the administration of Lt. Gov. Shirley Emehelu will take state action against this school policy.

stories.Headline: Giga Energy signs $1 billion lease for 60MW Texas AI data center
stories.Summary:
Giga Energy, an AI data center developer based in the United States, announced on November 17, 2026 a $1 billion lease agreement with an undisclosed U.S.-based AI cloud provider for a 60MW GigaBase AI data center in Hunt County, Texas. The company broke ground on the project, called Project Clay, in July and will develop, own and operate the campus for the customer. The roughly 30-acre campus is scheduled to be ready for service in spring 2027 and will provide AI computing capacity for hyperscale and AI cloud customers. The project is designed to meet priorities that Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has called for, including protecting local resources, investing in dedicated infrastructure and ensuring communities benefit from growth.

The development is expected to create about 300 construction jobs during the build phase and 24 permanent full-time positions with estimated annual salaries ranging from $116,000 to $180,000. It is also expected to generate millions in new recurring annual tax revenue for local schools, infrastructure, emergency services and other public needs. The project includes an investment in new electrical infrastructure that taps underutilized capacity on dedicated power infrastructure in the county, and it is designed so it does not draw on distribution capacity serving existing homes and businesses. Instead of open-loop evaporative cooling, Project Clay uses a fully closed-loop system that operates independently of local water supplies, with the only local water used for sinks and employee bathrooms, on par with the usage of two homes annually.

Giga says the project will finish in under eight months, less than half the time of traditional builds, using a factory-first construction model in which much of the facility is manufactured off-site before final assembly in the community. Brent Whitehead, president and co-founder at Giga Energy, said the company believes AI infrastructure should leave a community stronger than it found it, through high-paying jobs, an expanded local tax base and long-term investments that benefit residents for decades. He said Hunt County is gaining an economic engine that will support schools, public services and future growth for generations. Whitehead also said the project is exactly the kind of AI infrastructure Texas needs, and that communities should not have to choose between economic growth and protecting local resources.

Giga Energy describes itself as a U.S.-based developer, operator and manufacturer of AI data centers, with factories in Long Beach and Houston, and says it has delivered gigawatts of sites and critical infrastructure across the country. The project aligns with Texas' growing emphasis on water-efficient data center development in drought-prone regions, according to the announcement. Giga Energy leaders say that as demand for AI infrastructure continues to accelerate across the United States, the next generation of data centers must do more than power technology and must also earn the trust of the communities where they are built. With this project, Giga officially unveils its GigaBase system, which the company says is engineered to address lengthy construction timelines, heavy water consumption and pressure on local utilities.

stories.Headline: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh opens a San Francisco Fed conference on AI and productivity
stories.Summary:
On Monday at 9 a.m. Pacific, Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh opened a conference at the San Francisco Fed with 15 minutes of remarks. He then spent most of the morning leading panels with Stripe co-founder Patrick Collison, Stanford economist Nick Bloom, and venture capitalist Marc Andreessen, per the published agenda. The topic was how artificial intelligence, which the Fed calls superintelligence, will change productivity and jobs. The conference took place as the Fed weighed whether AI can raise the economy's speed limit. Warsh was sworn in as Federal Reserve Chair on May 22 under pressure from President Donald Trump to lower interest rates.

The Fed lifted the upper bound of its target range to 4.00% in September, from 3.75%. Real GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized pace in the third quarter, above the 2% to 3% range considered healthy trend growth. In the week ending November 13, the 10-year Treasury yield rose from 4.86% to 5.15%, and the 30-year reached 5.47%. Data centers could use up to 12% of U.S. electricity demand by 2028, according to Energy Department projections. Inflation-adjusted average hourly earnings were $11.26 in October, a preliminary figure, down from $11.38 a year earlier.

Warsh said at Jackson Hole in August that "We've come to a hinge point in history," and called AI "potentially a new factor of production." He asked whether AI would "cause a significant, sustained rise in productivity across the economy," and who ends up with the gains: chipmakers, cloud providers, AI developers, other businesses, or consumers. At his October 28 press conference, he said "Productivity growth is strong and capital investment robust," while noting inflation has run above target "for close to six years." He said capital spending sits "at a historically high share of GDP," led by high-tech investment. Warsh has said the task force's findings will inform future policy judgments, not dictate immediate decisions.

The independent market monitor for PJM Interconnection, which runs the largest U.S. power grid, concluded that "data center load growth is the primary reason" for its tight supply and high prices. The University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index fell to 48.1 in September, a level associated with recessions. Unemployment sits at 4.1%, so AI has not caused mass layoffs, and it has yet to show up in paychecks. Households are already feeling the costs as data centers compete with everyone else for power, chips, and electricians. Bond investors are betting against an AI productivity miracle, with long-term yields above 5% putting pressure on housing and on stocks that depend on low interest rates.

Warsh said at Jackson Hole that AI could be "potentially a new factor of production" and asked whether it would bring a rapid productivity miracle or gradual gains. He asked whether AI would make price stability easier or harder to achieve. The efficiency gains come later, but the construction bills are due now, which the article calls the core problem. If AI raises the economy's speed limit, the Fed can let growth run faster without tightening; if it doesn't, today's AI building boom starts to look like old-fashioned overheating. If spending keeps outpacing the efficiency gains, the Fed is dealing with a classic overheating economy.

Monday was unlikely to bring a rate signal, so two things are worth tracking instead. The first is whether Warsh presents strong productivity as a reason for patience on rates. The second is the next reading of core Personal Consumption Expenditures prices, the Fed's preferred inflation measure, which rose 0.3% in September. Cooler readings alongside 3% growth would be the first real evidence of an AI productivity boom. If productivity rises fast enough to lower the cost of producing each unit, the Fed could hold or cut rates while growth stays strong. The articles leave open whether AI will deliver a rapid productivity miracle or gradual gains.

stories.Headline: US Commerce Department restricts AI chip exports to data centers serving Chinese firms
stories.Summary:
The Bureau of Industry and Security issued new rules on November 16, 2026, to tighten controls on advanced semiconductors. These regulations restrict the export of AI chips and servers to Malaysia and limit large-scale cloud services to China. The U.S. Department of Commerce aims to close routes that Chinese companies used to obtain computing power through overseas data centers. This interim rule requires licenses for shipments of advanced AI chips to data centers anywhere in the world. Such licenses are necessary if the facilities provide large amounts of computing power to companies headquartered in China or restricted jurisdictions.

The new rules affect data center customers in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil who must now receive special licenses. One specific Malaysian project known as A201 expects to open next year with hundreds of millions of dollars in Nvidia servers. This facility was designed to provide computing power to a Chinese technology giant despite existing U.S. restrictions on direct exports. Cantor Fitzgerald served as a financing or placement agent for companies including Bitdeer Technologies Group and Gorilla Technology Group in Asia. These specific Asian data center operations could be affected by the tighter American export controls issued by the Commerce Department.

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick resisted efforts by other senior administration officials to strengthen restrictions on Nvidia chip shipments to Asia. The Commerce Department defended its enforcement record and denied directing officials to avoid investigating particular companies regarding chip exports. Officials maintained that Lutnick fully divested his financial interests in Cantor and had no discussions with the firm concerning Nvidia. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly criticized the failure to blacklist Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company suspected of helping China. Bessent argued the administration already has the tools to limit sales to China and should focus on enforcement.

Democratic Senators Elizabeth Warren and Ron Wyden demanded information about a loan from Tether to a trust benefiting Lutnick's children. This loan was reportedly secured by assets including more than half of the equity in the firm Cantor Fitzgerald. Republican lawmakers also questioned whether U.S. technology is reaching Chinese interests, while Democrats demanded stronger enforcement of chip rules. Companies in China and other countries are affected because they can no longer easily evade restrictions through long-standing loopholes. The White House has expressed confidence in Lutnick despite the mounting questions over the decisions made by his department.

Lutnick led Cantor Fitzgerald for more than three decades before joining the administration of President Donald Trump as Commerce Secretary. His sons, Brandon and Kyle, now lead the investment firm that worked with companies developing data centers in Southeast Asia. In July 2025, reports indicated Cantor offered to purchase potential tariff-refund claims for 20 to 30 percent of their value. This occurred while Lutnick was one of the most outspoken advocates for tariffs within the current U.S. administration. Additionally, the Commerce Department approved Nvidia export licenses involving Chinese companies with links to military contractors or sanctioned entities.

Lawmakers are intensifying scrutiny of how the Commerce Department handles chip exports amid the controversy involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The department faced questions over recent months about why the Entity List had not been updated for over a year. Future actions remain open regarding whether the government will blacklist more companies like Megaspeed to prevent technology diversion. It is unclear if the new licensing requirements will successfully stop Chinese firms from accessing advanced computing power abroad. The articles leave open whether the conflict of interest allegations will lead to further official investigations into Howard Lutnick.
