stories.Headline: DDN offers software-defined EXAScaler deployment for enterprise AI infrastructure
stories.Summary:
DDN announced a new software-defined deployment option for EXAScaler on November 17, 2026, in Santa Clara, California. This new option is enabled by the upcoming EXAScaler 7 release for enterprise AI infrastructure. The company allows customers to run high-performance data infrastructure software on qualified industry-standard servers. This change provides an alternative to using purpose-built systems or cloud partners for deployment. A limited beta for this software-defined deployment is planned for early 2027.

The software will start on DDN AI2200 servers, with qualified third-party appliances following later. This makes both EXAScaler and DDN Infinia available in software-defined formats for various customers. Hyperscalers and NCPs with established storage infrastructure can now deploy EXAScaler on industry-standard hardware. This model allows AI platform teams to select hardware suited to their specific requirements. DDN will continue developing purpose-built systems for those preferring integrated performance and reliability.

Omer Asad, the Chief Product Officer at DDN, is responsible for this product direction. He stated that AI infrastructure is becoming more diverse and customers want more freedom. Asad explained that making EXAScaler available as software extends flexibility across the company portfolio. He noted that customers can choose integrated systems or deploy software on third-party hardware. This approach maintains the core capabilities that customers depend on from the EXAScaler platform.

The new model affects organizations that bring AI and HPC workflows together in one environment. In life sciences, researchers use AI surrogate models on molecular dynamics simulation outputs to predict protein behavior. Software-defined EXAScaler on qualified hardware allows simulation and training to run on the same data. This removes the need for copying data between different environments during the research process. These capabilities help researchers avoid repeating every computationally intensive simulation during their work.

DDN has provided AI data storage and management platforms for over 20 years of innovation. The company serves national labs, research institutions, financial firms, and autonomous vehicle innovators. Its platforms support next-generation AI factories, hyperscale clouds, and Sovereign AI initiatives. DDN is recognized as a leading provider for the largest AI deployments on Earth. The company offers EXA, Infinia, and various intelligent data management platforms to its customers.

DDN is developing enhancements for multi-tenancy, performance, and data protection for the EXAScaler platform. These specific enhancements are targeted for general availability in the first half of 2027. The company will share validated performance data as it becomes available to the public. The articles leave open the specific dates for general availability, as they may change. It remains unclear which third-party appliances will be qualified for the software-defined deployment.

stories.Headline: Mullin says AI superintelligence may have caused Microsoft, bank and airline outages
stories.Summary:
Major technology disruptions hit Microsoft, several large banks, and the aviation industry throughout the week ending November 17, 2026. These outages affected core Microsoft 365 services including Teams, Outlook, Exchange Online, and Copilot across 74 different countries. On Friday, the Federal Aviation Administration grounded flights nationwide for over four hours due to instability in legacy equipment. Customers of Capital One, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, and Chase reported banking outages on Monday.

The situation requires an investigation into how rapidly advancing artificial intelligence might overwhelm older systems that cannot keep pace. Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin noted that a technology expert suggested superintelligence could be responsible for these events. He explained that AI programs capable of writing code might create a ripple effect when they attempt to self-fix. On November 14, officials from the FAA and the Transportation Department stated the aviation issues were not connected to the new SMART AI system.

Secretary Mullin told Fox News that he is 98 percent certain a cyberattack did not cause the disruptions. He argued that there are no footprints of an attack and no one has claimed responsibility for the events. Conversely, former national security adviser Michael Flynn suggested on social media that the patterns were suspicious and looked like a massive cyberattack. President Donald Trump dismissed the concerns on Tuesday, stating that such things happen when organizations are big and powerful.

stories.Headline: Tencent updates LightVela AI Agent to function as a personal assistant with long term memory
stories.Summary:
Tencent recently updated its cloud based AI Agent product called LightVela to evolve into a personal assistant. The company launched the public beta in April and opened the service to all users in late September. This new version allows users to create multiple AI assistants with independent personas and long term memory. It also includes a cloud computer that provides the Agent with an independent desktop environment. These upgrades aim to integrate AI more deeply into the daily work and life of users.

The product supports interaction via web pages and software including WeChat, Feishu, DingTalk and QQ. New users receive one month of free experience and 4500 AI points. The connector includes six applications named Tencent Meeting, Feishu, DingTalk, Tencent Docs, Tencent Securities and ima. Users can customize Bots using recommended templates or a persona test. The interface is divided into Daily and Explore sections to manage skills and settings.

Lei Tech conducted a real world test to evaluate the performance of the new LightVela version. The tester noted that the product is more convenient than deploying the open source Hermes Agent manually. However, the tester found that the interactive design for delivering files is not intuitive enough. The researcher Bot failed to provide a requested screenshot due to a display service conflict. The tester also experienced failures when trying to launch a personal display website.

The tester reported that the AI cited international site documents that were not applicable to domestic users. This suggests that users must still verify if sources actually support the statements made by the AI. The "My Workbench Beta" feature provides templates for data dashboards and personal display benches. These tools require technical stacks such as React, TypeScript and Tailwind to function. The tester found that the actual access to launched pages sometimes showed the page did not exist.

LightVela originally migrated the open source Hermes Agent to the cloud to save users from deployment and maintenance. It now positions itself as a cloud personal assistant for development, business operation and financial management. The product uses SkillHub to share existing AI skills and offers collectible persona cards. It includes a Diagnosis Center to help users reset the working environment. The design logic requires creating an assistant before deciding its materials and interaction methods.

The product remains far from perfect compared to other mature designs like WorkBuddy and Muse. Users must still understand environment failures and technical requirements to use the system effectively. The articles leave open whether ordinary users can smoothly find the functions they need. It is unclear if the cloud computer can operate software independently without user takeover. The final analysis suggests that the product details are not yet sufficiently polished.

stories.Headline: Trinity College philosophy faculty ban students from using AI in coursework
stories.Summary:
Trinity College’s philosophy department has barred students from using generative artificial intelligence on coursework, arguing the technology undermines its mission of teaching students to think, read, write, speak, reason and live ethically. The department’s faculty members, including Shane Ewegen, began deliberating on the policy with colleagues in the spring. Faculty members agreed in September on a concise three-sentence rule. The rule states that any use of AI in any capacity and for any purpose is forbidden. The department notified the campus community of the change last month.

The policy forbids students from using AI in any capacity whatsoever in preparation for classes or in the classroom for philosophy courses. It specifies that students cannot use AI for brainstorming, for writing or editing, or even to construct bibliographies. The policy states that using AI for any of those reasons undermines the core educational missions of the department. The department settled on a fairly short version of the policy after exchanging emails with different versions, some lengthy and detailed and some very short. The policy leaves any punitive repercussions for violating it entirely up to the individual professor’s discretion.

Ewegen said the philosophy department was univocal in adopting the policy and its language, though members may have differing perspectives on the reasoning behind it. He said that over the summer faculty started exchanging emails about adopting a single policy for all philosophy courses, above all to avoid confusion among students if each professor had a different policy. He said that the more they talked, the clearer it became that they were more or less in agreement in being emphatically against AI in its academic uses, really in any capacity. He said he wanted to include a sentence saying a student would fail the class if evidence of use was discovered, but it was pointed out that other members might feel differently and that a professor might in the moment feel a different outcome was warranted. Ewegen said he has tried to explain to students that the product being sold to them by billionaires’ companies promises something while in fact stealing something from them.

A Trinity College spokesperson said the college’s leaders recognize AI’s rapid expansion and remain committed to open, ongoing dialogue across the campus community. The spokesperson said that consistent with practices across higher education, faculty determine when and how AI is used in their courses based on their expertise and learning objectives. The spokesperson said the college believes students should be prepared for a world in which AI is increasingly present, including developing the knowledge and judgment to use these tools responsibly and effectively. The spokesperson said Trinity encourages faculty and students to engage thoughtfully with complex questions concerning the appropriate use of AI in an academic setting and the broader opportunities and challenges AI presents. The University of Chicago banned AI and tech in class in the social-sciences division, and Duke University’s classical-studies department expressly prohibits the use of AI on assignments.

Trinity’s collegewide AI guidance says faculty are responsible for defining the content and goals of their courses, communicating expectations, and evaluating students fairly and consistently. The guidance says students in turn make choices about their learning, from engaging in self-reflection to practicing integrity and deciding whether AI will replace their own thinking. The guidance says these practices extend to AI, shaping lifelong capacities related to purpose, resilience, and decision making. The administration devised its policies with minimal faculty input and with no faculty vote, and they are meant to apply to the college as a whole. Ewegen said he had heard students admitting to some confusion because they were not really sure, getting information from the administration and differing policies from each individual professor.

Ewegen said that in the department’s conversations, faculty agreed that really any use of AI for philosophy courses or philosophy research undermines rather than facilitates learning goals. He said the department has not seen evidence that using AI to help brainstorm, edit a paper, write a paper, or serve as an interlocutor for studying for oral finals promotes or improves students’ ability to engage in those skills. He said the department sees more and more reports about the harmful effects of AI on students’ abilities to think, read and write. He said the department was worried about ethical considerations surrounding AI, including the environmental impact of developing and using AI, such as mining massive mineral sites in the global south that contaminates water supplies. He said the department did not think the technology at this stage is redeemable in any way, at least when it comes to use in a philosophical classroom.

Ewegen said his personal hope is that the policy will provoke other departments to codify policies of their own and make those policies public. He said it is only beneficial if there is a broader conversation within the institution and across institutions about this technology and the dangers it poses. He spearheaded a faculty effort earlier this year calling on Trinity to divest from AI companies. Each faculty member now has the policy to include on their syllabi, and whether there are punitive effects and what they are will depend in each case. Ewegen said that in his case it usually means certainly failing the assignment and more likely the course if it comes to light that a student has used AI in some substantive way.

stories.Headline: Microsoft and Salesforce launch Copilotforce to bring Salesforce context into Microsoft Copilot
stories.Summary:
Microsoft and Salesforce announced Copilotforce on Nov. 17, 2026, from Redmond, Washington, and San Francisco, unveiling it at Microsoft Ignite. The partnership brings Salesforce customer context, business processes and actions into Microsoft Copilot and other AI-powered productivity experiences. It introduces integrations across Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Teams and Microsoft Fabric, including Salesforce in Copilot, a plugin in public preview with 38 or more prebuilt sales skills. Salesforce in Copilot is available in public preview as a beta beginning today. Microsoft Work IQ, the intelligence layer powering Copilot, provides context from Teams meetings, Outlook emails and documents across SharePoint and OneDrive.

Salesforce in Copilot connects customer context with work across the business so employees can decide and act without switching applications. Through authenticated Salesforce MCP access, sellers can retrieve customer information and take supported business actions within existing Salesforce permissions. Salesforce continues to govern access and business actions, while Microsoft applies existing enterprise compliance controls to communications and documents. Supported writeback actions to the CRM require explicit user confirmation and respect existing validation rules. A two-way Zero Copy connection between Salesforce Data 360 and Microsoft Fabric lets teams work across both platforms without building pipelines or maintaining duplicate datasets.

Judson Althoff, CEO of Microsoft Commercial Business, said AI is only as powerful as the data and context that grounds it. He said bringing Salesforce customer data and sales skills together with Work IQ context in Copilot lets joint customers unlock actionable insights across core business applications. He said Copilotforce will give sales teams intelligence for faster, higher-confidence decisions while maintaining the governance and trust enterprises demand. Miguel Milano, President and Chief Operating Officer of Salesforce, said Copilotforce brings Salesforce to the largest surface in enterprise software today. He said combining the number one CRM with the number one productivity surface transforms AI from a standalone tool into a driver of productivity, smarter decisions and customer success.

Julie Sweet, Chair and CEO of Accenture, said Accenture is a Global Partner of the Year for both Salesforce and Microsoft and one of their top customers. She said the combined strengths of the three companies will reinvent sales with AI, giving sellers more time with customers while trusted intelligence and agents work alongside them. Accenture is the design and implementation partner, with expertise across 13 industries globally, and a pilot customer deploying the integrations in its own global sales organization. Accenture has scaled Copilot to more than 740,000 people and is one of the largest Salesforce users globally with 55,000 users. Accenture is also customer zero for Copilotforce, sharing learnings to help clients turn existing Salesforce and Microsoft investments into a better way to sell.

The Pipeline Review and Close Planning skills help decide which opportunities deserve attention and build a path to signature, with proposals and business cases in Word and PowerPoint. The Deal Review, Customer Health and Renewal Radar skills see beyond the recorded stage or renewal date to a customer concern in an Outlook thread, an escalation in Teams or an unresolved commitment behind a stalled deal. The Call Follow-Up skill turns customer conversations into follow-up drafts, internal recaps and proposed CRM activities. Sales Cloud in Teams, now available in pilot, brings Salesforce customer context into conversations so sellers can see pipeline and quota progress, get deal notifications and find briefing materials. With Data Federation, now generally available, joint customers can directly query and analyze supported Microsoft Fabric OneLake data within Salesforce Data 360.

A service agent can see a customer's recent purchases, a marketer can build a segment from spending behavior and an AI agent can answer from current data, all without moving source data out of Fabric. The Salesforce Data 360 shortcut, now in public preview, lets organizations share curated Data 360 customer intelligence into OneLake for analytics, reporting and AI workloads without duplicating data. Data sharing from Data 360 into OneLake is in public preview, and Sales Cloud in Teams is in pilot with enterprise customers, with open beta coming later this year. Statements about future direction and intent are subject to change or withdrawal without notice and represent goals and objectives only. Regional availability and customer access are governed by applicable customer agreements.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: Apra chair John Lonsdale says third parties are a focus as the regulator examines AI risks
stories.Summary:
The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority is examining the third parties that banks, super funds and insurers rely on as it deals with the risks of artificial intelligence, according to Law360 Australia. APRA Chair John Lonsdale said those third parties are a focus for the regulator, the report said. The report was published on November 18, 2026, and was written by Antony Scholefield. The report described APRA as being at the edge of its mandate in scrutinising third parties on AI.

The report did not give any further numbers, dates or names beyond those of Lonsdale, Scholefield and the regulator itself. It did not say what the scrutiny requires of the third parties or what changes it might bring for the banks, super funds and insurers involved. The report also did not set out a timeline for any action by APRA. The available article was a preview that stopped before the full text.

The report said Lonsdale made the comments about the third parties being a focus for the regulator. It did not give further detail of what he said beyond that. The report did not say who else was responsible or what other officials said. The report did not give the context behind the comments or say what happens next.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: UC law school launches three-day certificate lab to teach lawyers AI tool building
stories.Summary:
LexLab, which serves as the legal technology hub for the University of California College of the Law at San Francisco, is launching a new educational program. This intensive three-day course, known as the Law & AI Certificate Lab, will take place from December 1 to December 3, 2026. The program provides lawyers and organizational leaders with a condensed version of a semester-long course previously offered only to law students. Participants will engage in a deep dive into the logic of legal artificial intelligence through hands-on exploration of various systems.

The curriculum requires students to utilize the AI platform Harvey and the AI company Legora, along with the website builder Replit. Graduates of the certificate program should be able to create repeatable checklists, playbooks, and other workflows instead of simply using chat functions. The training teaches students how to evaluate different AI vendors and decide if technology should be purchased or built internally. Additionally, the course covers how to manage competence, conflicts, confidentiality, and privilege issues within an AI-augmented legal practice.

The University of California College of the Law at San Francisco is responsible for implementing this specialized training for legal professionals. The institution designed the course to help practitioners move beyond basic AI interactions toward more sophisticated tool building and management. By providing this technical foundation, the school aims to equip leaders with the skills necessary to navigate the complexities of modern legal technology. The program focuses on the practical application of AI to improve efficiency and maintain professional standards in the law.

stories.Headline: Fed governor Barr warns AI borrowing boom poses ten risks to financial stability
stories.Summary:
Fed Governor Michael Barr gave a long speech on November 16, 2026, regarding AI investment risks. He detailed ten big, complex, and opaque threats to financial stability. These risks stem from a borrowing boom, circular financing, and high equity prices. The Federal Reserve also warned about these stability aspects in its latest Financial Stability Report. This report was released on the Friday preceding the governor's speech.

On-balance-sheet debt for the seven largest AI firms may exceed 800 billion dollars by year end 2026. Off-balance-sheet liabilities, including lease commitments and energy contracts, are estimated to exceed 3 trillion dollars. Smaller firms have over 100 billion dollars in circular financing from hyperscalers and GPU producers. These arrangements involve equity investments used to rent or purchase compute from the investors. Some firms also use collateral guarantees for asset-based financings to support their credit.

Governor Barr stated that investment losses could lower output growth through direct drops in investment. He noted that a significant repricing of AI investments could be amplified by complex financing. Barr warned that rapid deleveraging and self-reinforcing fire sales could occur due to high risk appetite. He mentioned that counterparty exposures could rise during periods of equity market volatility. The governor also cautioned that AI trading models might autonomously develop collusive behavior.

Unsophisticated investors are affected because financial complexity makes it hard to know where risk resides. Lower-credit-quality firms are impacted as their cost of capital has risen significantly in recent months. Hedge funds are mentioned as having high leverage that could lead to rapid deleveraging. Large dealers are involved because they provide leverage via prime brokerage services. The broader economy could suffer if wealth losses lower consumer and business spending.

The current boom is compared to the telecom investment cycle of the late 1990s and early 2000s. This earlier period was characterized by a similar boom and bust cycle of investment. The articles mention dark fiber as an example of excess capacity that took years to become useful. Some theoretical research shows that Q-learning trading algorithms can learn to manipulate markets through spoofing. These algorithms can create and exploit bubbles, which then destabilize the markets.

Specialized chips may depreciate quickly as newer technologies overtake them, making current capacity useless. It remains unclear if electrical infrastructure like substations and grid connections will find other uses. The Federal Reserve will continue monitoring exposures to counterparties with large positions in AI. The articles leave open whether smaller firms can replace supplier funding with revenue from customers. It is also unknown if the current debt levels will surpass those of the telecom boom.

stories.Headline: Minnesota doctors and lawmakers say AI healthcare oversight lags behind the technology
stories.Summary:
Artificial intelligence is already shaping care in Minnesota, but doctors and lawmakers say oversight is not keeping pace with how quickly the technology is changing. At Fairview, AI helps predict where ambulances may be needed, gives families real-time updates and creates electronic medical notes from doctor and patient conversations. The health system also uses AI to check the quality of MRIs before patients leave, according to KSTP. Dr. Sameer Badlani, Fairview’s chief digital and AI officer, said the tools let people get picked up sooner and dropped off sooner, with better use of the fleet and crew.

Badlani said AI is definitely evolving faster than regulations are, and Minnesota currently has no blanket law requiring healthcare providers to disclose every time AI is used. Rep. Peggy Scott, a Republican from Andover, said she wants stronger protections for Minnesota patients and has already tried to put guardrails around AI in healthcare. Asked whether there should be disclosure any time AI is being used, Scott said 100%. The Minnesota Medical Association said bias is one of the main concerns with AI in healthcare, and a task force led by Dr. Rebecca Thomas studied the issue for more than a year.

That task force determined there is an urgent need for more oversight of AI in healthcare. Thomas said the question of who would be responsible if artificial intelligence makes a harmful mistake is not straightforward right now. Fairview said patient recordings from the note-taking tool never leave its secure network, have restricted access and are deleted within a few weeks after they are converted into medical records. Fairview said it already notifies patients about AI and plans to add a notice to its online patient portal so patients can opt out of the note-taking tool.

Articles.Title: AI already plays key role in healthcare. It’s also evolving faster than Minnesota laws.

stories.Summary:
The legal technology hub known as LexLab at UC Law San Francisco announced a new educational program on November 13, 2026. This initiative is called the Law and AI Certificate Lab, which is designed as a three-day course for building legal tools. The intensive program will take place from December 1 to December 3 for a small group of participants. It provides a condensed version of the AI curriculum that the law school typically offers its students over a full semester. The course requires the participation of up to 24 individuals, including lawyers, government officials, academics, and technologists.

These attendees will use specialized technology provided by companies such as Legora, Harvey, and the website builder Replit. The curriculum focuses on the actual development of artificial intelligence tools while addressing important ethical considerations. This training allows professionals to build and evaluate their own software solutions within a short timeframe. Adjunct professor Damien Charlotin, who created the AI Hallucination Cases database, is directing the program alongside adjunct professor Erin Fraser.

Fraser also serves as an associate at the firm McDermott Will & Schulte while helping to lead this lab. These directors intend for the course to support professionals in navigating the complexities of modern legal technology. They aim to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and the practical application of AI in legal settings. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Nvidia reports record quarterly revenue of 115.8 billion dollars under interim CEO Colette Kress
stories.Summary:
Nvidia released its third quarter fiscal year 2027 financial results in the early hours of November 18, Beijing time. The company reported record revenue and profit following the sudden departure of founder and former CEO Jensen Huang. Interim CEO Colette Kress, the former CFO, led the company during this high profile financial reporting period. The report arrived amid turmoil that caused the company's market value to drop by 800 billion dollars. This loss is equivalent to three and a half times the total market value of the company Alibaba.

Quarterly revenue reached 115.8 billion US dollars, while net profit hit 65.3 billion US dollars. Data center business revenue was 107.6 billion US dollars, which accounted for 93 percent of total revenue. Revenue from Hong Kong and mainland China was 11.05 billion US dollars, representing a 272 percent increase. The board established a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee to manage global trade risk and compliance. These changes dismantle the previous model where Jensen Huang personally mediated between Washington and global customers.

Interim CEO Colette Kress oversaw the release of these record breaking financial figures for the third quarter. Jensen Huang stated he is willing to return to lead Nvidia if the board invites him. Chairman Harvey Jones firmly stated the board has no intention of restoring Huang to the CEO position. Jones also refused to accept any questions from analysts regarding the potential return of the former leader. The company continues to exclude Chinese data center computing revenue from its financial guidance for the next quarter.

Cloud vendors and AI enterprises in China are now accelerating the adaptation of domestic GPUs for their needs. Some Chinese firms are contacting Southeast Asian computing power lessors to lock in resources before policies tighten. A cloud vendor salesperson noted that computing power shortages make business easier for those holding existing stock. Other industry insiders believe that domestic acceleration cards may soon be required for 80 percent of subsidy projects. US cloud service providers and chip manufacturing partners also saw their stock prices drop sharply during this turmoil.

Nvidia built a massive industrial network of chip manufacturing and cloud computing using high end GPU advantages. The US Department of Commerce issued new regulations on November 16 to supervise data centers in third countries. These rules extend restrictions on Chinese computing power from physical chip exports to overseas remote access services. Domestic chips like Huawei Ascend, Cambricon, and Moore Threads have seen increased adaptation since February of this year. Huawei Ascend entered the official PyTorch support system in September to expand the underlying software ecosystem.

Supporters of Jensen Huang are creating a war room with Silicon Valley executives to seek White House support. An online petition asking for the reinstatement of the founder has attracted more than 180,000 signatures. The market remains volatile, with stock prices rebounding by about 3.4 percent after the financial report release. It remains unclear if the new management will make it more difficult for Chinese firms to get GPUs. The articles leave open whether the complex contradictions behind the founder's departure will be fully resolved.

stories.Headline: Dell says context lifts AI agent accuracy from 60% to 94% in its testing
stories.Summary:
Dell Technologies executives said at SC26, in an interview broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media's livestreaming studio, that feeding AI agents the right context lifted accuracy in Dell's own testing from roughly 60% to about 94%, and they described new data intelligence features meant to bring enterprise AI factories into production. Srinath Alapati, senior director of product marketing for AI Data Platform at Dell, said the bottom line is that wrong data produces wrong outcomes. He appeared with Alison Biers, senior director of product marketing for compute, networking and global industries, and Adam Glick, senior director of AI solutions product marketing for compute, in a conversation with theCUBE Research's John Furrier. Dell recently extended its AI Data Platform with semantic and knowledge graph features aimed at enterprises that want the large-scale AI capabilities neocloud providers built first.

Dell's newly announced Agentic Data Gateway sits in the orchestration layer as a single point of control backed by a Model Context Protocol server, according to Alapati, because enterprises cannot give agents unfettered access to their systems. Storage intelligence tells customers what data they hold, who owns it and how large it is, while the new data intelligence capabilities track lineage and provenance, and hybrid workflows extend the model across the edge, the cloud and the data center. Alapati said other data platform providers want customers to bring all data to the platform, which is not always possible because it is expensive and data is always being generated, so Dell sends only metadata and leaves data where customers want it. On infrastructure, Dell OpenManage Rack Scale extends management beyond compute endpoints to the network fabric, power and cooling, giving operators a single operational plane from day zero through day two, Biers said. A rebuilt, intent-based Dell Fabric Manager replaces SmartFabric Manager, and PowerRack systems treat the full rack as the unit of deployment.

Biers said a rack goes from the loading dock to full production in literally six hours, work that used to take months and is now cut in half or less. Glick said more than 6,500 customers now use the Dell AI Factory, and a growing share are core enterprises asking for help putting AI to work, while validated designs built with Nvidia and other partners cover both hardware and the full software stack and Dell is expanding its labs as independent software companies join the ecosystem. He compared compute to a factory's assembly line, which does not run without a warehouse feeding it raw materials, meaning the data that goes into it. The segment was sponsored by Dell, and the disclosure states that neither Dell nor other sponsors have editorial control over content on theCUBE or SiliconANGLE.

stories.Headline: Kaiser mental health clinicians ratify contract with AI advisory role and 17% wage increase
stories.Summary:
About 2,200 Kaiser Permanente mental health clinicians in Northern California and the Central Valley ratified a four-year labor contract, with 97% voting in favor after more than a year of contentious negotiations. The National Union of Healthcare Workers said Monday that its group of some 2,200 Kaiser mental health therapists, social workers and psychologists had voted to approve the agreement. About 80% of workers cast ballots during a several-day voting period that concluded Sunday. The contract was ratified with 97% support, the union said. Kaiser said it could not immediately respond to a request for comment about the agreement.

The contract bars layoffs through late 2029 and gives clinicians a role in advising Kaiser on AI and other technology changes. The contract includes wage increases of about 17% over the course of the contract. The union's last contract expired at the end of September 2025, and the new four-year agreement retroactively covers a period beginning from that expiration. The company will be required to notify workers in advance of changes in its model of care, including use of AI or other new technologies. The contract creates a process for a union-appointed group of mental healthcare clinicians to give advice to management on the changes and for the union to bargain over effects if the company moves forward.

Kaiser social worker Ilana Marcucci-Morris, who has been involved in the bargaining sessions, called the contract "a big victory" but said the company's behavioral healthcare still falls below the mark. She said workers "bought ourselves some time to give public leaders and legislators time to put parameters in place around AI." She said they "didn't get fully what we wanted in the language" but that it is a win that gave them time to strategize and make sure mental health care stays human. Marcucci-Morris said Kaiser had largely held firm in rejecting union language saying AI tools could be used to support, but not replace therapists. She said the company also pushed to negotiate severance and other layoff provisions, indicating that industry headwinds around AI had made layoffs "a real threat," even amid climbing patient demand for mental health services.

Kaiser spokesperson Candice Lee previously told The Times that "AI does not replace human assessment and care," but that it "holds significant potential to benefit healthcare by supporting better diagnostics, enhancing patient-clinician relationships, optimizing clinicians' time, and ensuring fairness in care experiences and health outcomes by addressing individual needs." NUHW President Emeritus Sal Rosselli said that now that the contract is ratified, workers will need to "be vigilant" to "make Kaiser fully respect the work of its clinicians and the needs of its patients." Kaiser's mental health workers in Southern California who are also represented by NUHW reached a bargaining agreement last year after a nearly seven-month strike. Workers have accused Kaiser in recent months of implementing harsh productivity metrics on clinicians, cutting into their time to respond to patient calls and emails, record notes and prepare for appointments and pressuring the staff to overbook patients. Kaiser did not immediately respond to questions about the productivity metrics.

Last fall, a group of Kaiser workers traveled to Las Vegas to protest remarks by Kaiser Chief Executive Greg Adams and pass out fliers to conference attendees about staffing shortage problems. The union had held a one-day strike in March over AI language. In October, workers authorized a three-day work stoppage, but held off on moving forward with it ahead of a scheduled mediation session with Kaiser that month. Over the summer, the union filed a complaint with the California Department of Managed Health Care over Kaiser's use of digital algorithms to screen patients seeking care. The union alleged that the practice continued despite state law requiring that treatment determinations be made by licensed providers.

Kaiser has maintained that those decisions are still being made by licensed professionals, saying in a statement to news outlet CalMatters that the tool conducts supportive screening and "does not use AI to diagnose patients, make clinical decisions, or determine medical necessity." A Kaiser spokesperson said to the news outlet that patients could still reach a live person by calling a phone number displayed during the e-visit process, and that the online screening tool was "not the only path" to care. The state Department of Managed Health Care has not yet issued a determination about the complaint. Kaiser did not respond to questions from The Times about the complaint. Marcucci-Morris said Kaiser's shift in negotiations came after the Democrats' sweep during the midterm elections that indicated some voter backlash to AI.

stories.Headline: Autodesk says AI will reshape Indian design and manufacturing jobs and pledges $350 million to train talent
stories.Summary:
Autodesk, the California-based company that makes 3D design and engineering software, said on November 17, 2026 that artificial intelligence will reshape employment across India’s design, manufacturing and creative industries rather than eliminate jobs. The company said demand for professionals with AI skills is expected to rise as firms adopt automated design and production workflows. It said AI-related jobs across the Design and Make industries, covering digital modelling, engineering, manufacturing and creative production, increased 147% in two years. Demand for AI skills also grew 75% faster than for non-AI roles, according to the company.

Parminder Singh, Autodesk’s Country Head for Design and Manufacturing and Media and Entertainment for India and SAARC, said AI is a capability enhancer for these industries and will reshape jobs far more than replace them. He said every major technological shift, from CAD to cloud computing, has automated routine tasks while creating new opportunities for innovation and productivity. Autodesk announced in June 2026 a $350 million commitment over three years to prepare talent for AI-powered jobs. By 2028 the initiative aims to give free software access to 60 million students and educators, train nearly one million people in AI workflows and enable more than 200,000 to earn certifications.

The company is partnering with the Directorate General of Training across 14,500 Industrial Training Institutes, besides IIT Bombay, IIT Palakkad, Anna University and VIT Vellore. Its earlier initiatives have reached five million learners across 16,000 institutions. Singh said the skills gap in India is real but addressable when industry, academia and government work together, and he advocated integrating industry-relevant tools and certifications into education. Autodesk’s AI foundation models, developed with MIT and Cornell University, are designed to reason across 3D geometry, materials, fabrication methods and performance constraints.

More than half of Autodesk Store users in India are now startups, freelancers and small and medium businesses, and the company’s Flex offering of prepaid daily tokens seeks to lower entry barriers to cloud adoption. Electric vehicle maker Vayve Mobility used Fusion to reduce design time by 50%. India’s animation and visual effects sector, valued at $1.24 billion in 2024, is projected to reach $1.75 billion by 2027, while the broader animation, visual effects, gaming and comics industry is expected to need nearly two million professionals by 2030.

stories.Headline: Dell adds Nvidia and AMD systems to its AI Factory to move agentic AI into production
stories.Summary:
Dell announced new additions to its Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA on 16 November 2026, according to IT Brief Australia, extending a portfolio it says now includes more than 420 offerings and serves more than 6,500 customers. Dell Technologies also expanded its Dell AI Factory with new AMD-based infrastructure products spanning servers, modular platforms and rack-scale systems, IT Brief Asia reported on 17 November 2026. The Nvidia announcements focus on four areas: data preparation for AI, management software for AI infrastructure, partner-built validated solutions, and new storage options for large AI workloads. The AMD update includes the Dell PowerEdge M8825 server, new configurations for the Dell AI Platform with AMD, and the AMD Helios Rack-scale Solution from Dell. Dell says the changes are intended to help companies move agentic AI projects from pilot stages into production.

The PowerEdge M8825 is an air-cooled server based on AMD EPYC processors, offering up to 512 cores and 1,024 threads per node for agentic AI and other compute-intensive workloads. Dell expanded its Dell AI Platform with AMD by adding modular configurations built on the PowerEdge XE7745 and R7725 servers, which use AMD Instinct MI350P PCIe GPUs. The AMD Helios Rack-scale Solution can deliver up to 2.9 exaflops of performance with 72 AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs, paired with Dell PowerRack for networking and storage. Dell added Agentic Data Gateway, which in internal testing reduced token consumption by as much as 76% and increased answer accuracy from 60% to 94%. Dell introduced Dell OpenManage Rack Scale, which can manage up to 100,000 devices, up from 8,000 in the previous generation.

Arthur Lewis, President, Infrastructure Solutions Group, Dell Technologies, said AI outcomes do not come from models alone and take data with the right context, infrastructure that scales and solutions validated to work together. Lewis said the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA is that full-stack foundation, one you own and control, with 6,500 customers already proving it works. Dell said Dell and AMD are giving customers more ways to deploy AI with confidence, whether they are starting small, scaling fast, or going all-in on frontier infrastructure. Dell describes the liquid-cooled storage platform as a 2OU platform supporting up to 32 NVMe drives and designed for file, block, object or parallel file storage. Dell says the 1U platform offers 67% higher drive density per rack unit than the previous generation.

Ashish Nadkarni, Group Vice President and General Manager, Global Domain Lead, Enterprise Infrastructure, IDC, said success increasingly depends on combining trusted data, scalable infrastructure, operational simplicity and ecosystem integration into a repeatable model for AI deployment. Nadkarni said vendors like Dell that help reduce complexity and accelerate time to value will be well positioned to support enterprise AI adoption. Dell says software-defined PowerScale on Dell Exascale has achieved NVIDIA-Certified Storage validation at the Foundation level. Dell says Dell Fabric Manager, in internal lab analysis, could cut Day-2 operational effort by up to 80% while maintaining a fully accurate device inventory. Partners in the latest wave include F5, JFrog, DataRobot, Dynatrace, Ipsotek, Iternal Technologies, Teradata, Aible, Atolio, Maven AGI, OpenAI and ClearML.

Dell is also adding hybrid data pipeline orchestration so pipelines can run where data already sits, including on-premises private clouds, Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA environments, non-Dell systems and public clouds. Other changes include Storage Intelligence and Data Intelligence tools to show data provenance, quality and usage across large file environments, along with a unified data access layer for tables, images, video and documents. Dell says the system can route vectors to existing databases without requiring migration, and cited indexing speeds of up to 12 times faster based on external benchmark data. The platform is also being linked with tools from LangChain, OpenAI, Codex and Unstructured.io. The Enterprise SONiC Distribution by Dell Technologies is being extended to support additional platforms, including the Z9964F-ON and NVIDIA Spectrum SN4700 switches.

The broader architecture also includes modular infrastructure built around Dell PowerStore, Dell PowerEdge XE9785 systems with NVIDIA HGX B300 GPUs, and Dell-supported NVIDIA AI Enterprise software. The expanded AMD platform will include validated support for AMD Enterprise AI Suite, Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform and Red Hat AI Enterprise. Dell says its AI Factory Engineers model brings together teams across platform design, workload delivery, data, governance and security, while its data centre services focus on power, cooling and space planning for AI deployments. Dell says the modular approach lets customers start with a single compute node and add GPUs, nodes, storage or networking as demand grows. Dell said the AMD package is backed by deployment and lifecycle services, giving customers a single supplier for integrated AI infrastructure.

stories.Headline: Former Commerce officials allege Howard Lutnick failed to act on sensitive computer chip smuggling
stories.Summary:
Former Commerce officials allege that Secretary Howard Lutnick failed to act on sensitive computer chip smuggling. These ex-employees describe his tenure as being marked by chaos and micromanaging. The allegations involve a refusal to use national security tools over the last year. This situation came to light as scrutiny heightened in November 2026. The controversy follows the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

The department stopped adding firms to the Entity List after October 9, 2025. This created the first yearlong gap in additions since 2008. In May 2025, Lutnick rolled back a January 2025 rule blocking adversaries from AI chips. A new rule on Monday requires licenses for exports to Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand. This aims to close loopholes used to route chips to China.

Howard Lutnick and his deputy, Jeffrey Kessler, are accused of blocking enforcement. Former staff claim Kessler micromanaged every minor decision and created a bottleneck. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent expressed frustration that Lutnick failed to follow through on chip bans. Bessent stated that President Trump clearly wanted to stop China from receiving sophisticated Nvidia chips. The Commerce Department did not respond to requests for comment.

Four anonymous former officials fear professional reprisals for discussing their government experience. They claim enforcement officers found suspicious activity at Southeast Asian sites where Nvidia chips were delivered. An OpenAI researcher found evidence that banned Nvidia chips trained top Chinese AI models. Epoch estimated between 290,000 and 1.6 million chips were smuggled into China in 2024 and 2025. These chips provided a quarter of China's acquired computing power.

The Biden administration first issued AI chip export controls in 2022 and 2023. In February 2025, Lutnick started running the department and let go of veteran officials. These included Matthew Borman and Eileen Albanese, who were highly respected experts. An exodus of up to 50 skilled staff members followed over 18 months. This resulted in a loss of institutional memory regarding AI and diversion.

Key roles in the Bureau of Industry and Security currently remain vacant. These include the chief of staff and the principal deputy assistant secretary roles. The department claims the new licensing rule was directed by Treasury and the National Security Council. Reports suggest $7.5 billion in Nvidia chips reached China via Alice Huang. The articles leave open whether the White House will address these failures.

stories.Headline: Judge denies SpaceXAI request to split from AI antitrust class action
stories.Summary:
A California federal judge denied SpaceXAI's request to separate itself from a proposed class action on November 16, 2026, according to a Law360 report by Aneeta Mathur-Ashton. The suit was brought by artificial intelligence users who accuse the leading AI platforms of violating antitrust law through their collaboration. The order keeps SpaceXAI, which the report identifies as Space Exploration Technologies Corp., inside the case rather than letting it proceed on its own. The judge issued the ruling in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, where the case is pending.

The articles give no further numbers, dates or names beyond the November 16, 2026 ruling date and the court. The case information section lists the parties as Anthropic PBC, Google LLC, OpenAI OpCo LLC and Space Exploration Technologies Corp., with the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California named as the court. The law firms listed in the case information are Dechert LLP, Freshfields, Keker Van Nest & Peters and Willenken LLP. The articles do not state the size of the proposed class or any damages figure.

The judge is responsible for the ruling, and the articles do not name the judge or give any statement from the court. The articles also carry no comment from SpaceXAI, from the other companies named or from the plaintiffs' lawyers. The only description of the dispute is that AI users accuse the leading platforms of violating antitrust law through their collaboration. The articles do not say what the plaintiffs want the court to order or how the companies responded to the claims.

The context is a proposed class action in California federal court against several major AI platforms, and the ruling means SpaceXAI stays a party as the case moves forward. The articles do not say what happens next, such as any scheduling order, motion or trial date. The case information lists the law firms and companies involved but gives no further detail on the proceedings. The articles do not say whether SpaceXAI or the other parties plan to appeal or seek any other relief.

stories.Headline: US SAT sites ban AI glasses in 2026 to prevent illegal filming and privacy violations
stories.Summary:
Various institutions across the United States, Australia, and Europe have banned AI glasses starting in 2026 to prevent illegal filming and privacy violations. The U.S. has prohibited these devices at SAT test sites, while the U.S. Marine Corps is banning them at bases like Camp Lejeune. In Australia, Western Australia banned smartglasses in public schools on October 12, 2026, and the City of Canterbury-Bankstown restricted them at swimming pools and leisure centres. Additionally, the Paris prosecutor's office in France opened an investigation in September 2026 after reports that women were filmed without consent.

These restrictions require users to leave devices with security officers or face severe penalties, such as the cancellation of SAT test scores. New York State banned glasses with computers, microphones, or cameras from 1,240 state and local courts starting July 20, 2026, including prescription Ray-Ban Meta models. In October 2026, Pakistan's Punjab province banned the sale and use of camera-equipped glasses and hidden recording devices for 30 days. Victoria plans to implement school restrictions on January 27, 2027, and courts in England and Wales now ban Meta glasses.

Authorities and officials implemented these rules after receiving complaints about harassment, threats, and illegal surveillance. Judge Carolyn Kuhl warned security personnel during Mark Zuckerberg's February 2026 testimony that any person recording with glasses must remove them. Meta claims a white indicator light signals when the device records, and the camera disables if that light is damaged. However, product guides suggest some AI functions operate while the light is off, which continues to fuel privacy concerns.

The broader context involves a growing conflict between device functionality and the right to privacy in public and private spaces. British cinemas are blocking camera glasses to stop film piracy, and Royal Caribbean bans them in youth areas, medical facilities, and casinos. The Norwegian government is currently considering temporary restrictions in gyms, shopping centres, beaches, and parks. While some devices like Even Realities' G2 lack cameras, the trend toward stricter regulation of photo-capable glasses remains steady.

stories.Headline: FPT Software chair Chu Thi Thanh Ha says AI shifts firm from hourly billing to outcomes
stories.Summary:
FPT Software, which serves as the IT services arm for a major Vietnamese technology firm, is changing its business strategy. The company is moving away from a traditional offshore outsourcing model that focused on providing engineering manpower to international clients. This shift is happening because artificial intelligence is altering how the industry operates and how services are delivered. The announcement was made public on November 17, 2026, following discussions about the evolving global tech landscape.

The transition requires the company to stop relying on a billing model based on the number of engineering hours worked. Instead, the firm must now focus on delivering specific outcomes to satisfy the changing demands of its American customers. This change marks a significant departure from the previous approach of simply offshoring labor to reduce costs for clients. The company is transforming its entire operational framework to remain competitive in an era dominated by automated intelligence.

Chairperson Chu Thi Thanh Ha explained these changes during an interview with Nikkei Asia on November 10 in Tokyo. She spoke while attending the Nikkei Forum Global Management Dialogue 2026 to describe why the company had to transform. According to the chairperson, the shift is necessary because U.S. customers no longer want to pay for hours of labor. She emphasized that the business must move beyond being an offshoring provider to survive the current technological shift.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: Pierre school officials draft AI classroom procedures after survey
stories.Summary:
The Pierre School District has spent the past several months working to address the growing use of artificial intelligence in classrooms, with district officials meeting alongside a staff committee to develop procedures for AI use after a community survey was conducted earlier this year. Superintendent Donavan DeBoer said he entered the role knowing that discussions about AI would be necessary as the technology becomes increasingly common, not just in schools, and he noted that AI has been a frequent topic at education conferences and professional retreats because of how quickly the technology evolves. Drawing a comparison to the introduction of cellphones in schools, DeBoer said educators learned that simply allowing students unrestricted access often created challenges that continue today, and he said the district needs to put guardrails on AI sooner rather than later because having some sort of plan is better than having no plan at all. District conversations began earlier this year with an AI-focused survey sent to staff, students and parents, and about 1,655 responses gave the district a starting point for committee discussions as members work toward establishing AI procedures for the 2027-28 school year. Eighty percent of students surveyed said they had used AI before, and nearly half of those students said they use it monthly or more often, while of the 832 student respondents, 309 said they use AI for homework help and 412 said they use it for research, with others reporting use for writing assistance and studying.

Of the 209 staff members who responded, about half said they had used AI for tasks including lesson planning, and most respondents agreed AI can help teachers save time, though many also expressed interest in additional training, recommended tools and established expectations for student use. Across all respondent groups, students, staff and parents expressed awareness that AI tools can sometimes produce inaccurate information, and DeBoer said many students also voiced concerns about academic integrity similar to those expressed by adults in the community. The district has since formed an AI committee that has met twice, and the group includes principals representing the elementary, middle and high school levels as well as Technology Director Bryan Linn, with DeBoer saying he and Linn are currently working to draft procedures and protocols for AI use. The committee plans to meet again in January to further develop those ideas before sharing them with building leadership teams for additional feedback, and DeBoer said he hopes to bring a proposal to the school board this spring and receive approval before the next school year. Currently, websites such as ChatGPT and Gemini are blocked on student devices because of privacy concerns, though DeBoer said the district may have opportunities to incorporate more secure AI tools into classrooms for activities such as project brainstorming or creating renderings in technical education courses.

DeBoer said he does not intend this to be a hard and fast policy because the world is moving at warp speed and the district's AI expectations and protocols will change as things change, and he said the district is looking at a set of processes and procedures to guide staff on consistent expectations for students rather than a policy that would constantly need revision. DeBoer said he expects AI use to be more common at the high school level than in elementary or middle school classrooms, particularly as students prepare for college, technical school and future careers where the technology is becoming increasingly prevalent, and he noted that AI-detection tools used during grading are not always accurate, prompting some teachers to return to pen-and-paper assignments to avoid concerns about misuse. While the district continues to develop expectations for classroom use, officials also hope to help teachers identify effective AI tools, provide additional training and continue evaluating the technology as it evolves, and results of the district's AI survey are available on the district website. AI policy is expected to remain a topic of discussion at Pierre School Board meetings, and the board meets at 5:30 p.m. on the second Monday of each month at the district administration building, with meetings open to the public.

stories.Headline: Germany's draft asylum AI law relies on staff training that a review finds cannot stop automation bias
stories.Summary:
Germany's draft AI migration-administration law, the KIMVG, relies on manual review of results and special training for staff as its two safeguards against over-trust in machine output. The bill text never uses the term automation bias, and a 2010 Human Factors review found the effect occurs in novices and experts alike and cannot be prevented by training or instructions. On Monday, 37 civil society organizations including AlgorithmWatch published an appeal asking the Bundestag to rework the bill before a public hearing in its Interior Committee. The hearing is scheduled for Nov. 23 at 8 a.m. ET, 2 p.m.

in Berlin, according to netzpolitik. Anyone with an asylum or residence file at the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF) or a local foreigners authority could be affected. The government bill, Bundestag printed paper 21/8275, amends the Asylum Act and the Residence Act. One provision allows case data to be used to train, validate and test AI systems, a second allows procedure monitoring of how cases move through the authorities, and a third allows an internet comparison against open-source information about applicants. The cabinet took note of the underlying key-points paper on Nov. 5, 2025, and approved the bill on July 29, 2026.

The interior ministry counted 113,236 first-time asylum applications in Germany in 2025. The bill requires staff to assess the results of an internet comparison manually, and its explanatory memorandum says the automated comparison confers no decision authority. The bill also requires that employees who run procedure monitoring and internet matching be specially trained. In an answer to the Bundesrat, the federal government said individual examination and decision remain with the responsible staff and that automated procedures neither replace the legal assessment nor shape decisions bindingly. In a Verfassungsblog essay, constitutional-law author Arian Henning describes the human reviewer in such systems as a fig leaf for the machine.

Authors Anna-Lena Priebe and Lise Känner argue on the same site that a human final decision plus training duties are not enough because of automation bias. Priebe and Känner also say procedure monitoring and internet matching are likely high-risk under the EU AI Act. According to netzpolitik, federal anti-discrimination commissioner Ferda Ataman raised serious concerns during government deliberations, and the rights group Pro Asyl calls the bill's safeguards insufficient. Federal Integration Commissioner Natalie Pawlik views the plan positively, saying AI could shorten waiting times. The AlgorithmWatch appeal asks for anonymization as the general rule, limits on use of whole asylum files and central register data, stricter conditions on internet matching, a fundamental rights impact assessment involving civil society, and transparency, redress and registration of the systems.

The bill contains no general duty to anonymize, and according to the explanatory memorandum, anonymization or pseudonymization is unnecessary where it is technically impossible, disproportionate, or would substantially impair result quality. The memorandum also treats names and birth dates as data that carry context useful for plausibility checks and mentions a possible obligation to use real data. The internet comparison the bill allows searches open sources for information about applicants, so people who share an applicant's name or appear alongside them in public material could also surface in results. Asylum files can contain information on ethnic origin, religion and health, which GDPR Article 9 treats as special categories of personal data.

According to netzpolitik's August reporting, the data protection commissioner's office, then led by Louisa Specht-Riemenschneider, wanted anonymized data used first, then pseudonymized data, and personal data only where necessary, and Moritz Hennemann has led the office since Oct. 1. BAMF already uses dialect-identification software known as DIAS, which AlgorithmWatch calls controversial, and the bill's explanatory memorandum gives a spoken language or dialect that does not match a claimed region of origin as an example of justified doubt. The AI Act lists AI used to assist the assessment of asylum, visa and residence applications as high risk under Annex III, and under Article 6(3) and 6(4) a provider can claim an Annex III system is not high risk if it only detects decision patterns without replacing or influencing a prior human assessment absent proper human review, but the exemption never applies to profiling. The Digital Omnibus, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, entered into force July 27, 2026, and pushed Annex III obligations to Dec. 2, 2027, so the high-risk rules would not yet bind a system deployed earlier.

The Bundestag held a 20-minute first reading on Oct. 8 and referred the bill to the Interior Committee. The Bundesrat asked that internet matching also cover establishing identity and nationality and determining return options, and the federal government said it would examine that request. Karlsruhe's 2023 ruling on automated data analysis required sufficient legal thresholds for such tools, though it concerned police laws in Hesse and Hamburg, not migration administration. According to netzpolitik, the invited experts include Alexander Steen of the German Informatics Society, Franziska Görlitz of the Society for Civil Rights and Eric Töpfer of the German Institute for Human Rights.

stories.Headline: Marc Andreessen predicts AI job losses will be limited in regulated sectors but growth will suffer
stories.Summary:
Venture capitalist Marc Andreessen, who co-heads Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's task force on jobs and productivity, said on Monday, November 16, 2026, that artificial intelligence will have a dual effect on the job market. He predicted that job losses in sectors covered by government regulation will be largely insulated from major losses, but that those same regulations will limit economic and productivity growth. You might read that as good news, he said, because a revolution will not destroy all the jobs or kill everybody. You could also view it as very negative, he added, because productivity growth and economic growth simply may not grow very much.

Andreessen divides the economy into two categories of sectors, the first being fast-moving ones that see rapid technological and economic change along with rapid job turnover, such as consumer electronics and media entertainment. The second category is a combination of law and government, which is not structured to change rapidly and is typically characterized by extensive subsidization. He said the fastest-growing sectors will see their prices go down, while the slower-growing regulated or government-subsidized sectors will see their prices go up. Your iPhone is getting cheaper and the flat-screen TV on your wall is getting cheaper, he said, but college education is going to cost a million bucks, healthcare is becoming unaffordable, and good luck buying a house.

Andreessen is responsible for the prediction as co-head of the task force on jobs and productivity under Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh, and he set out the two-sector view himself in the remarks reported by Jennifer Schonberger of Yahoo Finance. The article gives no further comment from Warsh or from other members of the task force on the prediction. The report places the remarks against a backdrop of other warnings about AI and work, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's warning of 5% to 10% GDP growth with 10% joblessness, a combination he said is not one we have almost ever seen before. The article does not say what the task force will do next or when it will report.

stories.Headline: JPMorgan is working on AI agent transactions that don’t involve humans
stories.Summary:
JPMorgan Chase and South Korea's Hyundai Card completed a proof-of-concept in which AI agents carried out simulated foreign exchange transactions without direct human intervention, the companies said. In the initial trial, a Hyundai Card AI agent requested a foreign exchange transaction to maintain euro liquidity in its Kinexys blockchain deposit account. JPMorgan said it was the first private blockchain-based autonomous bank-agent-to-client-agent test for corporate treasury management. The companies aim to expand testing in the first half of 2027 to more complex transactions involving multiple AI agents, according to Wee Kee Toh, global head of Kinexys Insights at Kinexys by JP Morgan.

JPMorgan has yet to set a timeline for commercializing the technology. Toh said building the technology itself was relatively straightforward, but establishing appropriate governance and internal controls proved more difficult, and he pointed to questions around accountability and the risks of allowing AI agents to execute financial transactions without direct human oversight. To address those concerns, Kinexys developed a framework that restricts AI agents to predefined transaction parameters and automatically rejects requests that fall outside authorized limits. Toh said an AI agent authorized to transact up to $5 million would be blocked from executing transactions above that threshold, and he described drawing a box around the agent that it can never act outside of.

The companies are also exploring whether to extend their collaboration to other businesses within Hyundai Motor Group, whose broader operations were one reason JPMorgan selected Hyundai Card as a partner, Toh said, and no specific projects have been announced. Hyundai Motor Group holds a combined 78.04% stake in Hyundai Card through Hyundai Motor, Kia and Hyundai Commercial, according to the card issuer's website. Hyundai Card said in July that it completed a proof-of-concept involving a $20,000 transfer using the USDT stablecoin between Hyundai Motor's U.S. and Mexican subsidiaries, with the transfer and verification process taking an average of seven minutes. Kinexys said in August that it had processed more than $4 trillion in transactions since inception, averaging about $7 billion a day, and JPMorgan launched a proof-of-concept for its dollar-denominated deposit token, JPMD, in June 2025, before making it available to institutional clients that November.

stories.Headline: Genpact launches Onyx platform for building and governing enterprise AI agents
stories.Summary:
Genpact announced on November 16, 2026 the availability of Genpact Onyx, an Agentic Operations platform for building, running, and governing AI agents in enterprise operations, and the company had unveiled the platform at its Agentic Operations Day in New York on November 12. The platform is powered by Genpact's Process Intelligence Core, which the company describes as operating knowledge codified from decades of running mission-critical work for global enterprises, so that agents start with context on how the work gets done rather than learning it from scratch. Genpact Onyx is the foundation for Genpact's proprietary agentic solutions, starting with the Genpact Accounts Payable Suite, and for custom solutions Genpact builds for clients. The platform embeds into a client's existing technology stack, connects to the client's data and AI foundations, and supports a choice of leading AI models across Genpact's partner ecosystem.

The platform's capabilities include a Process Intelligence Core codified across finance, risk, supply chain, banking, insurance, and procurement, with prebuilt workflows and agents so clients are ready on day one, drawn from doing the actual work and capturing edge cases, exceptions, and human decisions. A learning loop feeds reviewed exceptions and expert decisions back into the core so intelligence compounds over time, and earned autonomy lets agents start by proposing actions for a human expert to approve and take on more of the decision as they prove themselves. Built-in governance makes every agent action controlled, auditable, and traceable to the reason behind the decision, with guardrails and a responsible AI framework built into the platform, along with security and data isolation that meet enterprise standards. Genpact said the platform was launched at its third annual flagship event, held at Spring Studios in New York, where hundreds of clients, partners, and industry analysts attended a program of announcements, product demonstrations, and client presentations, and leaders from Advantage Solutions, Wesco, USA Today, and Ryan Specialty shared how they are putting Genpact's agentic solutions to work.

Balkrishan "BK" Kalra, President and Chief Executive Officer of Genpact, said the company runs mission-critical operations for many of the world's largest enterprises and that is where the return on AI is decided, adding that Genpact Onyx codifies three decades of process intelligence and makes it the foundation for Agentic Operations, with agents running the work and Genpact's experts owning the outcome. Priya Vijayarajendran, Chief Product and Platform Officer, said enterprises get value from AI when they turn operating knowledge into trusted execution rather than simply by adding more agents, and that Genpact Onyx grounds agents in how the work actually gets done, builds governance into every step, orchestrates across agents and human expertise, and lets autonomy be earned one decision at a time. Genpact describes Agentic Operations as a new operating model in which AI agents handle the volume of execution and its domain experts bring judgment and accountability, combining process intelligence, data and AI, a combined human and agent workforce, a partner ecosystem, and governance and security. Genpact said it uses the platform for its own agentic solutions, for custom client solutions in areas where it does not yet have an agentic solution, and for solutions delivered with technology partners.

stories.Headline: NTT Data launches generative AI service to rebuild COBOL systems in Java and targets ¥50 billion in revenue
stories.Summary:
NTT Data said on November 17 that it has begun offering a service called Clean Modernization, which uses generative AI to analyze core systems built in COBOL and other legacy languages and redesign them into highly maintainable Java systems. The company applies generative AI across processes that run from recovering business specifications to testing, and it expects to cut project timelines by about 40% compared with manual work. It will target financial institutions and government agencies, aiming for cumulative revenue of ¥50 billion, or approximately $313.9 million, over the three years starting in fiscal 2027. The service migrates existing core systems in stages to a state that is easier to maintain and modify over the long term.

The service covers four domains, which are applications, infrastructure, operations and organization, and it reviews existing systems from two angles. The first is visualization, which documents the current state to make it easier to understand, and the second is change enablement, which restructures systems to make it easier to limit the scope of change impacts. In the core application overhaul, generative AI recovers business specifications from COBOL and other programs and design documents, organizes intricately intertwined processing into functional units, and then redesigns the system into highly maintainable Java. The AI models used can be selected from multiple frontier AI options depending on the customer's environment and policies.

At companies and local governments across Japan, core systems written in COBOL remain in operation, and the aging and retirement of engineers who understand the specifications has become a serious problem. Against this obsolescence risk, known as the 2025 cliff, the approach of recovering specifications with generative AI could help compress modernization costs and timelines. At the same time, how to verify the accuracy of specifications recovered by generative AI is an important consideration for adopting companies. NTT Data has indicated a policy of advancing visualization and change enablement in stages, aiming to reduce migration risk by avoiding wholesale replacement.

Demand for core system modernization is expected to remain at a high level, and the company's order trends are likely to affect the competitive environment in Japan's IT services market.
