stories.Headline: China integrates artificial intelligence into national education to create an AI-native generation
stories.Summary:
Beijing is currently pushing to integrate artificial intelligence into its national education system to create an AI-native generation of students. This state-led effort involves nearly 200 million primary and secondary students across the country in a massive learning experiment. The government wants universal AI literacy for all school children by the year 2030 to ensure economic success. This initiative aims to nurture homegrown innovation to help China win its technological rivalry against the United States. President Xi Jinping has declared that AI education is fundamental to the reform of the national schooling system.

The Beijing New Talent Academy costs 39,000 dollars annually and serves over 2,000 students on a 12 hectare boarding campus. Shanghai mandates 30 hours of annual AI teaching per grade, while Beijing plans 100 AI pilot demonstration schools. Ningxia and Gansu plan to include AI literacy in high-stakes entrance exams by 2027, and Yunnan will record 14,000 classrooms. Guizhou uses AI facial recognition and behavioural analysis, while Shanghai deploys systems for monitoring the mental and physical health of students. The education ministry has encouraged AI courses, teacher training, and pilot programmes since the start of 2024.

President Xi Jinping vowed to make AI for all during his debut at the top tech summit in China. Headmaster Liu Wei stated that AI should be an everyday tool for most students rather than just for future scientists. Headmaster Yang Tianliang said AI agents do not suffer from fatigue and never make students feel stupid for asking questions. An Alibaba spokesperson noted that the Cloud for Youth Programme gives students direct access to AI tools and education. Ted Mo Chen of ClassIn said implementation is all over the place and few schools integrate AI effectively.

Parents like Rita Luan worry that AI might shortcut learning and require close supervision to ensure children digest the solutions. Students using AI three times weekly showed lower memory, comprehension, analytical, and creative skills than those who used it less. A study of 27,000 teenagers found an 18 per cent homework score increase but a 20 per cent exam score decline. Rural students may be more vulnerable to device addiction and cognitive outsourcing, where they delegate mental tasks to the technology. Many educators are grappling with how to deploy AI without reinforcing the rote-learning habits that policymakers want to move beyond.

The US relies on non-binding guidance and lacks dedicated funding or state-level teacher standards, according to the 2026 Stanford AI Index. Government procurement records show at least 31 million dollars spent last year on AI classroom equipment, training, and teaching platforms. iResearch estimates 2025 spending on education digitalisation at just under 83 billion dollars, with generative AI taking 46 per cent. Funan County Qinqing High School in Anhui uses AI to solve teacher shortages for 4,000 pupils who are migrant children. This school uses AI models from Z.AI, ByteDance, and Alibaba's Qwen to generate interactive lessons, text, images, and videos.

China has not yet established a standard framework for measuring AI literacy, leaving schools to experiment without a clear scorecard. Selena Guo of China Policy noted that mature assessment rubrics for compulsory school-level AI competency are still being built now. The education ministry did not respond to requests for comment, and ByteDance and Z.AI also did not respond to inquiries. It remains unclear if the short-term gains in homework scores will lead to long-term intellectual development or cognitive decline. The articles leave open whether the government can successfully balance AI efficiency with the need for independent and critical thinking.

stories.Headline: US stocks drop as investors sell AI shares before Nvidia earnings report
stories.Summary:
U.S. stock markets experienced a sharp decline on Monday, November 16, 2026, as investors sold off artificial intelligence shares. This downturn occurred just before Nvidia was scheduled to release its quarterly financial results. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 739.38 points, which is 1.41 percent, while the S&P 500 dropped 145.08 points, or 1.92 percent. Additionally, the Nasdaq Composite Index fell by 626.52 points, representing a 2.5 percent decrease.

The market shift saw nine of the eleven S&P 500 sectors end in the red, with technology falling 2.98 percent and communication services dropping 2.82 percent. Nvidia shares fell 4.12 percent following the recent resignation of chief executive officer Jensen Huang, whom the board is not considering rehiring. Other chipmakers suffered heavily, as Intel, Micron, Marvell, and Arm each dropped over 6 percent, while Advanced Micro Devices fell 5.58 percent and Broadcom fell 3.92 percent. Dell Technologies and Oracle declined nearly 7 percent and 5 percent, respectively, while the VIX volatility index hit a high of 24.52.

David Kelly, the chief global strategist at J.P. Morgan Asset Management, stated that there are many doubts regarding technology currently. He advised investors to diversify their holdings in artificial intelligence because the trade is entering a more volatile period. Meanwhile, Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh spoke in San Francisco about three different economic scenarios regarding artificial intelligence. These models range from a productivity boom to increased unemployment or a disappointing payoff that could lower share prices.

Other economic indicators showed the Empire State manufacturing index fell to 7.8 in November from 25.5 in October. West Texas Intermediate crude oil dropped 3.21 percent to 85.72 U.S. dollars a barrel due to recovering shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. In contrast, Tyson Foods rose 8.72 percent after reporting fiscal fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of 61 cents per share. Looking ahead, Anthropic plans to price its initial public offering on Wednesday and begin trading on the Nasdaq this Thursday.

stories.Headline: NTT Data's supply chain head urges firms to connect isolated AI uses through multiagent systems
stories.Summary:
Pedro Béjar Castán published an article on 13 November 2026 on nttdata.com urging organizations to stop doing isolated AI and to implement multiagent systems. He wrote that the CEO talks about AI in broad terms while the innovation team runs proofs of concept and some business functions have started pilots. He said demonstrations, vendor conversations and internal experiments are all happening at the same time. He wrote that proof is emerging that AI adds value, yet he keeps hearing the same thing: "We don't know what to do next." His answer is that organizations probably don't need another use case and need to connect the ones they already have.

He described multiagent systems, where multiple AI agents work together across a business process to interpret what is happening, coordinate the response and take action. For a manufacturer that wanted to define and implement agentic intelligence throughout its value chain, NTT DATA ran 14 workshops for customer service, production, logistics and warehousing departments. The team spoke with more than 60 people and cataloged 129 improvement opportunities by the end of the process. Following a multiagent approach let NTT DATA group the 129 individual improvement opportunities into just 36 prioritized AI use cases. In one project, some shifts needed 10 frontline operators and others 4, and truck arrival patterns drove much of the staffing volatility.

Béjar Castán, managing director and global head of supply chain at NTT DATA, said he is responsible for leading NTT DATA's work with the World Economic Forum's Advanced Manufacturing and Supply Chain initiative. He wrote that NTT DATA combines deep industry and process knowledge with AI strategy, consulting, engineering and implementation expertise. He said NTT DATA can look across a value chain to identify where AI can make the biggest difference, connect opportunities that might otherwise be treated in isolation and then design, build and integrate the multiagent systems. He said plenty of firms will help you think, some partners specialize in strategy and others are strongest at implementation. He said what is harder to find is a partner that can do both.

He wrote that in supply chain management AI is already improving forecast accuracy, flagging changes in demand patterns, surfacing supplier risk earlier and optimizing transportation routes. He said each use case enhances only a single activity and a human is still required to pass the separate pieces of intelligence on. He described a multiagent environment where the system reads an order, checks the quantity against expected demand, identifies anomalies, evaluates stock-out risk over a two-week horizon, recommends a revised quantity, updates the planning system and notifies the people who need to know. He said multiagent systems are mostly used in software at the moment but will increasingly extend into the physical world through autonomous handling equipment, vision systems and connected assets on plant floors. He said a logistics specialist thinks about transportation and a warehouse manager thinks about staffing, and AI creates more value when you look at the process connecting the two.

He wrote that organizations have introduced AI capabilities function by function, launched pilot programs and encouraged employees to experiment with AI tools. He said this has led to many small use cases that save individual teams time and effort, but those use cases must be organized and connected for the organization as a whole to benefit. In one project, warehouse managers worried about staffing while the logistics team reported that trucks turned up early, late or in clusters at the docks. He said the two problems were in reality one use case, and looking at them together has allowed NTT DATA to synchronize operator availability with inbound and outbound truck movements. He said that if you can predict an important truck will be two hours late, you can place fewer employees in loading and more in preparing customer orders before the gap opens up.

He listed six steps: set the ambition, identify improvement opportunities, define the use cases, prioritize the use cases, choose your technical architecture and build a roadmap. He said most discussions and arguments are about prioritizing use cases, weighing the value each could create and whether the organization is ready to deliver it. He asked whether an organization has the data availability, process maturity and systems integration to make an effective AI use case. He wrote that the processes connected today could eventually be executed by physical AI, so it makes sense to prepare for that transition. He invited readers to request a half-day workshop to identify where AI will create value and turn a long list of possibilities into a practical plan.

stories.Headline: Apple asks developers to build Siri integrations for its 2027 smart glasses
stories.Summary:
Apple plans to lean heavily on Siri AI for its smart glasses, according to a Bloomberg report by Mark Gurman, published in Sunday's "Power On" newsletter and covered by Gizmodo on November 16, 2026, and AppleInsider on November 15, 2026. Apple wants to challenge Meta's Muse AI by giving its smart glasses smoother agentic capabilities, specifically tighter integrations with third-party apps that Siri can control. Gurman reported that Apple expects app developers to prepare for the eventual introduction of its smart glasses in 2027. Apple's long-rumored smart glasses are expected to lean on AI processing for its first release. The way the glasses function with AI will be key to their success, according to AppleInsider.

Apple wants developers to focus on Siri integrations rather than having apps running fully on the glasses, so specific functions within apps are accessible to Siri and can be called upon by users wearing the glasses. Because the Siri integrations are being developed for the iPhone first, software makers won't need to build separate applications for the glasses. Developers will be able to make specific functions within their existing apps accessible to Siri, allowing users to complete tasks through voice commands without opening or navigating the apps themselves. Apple's approach is similar to the rollout of HomeView, a device that does not allow third-party apps to run directly but lets apps with existing CarPlay support play audio and video. Apple is also looking into integrations with Starbucks that could let you order a drink with the Siri AI voice assistant on its smart glasses, shop through Amazon, and book movie tickets through Fandango.

The thinking inside Apple is that while Meta has the increasingly popular Muse agent, Apple has the App Store, according to Gurman. Apple believes it has the upper hand on current market dominator Meta, with its advantage coming from its pool of developers. Apple has a much larger pool of developers at its disposal in the App Store and worked on Siri integrations for the iPhone long beforehand, so there should be little effort needed to make those Siri integrations work with the smart glasses. Apple is making a similar plea to developers to work on those elements before the launch of the Apple Vision Pro. With any luck, it should launch with a robust and vast number of things you can call upon Siri to do, without waiting for developers to catch up.

Among the rumored agentic capabilities are using your voice to have Siri AI order you a car through Uber or book you a reservation at a restaurant through OpenTable. Meta has the same vision for Muse, which already lives on its smart glasses, but Apple hopes its more tight-knit relationship with developers will make app integrations easier. Bloomberg notes that Apple's advantage isn't unique, because Samsung's and Google's relationships with developers through Google's Android XR platform are equally as established and could offer the same opportunities. Meta's Muse has found ways to offer agentic capabilities through web browsers as opposed to specific apps.

Whether Apple has bright ideas on solving increasing privacy concerns or convincing people that smart glasses aren't a bad idea in general remains to be seen. Meta popularized the modern-day template for what smart glasses are, and Samsung and Google now have their own equivalent in a recently launched lineup of "intelligent eyewear." For a device like smart glasses, leaning on Siri integrations makes sense, especially if Apple keeps to its plan of making thin and light smart spectacles, because it won't have enough onboard processing available to handle much in the way of apps. CarPlay and Siri AI solve that by pushing the hard work to a nearby iPhone.

Apple's smart glasses will work with apps, but probably through Siri AI, in a similar way to the CarPlay-like HomeView. Apple's plan for its AI-equipped smart glasses is to lean on integrations with a user's existing iPhone apps. Apple is expecting app developers to prepare for the eventual introduction of its smart glasses in 2027, and the Siri integrations are being developed for the iPhone first. Whether Apple has any bright ideas on solving increasing privacy concerns or convincing people that smart glasses aren't a bad idea in general remains to be seen.

stories.Headline: TCS study finds AI productivity gains outpace trust
stories.Summary:
Tata Consultancy Services published a global study on enterprise artificial intelligence adoption, IT Brief Australia reported on 18 November 2026. The study found that 84% of executives cite productivity as AI's top benefit. The research was based on responses from 1,333 senior business and technology leaders across 25 countries. These included 44 respondents in Ireland from 11 industries. The findings point to a gap between the value companies say they get from AI tools and their willingness to let AI systems act independently.

Only 10% of global enterprises said they allow AI agents to execute decisions without human approval across multiple functions or business areas. Nine per cent said they have AI agents that can securely orchestrate workflows across enterprise applications. Security, risk and governance emerged as the main factor shaping deployment decisions worldwide, ahead of cost, speed and ease of deployment. In Ireland, leaders identified cost, speed and ease of deployment as the main driver of AI deployment. Seven per cent of Irish enterprises said they allow AI agents to execute decisions without human approval across multiple functions or business areas, compared with 10% globally.

Amit Kapur, Chief AI and Services Transformation Officer at TCS, said the shift is clearly in AI moving from assisting people to taking more autonomous action with deep access into an enterprise. He said productivity is clearly where enterprises are seeing the greatest value from AI today, with 84% of executives ranking it as the leading source of value from their AI investments. He said 10% have also indicated that they have seen an uplift in revenue. He said concerns around security, governance and resilience seem to be holding organisations back, and rightly so. He said deploying AI responsibly, with the right guardrails and enterprise controls, will be the big focus in the next stage of this journey.

On model independence, 86% of Irish respondents said it was an important factor in AI investment decisions, versus 90% worldwide. Thirty-nine per cent of Irish respondents identified AI sovereignty-related requirements as a high or very high organisational risk, above the global figure of 34%. Across Europe, 43% of respondents described sovereignty-related requirements as a high or very high organisational risk. Although 90% of respondents said model independence matters in investment decisions, only 7% reported having organisation-wide provider-switching continuity plans. Thirty-nine per cent of enterprises said they are still assessing whether AI initiatives generate enough value relative to token and compute costs.

Forty-four per cent of respondents said important business knowledge remains embedded within employees or scattered across fragmented documentation. Globally, 46% of respondents said they had targeted deployment of open-source AI for selected use cases, while in Ireland the figure was lower at 32%. The proportion of leaders who said it is still too early to determine AI's impact on the workforce rose from 4% in 2024 to 19% in 2026. North America showed stronger scores on some enterprise AI foundations, while Europe recorded greater concern about sovereignty. The UK and Ireland stood out on operational resilience, with comparatively stronger levels of AI continuity planning and governance integration.

The survey covered senior leaders from organisations with annual revenues ranging from USD $500 million to more than USD $20 billion, spanning 12 industries. Respondents included C-suite executives, divisional leaders, Senior Vice Presidents and Vice Presidents. On 12 November 2026, the Federal Reserve Board published working paper FEDS 2026-074, titled Artificial Intelligence and the U.S. Economy: Current Evidence. It was authored by Federal Reserve Board economists Nick Carollo, Leland D. Crane, Daniel Garcia Molina and Joseph Nichols. The paper documents that U.S. capital commitments for AI data centers have surged past $1 trillion while aggregate macroeconomic productivity gains and labor market disruptions remain muted.

stories.Headline: BlackLine unveils agentic finance platform with governance console and Databricks connectivity
stories.Summary:
BlackLine, Inc. (Nasdaq: BL) unveiled a series of platform innovations at BeyondTheBlack 2026 in Orlando, Florida, on Nov. 17, 2026, according to a GlobeNewswire release dated the same day. The release said the innovations span next-generation platform architecture, Record-to-Report, and Invoice-to-Cash. BlackLine described the advancements as a shift for the Office of the CFO away from fragmented, task-level automation toward full-scale, governed financial orchestration. The release said enterprises accelerating AI adoption face the challenge of scaling agentic execution across complex financial workflows without compromising deterministic accuracy, auditability, or governance. BlackLine said it built the platform on more than 25 years of financial process expertise.

The release said the platform unifies financial data, core applications, and specialized AI agents into an orchestrated digital workforce. It introduced a Finance Control Console, described as a centralized governance, policy-enforcement, and observability command center giving real-time visibility into agent actions, enforcing deterministic guardrails, enabling human-in-the-loop approvals, and guaranteeing auditability. It introduced Agentic Orchestration, a coordination engine connecting AI agents and financial processes into multi-step workflows that merge autonomous execution with enterprise financial logic and compliance policies. It introduced a Unified Data Foundation and Verity Integrate, an enterprise data architecture connecting financial data, ERPs, and applications, plus Agent-Ready Connectivity via open standards including the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The release said BlackLine introduced native connectivity with Databricks, with Databricks OpenSharing letting customers share governed data without duplicating data or building complex pipelines, and said Verity Accruals is built on Databricks using the Databricks Partner Well-Architected Framework.

Jeremy Ung, Chief Technology Officer at BlackLine, said the true measure of AI in finance is not simply what it can calculate but what an enterprise can trust it to execute autonomously. Ung said BlackLine is delivering a trusted digital workforce for the Office of the CFO. He said combining intelligent agents with deep financial expertise and deterministic controls is transforming how financial work gets done. He said this frees finance leaders from manual process management to steer strategic business outcomes. Sarah Branfman, Global Vice President, ISV at Databricks, said customers shouldn't have to choose between control over their data and speed to value.

Branfman said that with BlackLine they don't have to, and that through OpenSharing customers share governed data between BlackLine and their lakehouse without copying it or building pipelines. She said Verity Accruals built on Databricks delivers AI-native finance automation on the platform enterprises already trust with their data. Christopher Giambra, Senior Manager of Corporate Accounting at Delaware North, said his company trusts BlackLine more than anybody else in the business and that trust is paramount when it comes to AI. Giambra said deploying Verity Prepare has fundamentally elevated reconciliation workflows and that expanding into Verity Match across high-volume treasury and credit card operations will be transformative. The release said Delaware North, a global hospitality and entertainment leader, is already putting the agentic innovations to work.

The release said BlackLine brought consolidation and financial close together into an integrated, high-velocity Record-to-Report engine, with Financial Consolidation taking an AI-native approach that unifies enterprise financial close and consolidation in a single connected workflow. It said Autonomous Close advances toward a touchless close through Agentic Reconciliations, Verity Score, and Verity Retrieve, automating reconciliation cycles, benchmarking reconciliation quality and audit readiness, and retrieving supporting documentation while preserving human oversight. It said Verity Match applies machine intelligence to high-volume transaction matching, isolating true exceptions so accounting teams focus on items requiring complex analytical judgment. The release said BlackLine expanded agentic capabilities across the receivables lifecycle, building on the commercial momentum and general availability of Verity Collect and Verity Remit. The release said approximately 4,300 customers across multiple industries partner with BlackLine.

The release said the innovations address a time when trust is on the line, combining agentic execution with the accuracy, control, and oversight finance demands. It said BlackLine is turning trust into a catalyst for transformation, empowering finance teams to confidently scale AI and drive better business outcomes. It said the BlackLine Agentic Financial Operations Platform, powered by Verity AI, is where the Office of the CFO scales AI across Record-to-Report, Invoice-to-Cash, and the processes where finance owns the controls. It said BlackLine is supported by industry-leading R&D investment and world-class security practices. It directed readers to www.BlackLine.com to explore the platform and the innovations unveiled at BeyondTheBlack 2026.

The release listed Invoice-to-Cash innovations including Credit & Risk Management for AI-powered credit scoring, underwriting, and portfolio risk monitoring, Customer Onboarding for streamlined customer evaluation and account setup through connected digital workflows, and Disputes & Deductions for automated dispute intake, classification, and investigation. It also listed a Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) Agent that analyzes payment trends, predicts collection bottlenecks, and prescribes prioritized intervention strategies to compress cash conversion cycles. A separate KPMG Azerbaijan interview with Tural Jahangirov, Manager at KPMG Azerbaijan, dated Nov. 14, 2026, said the role of tax within a business is expanding beyond calculations and compliance. The interview said understanding the financial impact of tax decisions, maintaining data consistency, and identifying potential risks early are becoming increasingly important. It said technology should complement, rather than replace, professional judgement in tax decision-making.

stories.Headline: ECB vice president Boris Vujčić warns rapid AI expansion threatens EU financial stability
stories.Summary:
European Central Bank Vice President Boris Vujčić warned on Monday, November 16, 2026, that the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence could threaten financial stability in the region. Speaking at Euro Finance Week in Frankfurt, the official noted that stock market valuations for AI remain stretched and the risk of a repricing has risen. He observed that a recent correction following the mid-term elections in America serves as a necessary reminder for the industry to remain cautious. Vujčić argued that system-wide stability is now threatened by a range of additional factors beyond simple market valuations. These risks include the expansion of external funding from equity to debt markets and the concentration of exposures across the sector.

The Vice President also highlighted the dangers of quickening AI adoption and the potential for devastating cyberattacks against financial institutions. He emphasized that a resilient banking sector is critical given current geopolitical headwinds and elevated risks to overall stability. Furthermore, he stated that supervision must be maintained over non-banks, specifically mentioning the rapid growth of the private credit space. Boris Vujčić explained that private credit warrants close monitoring because of limited transparency and growing interconnectedness with insurers and banks.

He expressed concern regarding potential liquidity mismatches that could arise within these less transparent financial environments. These warnings follow a report from the International Monetary Fund titled Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity in the Financial Sector. The organization argued that AI can accelerate the discovery of vulnerabilities and turn isolated incidents into correlated disruptions affecting many institutions. The report suggests that AI transforms cyber risk from a technical security concern into a broader issue of enterprise governance.

It questions how much autonomy these systems should receive and whether organizations can contain them when something goes wrong. The International Monetary Fund noted that AI does not need to invent new forms of attack to change the risk equation. Instead, powerful models can cause significant damage when they are given network access or credentials in poorly configured environments. More to follow.

stories.Headline: LanceDB raises $57.5M Series B to speed AI model training on multimodal data
stories.Summary:
LanceDB Inc. announced on November 17, 2026 that it raised $57.5 million in early-stage funding to bring a multimodal lakehouse to researchers, model builders and platform teams. Bessemer Venture Partners and Innovation Endeavors led the Series B round. Theory Ventures, Dimension, Swift Ventures, CRV and Y Combinator also invested in the round. The round brought the company's total funding to $98.5 million. The company develops database technology designed to speed up artificial intelligence models.

LanceDB provides a unified multimodal data lakehouse that gives researchers, enterprise outfits and AI agents a unified way to access, find, prepare and train on data without spending weeks managing underlying infrastructure. Its technology is built on Lance, an open-source data format designed for AI workloads that combines structured information with images, video and other large files. Lance supports rapid retrieval and modification of individual records, unlike traditional analytics formats optimized for processing entire tables. The company built the format into a large-scale data lakehouse for retrieval. The platform can connect directly to customers' existing cloud storage, where the data remains, while distributing computational workloads across the infrastructure required to process it.

Co-founder and Chief Executive Chang She said research teams typically have to put different parts of their dataset in different places and lose weeks or months getting a whole training dataset ready for a single training run. He said there is a missing data layer for AI today and that is what the company is trying to build. He said part of what makes multimodal data different and more difficult is the size of the data. He said the data stays in place, remains the customer's and does not need to be copied. He said the faster the AI flywheel can spin, the faster research teams can get to higher quality models and make more interesting AI applications.

Runway Chief Technology Officer Kamil Sindi said a training example at Runway does not stay still, starting as a video and a prompt before embeddings, resolution and duration metadata are added for whatever the next experiment needs. He said Runway first started using the Lance format in 2024 because it was the only option that handled unstructured data, column appends, distributed reads and ad-hoc SQL all at once. He said Runway has since become a LanceDB Enterprise customer. Notable customers include Runway AI Inc., which adopted LanceDB's enterprise platform as its AI training needs expanded. Netflix Inc. built a media data lake on the technology for content creation, and Microsoft Corp. uses the platform as a data layer for training models on tens of billions of rows of image and code data.

Multimodal AI involves more than combining text, audio, images and video, because autonomous vehicles, robotics and world models also involve three-dimensional sensor information, geospatial coordinates, time-series data and annotations explaining what sensors are detecting. A self-driving car's sensors might produce a three-dimensional representation of the surrounding environment that then needs to be associated with information identifying roads, pedestrians, vegetation and other objects. The amount of data in lidar 3D clouds, images, video, audio and more can take up, on average, 10 to 20 petabytes in a single table for many large training workflows, with some becoming even larger and potentially approaching 80 to 100 petabytes. Researchers and model builders may maintain huge pools of data across different systems because conventional platforms were not designed around the requirements of multimodal AI. Curating a training dataset can take weeks or months just to move, prepare and process.

She said LanceDB intends to use the new funding to expand its multimodal data platform and accelerate the AI model development cycle, particularly by improving large-scale data curation, feature engineering and data loading to keep thousands of graphics processing units supplied efficiently during training. The company will also deepen its support for emerging AI workloads, including video generation, world models and robotics, where researchers must manage growing volumes of first-person sensor data, synthetic data and other multimodal information. The platform lets organizations consolidate data management, search, curation and feature engineering into a unified workflow, helping researchers prepare training datasets at petabyte scale without juggling separate infrastructure systems. The articles do not state when the funding is expected to close or how the new money will be divided among the named priorities. The articles do not give a valuation for LanceDB or a timeline for the expanded platform.

stories.Headline: South Korea tightens college exam security after top tax accountant test scorer admits to using AI
stories.Summary:
South Korea is facing a cheating scandal just days before its major college entrance exam. Han Won-seok, the top scorer on a tax accountant test, admitted to using artificial intelligence. He used a hidden camera to capture questions and received answers on a smartphone. This revelation has caused national alarm regarding the security of upcoming high-stakes academic tests. Police are currently investigating the case after Han confessed through his lawyer on YouTube.

The Suneung exam for the 2027 academic year will be taken this Thursday by 500,000 students. It will occur at 1,312 testing centers where authorities will deploy specially trained supervisors. These officials will look for AI-powered glasses at each of the 1,300 sites nationwide. Prime Minister Han Seongsook's office is considering shutting down public Wi-Fi and collecting smart devices. All electronic devices, including smartwatches and smartphones, are banned from the examination rooms.

Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin rejected calls from lawmakers to postpone the national college entrance exam. He stated that delaying the test would cause an even larger disruption for the students. The Ministry of Education pledged zero tolerance for any candidates caught cheating during the exam. Offenders will have their scores invalidated and lose eligibility to test the following year. They could also face criminal charges for the obstruction of business in the future.

Some experts worry that miniature cameras are almost impossible to detect through simple visual inspection. They argue that relying on conventional supervision is outdated given the rapid evolution of cheating. Approximately 550,000 students are affected by these security concerns during this intense academic competition. Critics suggest that installing electronic screening equipment at every center would be a better solution. However, they note that procuring such devices before Thursday would be very difficult now.

Han scored 397.5 out of 400 in April and 663 out of 800 in July. Other AI cheating incidents occurred in June on English tests and in October on essays. South Korea typically pauses flights and delays the stock market to help the test-takers. The military sometimes suspends training and police escort late students to ensure an ideal environment. This competition is critical because university attendance affects jobs, social standing, and even marriage prospects.

Authorities will now deploy specialized staff to identify sophisticated devices at the various testing sites. They are also seeking a full investigation into the suspicions surrounding the tax accountant exam. The articles leave open whether wireless communication blocking will be implemented before the exam starts. It remains unclear if Korea will adopt Chinese safeguards like drones and metal detector checkpoints. The government must decide if current measures are proportionate to the sophistication of AI threats.

stories.Headline: Air Marshal Tejinder Singh highlights AI's role in future military capabilities at Pune seminar
stories.Summary:
Air Marshal Tejinder Singh, the Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee, spoke about the strategic importance of Artificial Intelligence in shaping future military capabilities and operational preparedness, according to a Defence Ministry official. He made his remarks at a seminar held as part of a three-day Capsule on Science, Technology and Applied Research Programme at the Military Institute of Technology in Pune. The seminar carried the theme of AI versus AI as a new frontier of warfare and brought together tri-service leadership along with technology experts from academia and industry. Those present deliberated on the changing character of warfare in the AI era, the Integrated Defence Staff Headquarters said in a post on the social media platform X. The seminar included sessions by subject matter experts from the Armed Forces, academia and industry that covered emerging AI technologies, Sovereign AI, AI-enabled weapon systems, autonomous and counter-autonomous systems, human-machine teaming and decision superiority in multi-domain operations.

A key highlight was an event called Navonmesh, described as a meeting place for innovation and new ideas, where leading industry partners showcased cutting-edge AI technologies and innovative solutions along with their potential military applications. The seminar reinforced the importance of jointness, indigenous technological capabilities and collaboration between the Armed Forces, academia and industry in preparing for the evolving challenges of future warfare. Before the seminar, Air Marshal Tejinder Singh visited the National Defence Academy at Khadakwasla in Pune, where he reviewed key training infrastructure, the curriculum and forthcoming development projects aimed at further enhancing the training environment. The Integrated Defence Staff Headquarters said he also visited the outdoor tactical training site and interacted with cadets undergoing camp training, gaining insights into their training experiences and professional development. Addressing the cadets, he urged them to uphold the highest traditions of military ethos and to imbibe the core values of discipline, integrity and dedication while fostering a spirit of jointness.

He further urged them to strive for professional excellence and to prepare themselves to shoulder future responsibilities, carrying forward the legacy of what the statement called a distinguished cradle of military leadership. In a separate message, the Indian Air Force said on X that a exercise named AJHE26 was set to commence at Air Force Station Jamnagar from November 17 to 19, 2026. That exercise will bring together the Indian Defence Forces, the National Disaster Management Authority, the Indian Coast Guard and friendly foreign countries, according to the Indian Air Force message. The stated aim of the exercise is to strengthen joint preparedness and coordination in disaster response among the participating forces and agencies. The articles do not say what decisions, if any, followed from the seminar or the academy visit, and they give no further details on the outcomes of either.

stories.Headline: South Korea bans electronic devices at 1,312 test sites to block AI cheating on November 19 exam
stories.Summary:
The South Korean government decided not to postpone the College Scholastic Ability Test scheduled for November 19. Officials considered a delay but concluded that such a move would be too difficult to implement. This decision followed public concerns regarding cheating assisted by artificial intelligence during national exams. The government announced its final security measures on November 17 to prevent electronic misconduct. These rules aim to maintain the integrity of the high-stakes university admissions process.

The government will ban all electronic devices at 1,312 test sites and use emergency alerts to find phones. Authorities will deploy 1,800 smart device specialists and 6,600 hallway proctors, adding 8,400 staff to 75,000 existing proctors. Proctors will inspect every pair of eyeglasses, every clothing button, and require students to roll up both sleeves. Students should avoid wearing hats, rings, necklaces, or buttoned clothing to ensure smooth supervision. A full inspection of personal belongings will occur again after lunch before the third period begins.

Prime Minister Han Seong-sook stated from the Government Complex Seoul in Jongno District that the government would expand inspections. Vice Education Minister Choi Eun-ok explained that postponing the exam would create serious security problems for finalized questions. Choi noted that a delay of one to two weeks would cause major disruption for test-takers. Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin vowed a zero-tolerance approach and will actively seek criminal punishment for offenders. Kim Kwang-yong said critical emergency alerts cannot be blocked, ensuring all active phones will sound.

New Reform Party floor leader Chun Ha-ram argued the government should not ignore pleas to postpone the exam. A Korean Teachers and Education Workers Union spokesperson suggested that AI advances require changing educational evaluation practices. Students are affected by these strict rules, as are those who may face criminal charges. The public expressed outrage after a top tax accountant exam scorer admitted to using AI to cheat. Police are now investigating that individual who missed only one of 160 questions in one round.

Recent cases involved one middle school and three high school students caught using AI glasses during school exams. Other students used similar devices during university application tests to scan questions and produce answers in seconds. The CSAT, or Suneung, is so critical that flight schedules and military drills are adjusted on exam day. This environment makes the exam a primary path to stable careers for many young South Koreans. The current crisis stems from a loss of trust in the ability to catch AI cheaters.

Cheaters will now be barred from the exam for 10 years instead of the previous one year. Serious offenders face up to five years in prison for obstruction of official duties by deception. The government will investigate communication records and AI service access even after the exam ends. Authorities plan to investigate sellers and buyers of miniature cameras and online posts announcing cheating plans. The articles leave open whether electronic device detectors or metal detectors will be used in future exams.

stories.Headline: Applied Materials plans to double equipment output by 2028 to meet AI chip demand
stories.Summary:
Applied Materials announced plans to double its equipment output by 2028 to meet rising demand for artificial intelligence chips. The company shared these details during an earnings conference call held on November 12 local time. This growth is driven by increased investments in advanced packaging, DRAM, and advanced logic chips. The firm expects wafer fab equipment demand to grow more than 30 percent next year from 2026. This strategy follows a period of rapid earnings growth for the US semiconductor equipment maker.

The company aims to more than double its manufacturing and research facility capacity by 2030. Brice Hill stated the output goal for 2028 is compared with the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. The Santa Clara, California firm operates a facility in Austin, Texas, as part of Apple's American Manufacturing Program. China sales rose 35 percent to 2.64 billion dollars, though they were 25 percent of fourth quarter revenue. The company also opened a 600 million dollar plant in Singapore that adds 1,000 jobs.

Chief executive Gary Dickerson said that major customers are placing orders earlier and updating their demand forecasts for eight quarters. He noted that the company continues to receive requests to ramp up production and accelerate deliveries to clients. Dickerson stated that no customers were seeking to delay equipment deliveries during the recent earnings conference call. He expects 2027 to be another record year for both the market and for Applied Materials. The company is benefiting from chipmakers racing to meet extraordinary AI led demand for chips and memory.

Bob O'Donnell of TECHnalysis Research said that actual market metrics show that the current demand is still very strong. He added that the results show foundries and chipmakers are buying as much equipment as they possibly can. The company's growth affects its partners and the broader semiconductor supply chain across the United States and Singapore. Short term supply constraints for certain components have already created some challenges for the company's recent revenue. These constraints prevented the company from securing all the components needed to reach a higher quarterly revenue forecast.

Fiscal 2026 ran from October 27, 2025, to October 25, 2026, with record revenue of 34.45 billion dollars. This marked the seventh consecutive annual revenue record for the company since the start of fiscal 2020. Fourth quarter fiscal 2026 revenue hit a record 10.41 billion dollars, which was up 53 percent from last year. Operating income for that quarter reached 3.66 billion dollars, while the annual operating income climbed to 11.09 billion dollars. The company's stock has risen about 48 percent throughout 2026 as AI chip demand continues to fuel spending.

Applied Materials forecast first quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of 11.1 billion dollars, plus or minus 500 million dollars. This represents a 58 percent increase from a year earlier and exceeds Wall Street estimates of 10.89 billion dollars. The company identified more than 20 projects for new fabs and line expansions starting operations in 2027. Over 10 additional major projects are scheduled to begin operations in 2029 or 2030 according to company data. The articles leave open how the company will resolve the short term supply constraints for certain equipment components.

stories.Headline: Global leaders and educators call for collaboration to use AI to close learning and economic divides
stories.Summary:
John Lee Chi-kin chaired a high-level session on AI ethics and social responsibility in Hong Kong on October 27 and 28, 2026. This event occurred during the Global University Presidents and Leaders Summit 2026 to discuss high-tech innovation and the future of education. China also hosted APEC 2026, which focused on the three pillars of openness, innovation, and cooperation for the Asia-Pacific community. Participants at the 2026 Global South Modernization Forum in Cairo, Egypt, also called for the effective use of artificial intelligence. These leaders aim to use technology to close divides in learning, information, and economic opportunities across different global societies.

The mission requires collaboration between governments, academia, the technology sector, and the business community to dismantle barriers to accessibility. Hong Kong serves as a bridge to ASEAN and Belt and Road Initiative countries, supported by the Chinese mainland. The Education University of Hong Kong, or EdUHK, is ranked within the top seven globally in education by QS. Since 2017, EdUHK has served as a core consultant for World Bank education initiatives in Vietnam to foster digital transformation. The university also promotes policy dialogue and talent development in the United Arab Emirates, Kazakhstan, and various ASEAN countries.

John Lee Chi-kin and other leaders believe that education is central to harnessing AI for productivity and human development. Shannon Kane, an assistant clinical professor at the University of Maryland, says candidates must be prepared to judge AI outputs. Jennifer Kidd from Old Dominion University believes teachers must understand how AI works and its different impacts on learning. Justin Reich of MIT's Teaching Systems Lab argues that domain knowledge is necessary to tell if AI output is useless. Tracy Rock from the University of North Carolina at Charlotte says faculty should be critical rather than just AI cheerleaders.

Novice educators are affected by these changes, as over half of teachers now use AI for parts of their jobs. A 2023 ISTE report found that 56 percent of new teachers lack confidence in using technology in the classroom. K-12 school districts are affected by inconsistent policies, with some districts banning AI while others embrace the new technology. Students at George Mason University in Fairfax, Virginia, are now studying the benefits and drawbacks of AI in instruction. Many teacher candidates are also affected, though nearly a quarter of them do not want AI preparation in programs.

Teacher preparation has long struggled to effectively prepare aspiring teachers to integrate technology into their classroom instruction. An EdWeek Research Center survey of 268 teacher educators in August and September 2026 revealed various hurdles in AI integration. About 60 percent of faculty members decide individually whether to include an AI focus in their specific university courses. Many programs struggle to offer AI instruction because other priorities and national accreditation standards take precedence over new technology. Faculty professional development is limited, with only 14 percent of respondents reporting that they receive ongoing professional development.

Next, programs must navigate the rapid development of AI, which 57 percent of respondents cited as a major hurdle. Faculty at the University of North Carolina at Charlotte are using communities of practice to learn about tools like Gemini. Some instructors, like Jennifer Kidd, must revamp their course materials every single semester because the technology changes so quickly. The articles leave open whether K-12 school district leaders will actually prize AI skills when hiring new teacher candidates. It remains unclear if high-quality research will soon prove whether AI tools can actually improve student learning outcomes.

stories.Headline: Colette Kress faces investors as Nvidia reports first earnings without Jensen Huang
stories.Summary:
Nvidia reports its first earnings without Jensen Huang on Tuesday, after his departure ended 33 years at the company he built. Interim CEO Colette Kress now faces investors at the world's most important AI hardware company. Anthropic is expected to begin trading on Nasdaq on Thursday at a valuation approaching $1.4 trillion. The offering could raise as much as $64.4 billion, one of the largest public offerings in market history. Wall Street had barely recovered from Huang's departure before this five-day stretch began.

Nvidia's market capitalisation fell from approximately $5.8 trillion in early October to $3.9 trillion by Friday, nearly $2 trillion of shareholder wealth gone in a little over a month. The S&P 500 registered its first weekly gain after four consecutive declines and was up approximately 10.5% for the year. LSEG consensus cited in the market preview expects earnings growth of approximately 90% on quarterly revenue of $109 billion. Anthropic's latest prospectus outlined a transaction involving as many as 825 million shares and proceeds of up to $64.4 billion. Building a one-gigawatt data centre can cost at least $30 billion, and US technology companies have raised at least $220 billion through follow-on equity offerings this year, according to Bloomberg's compiled figures.

Colette Kress is described as an experienced executive with an intimate understanding of Nvidia's financial operations. Huang's influence extended beyond the usual responsibilities of a corporate CEO, as the industry's chief salesman, principal strategic negotiator and the man who could bring together customers, investors, infrastructure developers and technology suppliers. Nvidia reportedly took responsibility for the data-centre lease tied to Anthropic's reported $35 billion cloud-computing agreement with Nvidia-backed Lambda. The article asks whether new leadership will support customers and ecosystem partners with the same enthusiasm and whether it will become more conservative about strategic investments. It also asks whether regulatory scrutiny over semiconductor exports could make some of those relationships harder to maintain.

Bankers have discussed raising the offering price, and the order book is reportedly several times oversubscribed. Anthropic competes against OpenAI, Google and an increasingly capable collection of lower-cost open-weight models. Asia's semiconductor suppliers have considerable exposure to Nvidia's next move, the article states. The American consumer and the Fed have their own appointments with Wall Street next week, with retail sales, Fed minutes and a parade of consumer earnings on the calendar. The article says investors are increasingly distinguishing between the companies generating the AI spending and the businesses financing it.

Nvidia has become the unofficial central bank of the AI ecosystem, supplying chips, capital commitments and strategic relationships that helped finance an extraordinary infrastructure expansion. When capital was plentiful and GPU capacity scarce, the arrangement worked beautifully, letting Nvidia support selected customers and infrastructure partners and benefit from the resulting expansion in orders. Anthropic is preparing to test whether the public equity market will take on a much larger share of that financing burden. A successful listing could let Anthropic raise additional equity through follow-on offerings, issue convertible bonds, negotiate private placements or eventually access more conventional debt markets. Convertibles have become an important source of capital, allowing companies to borrow at relatively modest coupons while offering investors potential equity upside.

The article says the real test begins after the stabilisation bid disappears and shareholders discover that a $1.4 trillion valuation comes with a rather demanding earnings assignment. Unlike the private market, where valuations can remain insulated between financing rounds, public shareholders get to change their minds every trading session. The article leaves open whether the Bank of Nvidia intends to keep running the lending desk as aggressively without its chairman. It also leaves open how generous shareholders remain once the opening-day champagne runs out. The article states that the product road map is still intact and the hyperscalers are not about to stop building data centres because Huang is no longer wearing the leather jacket.

stories.Headline: India opens Consent Manager registration as data board remains unstaffed
stories.Summary:
India's digital personal data regime entered the second phase of implementation, with a milestone under the Digital Personal Data Protection framework meant to let individuals manage permissions through registered Consent Managers, Trisha Shreyashi wrote in a November 17, 2026 opinion article. She wrote that consent is collected in seconds on a click, while withdrawing it can mean navigating a maze of settings. She wrote that the imbalance between giving consent and withdrawing it persists. She wrote that the upcoming milestone promises to address the imbalance. The article appeared on moneycontrol.com on November 17, 2026.

The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 set up a map for phased implementation through the DPDP Rules, 2025. The framework applies to processing of digital personal data within India or connected to an activity related to data principals within India, and includes foreign SaaS companies, e-commerce platforms and offshore businesses offering services or goods to individuals in India even if processing takes place outside India. The first phase, the DPDP Rules, 2025, put in place the Data Protection Board of India and its operationalization. A Consent Manager is an entity registered with the Board that allows an individual to give, manage, review or withdraw consent across businesses through a single channel, must be incorporated in India and must meet the Board's conditions including a minimum net worth of Rs 2 crore and stipulated certifications. Registration rules for Consent Managers are scheduled to commence this month, ahead of substantive compliance obligations due in May 2027, and applications for registration opened from November 13, 2026.

The article said the chairman and members of the Data Protection Board of India have not yet been formally appointed or staffed, posing major risks in implementation of the second phase. It said appointing the Board's Chairperson and Members is an immediate priority and prolonged institutional vacuum risks undermining the framework's effectiveness. It said Consent Managers, whose value lies in protecting individual choice and the right to privacy, must demonstrate that their incentives align with their roles and do not interfere with them. It said transparent governance and effective oversight of Consent Managers are essential to preventing misuse. It said the role of the regulator is pivotal in ensuring clarity and consistency.

The article said the commencement notification brings Section 6 (9) of the act mandating registration into force prior to Section 6 (7), which provides for management of consent through the Consent Manager, and Rule 4 of the DPDP Rules, 2025 governs entities operating as Consent Managers. It said registration of a Consent Manager does not by itself require a data fiduciary to immediately connect its systems to the Consent Manager's platform. It said the data fiduciary remains accountable for processing undertaken by it or on its behalf, and where consent is disputed the data fiduciary will have to prove requisite notice and valid consent under Section 6 (10). It said a Consent Manager only administers permission and manages conflicts without acquiring unrestricted access to the individual's underlying personal data.

It said the phasing allows data fiduciaries a transition period to reconcile data collected, processed and shared, followed by mapping the data, reviewing privacy notices and consent mechanisms, assessing internal accountability, vendor agreements and third-party sharing arrangements, establishing data retention, deletion and other security practices, preparing for breach response and setting up a grievance redressal mechanism. The article said the Act's compliance machinery rests on three limbs, accountability, proof of consent and consequences of failure in safeguards, all within the constitutional frame set in KS Puttaswamy Vs. Union of India (2017), which settled the right to privacy as a part of Article 21. It said consent must be continuing, not just a record that a button was once clicked.

It said the Consent Manager is expected to assist individuals in giving, managing, reviewing and withdrawing consent in an accessible and transparent manner, enabling greater continuing control over their data. It said businesses and other data fiduciaries might face immediate difficulty in integrating compliance requirements vis-à-vis vendors. It said data fiduciaries should begin preparing to fulfill their obligations under the Act and the Rules, and that the principal duties concerning notice, consent and processing will follow at a later phase. The article said phased implementation might be easily misconceived as simultaneous compliance, and doing so adds an unnecessary compliance cost.

It said the milestone is a significant development for the consent management ecosystem and businesses involved in building or using consent management mechanisms and vendors. It said compliance extends well beyond obtaining consent and updating privacy policies. It said India's data privacy regime will ultimately be judged by the extent of authority an individual's choice carries over her information, and that consent management ecosystems will count for little if a change in preference does nothing beyond the screen. It said the decisive test is whether the whole, including the data fiduciaries, can honour the right to privacy across the systems and commercial relationships, and prove that they have done so.

stories.Headline: Prime Minister Han Seong-sook forms emergency team to prevent AI cheating on 2027 CSAT
stories.Summary:
South Korea is forming a pan-government emergency response team to stop AI-assisted cheating on the 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test. Prime Minister Han Seong-sook announced this team on Monday, November 16, 2026, during a meeting of related government ministries. The decision follows a confession from the top scorer of this year's certified tax accountant exam regarding AI use. This individual admitted on a Sunday YouTube appearance to using generative AI and electronic devices during both exam rounds. The Human Resources Development Service of Korea is filing a criminal complaint for obstruction of business against him.

The team will manage the national entrance exam taking place this Thursday to ensure that no advanced AI cheating occurs. Prime Minister Han ordered the Ministry of Education to review how testing sites are managed and proctored for the exam. Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin visited Yeongdeungpo Girls’ High School in western Seoul on Monday to check on various site preparations. The Ministry of Education previously ran safety inspections at 1,312 testing sites across 85 test districts over three weeks. These checks included outdoor structures and measures against fires, cold snaps, and earthquakes starting on October 20, 2026.

Prime Minister Han Seong-sook stated that suspected AI cheating is spreading across various exams and has deepened public concern about fairness. She said that hard working test-takers should not be negatively affected and confidence in the exam system must not erode. Han noted that existing ways of managing national exams are limited when dealing with new and sophisticated AI cheating techniques. She urged officials to use objective data to investigate any signs of irregularity found in the results after the exam. The Prime Minister believes the country must focus all its capabilities on preparing for the upcoming College Scholastic Ability Test.

Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin promised to spare no effort to prevent cheating and will respond with a zero-tolerance principle. He acknowledged that authorities cannot guarantee the detection of all AI-assisted cheating just days before the national college entrance exam. The Human Resources Development Service of Korea is affected by the tax accountant scandal and is pursuing criminal legal action. Other national exams are affected, as authorities will investigate potential AI-assisted cheating across 528 different state-run national examinations. Lawmakers on the National Assembly’s Education Committee in Yeouido also reviewed the preparations to block AI-assisted cheating on the test.

The government is reacting to the rise of ultrasmall electronic devices, outside help, and smart glasses used for cheating in exams. A smart glasses company representative demonstrated device functions to inspectors at the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education in Yongsan District. This training session occurred on November 11 to help inspectors screen students at testing sites located throughout the city of Seoul. The government is concerned that the basic principle of fairness, which upholds trust in society, is being threatened by technology. These measures are part of a broader effort to secure the integrity of the national university entrance exam system.

The emergency team will carry out both preventive and follow-up measures to ensure the fairness of the College Scholastic Ability Test. Relevant ministries must promptly prepare related measures based on the specific conditions of the exams under their own legal jurisdiction. Stricter oversight of electronic devices and smart wearables will continue even after the current college entrance exam period has finished. The articles leave open whether the current detectors will be ready in time to stop all AI cheating during the test. It remains unclear if the government can fully block all sophisticated AI tools before the exam begins this coming Thursday.

stories.Headline: Genesys launches Standalone AI Agents and Arena for customer service deployment
stories.Summary:
Genesys launched Standalone AI Agents and Genesys Arena on 18 November 2026, according to IT Brief Australia. The launch gives organisations a way to deploy agentic AI in customer service without replacing their existing systems. Standalone AI Agents lets organisations deploy the Genesys Cloud Agentic Virtual Agent within existing customer service environments in a few days. The approach is aimed at businesses that want AI for a specific customer service task while leaving their wider technology estate unchanged. Genesys also introduced Genesys Arena, built around prebuilt Agent Kits for customer experience use cases.

Standalone AI Agents works without first migrating more widely to Genesys Cloud, and the software can operate within defined business rules. It can hand an interaction to a human employee, along with the conversation context, if a request needs further expertise. The Arena kits cover more than 50 industry-specific scenarios and let teams create a functional AI agent in as little as 10 minutes. Teams can then customise the agent with natural language and deploy it into Genesys Cloud. The new pricing structure groups interactions into simple, moderate or complex tasks and measures usage in Experience Units, the new name for what Genesys previously called AI Tokens.

Tony Bates, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer at Genesys, said enterprises want to move faster with AI but need flexibility to do it on their own terms without compromising trust and governance. Bates said Standalone AI Agents, Genesys Arena and the effort-based pricing model give organisations more choice in how they put agentic AI to work today and scale it as their needs evolve. Youssef Nokta, Senior Vice President of AI Forward Deployed Engineering at Genesys, said AI is advancing quickly and enterprises should not have to start from zero every time they want to put a new idea to work. Nokta said Genesys Arena gives teams a practical head start so they can spend less time on foundational work and more time shaping AI around their customers, business and results. Genesys said each Agent Kit includes a working model with prebuilt knowledge, integrations, skills and guardrails for a given use case.

Mila D'Antonio, Principal Analyst, Customer Engagement at Omdia, said enterprises are under pressure to move agentic AI from experimentation into production quickly but are not all starting from the same place. D'Antonio said some are operating in the cloud while others are navigating complex hybrid or on-premises environments. She said Genesys Arena and Genesys Standalone AI Agents give organisations different paths to deploy agentic AI based on their existing environment and requirements. D'Antonio said the introduction of effort-based pricing highlights how commercial models are evolving as organisations consider how to adopt and scale agentic AI. Genesys cited Charles Sturt University as an existing user of its agentic virtual agent technology.

Michael Buttsworth, Associate Director, Student Experience Service Centre at Charles Sturt University, said using Genesys Agentic Virtual Agent has shown how AI can improve the customer experience and drive efficiency by resolving more interactions autonomously. Buttsworth said getting that value into production depends on how quickly teams can move from an idea to an experience that works in the real world. He said Genesys Arena and Agent Kits will make that path easier by giving organisations a more accessible starting point for building and tailoring agentic experiences to their customers, operations and brand. The university said the software had already shown how AI could handle more customer interactions without human involvement while improving efficiency. The products arrive as businesses in Australia and elsewhere consider how to connect generative and agentic AI systems to older customer service software while keeping deployment times short and costs under control.

Voice customisation tools are due to be added to Arena and the Genesys Cloud platform, letting organisations choose and adapt how AI agents sound by adjusting personality, tone and delivery using natural language prompts. Genesys said Standalone AI Agents are generally available now, while Agent Kits through Genesys Arena are due to become generally available later this month. The pricing change addresses a practical concern as AI use grows: how to forecast and control spending. Effort-based pricing charges less for straightforward tasks and more for interactions that require a wider set of tools to complete. The articles leave open the exact date later this month when Agent Kits become generally available and the timing for the voice customisation tools.

Trefis reported on November 17, 2026, that Google uses its own TPU chips to train Gemini models instead of using Nvidia hardware. Nvidia faced a crisis when CEO Jensen Huang resigned on November 12 after a board investigation into foreign intelligence efforts. House committees requested a closed door interview with Huang on December 1 to discuss these intelligence reports. Google continues to develop its AI stack while Nvidia reports third quarter fiscal 2027 results without its former leader. These events occurred as Alphabet and Nvidia stocks experienced significant volatility compared to the S&P 500 fund.

Google launched Universal Cart in the United States on October 15 to help shoppers track prices and choose payment methods. Nvidia announced the Open Agent Safety Platform on September 28 to help banks like Citi and J.P. Morgan Chase. BBVA announced on October 21 that it would explore Nvidia technology to expand AI agents across its banking operations. Broadcom partnered with Google on TPUs, and Anthropic committed to spend 121.3 billion dollars with Google Cloud through July 2033. Broadcom reported AI chip revenue of 16.7 billion dollars in its latest quarter, which rose 221 percent in one year.

Trefis stated that Google Cloud revenue rose 103 percent in the latest quarter, nearly matching Nvidia's growth of 106 percent. Alphabet reported that Google Cloud earned 36.2 percent of its revenue as operating profit, up from 23.7 percent previously. Google says its Universal Cart tool keeps shoppers in control while allowing purchases through Google Pay or merchant websites. Nvidia says its safety technology can monitor activity and stop AI agents that attempt to move beyond established limits. Trefis noted that Alphabet's engineering numbers suggest it can already build strong AI without relying on Nvidia chips.

Banks are affected because Google's shopping tools may influence which card issuers win transactions based on visible payment benefits. Financial institutions must now establish permissions and monitor AI activity to determine when a human must intervene in processes. Trefis noted that Alphabet's free cash flow was negative for two quarters, reaching minus 5.9 billion and 9.1 billion. To cover costs, Alphabet raised 49.6 billion dollars in June and borrowed 49 billion dollars in new notes recently. The articles explain that Google Cloud rents both its own TPU chips and Nvidia chips to its various cloud customers. Alphabet previously suffered a 44 percent drop in 2022 and took 15 months to return to its old high. Nvidia experienced a 63 percent drop in 2022 and required seven months to recover from that specific market bottom. This background shows that while Google is technically independent, it remains vulnerable to broad market sell offs and cash constraints.

stories.Headline: Johns Hopkins researchers find hedging and collective phrasing make AI writing less formal and less sophisticated
stories.Summary:
Researchers at Johns Hopkins University conducted a study examining how different communication styles influence AI-generated professional writing, as reported on 17 November 2026. The study tested Meta Llama 3.1 3B Instruct, Mistral 7B Instruct, Gemma 2 27B, and GPT-4. Prompts containing features more commonly associated with women, including hedging phrases such as "maybe" and "I think" and collective references such as "we" and "our", generally produced responses that were less sophisticated, more readable, and less formal. The effects were strongest for emails and job applications, while findings for resignation letters were weaker. The researchers also changed the names used in the prompts to traditionally male and female names, and the name cues had virtually no effect on the outcomes while the linguistic differences persisted.

The study found differences in formality across the four models tested. In another preliminary experiment, the researchers asked GPT-4 to compare generated documents and assess which author appeared smarter and more competent. Across 105 comparisons involving GPT-4-generated responses, the judging model favoured responses produced from prompts containing male-associated features more often when it expressed a preference. The study examined specific model versions, including an older GPT-4 model, and the researchers acknowledge that they modified the prompts to create controlled comparisons. The linguistic features examined were drawn from research primarily focused on gender-associated language and are not exclusive to either gender.

Anjalie Field, Assistant Professor of Computer Science at Johns Hopkins University, said it is difficult to uncover exactly why a model produces a particular output. She said they speculate that in this setting the linguistic signal simply overpowers the signal from the name. She also said they speculate that these models may have been trained to resist name-associated biases, but not more subtle linguistic signals. Field cautioned that if you use AI to help draft application materials like cover letters or emails to potential employers, and you are not careful about the language in your prompt or monitoring the text the AI drafts for you, the AI may not be helping you make your best case. She said generated text still needs to be reviewed for whether it accurately and effectively communicates an experience.

Sambratha Shetty, Chief Operating Officer at Bengaluru-based think-tank Synergia Foundation, said the models responded primarily to how the request was expressed, not to the writer's stated identity. She said this means that conventional name-blind audits could miss the problem entirely. She cautioned against treating the results as a definitive assessment of current AI systems and noted that the behaviour of these systems may differ across newer versions. Shetty recommended paired-prompt testing, in which organisations submit similar requests using direct, hedged, individual and collaborative language, and argued that the level of scrutiny should depend on the application. Shipra Kamra, Head of People Operations at SaaS startup Responsive, said a polished email that an assistant mostly wrote tells you very little about the employee's skills, and that if a candidate's own writing is compared to AI-smoothed text, people with a different style or language background can be marked down unfairly.

The study does not establish whether these differences affect workplace communication or influence employment decisions. The study does not demonstrate that recruiters assess candidates differently because of these output variations. Whether AI writing assistants consistently encourage a particular communication style across organisations and applications remains to be examined. Research involving Indian English and other workplace languages could help determine whether the patterns observed in the study also appear in different professional contexts. The Johns Hopkins findings provide evidence that linguistic features can influence the form of AI-generated professional writing across the models tested, but they do not establish that these variations lead to differences in human judgement or employment outcomes.

Kamra recommended that organisations establish clear guidelines on where AI is used in recruitment and performance assessments, retain human accountability for decisions, and examine how these tools perform across different employee groups. She emphasised involving employees when selecting and testing these tools, and said employees should feel able to ignore a suggestion and should have somewhere to say so when a tool is changing their voice in a way that feels wrong. She said inclusion has to be part of how tools are chosen, not something added afterwards. Shetty argued that the level of scrutiny should depend on the application, noting that a tool used for routine correspondence has different implications from one used to draft performance evaluations, job descriptions, or recruitment recommendations. Evaluating AI writing assistants could involve examining how they respond to different ways of phrasing similar requests, which would help businesses understand whether variations in prompts lead to differences in the length, formality, reading level, or accuracy of generated text.
