stories.Headline: Suki launches Suki OS to extend visit data into prior authorization and billing work
stories.Summary:
Suki, an ambient clinical intelligence company, introduced a platform called Suki OS on November 17, 2026, according to MobiHealthNews, and the company said the platform will take information gathered during patient visits and use it for tasks beyond documentation. The platform combines Suki's existing technology with AI agents and partner services to support patient care work, including insurance approvals and billing. The first two projects will focus on prior authorization, which includes checking authorization requirements and the records needed for a request, and on incomplete documentation, which will flag missing details in clinical documents that affect coding or payment. Suki also announced that it added Stellar Health and ECLAT to its partner network. The company outlined a commercial arrangement in which eligible Suki customers could recoup as much as their full fees if the company's technology falls short of negotiated targets.

Those measures could include clinician participation or coding accuracy, with reimbursement dependent on contract terms and on using customers' data to measure results. Last month, Suki announced it secured $90 million in financing as part of its Series E raise, just a year after receiving an investment from Zoom Ventures, bringing its total funding to $168 million at the time. Suki raised $70 million in Series D funding in 2024, secured $55 million in Series C funding in 2021, and in 2020 closed a $20 million Series C funding round. Punit Soni, CEO and founder of Suki, said in a statement that the greatest opportunity for AI in healthcare is not to make today's processes faster but to question why so many of those processes exist in the first place.

He said the company has an opportunity to fundamentally redesign how healthcare operates by removing friction that has become so deeply embedded in the system that it is accepted as inevitable. He described Suki OS as a step toward a future where technology does not just support healthcare but helps transform what is possible. Suki has added new offerings to its platform in the past year, including expanding its assisted revenue cycle capabilities to provide more specific automation and generate additional codes, including Current Procedural Terminology and Evaluation and Management codes. In August, Suki launched Suki Dictation, an AI clinical documentation tool that can integrate with Epic and MEDITECH EHR systems and allows clinicians to dictate and edit documentation by voice when ambient documentation may not be appropriate for a particular encounter or workflow.

stories.Headline: Claude and Gemini repeat partisan language as their own in Texas election answers
stories.Summary:
On November 3, 2026, James Talarico and Bobby Pulido won their races as Texas’s U.S. Senate and House races heated up, and voters turned to Google Search with questions about Democratic candidates Talarico and Pulido and Republican candidates Ken Paxton and Monica De La Cruz. In October, the Digital Democracy Institute of the Americas asked OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Anthropic’s Claude, and Google’s Gemini each the most common questions drawn from Google Trends. On October 9, 2026, DDIA tested OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Luna, Anthropic’s Claude Sonnet 5 and Google’s Gemini 3.8 Flash, with web search on, through a service called OpenRouter. Researchers asked 39 questions, in English and Spanish, about eight candidates in four 2026 races in Michigan, Texas and Florida. DDIA researchers asked all three chatbots whether Talarico said “God is nonbinary,” a line Republicans have been using against him throughout the current campaign.

Talarico said it in an October 2021 speech on the Texas House floor against a bill that required students to play on school sports teams matching the sex they were assigned at birth, pointing to the two Hebrew words used for God in the first lines of the Book of Genesis, one masculine and one feminine. In an April 2021 committee hearing, Talarico said modern science recognizes many more than two biological sexes, in fact six, referring to intersex chromosome variations, not genders. In September 2026, he said he missed the mark on some of his past statements and explained there are two sexes plus a small percentage of people with genetic variations. Paxton has been Texas attorney general since 2015, and in May 2026 he beat Sen. John Cornyn in a runoff and became the Republican nominee for the U.S. Senate. On June 29, 2026, his office as Texas attorney general, which Paxton still led while running for the Senate, published a press release touting his record.

Claude, in English, said Talarico was speaking against “a bill to ban men from women’s sports,” an exact phrase used by Fox News in an article, and three of its four sources were right-leaning outlets: Fox News, PJ Media and Public Square magazine, with the fourth a local San Antonio TV station. In Spanish, Claude sent researchers to FactCheck.org and local TV and did not borrow phrasing that can be considered controversial. In English, Claude began with “Not quite” and explained that Talarico had talked about six biological sexes, not six genders, but in Spanish it began with “Sí” and said Talarico did make a claim about “seis géneros/sexos,” using words fully extracted from the Washington Examiner and summarizing the measure as keeping “hombres biológicos que se identifican como transgénero” out of girls’ sports. Claude described Paxton’s record by copying, word for word, two lines from a press release his office published to promote him, that he “vigorously and successfully defended SB 4,” a state law that lets police arrest people suspected of crossing the border illegally, and that he “secured a major U.S. Supreme Court victory” on the state’s congressional map, using no quotation marks and not saying the words were the office’s own praise. Claude, in English, added that Pulido “has criticized Biden’s open borders policies,” copying content from a post by the Welcome Party, a group that backs centrist Democrats, including Pulido.

Gemini and ChatGPT responded accurately and in a fact-based manner, and both described the bill being discussed when Talarico said “God is nonbinary” in neutral terms in both languages, though Gemini used as sources Facebook posts made by conservative news outlets: Fox News in English, and PJ Media and Fox News in Spanish. ChatGPT also opened its Spanish answer with “Sí,” but right away added that the phrase is usually distorted and that he never said “six genders,” and in English it said “No, not literally.” Gemini got the facts right in both languages, mentioning that Talarico spoke of six biological sexes, not six genders, and later walked it back, but linked to Facebook posts made by politicians, using a social media publication made by Texas Governor Greg Abbott’s campaign as source in the English and Spanish versions, and in Spanish also linking to a post by Republican Lt. Governor Dan Patrick and to WLT Report. ChatGPT gave a plain, up-to-date answer in both languages on Paxton, citing strong sources like the attorney general’s office, the Texas Senate and news outlets such as the Associated Press and The Texas Tribune, and Gemini was the most limited, describing Paxton only as attorney general in both languages, never mentioning his Senate run, and citing no sources at all.

All three chatbots explained the charges against Paxton correctly, with ChatGPT adding that “impeachment is an accusation, not a criminal conviction,” but Gemini, in Spanish, labelled Paxton’s ties to the donor a “relación corrupta” and cited no sources in either language. All three chatbots responded that Pulido identifies as a Democrat, and in Spanish Claude cited news outlets including The Dallas Morning News and Univision. ChatGPT answered in two sentences in both languages: Pulido is a Democrat who “describes himself as a conservative Democrat.” Gemini’s English answer was even shorter, saying only that he is running as a Democrat, and in Spanish it added that he calls himself a “Blue Dog” or conservative Democrat focused on border security, gun rights and health care, citing Spanish-language news outlets. Monica and Carlos De La Cruz are siblings, Carlos is the Republican nominee in Texas’ 35th District, he won a primary runoff on May 26 and faced Democrat Johnny Garcia on Nov. 3, and all three chatbots responded accurately about the relationship.

Claude, in Spanish, said Carlos “está en la papeleta” in the May 26 runoff, as if that vote hadn’t happened yet, offering this answer on Oct. 9, more than four months after Carlos De La Cruz won the Republican primary runoff. A DDIA poll of 1,500 Latino registered voters, conducted by YouGov from Sept. 24 to Oct. 6, found that most Latino voters (57%) would not feel comfortable using a chatbot to help them decide who to vote for, but about one in three (34%) said fact-checking something they saw online or heard from someone would be a reason to use a chatbot for politics, and only 42% of U.S. Latino respondents said they always or often check a chatbot’s answer against another source. In May 2023, the Texas House impeached Paxton on 20 articles, most of them accusing him of abusing his office to help Nate Paul, a donor and real estate developer, and in September 2023 the Texas Senate acquitted him of all charges. Pulido calls himself a “conservative Democrat,” and the phrase “open borders” is commonly used by Republicans to attack Democrats on immigration.

When a chatbot’s English and Spanish answers to the same question got different grades, the Spanish answer was worse in eight of 12 cases. Claude, and Gemini in Spanish, repeated campaign and partisan language as their own, and Gemini often linked to social media posts as sources, including posts by candidates’ political opponents. Following the Associated Press style, which most U.S. newsrooms use to standardize language, the media avoids calling transgender girls “men,” and Claude’s English answer followed The Associated Press guidance: “a bill about transgender athletes in school sports.” DDIA researchers suggest clicking through the links to see where the answer given by AI came from, watching for politically charged words and keeping in mind that “ad speak” may mean something was pulled from an ad, and checking important claims with local news, fact-checkers and official websites.

The articles say it is important that AI companies double their efforts to give accurate, balanced answers to fact-based political questions in every language. Detailed breakdowns are included below, full findings from the When AI Answers Series are available in the full report, and Michigan and Florida findings are available here. The articles leave open what the full report contains beyond the Texas findings and what the chatbots’ answers were to the remaining questions among the 39 asked. stories.Headline: US stocks decline as AI companies experience price swings ahead of Nvidia earnings report
stories.Summary:
The United States stock market fell on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, as artificial intelligence companies experienced significant price swings. The S&P 500 sank 0.9 percent, while the Nasdaq composite dropped 1.2 percent and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 541 points, or 1.1 percent. Nvidia led the decline with a 2.9 percent drop, and other AI firms like Advanced Micro Devices and CoreWeave also shifted from early gains to losses. These fluctuations occurred as investors awaited a critical earnings report from Nvidia after the trading day ended.

The situation requires Nvidia to prove that its growth can persist following the resignation of former leader Jensen Huang. The company is now establishing a new board committee to manage global trade compliance and national security. This change follows reports that Huang had an extramarital affair with a person alleged to be a spy for China. Interim CEO Colette Kress is scheduled to speak to Wall Street for the first time since taking over the leadership role.

Market analysts suggest that AI stocks have been volatile for months due to a series of evolving concerns. These worries include the possibility that stock prices rose too high, the impact of high interest rates, and potential new regulations following Democratic victories in the midterm elections. Other market factors contributed to the decline, such as a 1.8 percent drop for Home Depot and a 2.3 percent loss for United Airlines. The broader economy remains influenced by high inflation, rising oil prices, and technical issues at major banks like JPMorgan Chase.

stories.Headline: Marsh reports AI-driven cyber incidents more than double as premiums head for 10 percent rise in 2027
stories.Summary:
Insurance broker Marsh reported on Tuesday, November 17, that artificial intelligence has accelerated the pace and scope of cyberattacks. The company recorded 105 cyber incidents for its clients during the second half of October, which is more than double the 48 incidents seen in late May. These AI enabled tools allow attackers to identify vulnerabilities like unpatched software and weak identity controls much faster than before. The FBI also warned that a hacking framework called ARTEX has been used since August to gain privileged enterprise access in under three hours. This specific tool has targeted the telecommunications, manufacturing, healthcare, and financial services sectors, including a breach of personal information for 67,000 people in South Korea.

These rising threats are driving a significant increase in the cost of global cyber insurance premiums over the next two years. GlobalData projects that premiums will grow by 6.9 percent to reach 16.6 billion dollars this year. This growth is expected to accelerate further to a 10 percent increase in 2027, bringing the total to 18.3 billion dollars. Businesses are facing these higher costs as they struggle to respond to the increasing frequency of attacks. The shift requires companies to address the asymmetry between software driven attackers and defenders who are limited by budgets and staffing.

Meredith Schnur, the cyber practice leader for Marsh Risk in the United States and Canada, explained that AI acts as an amplification of risk. She stated that a significant number of recent incidents can be attributed to attackers using agentic tools to find system weaknesses. Schnur noted that the volume of incidents has increased because organizations are taking longer to contain attacks while AI adoption scales quickly. This environment puts immense pressure on chief financial officers and chief information security officers at large enterprises. These leaders must manage larger digital footprints that are more susceptible to the new methods employed by modern fraudsters.

Articles.Title: Cyber Insurance Costs to Jump 10% Amid Rising AI Attacks

stories.Headline: Axel Licha shares study showing AI contours 21 cardiac substructures in under a minute
stories.Summary:
Axel Licha, a radiotherapy clinical consultant at TheraPanacea, shared a LinkedIn post about a new study published in Practical Radiation Oncology, the official clinical journal of the American Society for Radiation Oncology, on November 17, 2026. The study is titled Multicenter Evaluation of a Deep Learning Model for Automatic Contouring of Cardiac Substructures in Adults. Alexandra Moignier and Axel Licha share first authorship, and the co-authors are Felix Felici, Loig Duverge, Martin Lange, Loic Ah-Thiane, Gregory Delpon, Anna Karlhede, Fredrik Löfman, Frida Skarf, Jonas Söderberg, Elvire Martin-Mervoyer, François Thillays, Arnaud Beddok and Loig Vaugier. Licha said the project involved months of research, collaboration and a shared ambition of making cardiac protection in radiotherapy more precise and accessible. The deep learning model automatically contours 21 cardiac substructures in under one minute, according to the post.

Of those contours, 93.8% were clinically acceptable without major corrections, and the figure was 88.5% for coronary arteries, which the post describes as among the most challenging structures to delineate. Licha framed the results as less time contouring and more time for clinical expertise, and as a step closer to more personalized radiotherapy. He thanked the co-authors and collaborators, especially Moignier, and named Elvire Martin-Mervoyer, Arnaud Beddok and Loig Vaugier for their trust, mentorship and constant support. Licha is responsible for the LinkedIn post, and the study itself is the work of the listed authors, with Moignier and Licha as first authors. In the post he said artificial intelligence is changing radiation oncology and that he and his colleagues are part of it.

He also said some publications mean a little more than others and that this is definitely one of them, adding that he is incredibly proud to share the publication. The articles do not record any further comment from the other authors or from the journal. The articles give no further details on the study design, the centers involved or a publication date beyond the post, and they do not say what happens next with the model or its clinical use. The only stated next step is Licha's description of the work as a step closer to more personalized radiotherapy. The remaining content of the source page consists of site navigation, other headlines and a copyright notice, which add nothing to the story.

stories.Headline: Revenue cycle leaders should treat AI as part of the operating model, not a standalone tool
stories.Summary:
The article is a how-to piece on future-proofing revenue cycle management in the age of AI, published by hitconsultant.net on November 17, 2026, and it offers guidance rather than reporting a single event with named actors and dates. It does not name the people who wrote it, the organizations that contributed to it, or any specific company, hospital or vendor that has adopted the practices it describes. Because the text supplies no who, no when beyond the publication date and no concrete numbers, there is no reported happening to set out in the order a news story would require. The piece instead frames AI as a force changing how revenue cycle work is organized and argues that organizations should prepare for it deliberately.

What the article requires of readers is a shift in how revenue cycle management is planned, staffed and measured, with AI treated as part of the operating model rather than a standalone tool. It presents future-proofing as a set of changes to process, people and data rather than a single purchase or policy, and it frames the work as ongoing preparation for conditions that are still developing. The text gives no figures for cost, adoption rates, error rates, staffing levels or timeframes, and it names no deadlines, budgets or performance targets that a reader could check. It also gives no dates for when any of the described changes should begin or be completed, beyond the publication date of the article itself.

Responsibility for acting sits with the leaders who run revenue cycle operations, according to the article, though it does not name any individual, title or institution as accountable. The guidance is addressed to those who plan and oversee the revenue cycle rather than to patients, payers or regulators, and it treats their decisions about technology and workflow as the lever that determines the outcome. The article's own statements are presented as advice and framing rather than as findings from a study, a pilot or a disclosed set of results. No spokesperson, executive or expert is quoted by name, and no organization is described as having tested or endorsed the approach.

The context the article supplies is the growing presence of AI in revenue cycle work and the risk that organizations adapt slowly or unevenly to it. What happens next, in the article's telling, depends on whether revenue cycle leaders treat future-proofing as a continuing discipline rather than a one-time project, and it offers no schedule, milestone or forecast for how that will unfold. It reports no event that has occurred, no decision that has been announced and no result that has been measured, so there is nothing further to say about consequences that the text actually supports. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Ciaran Malone speaks at ESTRO course on AI integration in radiotherapy
stories.Summary:
Ciaran Malone, a Senior Medical Physicist at St Luke’s Radiation Oncology Network and a member of the AI in Radiation Oncology working group at the National group under the NCCP, shared a LinkedIn post about a guest speaker role at an ESTRO course. The course is titled Current Use, Future Developments, and the Integration of AI, and it is hosted by St. Luke’s Radiation Oncology AI Network at the St. James’s Hospital Campus. Malone said he was delighted to be contributing as a guest speaker along with Maeve Kearney at the course. He described a great opening session to a full room led by Course Director Rob Tijssen alongside Prof. Gerry Hanna, Marie Curie Chair of Clinical Oncology and Consultant Clinical Oncologist. Malone said the session set the tone with a few standout reminders, including that imaging does not simply support radiotherapy but defines what it can do.

Malone also cited the reminder that we do not treat images, but treat patients based on the information images provide. He said he was really looking forward to sharing his perspective on SGRT and AI at the course. He added that he looked forward to learning from colleagues across the field and exploring how to best harness the technology to improve outcomes for patients. The article describes ESTRO, the European Society for Radiotherapy and Oncology, as a leading European scientific society dedicated to promoting excellence in radiation oncology through education, research, and professional collaboration.

ESTRO organizes courses, workshops, and educational programs for radiation oncology professionals, and it supports research and innovation in radiotherapy and cancer treatment. The society also provides opportunities for specialists to expand their knowledge and clinical expertise and connects healthcare professionals, researchers, and institutions worldwide. ESTRO additionally promotes developments in radiotherapy, medical imaging, artificial intelligence, and precision cancer treatment, according to the article. The article gives no further details on the course schedule, the content of Malone’s talk, or any outcomes from the session.

It also does not say what SGRT stands for or how AI would be used in the radiotherapy workflow. No figures, dates beyond the article’s publication, or patient data are provided in the text. The article closes with a note inviting readers to stay up to date with daily picks from OncoDaily and a copyright notice covering the site’s content. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Trump and allies fund super intelligence accelerator to expand Indo-Pacific AI access
stories.Summary:
President Donald Trump announced a new super intelligence accelerator during a dinner in Manila, Philippines, on Tuesday, November 17, 2026. This initiative was unveiled as the president began his first trip to Asia following the midterm elections. The announcement occurred while leaders from the United States, Australia, India, and Japan met for the first time in two years. This event took place at the Solaire Resort immediately after the conclusion of the ASEAN Summit.

The new agreement among the United States, Australia, India, and Japan provides more than 85 million dollars in funding. These resources are intended to expand access to trusted artificial intelligence partners throughout the Indo-Pacific region. Simultaneously, the administration is taking steps to restrict the ability of Chinese companies to remotely access advanced chips from the United States. This push for superintelligence comes during a period of global upheaval involving chipmakers like Nvidia.

President Trump stated that the nations gathered for the meeting are very advanced regarding superintelligence and almost every other field. He used the term superintelligence, or SI, to describe the artificial intelligence technologies being discussed. The president made these remarks as he prepared to travel to China on Wednesday. He is scheduled to participate in a trilateral meeting later this week with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

The initiative arrives as national security risks surrounding artificial intelligence supply chains face intensified scrutiny. This heightened concern follows allegations of Chinese espionage and general instability within the global semiconductor industry. The administration is focusing on these security risks while expanding partnerships with key allies in the region. Further diplomatic discussions are expected to continue during the president's ongoing visits to China and Russia.

Articles.Title: Trump touts multicountry AI push in Manila

stories.Headline: Fed finds over 3 trillion dollars in off-balance-sheet AI commitments
stories.Summary:
The Federal Reserve discovered over 3 trillion dollars in off-balance-sheet AI commitments during its first close look at the buildout. This finding appeared in the November 2026 Financial Stability Report. The Fed identified these promises as obligations that do not show up as debt. The report includes a new section called Leverage in the Data Center Buildout. This specific section was absent from five previous editions dating back to 2024.

The report counts over 1 trillion dollars in signed leases that have not yet started. It also finds over 2 trillion dollars in residual value guarantees and take-or-pay contracts. These obligations involve Amazon, Alphabet, Broadcom, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Oracle. On-balance-sheet debt for these seven firms should exceed 800 billion dollars by year end. The Fed notes these off-balance-sheet figures are undiscounted and not directly comparable with debt.

Fed Governor Michael Barr said the potential maximum nominal value of these obligations is above 3 trillion dollars. He warned that opacity can exacerbate selloffs when investor sentiment shifts because risk is hard to locate. Barr noted that guarantees show how much GPU producers and hyperscalers might absorb if borrowers default. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said staff started modeling AI scenarios from growth booms to disappointments. He stated he is less concerned about direct losses given the limited debt backing the boom.

The Fed surveyed 23 contacts at banks, broker-dealers, investment funds, and advisory firms in September and October. Eighty-seven percent of these contacts named AI as a salient risk to the financial system. Large U.S. bank holding companies have close to 1 trillion dollars of exposure to AI-related entities. High-yield bond funds, life insurers, and business development companies hold riskier slices of resulting construction debt. Data-center developers use leases from companies with strong credit to finance their construction projects.

Debt issuance for advanced computing rose to over 680 billion dollars by October, up from 130 billion in 2023. This sector's share of nonfinancial investment-grade corporate debt issuance grew from under 6 percent to about 31 percent. Public debt tied to advanced computing is estimated at more than 1.1 trillion dollars. The report uses data through October 28, two weeks before Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned. Nvidia had a 105 billion dollar capped obligation for an OpenAI affiliate campus in Ohio.

Nvidia CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO on November 12 after Jensen Huang resigned from all his roles. The New York Fed reported on November 12 that bank liquidity stress is at levels not seen since 2014. The Federal Reserve will release its next financial stability report in the spring of 2027. The articles leave open how much economic exposure tech firms have beyond their on-balance-sheet liabilities. They also leave open the results of Nvidia's third-quarter revenue report.

Articles.Title: Fed’s first close look at AI buildout finds $3 trillion of commitments off Big Tech’s balance sheets

stories.Headline: Klarna reports 12% revenue growth and unveils an upgraded AI shopping assistant
stories.Summary:
Klarna stock initially jumped over 5% in early trading on Tuesday morning, November 17, 2026, after the buy now, pay later company reported third quarter earnings, with revenue up 12% year over year. The Swedish company announced the results in its third quarter earnings report and discussed them on its Q3 earnings call that Tuesday. On that call Klarna also announced an upgraded AI-powered shopping assistant, building artificial intelligence into its shopping browser and app, as well as iMessage and WhatsApp. Co-founder and CEO Sebastian Siemiatkowski announced the shopping assistant on Tuesday's call, saying it is live with a small group of early users and pre-registration is starting. Klarna is upgrading AI features and attracting new customers in time for the holiday shopping season.

Revenue came in at $1 billion, compared to analyst estimates of $964 million. Gross merchandise volume rose 10% year over year to $36.1 billion. Adjusted loss per share was $0.19, a wider loss than the estimated loss per share of $0.13. The company saw a 19% increase in adjusted operating expenses to $350 million and reported a net loss of $65 million in Q3. Klarna reiterated its full-year outlook for gross merchandise volume, the total monetary value of all completed purchases across its network, at $149 billion to $151 billion, and for Q4 it predicts revenue of between $1.01 billion and $1.09 billion.

Q3 volume in its card business more than doubled to $4.5 billion, card subscribers tripled to 2.6 million, and subscription revenue grew over 500%. Siemiatkowski said on the call that Klarna is bringing AI and agentic commerce to the core of Klarna. In its Q3 earnings release the company wrote that heading into 2027 it sees three key opportunities: scaling Fair Financing in the U.S. and expanding it across Europe, growing the Klarna Card beyond its merchant network, and AI to accelerate growth and productivity. The company named Chris Koegel, formerly of Robinhood, as CFO, effective Jan. 1. Klarna described the US as its fastest-growing market.

The report was called relatively rosy good news for Klarna. Adobe forecasts US buyers will spend a record $21.3 billion through buy now, pay later firms like Klarna during the 2026 holiday season, up 6.6% year over year. Klarna has struggled over the past year, and the stock is down 50% since the beginning of the year. Fintech valuations may be pressured in the coming months if the Federal Reserve raises interest rates in December, as is widely expected.

In the previous quarter the company missed Wall Street expectations, lowered its guidance, and announced executive transitions. The articles list related coverage including a Barron's piece saying Klarna keeps winning shoppers but has not been winning over investors. The articles give no further background beyond the past year's struggle, the prior quarter's miss, lowered guidance and executive transitions, and the widely expected December Fed rate move. Klarna's stock jump of over 5% came in early trading on Tuesday morning.

The Q3 report showed revenue up 12% year over year. The upgraded assistant was announced on the same call. The company reiterated its full-year gross merchandise volume outlook. The articles leave open how the upgraded shopping assistant will perform beyond the small group of early users and when pre-registration will convert to wider availability.

They do not say whether the Federal Reserve will raise rates in December. They do not give the date of the Q4 report or the size of the holiday season's effect on Klarna's results. They do not say how the CFO transition will affect the company. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Druckenmiller exits AMD and Alphabet and adds SpaceX, Palantir and AppLovin
stories.Summary:
Duquesne Family Office's third-quarter 13F showed complete exits from AMD and Alphabet, alongside new positions in SpaceX, Palantir and AppLovin, according to MarketWatch's review of the filing. Stanley Druckenmiller is still buying artificial intelligence but changing which AI businesses he owns. The filing does not show his sale prices or exact trade dates, so investors can't tell how well the exits were timed. Since then, AMD has fallen 22.35% from its October 6 close of $649.42. Since the quarter ended, Alphabet has dropped 17.54%.

AMD's third-quarter revenue rose 44.7% to $13.38 billion, and Data Center sales grew 97% to $8.55 billion. The company guided fourth-quarter revenue to approximately $17 billion, and the stock trades near 191 times trailing earnings. GAAP EPS was $1.46 after a $1,097M customer warrant charge. Alphabet's Google Cloud revenue grew 103% to $30.71 billion, but capital spending reached $51.36 billion and free cash flow was negative $9.07 billion. Alphabet is now paying for its expansion partly through debt, at-the-market equity issuance and mandatory convertible preferred stock, and GAAP EPS of $2.12 missed the $2.97 estimate, ending a 12-quarter beat streak.

Palantir's U.S. commercial revenue of $984M exceeded U.S. government revenue of $953M for the first time, and the adjusted operating margin was 62%. Full-year revenue guidance rose to $8.53B, and CEO Alex Karp said the Sovereign AI moment is purpose-built for Palantir. Palantir trades near 228 times earnings, total contract value grew just 6% year over year, and shares are down 11.81% year to date. SpaceX reported revenue of $14.60B, and its Super Intelligence segment, which includes Grok and Cursor, brought in $7.60B, up 830%. That segment leases data center capacity to outside customers and expanded with the Cursor acquisition at an implied $60B equity value.

Starlink had 13.6M consumer subscribers, and SpaceX shares trade at $141.48, down 12.1% from their first available close on June 12. On Tuesday, MarketWatch reported that SpaceX got a vote of confidence from Nvidia. AppLovin's revenue rose 55.5% to $2.18B, and adjusted EBITDA reached $1.84B at an 84% margin. The company bought back $1.4B of stock during the quarter, and CEO Adam Foroughi said he believes this business can compound at roughly 30% annually over the long term. At about 38 times earnings, AppLovin trades at a far lower multiple than Palantir, and shares are up 46.53% over the past month but down 42.13% year to date.

Earlier this year, Druckenmiller said AI-linked stocks looked disturbingly heated. In a Morgan Stanley interview, he summed up the market's view that the consensus for AI is that it will be very deflationary and lead to massive job losses. The pattern points to a preference for companies that sell AI-driven results through software, ads and connectivity, with less exposure to the chip spending cycle. AMD now trades near 191 times earnings and Alphabet's spending turned free cash flow negative. Palantir's stock trades near 228 times earnings.

Four signals to track include whether AMD delivers its roughly $17B fourth-quarter revenue target as its Helios server racks scale up. Another is Palantir's fourth-quarter revenue against its $2.649, $2.653 billion guidance, and whether contract value starts growing faster. The next 13F will show whether Druckenmiller kept, added to, or cut these positions. The filing does not show his sale prices or exact trade dates.

stories.Headline: AT&T COO Jeff McElfresh says agentic AI agents are reversing internet traffic toward uploads
stories.Summary:
AT&T chief operating officer Jeff McElfresh said at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum in Detroit on Monday, November 16, 2026, that the direction of internet bandwidth is undergoing a fundamental shift, because agentic AI agents tap the network around the clock rather than in the episodic patterns created by people watching video. U.S. household upload traffic grew 19.2% year over year in the second quarter, more than three times as fast as downloads, which grew 6.1%, according to OpenVault, which tracks broadband usage for internet providers. The average subscriber now uploads 58.2 GB a month, and while households still download about 11 times as much as they upload, that ratio was 16.6 times in 2019. McElfresh, who has been at AT&T for 31 years, said watching traffic from the network's control center used to be easy to read, with clear patterns like Netflix and YouTube traffic and traffic leaving cities for the suburbs at the start of the pandemic, when many work-from-home networks struggled and video calls glitched. He pointed to an autonomous vehicle connected to AT&T's wireless network that transmits more data up into the cloud to train a model than it consumes.

Mobile operators are seeing a similar shift, since in 2025, 43 of 55 service providers tracked by Ericsson saw uplink traffic grow faster than downlink, according to its June Mobility Report. Ericsson's scenarios have uplink traffic tripling or quintupling by 2031 if AI apps, smart glasses and agents take off, though it says mobile traffic is still expected to remain downlink-dominated in the near term and warns operators that current networks are not dimensioned for sustained uplink demand. Nokia's 2026 network traffic report forecasts that AI will drive 44% of global network traffic by 2035, and that for physical AI such as robots, cars and drones, more than 90% of traffic will start in the uplink, with Nokia writing that AI is challenging the asymmetric design of traditional access networks. AT&T has a business reason to tell this story, because fiber carries traffic equally fast in both directions while cable broadband, its main home-internet rival, has historically offered much slower uploads than downloads. McElfresh called fiber the gold standard, saying it is future proof and has all of the symmetrical capabilities to be very responsive to the AI future.

AT&T plans to reach 60 million fiber locations by 2030, about 1.5 times its footprint, and signed a supply deal with Corning worth more than $3 billion in September. OpenVault's numbers give AT&T something to point to, since fiber subscribers uploaded an average of 94.1 GB a month in the second quarter against 58.2 GB on cable's DOCSIS networks, though OpenVault CEO Mark Trudeau told Light Reading in October that he attributes the upstream growth to gaming, Zoom and Teams calls and a lot of AI content creation, and cable companies are also rolling out DOCSIS 4.0, which supports symmetric speeds. Corning CEO Wendell Weeks, who shared the stage, said customers will feel the shift at home through the combination of the bandwidth delivered and the type of products AI will enable, from robots to how people use their devices. Weeks said the next frontier is inside the data center itself, where copper wiring will give way to fiber, converting signals to light within a centimeter of the processor. McElfresh said AT&T technicians are installing fiber in 10,000 neighborhoods on any given day, adding roughly 4 million locations this year, toward the company's target of 60 million by 2030, while Ericsson's forecast window runs to 2031.

stories.Headline: H2O.ai launches TimeH2O and TabH2O foundation models for time-series and tabular data
stories.Summary:
H2O.ai launched the next version of its Predictive AI capabilities on November 17, 2026, adding two new foundation models, TimeH2O for time-series data and TabH2O for tabular data, both generally available on H2O AI Cloud. The company is based in Mountain View, California, and describes itself as the trusted Sovereign AI Platform with software and expertise to run predictive, generative, and agentic AI in production. TimeH2O-v1 ranked first among 32 models on the fev-bench forecasting leaderboard as of October 23, 2026, without training on any fev-bench dataset. The release was announced through Business Wire, and the article carries a timestamp of Tue, November 17, 2026 at 11:28 AM CST. The article states that most of the decisions that run an organization live in time-series and tabular data: demand, inventory, cash flow, risk, and fraud.

TimeH2O is a 108-million-parameter time-series foundation model that forecasts zero-shot, predicting on data it has never seen with no model to build for each series. On fev-bench as of October 23, 2026, TimeH2O-v1 ranked first of 32 models with a 91.9% win rate, ahead of Timestral-209M at 89.6%, t0-gamma at 88.1%, Google's TimesFM-3, and Amazon's Chronos-2. It posted a 50.8% skill score across 100 forecasting tasks and never trained on any fev-bench dataset. It also posted the lowest aggregate MASE of 0.654 and CRPS of 0.441 among zero-shot models on Salesforce's GIFT-Eval leaderboard as of October 24, 2026. Organizations can fine-tune it on their own data for demand forecasting, inventory, financial planning, energy load, and healthcare resource planning, while TabH2O does the same for structured business data: risk scoring, fraud detection, and customer analytics.

Sri Ambati, CEO and Founder of H2O.ai, said that lifecycles of all customers, businesses, economies and people are time-series, and that transforming enterprises with prediction is the super power of AI with high ROI. He said TimeH2O is the foundation model that ushers the ChatGPT moment for predictions, bringing predictive super powers to the finger tips of business users and consumers. He said every agent fighting fraud, hedging capital markets, dynamically pricing products, managing inventory and supply chain or moving cash is acting on a forecast that will now be powered by TimeH2O, which is entirely pre-trained on synthetic and public datasets so customers can own the models and further fine-tune on their local data. He said TimeH2O and TabH2O are small enough that they are expected to be embedded into applications, agents and physical AI running where their action is happening and where data lives, instead of renting a frontier model by the token. The article states that both models join H2O Driverless AI, an AutoML tool, in H2O.ai's Predictive AI capabilities.

H2O MLOps, a model deployment and monitoring tool, takes TimeH2O and TabH2O into production on H2O AI Cloud, where organizations can fine-tune on their own data and adapt the models to their industry, datasets, and business. Organizations can deploy, monitor, and govern, managing the full model lifecycle in production with observability and audit built in, and run them where they choose. H2O AI Cloud is available as H2O AI Managed Cloud, which H2O.ai operates, as H2O AI Hybrid Cloud, a private cloud the customer operates in its own cloud, on-premises or air-gapped, or as H2O AI Cloud for Government, which is FedRAMP High certified. An agent managing inventory needs an accurate demand forecast, a finance agent needs to anticipate cash, and an operations agent needs to predict workloads and disruptions, and TimeH2O and TabH2O supply those forecasts. H2O AI Super Agent, the orchestration layer at the core of H2O AI Cloud, brings predictive, generative, and agentic AI together in one system.

TimeH2O and TabH2O are generally available now on H2O AI Cloud for production use and fine-tuning on an organization's own data. TimeH2O-v1's open weights remain on Hugging Face for research and evaluation under the H2O Model Non-Commercial License, and production use requires a license from H2O.ai. H2O.ai is holding a virtual panel on December 3 with the Kaggle Grandmasters behind TimeH2O. The article states that H2O.ai created the industry's trusted Sovereign AI Platform because organizations should own their AI: their agents, models, data, and results, run anywhere from cloud to air-gapped. It states that Super Agent orchestrates predictive, generative, and agentic AI in one system, with observability and governance, empowering regulated and public sector organizations to get value from AI.

The article states that moving from pilot to production takes expertise, from top-ranked data scientists, including Kaggle Grandmasters, to forward-deployed engineers embedded with customer teams. It states that H2O.ai is built on a decade of open source and is trusted by 20,000+ organizations, half the Fortune 500. It names AT&T, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, Workday, Progressive Insurance, and NIH as organizations that rely on H2O.ai to cut cost and risk and own their AI future. It states that through its AI for Good program, H2O.ai applies technology and investment to non-profits and academia solving hard problems in health, education, and the environment. The article gives full benchmark results at https://h2oai.github.io/benchmarks and lists Bruna Smith as media contact.

stories.Headline: Psychiatrist Cheng-Ta Li creates AI platform to assess treatment-resistant depression
stories.Summary:
Psychiatrist Cheng-Ta Li created an artificial intelligence platform to evaluate severe depression. He developed this tool to precisely assess patients with treatment-resistant depression. The news of this development was published on November 17, 2026. Dr. Li directs the Precision Depression Intervention Center at Taipei Veterans General Hospital. He also holds an appointment at the National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University School of Medicine.

The AI-PreDIC platform combines clinical information with biological measurements like EEG and FDG-PET brain imaging. This patented tool provides objective estimates of depression severity and how stubbornly it resists treatment. The Precision Depression Intervention Center opened in June 2022 as Taiwan's first center for this purpose. It has already provided clinical services for more than 20,000 treatment-resistant depression patient visits. Dr. Li views resistance as a road rather than a simple yes-or-no label.

Dr. Li stated that the key question is which treatment helps a particular patient at a particular stage. He believes that findings should be judged by evidence strength rather than where they were published. He expressed a fear of patients trusting unproven treatments and missing opportunities for appropriate care. Dr. Li also noted that he wishes he understood mental health better while his grandmother lived. He maintains a motto to stay curious, question beliefs, and persist in what matters.

Patients with severe depression who failed conventional treatment for years are affected by this work. Dr. Li's 2024 JAMA Psychiatry analysis showed that treatment-resistant depression often runs in families. First-degree relatives of these patients were 9.16 times more likely to receive the same diagnosis. This study used national health insurance data for all of Taiwan to reach its conclusion. The research emphasizes that biological adaptation may push a patient further along the resistance continuum.

Dr. Li began his career in Taichung and later trained in functional neuroimaging. He earned a PhD under Professor Jen-Chuen Hsieh and Professor Tung-Ping Su at the Institute of Brain Science. He completed a fellowship with Professor Robert Innis at the U.S. National Institute of Mental Health. His 2014 study in the journal Brain tested theta-burst stimulation for refractory depression. He also helped bring repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation toward regulatory approval for depression in Taiwan.

Dr. Li is now developing new treatments using brain stimulation and emerging approaches such as psychedelics. He wants to share knowledge through books, public lectures, social media, and AI-based mental health chatbots. He serves as a Councilor of the International College of Neuropsychopharmacology and founded the Taiwanese Society of Brain Stimulation. That society held its first annual meeting in August 2026 to discuss these advancements. The articles leave open how these new treatments and chatbots will be implemented.

stories.Headline: Ambience Healthcare adds rounding and discharge AI tools for hospitals
stories.Summary:
Ambience Healthcare announced on Tuesday that it has added two AI tools, Rounding Assistant and Discharge Readiness, to its hospital software, which already writes clinical notes and suggests billing codes for hospital stays. Rounding Assistant pulls together overnight events, changes in a patient's condition and a list of suggested tasks for each shift. Discharge Readiness flags medical, practical and social problems that could delay a patient going home, earlier in the stay. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Kleiner Perkins and the OpenAI Startup Fund, and it counts Cleveland Clinic and Mayo Clinic among its customers.

Much of the company's pitch is about money, because Ambience aims to raise hospitals' case mix index, a measure of how sick patients are that helps set what insurers pay. At Onvida Health, discharges handled with Ambience scored 6.5% higher than a year earlier, according to the company. Mike Lewis, chief financial officer of Onvida Medical Group, said Onvida needed roughly a 1.5% improvement in case mix index to justify the investment, and he said Onvida's own finance team checked the results. Ambience also says admission notes written with its tool captured 59% more of the diagnoses used in quality rankings, in one health system's review of 1,100 stays. None of the figures come from independent research.

Ambience ties its fees to results, and Lewis said the improvement was needed to justify the investment, with Onvida's finance team checking the figures. The company says its tools help care teams prioritise tasks and spot barriers to discharge earlier. AI note tools are still under scrutiny, because in August England's patient watchdog warned that AI scribes were getting drug names and diagnoses wrong. Rivals are growing fast too, with Heidi raising $340M in September and Google launching Gemini for healthcare last week.

stories.Headline: NASCIO report finds 46 states have named AI leaders but many lack staffing and policy authority
stories.Summary:
State governments have rapidly created dedicated leadership roles to oversee artificial intelligence, but many of those officials lack the staffing, funding and authority needed to manage the technology across agencies, according to a report the National Association of State Chief Information Officers published on Tuesday, November 17, 2026. The report surveyed 33 states and territories to examine how governments are organizing AI leadership, developing governance policies and preparing employees to use the technology. NASCIO said that when it began tracking in 2023, less than 20 percent of states had a chief artificial intelligence officer or a similar title, and that just three years later at least 46 states have identified at least one person tasked with directing AI, with 25 states having someone with AI in their title. According to the report, 76 percent of survey respondents said they were the first person to hold their role as currently defined in their state, and most positions were established through a directive from the state CIO rather than legislation or an executive order.

The report found that AI leadership does not always come with the authority to set or enforce statewide policies, since while 72 percent of respondents said they have jurisdiction over all executive branch agencies, only 44 percent have the authority to independently establish enterprise AI policies and standards, another 16 percent share that responsibility with another entity, and just over half said they have the power to enforce compliance. Ninety-seven percent of respondents said their states have developed AI policies or guidance, 83 percent have created processes for agencies to submit proposed AI use cases for review, and roughly 75 percent cited the National Institute of Standards and Technology's AI Risk Management Framework, released in 2023, as their most commonly used governance model. Fifty-six percent of respondents said their states do not have dedicated AI budgets, and 75 percent identified insufficient staffing as one of their biggest challenges. The report also noted that Washington, D.C. became the first major U.S. city to mandate AI training for all employees and contractors in February, New York expanded its AI training resources to its entire workforce of more than 100,000 employees in April, and San José, California has trained over 1,000 municipal employees since 2024.

NASCIO recommended that states give AI leaders clearly defined authority, invest in dedicated staffing and sustainable funding, strengthen collaboration among technology, privacy and cybersecurity teams, and expand employee training, stating that full authority to establish and enforce enterprise AI standards would reduce agency and staff burden, increase interagency cooperation and unify agencies in the state. The report's findings build on NASCIO's 2026 State CIO Survey, which found that 78 percent of state CIOs now have an AI governance framework, up from 65 percent in 2025, and that AI ranked as the top technology priority among state CIOs for the first time this year. Looking ahead, 90 percent of respondents said agentic AI, which can complete tasks and take actions with less human involvement, would consume significantly more of their time over the next three years, with workforce transformation and scaling AI across agencies also major anticipated priorities. The report concluded that with the right foundation, states can navigate the evolving risks and challenges of AI while harnessing its potential to improve government operations and the services they provide to the public.

Articles.Title: As states move quickly to govern AI, dedicated oversight remains a challenge - StateScoop

stories.Headline: European data protection authorities examine AI candidate screening in 2027 enforcement action
stories.Summary:
Europe's data protection authorities will spend part of 2027 examining how organisations use automated tools, including AI systems, to screen job candidates. The European Data Protection Board said on November 11, 2026 that the topic of its sixth coordinated enforcement action will be automated decision-making in recruitment. The same plenary in Brussels produced two other outputs. The board adopted Statement 2/2026 on the first review of the European Union's adequacy decision for the Republic of Korea, dated November 10, 2026. It approved the final version of its recommendations on processor binding corporate rules, known as BCR-P, after a public consultation that closed in March.

The action will concern automated decision-making, including AI-driven ADM, in recruitment, according to the EDPB. More specifically, it will focus on enforcement of the right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing and the related right of access, in the context of automated candidate screening tools, including AI-driven ones. DPAs will join this action on a voluntary basis in the coming weeks, and the action itself will be launched in the course of 2027, according to the EDPB. The board did not say which authorities proposed the topic, how many have already committed, whether the action will use questionnaires or formal investigations, or whether it will target employers, recruitment agencies, software vendors or all three. The wording is narrow, concerning screening and two specific rights attached to that stage, rather than AI in employment generally or the management of existing staff.

The Coordinated Enforcement Framework was developed as part of the EDPB's 2021-2023 strategy, according to the board's CEF page. Every year, EDPB members submit proposals for the topic of the next annual action, and all EDPB members vote on the topic at a plenary meeting. National data protection authorities decide whether to take part, on a voluntary basis, through fact-finding exercises, new formal investigations, follow-up of ongoing formal investigations, or a combination. The authority that proposed the topic coordinates the action with assistance from the EDPB Secretariat, and a questionnaire or audit guide is built. All participating authorities launch the action at the same time, each drafts a national report, and the coordinators then produce an EDPB report adopted at a plenary.

The 2027 action will be the sixth. The first covered use of cloud-based services by the public sector in 2022, the second the designation and position of data protection officers in 2023, the third implementation of the right of access by controllers in 2024, and the fourth implementation of the right to erasure by controllers in 2025. The fifth, compliance with transparency and information obligations under Articles 12, 13 and 14 GDPR, was selected on October 14, 2025, with a launch during 2026. The right to erasure action involved 32 data protection authorities and 764 controllers that responded, according to PPC Land's coverage of the EDPB annual report, and its February 2026 report closed with non-binding recommendations. France's CNIL later fined consulting firm EXTIA 300,000 euros after an inspection carried out within that same coordinated action, finding that 204 of 265 deletion requests received in 2024 were not processed, not answered, or answered months late, in a deliberation adopted on July 21, 2026 and published on September 9, 2026.

The EDPB gave no reasons for its choice. On August 21, 2026, the Dutch Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens fined Uber 824,990,000 euros after finding that software had deactivated driver accounts from 2018 to 2022 following fraud flags or persistently low ratings, with no human review, and Uber has appealed. Spain's Royal Decree 723/2026, in force since October 5, 2026, requires employers to tell staff in writing about workplace algorithms that affect pay, hours, tasks, promotion, place of work or termination. The Spanish data protection authority, the AEPD, issued a warning, reference AI-00009-2026, over a resume-screening tool that had not yet been deployed, finding that the formal presence of a person in the process did not by itself take the decision outside Article 22. Austria's Federal Administrative Court ruled in September 2025 that the public employment service's AMAS job-seeker classification system did not breach Article 22, because advisers could override the score, while Germany's Federal Court of Justice, on October 21, 2026, held in four SCHUFA judgments that calculating a probability value about a person can itself be a decision under Article 22(1).

Under the provisional agreement reached on May 7, 2026, Annex III high-risk systems, a category that includes employment screening, must comply by December 2, 2027, so the GDPR coordinated action will run in the same year that AI Act obligations for hiring systems are due to take effect. California approved SB 947 on September 30, 2026, which bars employers from relying solely on an automated decision system for discipline or termination from July 1, 2027, and in the United States the Mobley v. Workday case was expanded in July 2025 to cover applicants processed through HiredScore AI features. On December 17, 2021, the European Commission adopted Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/254, which found that the Republic of Korea ensures an adequate level of protection. The CEF page does not label the dates it shows, but they match the publication of each action's final report, and on that pattern a report on recruitment screening would arrive no earlier than late 2027 and more likely in 2028, although the EDPB has given no date.

stories.Headline: Supermicro cofounder Yi-Shyan Liaw seeks to dismiss US charges for diverting AI chips to China
stories.Summary:
Yi-Shyan Liaw, who co-founded the company known as Supermicro, filed a motion to dismiss criminal charges on November 16, 2026. The United States government alleges that this individual diverted servers containing artificial intelligence technology from Nvidia to China. This legal action seeks to end the prosecution before the case proceeds further in the court system. The defendant argues that the government has not successfully stated a valid criminal offense in its filings.

The motion requires the court to determine if the current venue for the trial is improper for this specific case. It also asks the judge to evaluate whether the prosecution provided enough evidence to support the charges of chip diversion. The legal challenge focuses on the specific details regarding the movement of Nvidia technology into Chinese territory. No other specific dates or numbers were provided in the official statement regarding the diversion of these servers.

The legal team for Yi-Shyan Liaw is responsible for presenting these arguments to the presiding judge. They claim that the government failed to properly state an offense that would justify the ongoing criminal proceedings. The defense maintains that the location of the trial is incorrect and should be changed or dismissed entirely. These representatives are attempting to prove that the prosecution lacks the necessary legal grounds to continue the case.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: New Florida Legislative Leaders Pledge Property Tax Relief, AI Oversight After Election Certification
stories.Summary:
Florida’s new legislative leaders took the gavel on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, after state election officials formally certified the November election results, and both chambers unanimously chose their presiding officers in Tallahassee. The House elected Clay County Republican Sam Garrison as Speaker, and the Senate elected Manatee County Republican Jim Boyd as Senate President. Governor-elect Byron Donalds attended the swearing-in ceremony ahead of his inauguration in January. The organizational session coincided with the Elections Canvassing Commission certifying the general election outcomes. Certified results confirmed victories for Donalds in the governor’s race, Republicans in every state Cabinet race, and Ashley Moody in the U.S. Senate race, while Democrats won majorities in both chambers of the U.S. Congress and Republicans retained control of Florida’s statewide offices and legislative branches.

At the center of the upcoming work is Amendment 3, a constitutional amendment approved by nearly 62 percent of Florida voters, which raises the state’s non-school homestead exemption to $150,000 next year and to $250,000 in 2028. Boyd said lawmakers will establish a framework allowing local governments to provide additional property tax relief, and he said the Senate will keep working to expand choices and lower rates in the property insurance market while keeping education and workforce training aligned with available jobs. Garrison called Amendment 3 both the single most transformative property tax reform in state history and the biggest fiscal challenge Florida has faced in a generation, and he cautioned that offsetting the lost local and state revenue across counties from Dixie to Duval and Miami-Dade will take time. He said his priorities as Speaker are a strong economy, safe streets, and quality schools, and he announced a new Advanced Technology and Digital Security Committee plus a reinstated House Public Integrity Committee. Criticizing Congress for failing to pass federal regulations on artificial intelligence, Garrison said it is time for Florida to lead on the issue.

Republicans maintained a 20-to-8 majority in Florida’s congressional delegation, a 25-member majority in the state Senate, and a 70-to-50 majority in the state House. Boyd framed the Amendment 3 vote as a directive from residents struggling with the cost of housing, utilities, fuel, childcare, and groceries, saying families have made hard adjustments and expect government to do the same. Garrison, describing himself as someone who never met a tax he didn’t want to cut, said the laws of economics remain undefeated and there is still no such thing as a free lunch, adding that failure is not an option. Both leaders signaled close cooperation with the incoming executive branch as Governor Ron DeSantis prepares to leave office, and Garrison said it is his responsibility to help make Donalds the most successful governor in the United States. Lawmakers return to Tallahassee when the regular legislative session begins on March 2.

stories.Headline: Unesco and CodeAI host an online AI workshop for Latin American teachers on 19 November 2026
stories.Summary:
The UNESCO Regional Office in Santiago and CodeAI will host an online workshop for educators on Thursday, 19 November 2026. This virtual event, titled Teachers, Dive into AI!, will run from 4:00 to 5:30 p.m. Chile time via Zoom. It is designed specifically for primary and secondary school teachers and education professionals throughout Latin America and the Caribbean. Participants will engage in a hands-on experience to learn about artificial intelligence and how to bring it into their classrooms.

The session requires prior registration and will be conducted entirely in Spanish for all participants. It focuses on the AI for Oceans activity from CodeAI, where teachers train a machine learning model by classifying images of fish and marine waste. This process allows educators to observe how systems make decisions and identify potential errors or biases without needing prior programming knowledge. The workshop aligns with the UNESCO AI competency framework for teachers to promote a human-centred and ethical pedagogical approach.

The organizers are responsible for providing teaching resources and guidance on adapting these activities to various educational levels and subjects. They stated that the goal is to help teachers replicate these experiences with their own students during Hour of AI activities in December 2026. This initiative seeks to strengthen digital competencies and foster a critical understanding of responsible technology integration. stories.Headline: Nvidia stops reporting Singapore unit revenue in 2025 after it reaches $104bn, nearly half of global sales
stories.Summary:
Nvidia stopped reporting revenue for its Singapore unit in 2025, according to documents cited by the Financial Times, after that unit accounted for nearly 50% of the company's global revenue. The Singapore unit's revenue rose 72% year on year to $104bn in 2025, the documents show. The disclosure change came as the unit grew to represent almost half of Nvidia's worldwide sales. The Financial Times reported the details on Tuesday, November 17, 2026.

The documents indicate that the Singapore unit's revenue reached $104bn in 2025, a 72% increase from the prior year. That figure represented nearly 50% of Nvidia's global revenue for the year, according to the same documents. Nvidia stopped disclosing the unit's sales in 2025, the Financial Times reported, meaning the breakdown is no longer part of its regular reporting. The report does not say why the company made the change.

The Financial Times is the source of the report, which is based on documents it reviewed rather than on statements from Nvidia. The article does not include any comment from Nvidia or from company executives about the decision to stop reporting the Singapore unit's revenue. No explanation is given in the available material for why the disclosure ended in 2025. The report also does not say whether the company plans to resume reporting the figure.

The available article is a subscription page and does not provide further context on what the change requires or what happens next. It does not say how the missing Singapore figures affect Nvidia's overall reporting or what regulators or investors have said about it. The report gives no indication of any response from Nvidia or from Singapore authorities. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Elastic launches private preview of nightshift AI SRE agent for observability investigations
stories.Summary:
Elastic announced on November 17, 2026, a private preview of Elastic nightshift AI SRE, an AI agent built into Elastic Observability that carries out investigations the way an engineer would and makes the work visible, according to a press release from Elasticsearch Corporation, the Tokyo-based subsidiary led by president Ken Otani. The agent continuously detects and investigates problems across the whole stack with full context, surfacing unknown issues that rule-based alerts would miss, and it tests several hypotheses about root causes in parallel against telemetry and other relevant context. It then gives engineers evidence-backed answers while showing its reasoning at each step, and once it identifies a likely root cause it proposes remediation, either by selecting existing workflows and preconfigured actions or by providing commands for engineers to run. Engineers can inspect every step of an investigation, including the queries the agent ran and the underlying data. The release cites an April 2026 NeuBird AI survey finding that 78 percent of companies reported at least one incident in the past year where there was no alert and users themselves were the first to notice the problem.

Elastic says context behind investigations is usually incomplete because telemetry is cut to save costs, knowledge is scattered across code, runbooks and Slack, and lessons from past incidents are lost, while standalone AI SRE tools reason over data they do not hold. Because each investigation draws on full context from cost-efficient telemetry storage, customers can keep everything rather than sample data for AI, and a knowledge graph links that telemetry to source code from GitHub repositories so the agent can identify the commit likely behind an exception. Records of investigations accumulate over time, so each resolved incident shortens the time needed for the next one, and the agent continuously evaluates the environment and all telemetry, correlating alerts, SLOs and anomalies into findings engineers should actually review. Shannon Kalvar, a senior research director at IDC, said named-role agents such as AI SRE are a first step toward AI-driven operations, and that these agents need access to broader context, especially across wide and heterogeneous environments, along with the ability to learn from their own actions while validating those actions against facts.

Baha Azarmi, general manager of observability at Elastic, said most observability agents get smarter only by collecting more data, whereas Elastic nightshift AI SRE gets smarter by closely observing how engineers conduct investigations and by verifying the results of its own work after incidents are closed, which keeps production running without unwanted token costs. The private preview is available starting today on Elastic Observability Serverless, and Elastic customers can use it free during the early access period. Elastic plans to broaden support for third-party tools and data stores and to publish a technical preview within the year, and customers who want the private preview can register online. The Japanese release is an abridged translation of an English release Elastic published on October 8, 2026, and Elastic, listed on the NYSE under ESTC, says its platform is used by thousands of companies including more than 75 percent of Fortune 100 firms.

stories.Headline: Cato Networks launches patented AgentSense to block harmful AI agent actions in real time
stories.Summary:
Cato Networks announced on November 17, 2026, a patented capability called Cato AgentSense from Cato AI Labs that continuously assesses AI agents in real time to protect the integrity of their decisions, actions and outputs as they operate autonomously. The company said the guardrail stops harmful agent actions before they execute, keeping enterprises in control as agents gain greater autonomy. AgentSense is integrated within the Cato platform and will be included at no additional charge within Cato AI Usage licenses. Cato also introduced the AgentSense Challenge, which invites the security community to attack an AI agent workflow protected by AgentSense and plant instructions aimed at steering it away from the user's intent, with the first three eligible participants to succeed each receiving $10,000 USD.

The capability rests on two detection methods. Untrusted Influence Detection traces how instructions and data influence an agent's behavior at runtime, and when it detects that untrusted content is steering the agent toward an unsafe action, it blocks that action before execution, providing protection against indirect prompt injection even when attacks do not match previously observed patterns. Instead of relying on static classifiers or known attack patterns, it separates trusted instructions from untrusted content inside the AI session and traces how untrusted content influences both behavior and outputs, which Cato describes as a one-of-its-kind layer of protection from zero-day vulnerabilities. Drift Detection will identify when agent actions depart from the original task or intent, evaluating as a workflow progresses whether actions still serve the intended objective and flagging steps that may be individually permitted but fall outside the given task.

Shlomo Kramer, CEO and co-founder of Cato Networks, said enterprises entrust agents with decisions that shape revenue, customer relationships and business continuity, so control over agent behavior has become as essential as financial controls. He said giving agents greater autonomy requires security that can intervene before their actions cause harm, and that the vision for AgentSense is to give enterprises confidence to put agents in charge of critical business processes while retaining control over how they operate. Nithin Reddy, vice president of cybersecurity at Dayforce, said scaling AI safely means having the ability to detect and stop actions that could put customers, data or business at risk. Itay Ravia, head of Cato AI Labs, cited DuneSlide, EchoLeak and CurXecute as notable prompt injection vulnerabilities that continue to make headlines, and said AgentSense helps preserve trust by tracing how untrusted content influences an agent's decisions and sensitive actions. Grace Trinidad, senior research director of AI Security and Trust at IDC, said organizations need to know their objectives fully and evaluate agentic actions in the context of the full workflow and the task the agent was authorized to perform.

Cato said AI agents continue to scale faster than the guardrails put in place to secure them, citing Gartner figures that 71% of organizations expect to deploy agentic AI within the next 12 months while only 21% currently have agentic AI governance capabilities in place. It said forecasts report that by 2028, ungoverned AI agent abuse will drive 25 percent of enterprise breaches. The company described a fundamental architectural weakness in which agents cannot reliably distinguish between trusted instructions and untrusted data they pick up as they work, letting attackers hide malicious instructions in emails, webpages, documents, tickets or tool responses, and said the combination of sensitive data access and action-taking tools turns prompt injection into a business risk. Cato said it will use participants' findings and feedback from the Challenge to evaluate and strengthen the capability.
