stories.Headline: Jina Yoon reports decision models cut PostHog LLM costs and latency
stories.Summary:
Jina Yoon published "Not Everything Needs an LLM" in the PostHog newsletter on November 9, 2026, and the post appeared at newsletter.posthog.com on November 17, 2026 at 06:00:00Z. The article describes how PostHog experimented with decision models such as Jev and brought several use cases into production. It says LLMs return free-form and overly confident prose, while decision models give a typed answer with a probability. The article gives examples such as whether hedgehogs are mammals, answered Yes at 0.99, and their conservation status, scored Least Concern at 0.77. Yoon writes that in a calibrated model, answers that score 0.8 are right about 80% of the time, and a score of 0.5 is a coin flip.

The article says decision models are up to 444.6x cheaper and 193.6x faster than frontier models, according to TypeSafe AI. In Replay Vision, each session summary goes through two yes/no questions, and narrow questions cut false flags to about a tenth of what a single question produced. If either question scores 0.4 or above, Gemini rewrites the summary without the personal info and it gets checked again, and in production 98.7% skip the LLM call entirely. A probability score of 0.85 still means about 150 wrong answers per 1,000 checks, and the PostHog in Slack bot only sends messages that pass both checks at 0.85 or above. Jev takes 64k tokens per request and 32k per question by default, and TypeSafe's opt-in header raises both to 262k but warns that long-context mode is slower and less accurate.

Yoon writes that the PII threshold was set low at 0.4 because a false positive only costs an extra LLM call, whereas a false negative stores personal data as clean. She says thresholds changed between v1 and v2 of the same model during Error Tracking experiments, so thresholds had to be configurable per PostHog project with the judge kept in shadow mode while recalibrating on hand-labeled data. Fernando on the growth team pushed early for a model-agnostic interface, and PostHog now has an internal AI gateway for swapping and testing models, including self-hosted ones. Jeeves, developed by PostHog's in-house AI research team, reasons before deciding when it is unsure and is now the default for any decision call at PostHog that doesn't name a model. Yoon says she expects the article to be obsolete in two months.

The article says GPT Luna is described as a light and very cheap model good for short answers, lookups, summaries and very small edits. On 20 test queries, reranking Replay Vision search results by the decision model's probability improved ranking quality by about 25%. Before embeddings were ready, a Highlights feed job sent up to 32 sessions and 12-38k tokens each, flooded the model server and blocked other products' calls for hours. Jev scored an AUC of 0.52 on ranking the internal PR review agent's findings with five noul questions, and the article says similar variations exist by other developers, like Kev. The article lists open roles including Technical Customer Success Manager for EMEA and the Americas, AI Research Engineer, Animator & Motion Graphics Designer, Product Manager for Observability, and Site Reliability Engineer for US Pacific Time.

The article says PostHog used to pick a visualization using deterministic rules, such as a date column, a number column and multiple rows meaning a line chart, two or more text columns plus a number meaning a heatmap, and any number column meaning a bar chart. Now a decision model looks at the SQL itself if the org opts in, and the first three rows of results, to suggest a better chart. The article says the original rules picked a basic aggregate line chart for a pageviews by browser query, while Jev chose a bar chart split by browser. It says decision models judge what is in front of them in a single pass, and multi-step reasoning should be left to LLMs. The article credits Jina Yoon as the author and says she expects the piece to be obsolete in two months.

The article says decision models can be used to gate expensive LLM calls, as model routers, for face-value checks, and in place of overqualified LLMs. It says the PostHog in Slack bot was recently updated so it can answer questions without being tagged, checking every message in a channel for whether it asks for information and whether PostHog could answer it. The article says the bot first checks whether a tagged message asked for a specific model, and otherwise one choice question picks the cheapest option likely to finish the task correctly on the first try. It says a failed run costs more than a smarter option. The article leaves open how thresholds should be tuned across tasks and models, and it does not say what PostHog will do next with Jeeves or the AI gateway.

stories.Headline: Abits signs nonbinding letter of intent to acquire Boston Solar for vertical AI infrastructure
stories.Summary:
Abits Group Inc. (Nasdaq:ABTS), a U.S.-focused digital infrastructure company based in Duff, Tennessee, announced on November 17, 2026, that it signed a nonbinding letter of intent to acquire 100% of The Boston Solar Company LLC. Boston Solar is an established solar energy company founded in 2011 and headquartered in Woburn, Massachusetts. The proposed acquisition would advance Abits' strategy to vertically integrate its energy and digital infrastructure operations. It would add solar engineering and installation capabilities to support planned artificial intelligence and high-performance computing infrastructure development. Boston Solar would also give Abits an established operating business and a presence in the New England solar energy market.

The letter of intent contemplates Abits acquiring 100% of Boston Solar's outstanding equity interests from SinglePoint and any other selling equity holders. Except for customary binding provisions including exclusivity and confidentiality, the letter of intent is nonbinding and does not establish the final purchase price or the form of consideration. Completion remains subject to satisfactory due diligence, execution of definitive agreements, required financing, corporate and third-party approvals and other closing conditions. Boston Solar has served more than 7,500 households across New England and completed commercial projects including the MGM Music Hall at Fenway in Boston. According to preliminary information from the seller's management, Boston Solar generated over $25.0 million in unaudited revenue in 2025 and approximately $11.5 million through Q3 2026, with an additional $16.0 million in contracted solar projects awaiting installation, figures subject to financial and contractual due diligence.

Stephen Faucetta, Chairman and CEO of Abits Group, said the strategy is to build a vertically integrated energy and digital infrastructure business with greater control over the power supply and infrastructure needed for AI and high-performance computing operations. He said Boston Solar would bring an established operating business and engineering and installation capabilities to help advance that strategy. He said Abits sees opportunities to leverage those capabilities in developing solar generation at future infrastructure sites while evaluating additional opportunities at its existing Tennessee facilities. He also said each acquisition should stand on its own financial merits, with the objective of acquiring businesses with attractive fundamentals and growth opportunities that can also strengthen the broader platform. If the acquisition is completed, Abits intends to retain Boston Solar's senior management team, subject to mutually acceptable agreements, and pursue opportunities to expand its residential and commercial operations.

According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, commercial electricity prices in New England averaged approximately 22.5 cents per kilowatt-hour in 2025, compared with approximately 13.4 cents nationally. Boston Solar has expanded its commercial operations, including relationships with regional solar project developers. Abits currently operates its wholly owned facility in Duff, Tennessee and a facility in Memphis under a third-party hosting arrangement, with approximately 24 megawatts of existing power capacity and the potential to expand to 34 MW. Subject to completion of the proposed acquisition, Abits intends to leverage Boston Solar's engineering and installation capabilities to evaluate solar generation projects at its existing facilities and future infrastructure development sites. Abits intends to evaluate the feasibility of deploying solar generation at these locations, taking into account available land, site requirements, utility agreements, electricity costs and potential returns on investment.

Abits is pursuing a strategy to develop infrastructure capable of supporting AI and HPC hosting operations, centered on increasing its ability to develop and manage the power generation and physical infrastructure required for energy-intensive computing applications. By combining power generation capabilities, solar development expertise and prospective data center operations, Abits aims to reduce its dependence on third-party energy providers where economically feasible and gain greater control over its operating costs. The Company has not entered into definitive AI or HPC hosting agreements. Abits plans to pursue its infrastructure development strategy in phases, aligning capital investment with technical feasibility, available financing and commercial opportunities. Through its U.S. subsidiary, Abit USA, Inc., the Company owns or operates infrastructure supporting energy-intensive computing applications, and Abits is evaluating opportunities to expand into artificial intelligence, high-performance computing and related digital infrastructure services.

Any solar development would remain subject to technical feasibility, site control, permitting, electrical integration, financing and other project requirements. There can be no assurance that a definitive agreement will be executed or that the transaction will be completed, or as to the timing or terms of any transaction. The forward-looking statements in the release are subject to risks including that definitive agreements may not be executed or the acquisition may not be completed, and the accuracy of unaudited financial and operating information regarding Boston Solar provided by the seller, which the Company has not independently verified. Other risks include the Company's ability to integrate Boston Solar and retain its management, employees and customers, and changes in federal, state and local solar incentives, tariffs and net metering policies. Risks also include restrictions under the Company's existing financing agreements, the ability to obtain required consents, financing and approvals, environmental and regulatory requirements, the availability and cost of electricity, cooling and connectivity, the Company's ability to secure customers and strategic partners, and additional capital requirements.

stories.Headline: Nvidia reports 103 percent revenue growth and agrees to acquire Hugging Face
stories.Summary:
Nvidia reported its financial results for the third quarter of fiscal 2027 on November 17, 2026. The company achieved revenue of 115.8 billion dollars for the period ending October 25, 2026. This total represents a 103 percent increase from the same quarter one year ago. Revenue grew 20 percent compared to the previous quarter of the current fiscal year. The company also announced that it has shipped the Vera Rubin NVL72 computing platform.

The third quarter Data Center revenue reached 107.6 billion dollars, which is a 110 percent yearly increase. GAAP gross margins were 74.8 percent, while non-GAAP gross margins reached 74.9 percent for the period. GAAP earnings per diluted share were 2.70 dollars, and non-GAAP earnings per diluted share were 2.68 dollars. The board approved a 150 billion dollar increase to share repurchases in September 2026 without expiration. A quarterly cash dividend of 0.25 dollars per share will be paid on December 23, 2026.

Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress stated that the company's momentum is real and powered by innovation. She noted that the Vera Rubin platform is off to an explosive start for the company. Kress added that the company roadmap remains on track and its ambition has never been greater. The company returned 28.1 billion dollars to shareholders through cash dividends and repurchased shares this quarter. Approximately 227.3 billion dollars remains under the current share repurchase authorization as of the quarter end.

Cloud providers like Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure are running Vera Rubin NVL72 racks. Partners including Cisco, Meta, and Visionbay are helping to advance the infrastructure for the Vera Rubin platform. AI natives such as OpenAI, Meta, and CoreWeave are building with Vera CPUs to support business needs. Mercedes-Benz and Volvo Cars expanded partnerships to advance safe automated driving using new development tools and frameworks. T-Mobile completed the first AI-RAN call on a commercial network through a partnership with Nokia.

Edge Computing revenue was 8.2 billion dollars, which is a 42 percent increase from a year ago. The company launched DLSS 5 in Hogwarts Legacy and NBA 2K27 for GeForce RTX 50 Series GPUs. Nvidia announced an agreement to acquire Hugging Face to make intelligence more open and accessible to users. The company collaborated with Australia to support a planned buildout of 2 gigawatts by 2027 for factories. New RTX Spark laptops are now shipping from brands including Dell, HP, Lenovo, ASUS, MSI, and Microsoft.

Nvidia expects fourth quarter revenue to be 130.0 billion dollars, plus or minus 3 percent, for the period. The company does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China in this upcoming fourth quarter outlook. Expected GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins for the next quarter are between 71.0 percent and 72.0 percent. Full year fiscal 2027 tax rates are expected to be between 16.0 percent and 18.0 percent overall. The articles leave open the specific timing for the completion of the Hugging Face acquisition process.

stories.Headline: CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) Lands Frost Radar Honor As New AI Agent Risks Rise
stories.Summary:
CrowdStrike Holdings was named a Visionary Leader in the 2026 Frost Radar AI Security Operations Centers report, which cited the company for its work on agentic security operations centers and AI driven security tooling. The company also introduced Agentic Adversary Emulation, an AI system designed to simulate autonomous attacker behavior against customer environments. In addition, CrowdStrike launched Agent Insider Threat Detection to monitor and flag risky or abusive actions by AI agents inside organizations. The recognition and the two new tools were reported on November 17, 2026, by Simply Wall St, which noted that the news fits the existing investor Narrative rather than rewriting it.

CrowdStrike is a US based cybersecurity provider that sells software to help organizations detect and respond to digital attacks across their systems, and it has a market value of about $229.0 billion. The Visionary Leader label lines up with the company pushing agent focused tools on top of its Falcon platform, alongside a Saudi sovereign cloud rollout, to press the idea that it can secure endpoints, cloud workloads, identities and AI agents from one place. Analysts already assume Guardian, SafeMind and related AI offerings contribute a large share of the targeted US$20 billion ARR, according to the article. Product launches that harden AI agents and expand Falcon's use cases support the platform and Flex model thesis, while keeping pressure on execution and margin delivery that the Narrative flags as risks.

The article says the key sign will be whether management starts breaking out higher ARR or module adoption from AI security, next generation SIEM and sovereign cloud customers over the next few reporting periods. Consistent commentary on Falcon Flex deals that bundle Agentic Adversary Emulation, Agent Insider Threat Detection and Saudi based deployments into larger subscriptions would show the product cycle is translating into revenue concentration rather than just headlines. stories.Summary:
Charles Schwab recently rolled out AI powered tools, expanded crypto trading to five tokens, upgraded trading platforms, and completed several variable rate bond offerings totaling US$3.0b to support its operations, according to an article by Al Bentley published on sg.finance.yahoo.com on 17 November 2026. The article says the mix of generative AI assistants, extended hours options trading, and side by side crypto and traditional investing indicates Schwab's focus on deeper client engagement and product breadth rather than headline pricing changes. It reports that Schwab launched a Model Context Protocol server that connects clients' AI platforms directly to account data. The article states that for active users, the ability to query portfolios, manage alerts, and prep trades through their own LLM could deepen stickiness across trading and advice products. It says the new generative AI tools span thinkorswim and Schwab.com.

The article says the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St projects US$36.3b revenue and US$15.0b earnings by 2029, resting on forecast yearly revenue growth of 10.3% and an earnings increase of about US$4.7b from US$10.3b today. It says the more functions get exposed through external AI interfaces, the more Schwab needs tight controls around security, fraud, and compliance, especially after past issues tied to client protection. It states that any high profile data or supervision misstep would cut straight across the growth story and legal risk side of the equation. The article says some bullish analysts focus on Charles Schwab's AI driven productivity gains as the real swing factor. It states that if client activity or asset growth softens while this build out continues, the cost base could feel heavy, and that if user adoption and trading usage remain healthy, these tools can help support the existing growth path. stories.Headline: CommBank releases CodeCheck to help Australian businesses find software vulnerabilities with AI
stories.Summary:
Commonwealth Bank of Australia launched a new cyber security tool and AI harness called CodeCheck on 17 November 2026, designed to help Australian businesses identify potential vulnerabilities in their online systems, and it is available for Australian businesses to download from that day. The launch came as global websites run by at least 178 major organisations were hit by a suspected malware attack overnight, with affected sites including Zoom, Equifax, CNN, Salesforce, Ikea and the BBC, and Vodafone Australia, ASOS, Levi's Australia and HSBC Australia also identified as compromised. The banking and finance industry was hit hardest in the attack, with 32 organisations affected across the globe, and according to reports the attackers exploited a flaw in Optimizely, a website-testing platform, then planted code designed to steal payment data, hijack crypto payments and target older iPhones. While the Australian arm of HSBC was hit in the alleged attack, CBA's website was not.

CodeCheck, developed by CBA security engineers, gives businesses an AI-enabled approach to software security that draws on the bank's own method, and it is specifically designed for businesses that write their own code using OpenAI's Codex and Anthropic's Claude Code. The tool will guide the AI through analysing code, investigating potential vulnerabilities and providing information to assist engineers assess each finding, and CBA said businesses can advise what information to share with the AI so it better understands the code and makes more appropriate assessments, though engineers remain responsible for reviewing the findings and determining what action is required. In 2025-26 the Australian Signals Directorate's Australian Cyber Security Centre proactively notified organisations of potential malicious threats and activity more than 4,400 times, an increase of 80 per cent on the previous year, according to the ASD's latest Annual Cyber Threat Report. The ASD said it expects AI-driven tools to compress significantly the window for vulnerability exploitation, which mostly occurs within two weeks of a patch or mitigation advice being released, and it has already found instances where some vulnerabilities were successfully exploited within 48 hours.

CommBank Chief Security Officer Nicola Nicol said cyber security is a shared challenge and strengthening Australia's cyber resilience requires everyone to play a part, and that as cyber criminals increasingly use AI, AI also needs to be put to work on the defensive side. Nicol said that with thousands of engineers working across systems powered by around 2.5 billion lines of code, the bank has seen first-hand how AI can help identify potential vulnerabilities earlier, that it built the capability to strengthen its own defences, and that by making CodeCheck freely available it wants to share what it has learned and help more Australian businesses use AI to strengthen theirs. ASD Director-General Abigail Bradshaw said AI tools are needed to help automate defences and stay ahead of AI-enabled attackers, and that accelerating the modernisation of Australia's technology and cyber security foundations is critical to protecting the systems relied on every day. Bradshaw said giving businesses practical ways to identify potential vulnerabilities earlier and build security into software from the outset supports that effort.

stories.Headline: UAE joins US and eight others in signing San Francisco Declaration on AI safety
stories.Summary:
On Monday, the UAE joined the US and eight other countries in signing the San Francisco Declaration, which commits them to protect sensitive technologies and the critical infrastructure that underpins artificial intelligence systems. The declaration also focuses on safeguarding supply chains, software and knowledge, and it serves as a reminder that AI development cannot be left to tech companies and markets alone. The UAE has been expanding its ambitions in this field, and the editorial argues that a multi-pronged and multinational approach to regulation will be essential. This approach, it says, should ensure that innovation, while crucial, does not get too far ahead of responsibility.

The UAE has made several other commitments, including signing the Children First Declaration at the annual Paris Peace Forum last week, which aims to protect minors from untested AI models. In 2024, it was invited to join 49 other countries in the Hiroshima AI Process Friends Group, which is tasked with promoting safe, secure and trustworthy AI. The country has also adopted key global governance and management frameworks as part of its domestic and international alignment on AI safety and risk management. The editorial says these commitments reflect the breadth of the challenge, because AI has implications for national security, economic resilience, privacy, education, child development and the integrity of public institutions, each requiring a different set of protections.

The urgency is reinforced by the extraordinary amounts of money being invested in the industry, including Anthropic's much-anticipated stock market debut this week at a valuation of between $1.3 trillion and $1.45 trillion. Anthropic's prospectus has acknowledged risks ranging from cyberattacks and biological weapons to the possibility of powerful systems escaping human control, while uncertainty surrounding Nvidia, a significant supplier of advanced AI chips, has exposed the volatility of the industry's financial exuberance. The editorial argues that regulation should be nuanced enough to encourage research and investment while establishing clear boundaries around high-risk applications, which means rigorous testing, independent safety assessments, protections for children and safeguards against cyber and biological threats. It points to Abu Dhabi's recent agreements with OpenAI as showing how adoption can be accompanied by traceability and human accountability, and it cites OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman saying during his visit to the capital earlier this month that there is no room for debate over human control of AI.

The editorial says the recent declarations in San Francisco and Paris are vital contributions to the global effort to establish shared principles, because neither AI's benefits nor its risks will be confined by national borders or single-nation regulations. It says the task now for the countries involved, and eventually the international community as a whole, is to turn such commitments into coherent rules and meaningful oversight.

Articles.Title: AI needs more than market forces to keep it safe

stories.Headline: UBS warns AI agents may disrupt internet business models as Ermotti outlines bank AI plans
stories.Summary:
UBS Group warned on 17 November 2026 that AI agents could materially disrupt the traditional internet business model that supports digital advertising and enterprise software revenues, and chief executive Sergio Ermotti laid out the bank's own AI plans at the same time. Those plans focus on product upgrades, efficiency gains and new client offerings tied to the technology, according to the article. Ermotti also flagged potential risks from U.S. political uncertainty as UBS evaluates how AI driven changes might affect broader economic conditions. The article describes UBS as a CHF118.4b wealth manager and bank in the capital markets industry, and it says the firm is using its global advisory and financing role to test how AI agents might alter client workflows, product delivery and demand for traditional internet based services.

The article ties the AI agent focus to UBS's wider effort to turn the Credit Suisse integration and heavy digital spend into a leaner, higher return wealth and banking platform. It says continued investment in AI tools and digital platforms already used by a large share of front office teams, alongside digital distribution channels in Asia, can improve adviser productivity and client experience. The article points to a CHF44.87 fair value for UBS Group and says the push speaks to the view that UBS can extract more value from its fee base through productivity gains and a lower cost per client. It also says the strategy sharpens the firm's advisory pitch versus peers such as Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan, particularly for clients seeking guidance on which internet and software models could face pressure.

The article names the flipside as well, saying that if AI agents significantly accelerate a shift away from eyeball-based internet models, fee pools in parts of asset management and digital distribution could become less predictable. It adds that tighter Swiss capital rules and U.S. political risk related to AI infrastructure buildouts increase execution risk for the technology-focused strategy. The article says the same AI story can appear either as a productivity upgrade or as a new layer of uncertainty, depending on which narrative investors already lean toward. It notes that its analysis does not cover who is steering those calls or how their pay aligns with investor interests, and it states the piece was produced with the assistance of AI automation based on data and analysis from Simply Wall St.

stories.Headline: LVMH media division and OpenAI sign strategic AI agreement to deploy ChatGPT Enterprise across 17 brands
stories.Summary:
LVMH Group's Media Division and OpenAI announced on 16 November 2026 in Paris that they signed a strategic agreement to support new uses of artificial intelligence across all the division's publications and to make their journalism more accessible through ChatGPT. The agreement covers deployment of OpenAI tools and ChatGPT Enterprise to teams across the media division, which will let them build AI applications tailored to their day-to-day work. The two sides said their shared ambition is to let teams experiment with and develop practical uses of AI that support journalism and high-quality reporting. The partnership also enhances the presence of the division's content in ChatGPT, which will provide summaries and excerpts in response to relevant user questions, identify sources and include direct links to the original articles. The division, known as Groupe Les Echos-Le Parisien, brings together 17 media brands including Les Echos, Le Parisien, Challenges, Paris Match, L'Opinion, Investir, L'Agefi, Historia, Capital Finance, Connaissance des Arts, Radio Classique, Mezzo and medici.tv.

It has 1,800 employees, nearly 700 of them journalists, and reaches more than 27 million people in France every month. Teams will be able to explore applications such as document research, document comparison and preliminary translation, with the stated goal of giving them more time for investigative reporting, analysis and reporting in the field. The partnership is described as a company-wide initiative that will extend across all the division's publications, with training tailored to each person's use cases to support the rollout. Michèle Benbunan, CEO of LVMH Group's Media Division, said the agreement will position the publications at the forefront of the media industry and that integrating AI will become an everyday asset for all its teams, adding that the division is delighted to work with a partner whose expertise and reputation are recognised worldwide. Emmanuel Marill, Managing Director for EMEA at OpenAI, said quality journalism depends on the people who investigate, verify facts and help audiences make sense of information, and that OpenAI wants to help put AI to work for everyone across the division while respecting editorial independence.

He said the aim is to help teams spend more time on what makes their journalism valuable, and that the partnership will give ChatGPT users access to high-quality journalism that keeps pace with the news. The announcement frames the deal around two pressures on the division's business: newsrooms gaining time for investigation and analysis, and personalisation, which the announcement calls a major priority in an increasingly crowded information landscape. It says AI is an essential tool for developing and delivering products and services that meet the needs of customers, readers and advertisers, helping to attract and retain them and grow revenue across the publications. The announcement also says the partnership will support the evolution of roles throughout the organisation by streamlining operations, improving efficiency and encouraging innovation and creativity. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the rollout and the training.

stories.Headline: Advancing computer-use agents for healthcare teams
stories.Summary:
OpenAI said on November 16, 2026 that it was sharing new results measuring model performance, safety and cost in clinical and administrative workflows, and that it was working with Abridge, Ambience, Cigna Healthcare and CVS Health. The company said computer-use agents carry out multi-step workflows by clicking, typing and moving between applications. OpenAI said healthcare teams, developers and individual clinicians can access these capabilities today through the OpenAI API, ChatGPT for Healthcare and ChatGPT for Clinicians. OpenAI said it built a demo using synthetic patient data in which a patient messages a clinician about lower back pain. OpenAI said the agent reviews visit notes, physical therapy records and prior imaging in the EHR, drafts an MRI order, an encounter note and a reply, then prepares a prior authorization request in the insurer's portal.

OpenAI said it evaluated GPT-6 Astra on tasks clinicians handle in their EHR inboxes, shaped by physician input. OpenAI said 99% of 325 reviewed tasks were rated safe, and physicians selected "very helpful" or "extremely helpful" in 93% of 646 assessments on a five-point scale. OpenAI said GPT-6 Astra earned 94.3% of available rubric points on HealthAdminBench, an independent benchmark from Stanford researchers, while GPT-6 Luna earned 91.8% despite costing 98% less at 8.5 cents per task. OpenAI said both models were evaluated at maximum reasoning effort. OpenAI said organizations can support HIPAA-compliant workflows, configure approvals and agent access, and record audit logs, and that organization data is not used to train OpenAI foundation models.

Lagan Khare, Executive Director of Engineering at CVS Health, said less time on administrative work means more time for care and that this is a win for teams and everyone served. Madhu Nutakki, CIO of Cigna Healthcare, said moving from concept to deployment in under eight weeks shows what is possible when AI, care management expertise and the right guardrails come together. Nutakki said it means getting better, more complete insights to case managers sooner so they can focus on supporting patients with personalized, compassionate care. OpenAI said CVS Health uses validation checks and human oversight, with screenshots and action records to verify actions and application state. OpenAI said data remains within CVS Health enterprise-controlled infrastructure, governed by their enterprise AI Governance team and established responsible AI policies, and that production data is not used to train foundation models.

OpenAI said CVS Health is using computer-use capabilities to automate repetitive work across clinical systems, including sending documents, processing referrals and supporting specialist consults. OpenAI said one production workflow cleared a months-long document-sending backlog over a weekend, and another handles the system steps for tens of thousands of consults each day. OpenAI said CVS Health is open sourcing its Agent Kit, built with OpenAI's Agents SDK. OpenAI said Abridge is developing computer-use agents for care plans across applications, including those without APIs, and that its planned inpatient use case builds on the clinical conversation. OpenAI said Cigna Healthcare case managers previously had to navigate more than 10 separate clinical and administrative systems to gather context, and computer use can now bring relevant information together in seconds.

OpenAI said healthcare is fragmented, and teams often need to move information between systems manually before a patient can get care. OpenAI said when a clinician recommends an MRI, the information an insurer needs may be in a patient's medical record, but a team member still needs to retrieve it and enter it into a separate portal to complete an authorization request. OpenAI said its partners build software used in hundreds of health systems, coordinate care for members globally, and deliver care to hundreds of millions of patients. OpenAI said Ambience built additional controls, and that in a demonstration the agent stops and asks the clinician when the record is ambiguous, then waits for approval before submitting. OpenAI said health systems set which actions the agent can take, can pause it at any point, and get a step-by-step log for audit.

OpenAI said healthcare organizations can contact its sales team, and existing customers can ask their workspace administrator to enable computer use in ChatGPT Work and Codex. OpenAI said U.S. clinicians can sign up for a free ChatGPT for Clinicians account today and experience computer use in ChatGPT Work and Codex. OpenAI said developers can build healthcare applications with the OpenAI API and explore its computer use guide. OpenAI said organizations must use eligible services covered by their Business Associate Agreement with OpenAI and the required security and retention settings to support HIPAA-compliant workflows involving protected health information. OpenAI said it hopes these advances enable healthcare teams to spend less time moving information through systems and more time caring for patients.

Articles.Title: Advancing computer-use agents for healthcare teams

stories.Headline: OpenAI gives £1m to The King’s Trust to help 25,000 young people build AI skills
stories.Summary:
The King’s Trust announced a major partnership with OpenAI on 16 November 2026, and OpenAI is making a £1m donation to the youth charity to support the work. The partnership is designed to help up to 25,000 young people across the UK build AI skills for work, prioritizing those not in education, employment or training. The program aims to support those young people over the next 18 months, helping them develop practical skills and confidence to move toward education and employment in an AI-enabled economy. The announcement comes as The King’s Trust marks its 50th year and looks to the future in an increasingly AI-enabled world.

The partnership forms part of a wider program of nationally recognized AI qualifications that The King’s Trust will launch in the coming months, designed to help young people stay ahead of a changing labor market. The program will combine opportunities to learn AI skills with recognized qualifications and practical experience, and The Trust is working with employers, AI specialists and young people on the skills needed. The Open University’s Business Barometer 2026 found that 68% of 16, 24-year-olds surveyed who were not in education, employment or training would be willing to train or upskill to improve their job prospects. The Trust says it has supported more than 1.3 million young people over 50 years and wants the next generation to gain the skills and confidence to thrive in an AI-enabled economy.

Jonathan Townsend, UK Chief Executive of The King’s Trust, said AI could create enormous opportunities for young people if they have the chance to develop the skills and confidence to use it. He said the partnership would help thousands of young people build practical AI skills, gain recognized qualifications and prepare for a rapidly changing world of work, and he thanked OpenAI for its support. Tom Duff Gordon, VP and Head EMEA Policy at OpenAI, said young people who are out of education or work deserve a real foothold in the AI economy. He said OpenAI is committing £1 million and its AI expertise to help reach up to 25,000 young people with practical skills, recognized learning and support toward education and employment.

The Rt Hon Alan Milburn welcomed the partnership ahead of the final report of the independent Young People and Work review, reflecting on a shared ambition to improve young people’s opportunities to learn and earn. He said young people deserve to be equipped for a changing world of work, and that AI will bring disruption as well as opportunity. He said it is vital that young people get a fair share of the opportunity and do not bear the cost of the disruption. For OpenAI, the partnership forms part of a broader commitment that builds on wider efforts including OpenAI Academy, which provides free learning resources for students, job-seekers and other learners.

Articles.Title: The King’s Trust and OpenAI launch £1m partnership

stories.Headline: Holiday Extras executives use personal AI dots to surface data and flag issues
stories.Summary:
Holiday Extras, a UK travel technology company that helps travelers book airport parking, hotels, lounges and transfers, published an OpenAI customer story on November 16, 2026 describing how two of its executives use personal AI assistants called dots. Liam Thompson, the company's VP of AI Innovation, named his dot Beast, and the day after Holiday Extras launched a new feature in its app, Beast noticed the launch without being asked, pulled data from Google BigQuery through a ChatGPT plugin and brought him the results. David Lee, Director of Innovation & Growth, named his dot Brian and calls him on his morning commute to talk through the meetings ahead and to request reports built from connected company data. When some API keys needed to be retired, Brian flagged the issue, went back through David's email and surfaced a list of people who might be affected. Liam said he talks with Beast for his morning and evening briefings and spends at least two hours a day in a voice conversation with him, and Beast reminds him about replies he has not sent and finds answers from past conversations.

Liam had tried two other assistants, OpenClaw and Hermes, but said he was not comfortable giving them much information, while with anything OpenAI in the company environment he knows he can trust it, and he gave Beast access to his Slack, inbox, Drive and laptop. Liam, who trained as a designer, also gave Beast access to After Effects and Rive on his laptop to animate 3D characters for an app, work he says would have taken him several days and that Beast did in about ten minutes. Holiday Extras gives employees ChatGPT Enterprise as a foundation for using AI and Codex to turn expertise into working software, with dots simplifying the work in between. David said that by the time he gets into the office and sits at his desk, the report is there and ready to go, and that what he likes most about Brian is that he is thinking about things David has not even thought about. Liam said it relaxes him having Beast there because if he misses something, Beast has probably already covered it and is keeping an eye on all the things going on.

Liam's advice for anyone getting started is simply to create a dot and start a conversation, adding that there is no excuse not to get started and to just go. For Holiday Extras, the next opportunity is to help more people put their dot to work, and David wants the people experimenting with dots to share what they are learning so others can see what is possible and try it for themselves. The company says the next idea could come from anyone, whether they start with preparing for a meeting, building something or making everyday life a little easier. That builds on the ambition behind the company's work with OpenAI, giving people across the business the confidence and tools to work differently and helping useful discoveries spread.

stories.Headline: Fei-Fei Li warns that high compute and data costs price public sector and universities out of frontier AI research
stories.Summary:
Stanford University Professor Fei-Fei Li warned on November 18, 2026, that public sector entities and academic institutions are being priced out of frontier artificial intelligence research. The co-director of the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI argued that the massive costs of compute and data are creating a divide in the research landscape. She noted that the scale of infrastructure needed to train foundation models now exceeds the traditional budget capacities of public research agencies. This shift follows a period of rapid progress led by well-funded private corporations that set the benchmarks for performance.

The current situation requires thousands of H100 or next-generation GPUs, which can cost hundreds of millions or even billions of dollars for top-tier training runs. Researchers also face the prohibitive cost of acquiring high-quality proprietary datasets that are dominated by private firms through vertical integration. Furthermore, private companies offer massive salary premiums that draw top talent away from academic labs and hollow out the research pipeline. These barriers force academic researchers to depend on private partnerships, which may create conflicts regarding transparency and the overall research agenda.

Fei-Fei Li stated that the centralization of AI research power is a core issue that threatens the objectivity of scientific inquiry. She suggested that the reliance on private sector partnerships could stifle long-term exploratory research and limit the role of academia. The Association of American Universities added that universities risk falling behind in critical technology without significant increases in federal funding for infrastructure. Other stakeholders have called for a National AI Research Resource in the United States to democratize access to necessary compute power.

This crisis is the culmination of several years of expansion where the field shifted toward massive foundation models. Academic labs were previously at the forefront of innovation, but capital requirements for compute infrastructure have since grown exponentially. Federal agencies and policy bodies are now debating the next phase of initiatives to address these critical access gaps. Reports and policy recommendations from the National Science Foundation and the OSTP are expected in the coming year to outline sustainable paths for academic access.

Articles.Title: Fei-Fei Li: Public Sector and Universities “Priced Out” of AI Research

stories.Headline: Vincee Cole compares ten AI training data vendors and names Surge AI the top pick for expert data
stories.Summary:
Vincee Cole published an overview of ten AI training data vendors on November 16, 2026. The author named Surge AI as the top pick for expert human data. This report compares various companies based on their services, public pricing, and long-term outlook. The analysis focuses on vendors that fit the needs of United States buyers. It uses official product pages, funding announcements, and buyer feedback for its research.

The report lists Surge AI, Scale AI, and Mercor as the best labs for frontier models. Labelbox offers a free tier and services starting at about eight dollars per hour. Prolific charges a 42.8 percent fee plus participant pay of at least eight dollars per hour. Bright Data sells web datasets starting from 250 dollars per 100,000 records. Mercor raised 750 million dollars at a 20 billion dollar valuation on November 10, 2026.

Vincee Cole stated that Surge AI is the best overall company because it focuses on expert data. The author noted that Labelbox is the stronger pick for enterprises wanting software and managed experts. Cole observed that only three of the ten vendors publish real price points for buyers. The report suggests that buyers should budget for a paid pilot before signing any contract. Cole believes expert data and agent training will stay in demand through 2028.

Frontier AI labs, government agencies, and large enterprises are the primary buyers for these data services. Scale AI works with the Pentagon, Mayo Clinic, and Time, as well as most leading model builders. OpenAI and Anthropic reportedly cited benchmarks from Surge AI in their 2026 model releases. Microsoft used human evaluations from Surge AI for its MAI-Thinking-1 model. Meta bought a 49 percent non-voting stake in Scale AI for about 14.3 billion dollars.

Demand has shifted from simple image labeling toward paid experts like doctors, lawyers, and engineers. Surge AI reported more than one billion dollars in revenue for 2024 according to Reuters. Scale AI told Forbes its revenue was 870 million dollars in 2024 and nearly one billion in 2025. TechCrunch reported in July 2026 that the run rate for Mercor had reached about two billion dollars. Mercor now maintains a network of more than five million experts for AI work.

The report expects demand for professional data to hold through 2028 as AI agents enter professional fields. Scale AI may evolve into a defense and enterprise contractor rather than a neutral data lab. Surge AI faces a risk of customer concentration because a few labs drive most of its revenue. The benchmarks created by Surge AI could potentially become a second business for the company. The articles leave open how other vendors will price their custom quotes.

stories.Headline: Apollo places six evaluators inside OpenAI for four months to assess whether training incentivizes subversion
stories.Summary:
Apollo Research announced on November 16, 2026 that six of its evaluators will work inside OpenAI for four months to investigate whether its models attempt to subvert alignment or control mechanisms during training, evaluations and internal deployment. The team will examine four questions, namely whether training incentivizes subversion, whether evaluations can elicit it, whether subversion occurs during internal deployment and whether reasoning relevant to subversion would be detectable. The scope covers attempts to undermine a model's own alignment or controls as well as those of its successors, and the arrangement is meant to move external scrutiny beyond Apollo's earlier approach of evaluating after post-training and shortly before public release. Apollo considers that timing insufficient for testing misaligned behavior such as scheming or for examining non-public uses during internal deployment, and it describes the pilot as an ambitious first step rather than a full embedded evaluation. For the training-incentives assessment, OpenAI committed to provide relevant training code and datasets, reinforcement-learning rollouts with available reasoning traces and rewards, and the ability to query intermediate model checkpoints, while detailed access arrangements for the other assessment claims remain to be agreed.

The assessment is confined to agreed claims, models and time periods, and OpenAI may withhold in-scope items when it deems that reasonably necessary because of technical infeasibility, security risks or intellectual-property protection, but it may not withhold information or staff access simply because the material is unfavorable. OpenAI must tell Apollo that withheld items exist and give written reasons, and where it considers this feasible and relevant it must identify withheld records by category and approximate volume, while Apollo can request broader access through a designated contact and escalate refusals without any guarantee of expansion. The evaluators will work on OpenAI hardware using separate channels that can be monitored, they will by default lack access to general staff channels such as Slack, and formal conversations must be logged, with Apollo required to stop substantive discussion and route follow-up through its contact if another employee raises confidential information. Apollo plans two public reports, the first on training incentives for subversion and the second on evaluations, internal deployment and the detectability of subversive reasoning, each describing methods, conclusions, limitations, questions that could not be assessed and supporting evidence that can be published. OpenAI will review the reports and may request redactions of confidential information including evidence supporting findings, but it may not redact Apollo's verdicts or request redactions merely because a finding is unfavorable, and it can redact evidence it considers sensitive intellectual property whether or not that evidence directly contributes to a finding.

OpenAI will share the unredacted reports with its board's Safety and Security Committee, and claims based on employee discussions require OpenAI's formal attestation unless Apollo establishes them independently, with Apollo allowed to disclose a declined attestation and explain its effect without revealing the underlying confidential information. Separate meta-transparency rights let Apollo describe publicly the engagement's scope and conditions, the access requested and received, material withheld or delayed and the reasons given, requested report removals and their significance, and any pressure it believed shaped its work, all without prior OpenAI review. Apollo regards those meta-transparency rights as a minimum standard for every evaluation engagement, arguing that undisclosed restrictions can make absent problems look reassuring even when the absence reflects limits on investigation or disclosure. The pilot's conclusions will therefore need to be read alongside its account of access and publication limits, since the same verdict can carry different weight depending on what the evaluators were able to inspect and disclose.

stories.Headline: MinoHealth AI Labs warns of bioweapons threat after model designs thousands of toxins
stories.Summary:
Researchers at MinoHealth AI Labs in Accra, Ghana, removed guardrails from their drug discovery AI model during 2024. They asked the system to design toxins, and the model produced designs for 5,000 small molecules and 1,020 proteins. Software predicting toxicity scored all these designs as likely toxic, with some resembling the deadly poison known as ricin. The team uploaded their findings to the preprint server arXiv in May 2025 to warn others about dual use.

The study used a general purpose LLM trained for biology and drug discovery, which differs from previous chemical weapon experiments. The researchers never physically made the toxins, but they questioned if DNA synthesis companies would stop someone from ordering them. Brenda Obuya of Kenya's Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy says Africa now needs to regulate DNA synthesis providers. The lab's Moremi Bio model also proposed hundreds of drug candidates for tuberculosis, dengue, and cancer.

Founder Darlington Akogo said he was shocked by the results and has since traveled the world warning of existential bioweapons threats. He discussed these risks with Bill Gates in 2023 and at the World Bank and IMF Spring Meetings last year. Akogo believes the United Nations should create a dedicated working group to study AI risks and implement tighter synthesis controls. He stated that his goal is to balance AI optimism with caution rather than simply scaring people.

Bill Gates warned in September that AI can now empower bioterrorists to kill hundreds of millions of people. Ken McCallum of MI5 stated that AI's potential to change the stakes for bioweapons is the greatest misuse risk. Adam Abdullahi noted that this Ghanaian study shows African institutions are contributing to the global governance of artificial intelligence. Ayantola Alayande warned that lay users might now generate such hazardous output via chatbots as models become more capable.

Akogo founded MinoHealth Labs in 2016 to solve Ghana's health worker shortage, and his team began Moremi AI in 2022. The Gates Foundation provided 149,533 dollars in 2023 to build a foundation model for analyzing medical images and designing drugs. Investment in AI powered drug discovery grew from 4.1 billion dollars in 2023 to 8.4 billion dollars in 2025. Anthropic launched Claude for Life Sciences in October 2025, and OpenAI launched GPT-Rosalind in April of the following year.

The International Gene Synthesis Consortium is working with developers to detect AI designed sequences that might be engineered to evade screening. Heads of Google DeepMind, OpenAI, and Anthropic called on U.S. lawmakers in June to make DNA sequence checks mandatory. Intelligence agencies are now setting up specialized desks to track threats at the intersection of biology and cyber defense. The articles leave open whether governments will successfully mandate screening across the entire nucleic acid supply chain.

Articles.Title: The small African lab sounding the alarm on AI bioweapons

stories.headline_source: The small African lab sounding the alarm on AI bioweapons

stories.Headline: Reese Cooper accuses SSENSE of using AI images that misrepresent his designs
stories.Summary:
Designer Reese Cooper criticized the Montreal retailer SSENSE on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, for using artificial intelligence to create product images. He shared a series of Instagram Story posts pointing out rendering errors and inconsistent garment details in the digital imagery. Cooper claimed that these AI generated visuals misrepresent his actual designs and create a disappointing experience for creators. He expressed concern that customers would blame his brand rather than the retailer when orders do not match the website. The designer also questioned the fate of the professional photographers and stylists who previously worked at the company.

This public dispute follows a series of corporate changes involving CEO Rami Atallah and his brothers, Firas and Bassel. In February, the Superior Court of Quebec authorized an agreement allowing the brothers to reclaim ownership of the business from creditor protection. During a company meeting in April, Atallah stated that the firm would embed AI into its DNA to transform core functions. By June, reports indicated that SSENSE had dismissed approximately a dozen creative staff members from the cosmetics, retouching, and photo departments. The company shifted its strategy to superimpose garment images from mannequins onto the images of professional models.

Chief commercial officer Christine Sio stated that the company is evolving its content production to increase scalability, agility, and speed. A spokesperson for the retailer further explained that the new studio operating model aims to accelerate production and strengthen product storytelling. These official statements contrast with the views of a former photographer who described the technical process of using AI for model imagery. Cooper argued that the resulting work is low quality and lacks the consistency provided by human oversight. He specifically noted that certain details, such as tape on a shirt, disappeared in the AI versions.

The retailer continues to implement these automated systems to replace traditional in house photography and retouching workflows. This transition has sparked a larger conversation about the role of human creativity in the fashion industry's digital presence. While the company views the shift as a necessary evolution for efficiency, designers like Cooper fear the loss of artistic integrity. The conflict highlights the tension between corporate cost cutting measures and the precise representation of luxury design. It remains unclear if the retailer will adjust its AI processes to satisfy the concerns of its brand partners.

Articles.Title: Reese Cooper Calls Out SSENSE Over Alleged AI-Generated Images Of His Designs

stories.Headline: Multilingual by Design awards $1.05m to three teams piloting AI tools for multilingual teaching
stories.Summary:
Multilingual by Design awarded three grants totaling $1.05 million to teams developing AI tools for multilingual teaching, the organization announced on 18 November 2026. Teams led by the University of Wisconsin-Madison, the Joan Ganz Cooney Center at Sesame Workshop and DSST Public Schools will each receive $350,000. Their pilots are planned for 2026, 27 and will involve teachers and schools in Wisconsin, Massachusetts and Colorado. The projects address following small-group math conversations, preparing accessible versions of existing materials and adapting math lessons to students' English proficiency. Teachers will decide how the tools are used, review their outputs and retain control of instruction.

The Wisconsin team is developing Content and Language with AI, or CLAI, to give teachers a live view of students' small-group math discussions. The project brings together The Responsible AI for Learning (TRAIL) Lab, the Multilingual Learning Research Center and the WIDA Consortium, all at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. CLAI builds on real-time transcription and translation and is designed to identify students' use of mathematical concepts, connections to experiences from home and moments when they may need help. Six teachers in rural, suburban and urban Wisconsin school districts will pilot the tool. Organizers say students will control their own audio recordings, which will be stored locally and remain under district control.

In Massachusetts, the Joan Ganz Cooney Center and Medley Learning will develop Medley Studio, a tool for adapting materials that teachers already use. The planned supports include dividing text into shorter sections and adding definitions within the material, with recommendations matched to students' language proficiency. Teachers will be able to review and customize those supports before exporting or printing materials. The pilot will focus on five schools in Taunton, aiming to reduce preparation time while maintaining access to grade-level instruction. Medley's existing product is a browser extension that adds vocabulary support, translation and other scaffolds to classroom content, and the funding announcement puts the company's existing reach at 12,000 students across 48 school systems.

In Colorado, DSST Public Schools and Scale Up Partners will develop Premo, which uses AI to help teachers plan and adapt grade-level math lessons. Premo is intended to align lessons with established English language development frameworks and suggest teaching strategies and supports matched to individual students' English proficiency. Testing will take place within DSST's network of 16 public middle and high schools in Denver and Aurora. According to the announcement, more than 65% of students across the network are current or former multilingual learners. The work focuses on helping students engage with math content while developing the language needed to discuss and understand it.

Throughline Learning, a Providence-based education nonprofit, will provide technical assistance and lead research across the pilots. Teams will use a common set of measures to examine how the tools work for teachers and students, with outcomes ranging from classroom discussion to student achievement. The initiative's partner information also identifies ETS as a research partner. Before testing begins, Throughline will help teams establish their intended outcomes and data plans, with findings later developed into case studies and public resources. Each team will pilot under data-sharing agreements with its partner schools, and alongside the grants, teams will receive coaching and support for bringing their tools to schools beyond the initial pilot sites.

Multilingual by Design launched in March 2026 and is managed by Social Strategy Associates. Its open call attracted more than 180 applications from education nonprofits and AI builders, and thirty organizations attended a June workshop in Washington, D.C., where teachers described challenges in supporting multilingual learners. The initiative is supported by the Bezos Family Foundation, Gary Community Ventures, the Gates Foundation, the Hewlett Foundation, the Robertson Foundation and Sobrato Philanthropies. National Center for Education Statistics data for 2020, 21 show that 67.3% of U.S. public school teachers taught at least one English learner. Multilingual by Design plans to share findings from the funded pilots with educators, developers and funders as the projects progress through development and classroom testing.

stories.Headline: Hark releases Handoff², a computer-use agent it says completes 82% of tasks 2x faster
stories.Summary:
Hark released Handoff², the second version of the computer-use agent inside its Hark Pro app, on November 12, 2026, according to MarkTechPost. The agent operates websites the way a person does by clicking, typing and scrolling on live pages instead of calling APIs, and Hark says it finishes web tasks about 2x faster than the original on average. Hark previewed the original Handoff in August 2026 and shipped it in Hark Pro in October 2026, and since then it says it has logged over 5.6 million browsing sessions and handled over $20 million in purchases. Users send it groceries, flights, dentist appointments, refunds, warranty forms and job applications.

Each request runs on a dedicated virtual computer in Hark's cloud with its own browser, file system and terminal, and users reach it from web, iOS and Android with no local or quantized option. On Hark's 478-task internal benchmark across 238 websites, Handoff² completes 82% of tasks, up from 73% for v1, and takes 46% less time per task. Hark says the gains come from reinforcement learning that penalized wasted turns and latency, and the new harness lets the model emit more actions per turn, batch actions such as filling several form fields in one turn, and group repeated action patterns into reusable composite actions. Hark reports long research tasks more than 5x faster, with a 10-minute task dropping to 3 minutes and a 45-minute task to about 10, and flight booking up to 3.8x faster. On Hark's internal alignment benchmark, which checks that the agent never checks out without approval and asks for clarification only when a request is truly ambiguous, Handoff² scores 93.8%, up from 90.3% for v1.

Hark states that the speed gains come from the reinforcement learning recipe that penalized excess turns, unnecessary thinking tokens and end-to-end latency, and it co-evolved the agent harness and the training recipe together. Hark ran Claude Opus 5.5 (max) in the same harness as Handoff², and Handoff² lands within 5 points of it, though 82% browsing completion still trails that model by up to 5 points. Every Handoff² number is self-reported and no third-party score exists yet, and Hark has not posted an Online-Mind2Web result for Handoff², while the original Handoff scores 97.67% on that public human-eval leaderboard against 97.3% for Yutori's Navigator n1.5. The article notes that v1 was measured in its original harness, not the new one, and it does not say what happens next.

Articles.Title: Hark Releases Handoff², a 2x Faster Computer-Use Agent for Hark Pro

stories.Headline: European AI fintech founders chase defensibility as early stage funding rises 40%
stories.Summary:
Funding rounds raised by early stage AI-native fintech startups are up 40%, as European companies pile into the financial services back office hoping to become category leaders, Sifted reported on 16 November 2026. The report said early stage AI-native fintech funding rounds had risen by that share, with European companies crowding into back office work for financial services. The article described the back office as a crowded field where startups are competing to become the category leaders in their niche. The report said the crowded market has pushed founders to build what rivals cannot easily copy, rather than compete on features that any competitor can replicate.

It said investors and founders now argue that defensibility comes from proprietary data, deep workflow integration and regulatory know-how rather than from a thin layer wrapped around a model. The article gave no further figures beyond the 40% rise in early stage AI-native fintech funding rounds. The article quoted a founder saying that companies should build what cannot be cloned, and that durable advantage comes from data, workflow and compliance rather than from the model itself. It also quoted an investor saying that many startups look similar on the surface, and that the winners will be those that own a piece of the workflow rather than rent one.

The article said responsibility for building that defensibility sits with founders, who must decide where to dig in rather than spread thin across the back office. The context is a back office that is getting crowded, with European startups piling into financial services work in the hope of becoming category leaders. The article said the next step for these companies is to prove they own something rivals cannot copy, whether data, workflow or regulatory expertise. It did not say which companies will succeed or what happens to those that fail to build that defensibility.

Articles.Title: ‘Build what can’t be cloned’: Fintech’s AI-native back office is getting crowded

stories.Headline: Puja Tayal suggests AI supply chain alternatives for investors following a decline in Nvidia stock
stories.Summary:
Puja Tayal wrote an article on November 17, 2026, about AI stocks for Canadians. She discussed how Nvidia stock has fallen 32 percent and pulled the Nasdaq 100 down 14.7 percent. The decline follows the departure of Jensen Huang and questions regarding the company's corporate governance. A ban on Nvidia chips to China also contributed to the current stock market downturn. Tayal suggests that investors diversify across the AI supply chain rather than focusing only on chips.

Broadcom, Advanced Micro Devices, and Celestica are mentioned as potential alternatives to Nvidia in the chip industry. AMD data centre chips and Google tensor processing units could take the place of Nvidia GPUs. Celestica helps Google manufacture these units, while Hammond Power Solutions supplies transformers for various power grids. Bird Construction is building AI data centres for BCE and reported a 13 billion dollar backlog. Shopify is developing AI tools for merchants and saw net profit rise 75 percent in late 2026.

Jensen Huang previously described artificial intelligence as a five layer cake consisting of energy, chips, and infrastructure. He also included models and software applications as the final two layers of this specific AI structure. Puja Tayal stated that performance matters most in AI and alternatives must prove their mettle to investors. She noted that Shopify will thrive in the software space with AI supporting the company's overall growth. Tayal believes the current dip in Hammond Power Solutions is an opportunity for investors to buy.

Investors hit hard by the Nvidia downturn are the primary people affected by these market shifts. Bird Construction is benefiting from booms in energy export infrastructure and nuclear power infrastructure alongside AI data centres. Shopify merchants are affected by new AI tools designed to help them target their audiences more efficiently. The Motley Fool Canada team identified ten top TSX stocks for 2026, but Nvidia was not included. They previously recommended MercadoLibre on January 8, 2014, which grew from 1,000 dollars to over 19,000 dollars.

Nvidia's dip is not related to the performance of its graphics processing units, but security concerns may persist. Bird Construction reported 36.7 percent revenue growth and 61 percent earnings per share growth in third quarter 2026. Shopify's strongest net profit growth occurred in the fourth quarter of 2024, when it surged by 97 percent. Hammond Power Solutions serves mining sites, transportation systems, commercial buildings, public infrastructure, data centres, and industrial hubs. The Motley Fool Canada reports an average return of 103 percent compared to 88 percent for the S&P/TSX.

Investors may now buy Bird Construction as it recovers from a dip that occurred in October 2026. The chip industry must provide alternatives as billions of dollars of AI infrastructure investment remain on the line. It remains a black box how much of Shopify's recent profit growth is attributed to its AI tools. The articles do not state if companies will actually pull back on buying Nvidia GPUs over security concerns. It is not clear if AMD or Google will successfully take the market share from Nvidia.

stories.Summary:
Companies supplying the infrastructure for artificial intelligence data centres lost approximately $4.2tn in value since June, according to an analysis by The Financial Times. This significant decline wiped out nearly half of the $9.4tn these businesses gained during the previous twelve months. The sell off affected global mining, utility, and manufacturing firms, including Caterpillar and Okto, which contracted with Meta for nuclear power in Ohio. Investor confidence dropped quickly over the last four weeks due to concerns regarding debt funded spending and political backlash.

The market downturn impacted chipmakers like AMD, Micron, Broadcom, and TSMC, as well as manufacturers such as Dell, HPE, and Super Micro Computer. Vertiv saw its shares drop 23 percent after the midterms, falling to $202.07 from a May peak of $379.94 despite third quarter sales rising 61 percent to $4.31bn. S&P Global is tracking 157 projects that have been abandoned, paused, or severely delayed. Sightline Climate analysts estimate that 30 to 50 percent of US AI data centres planned for 2026 will be cancelled or delayed.

Dan Thompson of 451 Research at S&P Global Energy stated that community opposition and state regulation are key risks for projects across the country. Other factors include US midterm results in states like Iowa, Texas, and Ohio, and reports that Nvidia may have sold to blacklisted Chinese organisations. Conversely, Alex Cordovil from DellOro Group argued that revenue growth is baked in until 2027 because backlogs remain at record highs. He believes the financial fundamentals are solid and that the build out is not yet decelerating.

The sector has been the second worst performing part of the S&P 500 since the summer, trailing only technology. While 16 GW is due this year, only around 5 GW is currently under construction in the United States. Democrats now hold Congress and several governorships, leaving the future of environmental protections and moratoriums an open question. The full impact of campaign pledges on the tech sector will likely remain unknown until well into 2027.

stories.Summary:

The firm also lowered expectations for power consumption and HBM demand. These changes apply to the coming years through 2030. A clear shift is occurring in growth expectations for AI infrastructure investment.

Global AI accelerator capital expenditure for 2027 drops to $627 billion from $770 billion. The 2028 figure falls to $758 billion from $1.054 trillion, and 2029 drops to $796 billion from $1.352 trillion. By 2030, the forecast is $923 billion, down from $1.531 trillion. Cumulative expenditure from 2027 to 2030 is now $1.6 trillion less than previously estimated. Logic wafer shipments from 2026 to 2030 are cut by 17 percent.

SemiAnalysis stated that slowing revenue growth and a tightening financing environment are the main reasons. They noted that some cutting-edge AI labs saw third quarter recurring revenue fall short of expectations. The firm believes large AI customers now have more computing power platform choices. They explained that NVIDIA GPUs are no longer the most attractive solution in all scenarios. The agency emphasized that these revisions would occur even if Jensen Huang remains CEO.

NVIDIA is the most affected company, facing lower shipment forecasts and reduced product pricing power. Anthropic prefers Google TPU, Amazon Trainium, and AMD GPU over NVIDIA solutions. OpenAI is prioritizing its self-developed Jalapeno and Serrano ASICs alongside AMD GPUs. Neocloud providers are vulnerable because they rely on financing to purchase GPUs for rental. Chinese end customers face risks if the US RASA Act is passed.

The market previously expected annual AI accelerator expenditure to exceed $1 trillion by 2029. HBM prices previously drove infrastructure investment growth, but these premiums are now being readjusted. Some data center projects in Texas, including the Nexus project in Hubbard, face permit delays. The Crusoe/Goodnight project also faces potential delays for 275MW of capacity. US midterm election regulations may postpone 5.8GW of data center capacity.

NVIDIA will increase GB300 shipments by 130,000 units to fill a third quarter gap. Total revenue forecasts for the third and fourth quarters of 2026 are $109.1 billion and $125.3 billion. Broadcom shows more resilience because it helps customers with financing and infrastructure construction. stories.Headline: Chen Danqi joins Noeri part-time as the AI startup raises 110 million dollars
stories.Summary:
Chen Danqi announced on social platforms in the early hours of 17 November 2026 that she had joined Noeri on a part-time basis two months earlier. Danqi Chen is an Associate Professor of Computer Science at Princeton University. Noeri is a newly unveiled AI company co-founded by Yejin Choi, Professor of Computer Science at Stanford University, and Carlos Guestrin. The company focuses on developing AI systems that can continuously learn and self-improve. Noeri also announced it has raised 110 million US dollars in financing.

The round was led by Menlo Ventures, with participation from Madrona Venture Group, Kindred Ventures, Wing Venture Capital and NEA. NVIDIA, Cisco Investments and Snowflake became strategic investors. Noeri supports the use of closed-source models and open-weight models and can adapt as new models emerge. Customers can retain ownership of their own data and of the workflows and models developed through the system, but must still comply with relevant license agreements of third-party models. Every modification comes with an explanation and is submitted for human review and confirmation, a process Noeri compares to code review.

Chen said she is quite looking forward to the team's research direction, especially the application of AI in scientific discovery. She said she hopes to enable every scientist to apply AI to their most intractable research problems. She said she is very happy to work with Yejin Choi, who has long been her role model and friend. Choi and Guestrin serve as co-CEOs of Noeri. The company interprets its name as "The Plural of Intelligence".

Choi and Guestrin wrote in a vision article that they prefer an ecosystem composed of a large number of AIs of different scales and capabilities over one enterprise developing and mastering a superintelligence. They call the concept Plural Intelligence, in which every organization and individual can build, master and continuously improve their own AI. Enterprises are affected: Noeri will study an enterprise's own data and workflows and optimize the entire AI system around specific tasks. The scope it can adjust includes instructions and skills, tools and orchestration, model selection and model optimization.

Choi is a professor at Stanford University and a senior fellow at Stanford HAI, and she officially joined Stanford University in January 2025. She was previously a Professor of Computer Science at the University of Washington, Senior Research Manager at the Allen Institute for AI (Ai2), and served as Senior Research Director and Distinguished Scientist at NVIDIA. Guestrin co-created XGBoost with Tianqi Chen and co-founded the machine learning company Turi, which was acquired by Apple in 2016. After joining Apple, Guestrin served as Senior Director of Machine Learning and AI and participated in promoting Apple to establish an AI and machine learning R&D center in Seattle. Chen co-leads the Princeton NLP research group, serves as deputy director of the Princeton Language and Intelligence Research Program, and is one of the authors of RoBERTa.

Noeri wants to hand to AI the work that otherwise requires a professional AI engineering team, since most AI models have basically fixed parameters after training is completed. The system will learn from the enterprise's data, workflows and interactions during task execution, and every experience and correction in a task has the opportunity to become the basis for the next round of optimization. Noeri hopes to find a more appropriate combination through model specialization and agent collaboration, for example letting a smaller model be responsible for scheduling and calling other models and professional tools according to task requirements. Chen said she is particularly looking forward to the application of Plural Intelligence in scientific discovery, a direction Noeri hopes to explore. The articles leave open what Noeri's products will cost and when they will be available.

Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigned as the chief executive officer about one week before November 17, 2026.
