stories.Headline: How should we use AI? Let’s ask students
stories.Summary:
Princeton gave every student ChatGPT Plus, a decision announced without consulting students beforehand, according to a contributing opinion writer in The Daily Princetonian. The writer, Nick Manetas, a 2027 English major from Richmond, Virginia, made the case in a piece dated November 17, 2026. He wrote that The Daily Princetonian Editorial Board has argued the decision undermines Princeton’s stated educational mission. He called the ChatGPT news a symptom of the administration’s wider neglect of student voices on artificial intelligence. He said Princeton’s institutional AI policies are reshaping how students learn and what behavior they can be punished for.

Manetas wrote that the USG Academics Committee, the only student body directly representing academic concerns to administrators, does not list AI among its priorities for this year. He wrote that the McGraw Center for Teaching and Learning is exploring how AI might give students new power to create or invent, but is focused on communicating existing scholarly research rather than studying student perspectives. He described USG meetings as allowing public comment but unable to support the deliberation the issue requires. He wrote that the USG senate constitution stipulates the Academics Committee is composed of a committee chair, chairs of its three standing subcommittees, and any additional chairs appointed by the committee chair. He proposed a citizens’ assembly in which 40 randomly selected students spend a weekend learning about AI from experts at the McGraw Center, the Center for Digital Humanities, and organizations like the San Francisco-based Center for Humane Technology.

Manetas wrote that students, teachers and administrators would all benefit from a citizens’ assembly on AI and education. He said such a process convenes a representative cross-section of the population to study a question and create consensus-based policy recommendations. He wrote that peer institutions like Yale and Harvard have used this process to guide institutional policymaking on issues ranging from institutional neutrality to the overhaul of the student government constitution. He said the assembly’s learning would culminate in facilitated discussions where students produce recommendations about how to use AI in their learning. He wrote that the administration would not be beholden to the recommendations but that their breadth and intention would merit serious consideration.

Manetas wrote that recruiting student participants is the most difficult part of holding a citizens’ assembly on a college campus. He cited Princeton’s Tigers Leading Tigers workshop series, in which experts train students to be peer leaders on divisive issues, as an example of the administration using low cost freebies such as water bottles to incentivize students. He wrote that history professor D. Graham Burnett recently noted in Public Seminar that academics hoping to prevent abuse of the technology have little choice but to stand next to students and watch them do the work. He wrote that most of his own classes this year have experimented with new assessment forms ranging from oral examinations to modified blue-book essays. He wrote that low voter turnout and uncontested positions at recent USG elections suggest real student apathy toward existing deliberative bodies.

Manetas wrote that Princeton’s AI policy has largely focused on preventing students from using the technology to offload cognitive labor. He wrote that students face increasingly uncertain job prospects and that AI-proficiency is a marker of employability. He wrote that blanket bans fail students when they prohibit AI without encouraging reflection on what their education is for. He wrote that recent decisions like the Orientation changes have eroded trust between students and the administration. He quoted media theorist Marshall McLuhan saying that many a good argument is ruined by some fool who knows what he is talking about.

Manetas wrote that a citizens’ assembly won’t solve the current higher education crisis but that the current policymaking dynamic cannot continue. He wrote that cutting students out of deliberations on AI serves nobody except the AI companies profiting from the inability to decide together how to use their technology. He wrote that administrators will continue facing difficult funding decisions between budget cuts and increased political attention paid to institutions like Princeton. He wrote that in the longer term an assembly would act as a durable model for collaboration on decisions requiring community consensus. He invited readers to email him at nm1629[at]princeton.edu to chat more about citizens’ assemblies.

stories.Headline: Arthur Hayes names four tokens he expects to pump before the AI bubble ends
stories.Summary:
Arthur Hayes named four tokens he expects to pump before the AI bubble ends, calling the group the "Four Horsemen" in a post on X, according to a BeInCrypto report published on November 16, 2026. The call came after Bitcoin fell to nearly $62,000 on November 15, its lowest level since July. Hayes said the four would pump and then usher in the end of the AI bubble. The post follows his June exit from Hyperliquid, NEAR and ZEC, which he had grouped as a "holy trinity" two weeks earlier, and he sold ZEC after a vulnerability surfaced in its Orchard shielded pool.

His targets are $2,800 for Ethereum, $1,800 for Zcash, $6 for NEAR Protocol and $40 for Venice Token, the token of the privacy-focused AI platform Venice. He sized the trade small to medium because his conviction is low, writing that if the music is playing you have to dance, and he attached no timeframe to the targets. The $2,800 ETH target sits $2,200 below the $5,000 year-end level he forecast in August. Hayes said he kept only Bitcoin and ETH as core crypto holdings.

Hayes argues that a burst would trigger a financial crisis and a wave of central bank money printing he calls the "Big Print," which he expects to send Bitcoin sharply higher after an initial drop. In August he called the AI boom a credit bubble and said Bitcoin could reach $1 million. On-chain investigator ZachXBT has accused Hayes of pumping tokens such as ZEC and Worldcoin before selling to his audience. The trade rests on a $1.5 trillion AI debt wave that Hayes says has absorbed dollar liquidity, and if that debt avoids a crisis the trigger he describes never arrives and the pump loses its stated end point.

stories.Headline: Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora says AI leaders push an unnaturally negative narrative about their own technology
stories.Summary:
Nikesh Arora, the chief executive officer of Palo Alto Networks, criticized leaders of advanced artificial intelligence companies during a Semafor event on November 16, 2026. Speaking with Mat Honan from MIT Technology Review, Arora claimed that these industry figures are promoting an unnaturally negative narrative regarding their own technology. He argued that the current obsession with potential risks is overshadowing the immense benefits that this fast-moving technology could provide to the world. According to Arora, the people who should be championing the advantages of these tools are instead focusing on their dark side.

Arora described artificial intelligence as a transformational technology that could democratize intelligence and uplift a huge amount of humanity across the globe. He suggested that a villager in India could use these tools to summarize multiple websites and access the best available intelligence. Regarding the difficulty of building new data centers, he believed that scarcity of computing capacity would actually accelerate innovation in compression technology. However, he acknowledged that these growing capabilities intensify cybersecurity risks by making it easier to find vulnerabilities in software written over the last 50 years.

The executive warned that as more software weaknesses are discovered and exploited, companies may be forced to take systems offline to apply necessary patches. He stated that there is no quick solve or panacea for these security challenges, but believed the industry would eventually grind through them. Arora maintained that every technology possesses a dark side, yet the potential for positive global impact remains the more important story. He concluded that the industry must power through these inevitable security hurdles to realize the full potential of the technology.

stories.Headline: Liudmila Alekseeva and co-authors find AI adoption raises managerial demand and shifts skills
stories.Summary:
A study published in the Strategic Management Journal challenges the common assumption that adopting artificial intelligence automatically reduces the demand for managers, according to research by Liudmila Alekseeva, José Azar, Mireia Giné and Sampsa Samila. The authors analyzed United States job postings from 2010 to 2022 and linked firm-level AI adoption with managerial vacancies and the skills those positions require. Using instrumental-variable estimates, they found that a 1-percentage-point increase in the share of AI-related job postings is associated with a 1.2-percentage-point increase in the managerial share, which works out to about 7.5%. The same increase is linked to roughly a 9% rise in managerial vacancies, and the relationship is strongest in manufacturing and among firms that invest heavily in research and development.

The study also reports that the skills demanded of managers shift as AI adoption grows, with AI-intensive firms placing less emphasis on routine administrative capabilities such as budgeting and planning. Those same firms place more emphasis on stakeholder management, creativity, sales management and other growth-oriented skills. The authors state that they do not interpret their estimates as definitive causal effects, and they note that the study primarily covers predictive AI rather than the newer generative and agentic systems. For business leaders, the researchers say the implication is to redesign management rather than assume that automation simply removes managers from the organization. AI can reduce routine tasks while increasing the need for coordination, scaling and organizational adaptation, according to the study.

The research was published in 2026 in the Strategic Management Journal under the title "Artificial intelligence adoption and the demand for managerial expertise," with the DOI 10.1002/smj.70099. The article was provided by the Strategic Management Society, and the phys.org version was edited by Sadie Harley and reviewed by Andrew Zinin. The findings sit alongside other work the outlet lists, including a study reporting that generative AI boosts job growth and productivity. The articles do not say what further research or follow-up work is planned beyond the authors' caution that their estimates are not definitive causal effects.

Articles.Title: New research finds AI adoption is associated with more managers—and different managerial skills

stories.Headline: Tom Lee says AI trade remains structurally intact despite Nvidia leadership scandal
stories.Summary:
The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell nearly 12 percent from its October 6 record close by November 5, 2026. This decline followed the November 12 resignation of Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang after reports of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Nvidia shares lost about 35 percent of their value since October 6, which represents a loss of roughly 2 trillion dollars. The company experienced its worst week in 19 months, with shares dropping another 4.1 percent on Monday.

The Nasdaq closed at 24,315.00 on November 5, which was 11.9 percent below the October 6 record close of 27,599.79. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress is currently serving as the interim leader for Nvidia. While Nvidia shares fell, rivals Broadcom and AMD saw their stock prices rise on the day Huang resigned. The market now awaits quarterly results from Nvidia on Tuesday and a potential Nasdaq debut for the AI developer Anthropic this week.

Tom Lee, the head of research at Fundstrat Global Advisors, believes the artificial intelligence trade remains structurally intact. He argues that the current slide is driven by emotion, headlines, and margin selling rather than a fundamental wall for the industry. Lee suggests that capital is dynamic and could flow toward SpaceX or Anthropic if Nvidia becomes less central. Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co added that while Huang's exit cost Nvidia 1 trillion dollars in valuation, it will not stop 3 trillion to 4 trillion dollars in expected spending.

The leadership scandal has weighed on AI shares for several weeks as investors react to the loss of the founder. Future funding for the sector may broaden beyond a single chipmaker if the upcoming events go well. However, a stalled debut for Anthropic or a cut to the outlook for Nvidia could test the resilience of the trade. Analysts continue to monitor whether the industry can move past the loss of its most prominent leader.

Articles.Title: Tom Lee Sees No Cracks in the AI Trade Despite Nasdaq's 12% Drop

stories.Headline: S&P Global rates AI-linked debt as analysts warn concentrated exposure may magnify credit risk
stories.Summary:
S&P Global has taken a central role in rating a growing wave of AI linked debt instruments that are attracting institutional demand, according to a report published on November 16, 2026. S&P Global Ratings has assigned relatively high grades to structures backed by AI related projects that are drawing capital from insurance companies. Analysts have raised concerns that complex repayment terms and concentrated exposures within these AI themed securities could magnify credit risk. The report says the growing use of S&P Global ratings on AI related debt should not be the only factor investors consider today. The report says S&P Global operates in the capital markets industry as a provider of benchmarks, data and analytics, and its credit ratings on AI related debt directly influence how insurers and other large investors assess and compare risk across this emerging segment.

It says the S&P Global narrative rests on the group using AI, data and capital markets activity to turn complex financing trends into high margin, repeatable services. The report says the main condition for this thesis is that S&P Global converts its investments in AI driven productivity, private markets transparency and energy data into high margin growth across divisions. It says the news leans into the catalyst that S&P Global can monetise an 8 trillion dollar maturity wall through more structured and themed issuance. The report says the catch is that concentrated exposure to a handful of tech borrowers means those ratings are now more exposed to a single theme than traditional diversified securitisations. It says that pressure point sits squarely in the risk section that already flags dependence on healthy issuance volumes and investor confidence in Ratings.

The report says that if analysts start questioning whether AI related tranches are understood as well as they are scored, it gives critics of traditional ratings models fresh material, including at rivals like Moody's and Fitch. It says the more scrutiny builds, the more investors may look at S&P Global's own debt disclosures and risk frameworks for clues. The report says raw headlines about AI debt only become useful once you link them back to the S&P Global Narrative, because that is what turns a single theme into a full investment decision. It says readers might want to see where analysts expect the business to be a few years from now and how far that is from today. The article is general in nature and was produced with the assistance of AI automation, based on data and analysis from Simply Wall St, and it states that it is not intended to be financial advice.

stories.Headline: Nvidia continues financial support for AI ecosystem under interim CEO Colette Kress
stories.Summary:
Nvidia announced on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, that it will continue to provide financial support for the artificial intelligence ecosystem. Interim CEO Colette Kress stated that the company will remain a source of capital for startups and partners. This commitment comes shortly after the resignation of former CEO Jensen Huang last week. Huang stepped down following reports of a relationship with a woman linked to Chinese intelligence.

The company will now be more disciplined and selective regarding its future investments and guarantees. Kress noted that Nvidia will rigorously evaluate commitments as the market matures and other capital sources emerge. This approach specifically affects neoclouds, which provide computing capacity to regional operators and large AI players. While Nvidia will offer financing to some very strong customers and suppliers, it will not provide blank checks.

Interim CEO Colette Kress told investors and analysts that the company's momentum is real and demand is accelerating. She emphasized that employees are committed and the company is well positioned to handle current challenges. Board chair Harvey Jones confirmed that the board unanimously accepted the resignation of Jensen Huang. Jones stated that the board does not intend to reinstate Huang as the chief executive officer.

The leadership change follows an investigation into how cutting edge technology reached Chinese companies despite United States sales bans. The woman associated with Huang allegedly helped these firms gain access to restricted Nvidia technology. The company has declined to answer further questions regarding the departure of Huang or the ongoing investigation. Nvidia will continue to analyze whether specific guarantees are the right investments for the company to make.

stories.Headline: Arist CEO Michael Ioffe predicts AI agents will recommend most major corporate decisions including layoffs
stories.Summary:
Michael Ioffe, the cofounder and CEO of the startup Arist, said at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum in Detroit on November 16, 2026, that AI agents will increasingly recommend major corporate decisions, including layoffs, while executives keep the final say. He predicted that within the next few years the majority of significant enterprise shifts, such as products being launched or layoffs being made, will be recommended by agents. Arist uses AI agents to interview employees, comb through company data and recommend solutions to business problems, and it already works with more than 15% of the Fortune 500. Ioffe said the technology can gather insights from thousands of employees in just 72 hours, a process that traditionally requires teams of consultants. Ioffe said an executive will always make the final call, and he sees AI's biggest opportunity in helping companies identify problems and act on them faster rather than replacing executives or consultants.

Before an agent can recommend something as consequential as a layoff, it must understand what is happening inside a company, so Arist's agents can decide whom to interview, ask questions and weigh responses against information such as an employee's tenure, performance and past engagement scores. Ioffe said that helps the system distinguish the loudest complaints from problems affecting the wider organization, and that the agents will push back if an executive frames a question to get the answer they want. He argued that employees may be more candid with AI agents than with another person, and he said that if a company can get to the truth much faster, a 50,000-person enterprise can move at the speed of a 50-person startup. Ioffe said he did not set out to compete with consulting firms, and he described how at 19 he became interested in delivering education to students in war-torn Yemen and built a text-message-based learning platform before shifting Arist toward training employees at Fortune 500 companies and becoming one of OpenAI's early partners. He noticed that companies would pay consultants millions to diagnose a problem and then pay Arist a few hundred thousand dollars to train employees to fix it, and in his experience the consultants got the diagnosis wrong about 90% of the time, which prompted Arist to move from training employees to diagnosing problems.

He pointed to a major software company whose data was merely pointing out what was happening instead of why. The prediction comes as more companies cite AI when cutting jobs, sometimes drawing accusations of "AI washing," or blaming technology for cuts made for other reasons, and the article says that even when companies genuinely expect AI to replace workers, moving too quickly can backfire. HR leaders have warned that companies risk losing valuable talent when they cut workers without a clear plan for how AI will replace their work, according to previous reporting cited in the article. The article also notes that gathering information through AI agents could raise concerns about how candid employees are willing to be with an agent working on behalf of their employer, especially when its findings could influence decisions about their jobs.

stories.Headline: University of Cambridge researchers find governments are blind to one third of the global AI supply chain
stories.Summary:
A University of Cambridge team released a report on November 17, 2026, about the global AI supply chain. The study found that governments are blind to as much as a third of this production network. Researchers identified a vast zone of invisibility located in the middle of the global AI production process. This lack of attention from national and international policymaking creates significant vulnerabilities in the technology stack. The team mapped 14 supply chain layers and 137 elements produced in over 50 countries.

The study analyzed 117 policy documents from 43 countries, the EU, and the OECD. It identified 137 elements and 351 sub-elements involving nearly 800 firms across 56 countries and territories. Japan has 101 firms across 69 elements, while the U.K. is involved in 41 elements. The Dutch firm ASML relies on parts from German and U.S. companies for EUV lithography. Ajinomoto in Japan controls over 95 percent of the build-up film market for AI chips.

Director Verity Harding stated that no single country can control the AI supply chain alone. Lead author Dr. Siyi Liu said most policy discussions inaccurately reduce AI to compute, data, and models. Liu noted that governments are often unaware of the strengths and vulnerabilities they hold in the chain. She argued that understanding these positions is the basis for credible bargaining power in AI governance. Liu also urged governments to be pragmatic when collaborating with allies to build collective agency.

The report notes that the U.K. ignores its specialties in chip design and industrial gases. Japan's policy documents recognize only three elements despite its massive role in equipment and testing. Middle powers like Belgium, South Korea, and Qatar hold more leverage than their own governments realize. Ireland affects capacity as a host for U.S. firms like Google and AMD. Advanced packaging is concentrated in Asian territories including Taiwan, Vietnam, and the Philippines.

The research highlights a universal mismatch between top AI policy documents and actual supply chain positions. Policy often focuses on finished chips, GPUs, and data centers while ignoring the physical middle. This blind spot includes chip packaging and electronic design automation software from Synopsys, Cadence, and Siemens EDA. The U.K. holds leverage through Arm and the industrial gas company Linde. Qatar provides vital helium, while Belgium is strong in recycled semiconductor chemicals and imec research.

The team created a toolkit to help governments audit their place in the AI supply chain. This tool helps policymakers decide when to diversify providers or build national capacity by exiting suppliers. Experts from the AIxGEO project say that total AI sovereignty for any one nation is impossible. Disruption to upstream components could trigger a domino effect destabilizing global stock markets and productivity. The articles leave open how governments will use the toolkit to change their current policies.

Articles.Title: A third of the global AI supply chain is 'invisible' to governments, study finds

stories.Headline: State AI officers cite funding and staffing as top challenges, survey finds
stories.Summary:
The National Association of State Chief Information Officers released its first State AI Officer Survey on November 17, 2026, reporting trends in dedicated AI leadership across states along with the common challenges those officials face. The survey was informed by people leading AI work in 33 states and territories, and it follows annual State CIO Surveys that showed AI as a top issue, including governance in 2025 and maturity in 2026. AI was the number one priority among state CIOs in 2026, overtaking cybersecurity for the first time in 12 years. In 2023 fewer than 20 percent of states had a chief AI officer or a similar role, while today at least 46 states have identified at least one person to direct AI and at least 25 states have someone with “AI” in their title.

No fewer than 94 percent of state chief AI officer positions operate from within the central IT organization or the state CIO’s organization, with others in the state data office, department of administration or management, governor’s office or innovation office. Only 42 percent of respondents in these positions cited AI as their primary responsibility rather than one part of a broader role, and 56 percent said they had no defined or dedicated budget for AI. The most common funding sources were a dedicated or special legislative appropriation, the state CIO or central IT budget, or an innovation or modernization fund, and most respondents said their AI programs were still maturing. On governance, 59 percent described their approach as hybrid or federated, 31 percent as centralized and 9 percent as decentralized, while 78 percent of states in the 2026 State CIO Survey reported using an AI governance framework, up from 65 percent in 2025. Only 10 percent of respondents said they currently use frontier AI models, most commonly for software and code vulnerability analysis and vulnerability prioritization.

Respondents said the chief challenge in moving AI from pilot to production is funding, followed by a three-way tie between data readiness, security or privacy concerns and workforce skills. Mandatory statewide employee training and optional training each received 38 percent, and respondents named shadow AI as the most challenging workforce issue, ahead of a lack of general AI literacy and difficulty recruiting AI talent. When asked about top challenges in their role, 75 percent of chief AI officers cited a lack of staff, followed by rapidly changing technology, funding, cybersecurity or privacy concerns and data quality or readiness, and adequate staffing was the top answer for what would help them do their jobs more effectively. Respondents said agentic AI, workforce transformation, scaling AI across agencies, risk management and AI regulation will consume most of their time in the next three years. NASCIO offered four recommendations: establish clear authority for AI leadership, invest in staffing, funding and expertise, build collaboration into AI governance and procurement, and prioritize workforce readiness with AI training opportunities.

stories.Headline: North Carolina creates a dedicated Office of AI and reorganizes its IT department under CIO Nate Denny
stories.Summary:
North Carolina announced on November 17, 2026, that it is reorganizing its Department of Information Technology and creating a new office devoted to artificial intelligence, according to the state. The changes reshape how the N.C. Department of Information Technology works, from supporting other state agencies to managing its own operations. The reorganization does not involve layoffs or require additional funding, but it gives several areas of responsibility new leadership and a clearer place within the department. Agency chief information officers, business relationship managers and strategic partnerships will come together in a new Customer Division, led by Torre Jessup as chief customer officer. Lenae Storey is joining NCDIT as chief digital officer to lead a new Digital Experience Division, which takes over responsibilities previously handled by different teams.

Chief Operating Officer Keith Briggs will lead the new Operations Division, bringing together internal functions such as facilities, purchasing, human resources and internal auditing. NCDIT is moving its Enterprise Data Office, which includes the N.C. Government Data Analytics Center and the N.C. Health Information Exchange Authority, into the Technology Services Division led by Chief Deputy State CIO Greg Flynn. Artificial intelligence will have its own Office of AI within the Office of the Secretary and State CIO, led by Chief AI Officer I-Sah Hsieh, who previously served as NCDIT's deputy secretary of AI and policy. The team will help state employees and agencies learn how to use AI, guide its adoption and identify opportunities to change how government delivers services. The department is also bringing more responsibility for security and risk under the state chief information security officer, and legal matters will have a dedicated division led by General Counsel Julie Song, who is joining NCDIT.

Deputy Secretary Pryor Gibson will remain in charge of the Division of Broadband and Digital Opportunity, which works to expand high-speed Internet access and help people build the skills to use it. Annette Taylor will serve as senior adviser for community partnerships, focusing on NCDIT's relationships with communities and partners across the state. State Chief Information Officer and NCDIT Secretary Nate Denny said in a recent statement that the changes reflect the need for the department to keep pace with how quickly technology is changing government, noting that the agencies NCDIT serves need it to keep pace. Denny said the structure is designed around the work, not around any one person, which gives the department room to adjust as its responsibilities evolve rather than tying its structure to particular people or positions.

Articles.Title: North Carolina Reorganizes IT Leadership, Adds Dedicated AI Office

stories.Headline: Hariharan marks 50 years in music and raises concerns about AI
stories.Summary:
Legendary playback singer Hariharan sat down with The Hindu to mark a remarkable milestone of 50 years in the music industry, a career that has spanned more than 15,000 songs across 10 languages and 30 ghazal albums. In the conversation he discussed his musical journey and the roots that bridge Mumbai and Chennai, the two cities that shaped him. He also spoke about his training under legendary masters and about recording with Kishore Kumar during his long career. It presented his journey as one that connects the North and South of Indian music through his own life and work. Hariharan is the figure at the centre of the interview, and the account of his career and his concerns is presented in his own words as given to The Hindu. stories.Headline: Damac chairman Hussain Sajwani says his Anthropic stake earned more in under two years than 30 years of investing
stories.Summary:
Hussain Sajwani, the 72-year-old chairman of Dubai-based luxury real estate developer Damac Properties, said at the Bloomberg Invest Dubai forum that what he made in 30 years he made in Anthropic in less than two years, according to Livemint. His comment came as Anthropic, the AI startup behind Claude, prepares for a Nasdaq IPO on Wednesday at a valuation of $1.4 trillion. The listing is expected to make all seven co-founders, Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei, Tom Brown, Christopher Olah, Jared Kaplan, Jack Clark and Sam McCandlish, multi-billionaires, while around 50 early employees are projected to cross the $100 million threshold in stock wealth. Sajwani said he expects his investments in AI firms, including Anthropic, to draw billions in returns.

In July 2024, Damac Group announced notable investments in AI companies, including $50 million in Anthropic, as one of the top investors who bought into the company from the cryptocurrency exchange FTX. The group also invested in Elon Musk's xAI and in Mistral, a France-based AI company behind one of the best European open-source large-language models. Sajwani said at the time that the group was excited to be part of the AI revolution and to contribute to the growth of the industry, adding that its investments in Mistral, Anthropic and xAI underscored its dedication to fostering innovation. He said that between only three companies, OpenAI, SpaceX and Anthropic, the group is making a few billion dollars of profit.

Sajwani founded Damac Properties in 2002, and according to Forbes he started out in the food services business, catering to the US military and construction giant Bechtel, before shifting to real estate in 2001 after Dubai allowed foreigners to own property. Forbes puts his net worth at $15.3 billion, making him the 185th richest man in the world. Damac Group, his multi-billion-dollar conglomerate, divides its investments into seven core areas: real estate, capital markets, hotels and resorts, manufacturing, catering, high-end fashion and data centres, with a footprint across North America, Europe, Asia, the Middle East and Africa. Its notable activities include Damac Properties, the acquisition of Italian fashion house Roberto Cavalli and Swiss jewellery brand de GRISOGONO, the 50-storey DAMAC Towers Nine Elms in London and a luxury resort in the Maldives.

stories.Headline: Taisei launches a 150 million dollar fund for AI and robotics startups
stories.Summary:
The Japanese construction company Taisei announced on Monday, November 16, 2026, that it is establishing a new investment fund. This 153-year-old firm is dedicating 150 million dollars to support various startups specializing in robotics and artificial intelligence. The company intends to use these technological advancements to find viable workarounds for a shrinking domestic workforce. This strategic move aims to modernize the business by integrating automation into its traditional construction processes.

The fund will be managed by Pegasus Tech Ventures, a firm based in Silicon Valley that serves as the general partner. This partnership will focus on searching for new investments in automation and related fields through the year 2036. Taisei also plans to target startups that provide liquid-cooling infrastructure and high-density power solutions. These specific investments are intended to support the company as it expands its efforts into the construction of AI data centers.

Anis Uzzaman, who serves as the founder and chief executive officer of Pegasus, explained the purpose of the venture. He stated that the primary objective is to transform a traditional construction firm into a leader enabled by robotics and AI. Uzzaman further noted that the fund will help the company secure the necessary infrastructure for modern data centers. Pegasus currently manages over 2 billion dollars in assets and has previously worked with other Japanese companies like Aisin and Japanet Holdings.

This initiative comes as Japanese businesses struggle with chronic labor shortages, rising wages, and a general backlash against foreign workers. These economic pressures, combined with sliding domestic spending, are pushing more companies to adopt robotic solutions. Taisei has already shown interest in this sector by investing last year in a fund run by Met Fund Advisors. That previous investment focused on emerging startups coming out of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

stories.Headline: Japan defense minister Shinjiro Koizumi plans AI guidelines for military use by end of November 2026

Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi announced plans on Sunday, November 16, 2026, to issue new guidelines for artificial intelligence. These rules will govern how the Defense Ministry and Self-Defense Forces personnel utilize this technology. The government intends to release the official documents by the end of November 2026. This initiative was unveiled during a visit to Yokosuka in Kanagawa Prefecture.

The new guidelines will require an update to the basic AI policy that was originally compiled in July 2024. These rules will focus on three pillars, including the requirement that humans make all final decisions and accept responsibility for the results. The framework also aims to transform data into a defensive power for the nation. Finally, the ministry seeks to balance the fast spread of AI with the need for enhanced safety.

Minister Koizumi is responsible for this shift and told reporters that the government will not hesitate to revise policies. He explained that revisions are necessary because the field of artificial intelligence changes very rapidly. The minister stated that the government wants to show a new direction for national security. He believes that utilizing AI and data will strengthen the overall defense capabilities of the country.

stories.Headline: Kotozna secures two Japanese patents for conversational AI on its 10th anniversary
stories.Summary:
Kotozna Inc., a Tokyo-based B2B SaaS company led by CEO Genri Goto, announced on November 17, 2026, that it had secured two Japanese patents for its conversational AI technology. The announcement coincided with the company's 10th anniversary, marking a decade of work in multilingual communication and enterprise AI. Kotozna was founded in October 2016 with a mission to overcome language barriers, and it has since expanded from multilingual communication services to generative AI-powered digital concierges, enterprise chatbots and interactive AI avatars. Its solutions now provide customer assistance around the clock in more than 50 languages, which reduces repetitive staff inquiries. The two patents are JP 7898212, called a Prompt Creation System, and JP 7932206, called an Answer Generation System, and together they cover prompt optimization and knowledge retrieval.

Rather than sending large amounts of information to AI models for every question, the technology builds optimized prompts containing only the information needed to generate appropriate responses. Unlike conventional RAG systems that divide documents into fixed-length segments, Kotozna's approach organizes information into meaningful sections so that important context is preserved. The company says this reduces unnecessary processing and token consumption, which helps improve response accuracy, lower latency and optimize AI operating costs, while also supporting efficient knowledge base updates as information changes. Goto said the mission over the past ten years had stayed the same, which is to make communication easier through technology. He described the patents as an important milestone in the company's journey and as a reflection of its commitment to developing AI that is innovative, reliable and practical for businesses worldwide.

The company states that its technology addresses three critical challenges in enterprise AI adoption, namely accuracy, speed and cost efficiency, enabling businesses to deploy reliable and scalable conversational AI solutions. Kotozna's solutions are deployed at more than 500 hotels and over 50 facilities and organizations, including airports, tourism organizations, shopping malls and public institutions in Japan and overseas. As Kotozna enters its second decade, the company says it will continue advancing its conversational AI capabilities toward intelligent AI agents that can handle complex inquiries, execute tasks and automate customer service workflows. It aims to strengthen its global presence through new deployments and partnerships, bringing its AI solutions to more businesses in hospitality, tourism, retail and other sectors worldwide. Kotozna reported capital of 70,000,000 yen as of December 31, 2025, and its head office is on the third floor of Hulic JP Akasaka in Minato-ku, Tokyo.

stories.Headline: Meomuru uses AI to top South Korean music chart with The Adult I Dreamed Of
stories.Summary:
A song created with the assistance of artificial intelligence reached the top of a major music chart in South Korea for the first time. This musical achievement occurred recently and was reported by Erika Kobayashi on November 17, 2026. The track managed to outperform popular K-pop idols to secure the number one position on the chart. This event marks a significant milestone for the integration of technology within the competitive South Korean music industry. The song is titled The Adult I Dreamed Of and was produced by an artist known as Meomuru.

This specific piece of music has resonated deeply with listeners who are currently in their 30s and 40s. The success of the track demonstrates how artificial intelligence can be used to create emotional connections with a mature audience. It represents a shift in the types of content that can dominate the national music rankings. The reports indicate that the song's popularity stems from its ability to connect with the lived experiences of older listeners.

While the articles do not provide a direct quote from Meomuru, the achievement highlights a new era of digital creativity. The use of AI tools allowed the creator to reach a level of success previously reserved for traditional pop stars. This development suggests that the boundaries between human and machine creativity are becoming increasingly blurred. More to follow.

stories.Headline: KB Securities report says Nvidia's AI dominance may peak in 2027 as inference chips gain
stories.Summary:
KB Securities released a Global Insight report on November 12, 2026, suggesting that Nvidia's dominance in the AI industry could reach a turning point by 2027. The report indicates that profit distribution may shift away from Nvidia toward providers of alternative accelerators between 2027 and 2028. This transition is expected as Google's tensor processing units and Cerebras accelerators become more available to the market. Additionally, mounting financing costs and power procurement challenges for data centers are contributing to this projected structural change.

The shift requires a move toward inference accelerators and proprietary chips that offer better power efficiency and lower costs. External sales of Google TPUs are projected to grow from 12 billion dollars this year to over 135 billion dollars by 2028. Oracle intends to provide Cerebras inference systems to its cloud customers during the first half of 2027. Financial pressures are already appearing, as GPU leasing operator CoreWeave reported a net loss of 709 million dollars in the third quarter. Furthermore, 40 out of 41 recent U.S. midterm election ballot measures favored tighter regulations on data centers.

Author Kim Il-hyeok stated that while Nvidia's technological lead will not weaken immediately, the competitive landscape will fundamentally change. He noted that Nvidia's revenue is still expected to grow 70 percent in fiscal 2028 despite a gradual decline in market share. The report also mentioned market uncertainty regarding whether CEO Jensen Huang might depart, citing reports that the board was preparing for this possibility. Kim suggested that investors should diversify their holdings beyond Nvidia to include companies focused on proprietary accelerators and inference.

The industry is currently moving its primary focus from training AI models toward inference for use in various applications. This transition favors chips that can handle more workloads with less electricity as power supplies become more constrained. Data center operators may also change their financing structures to rely on customer contract cash flows rather than GPU secured loans. While Nvidia continues to support customers with billions in equity stakes and guarantees, rising credit risks and depreciation costs remain significant concerns.

stories.Headline: South Korean President Lee proposes AI cooperation initiatives with ASEAN and Mekong nations
stories.Summary:
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung proposed expanded cooperation with ASEAN and Mekong nations on Monday, November 16, 2026, during summits in Manila. He suggested new initiatives focusing on artificial intelligence, trade, and security to ensure that everyone shares in the benefits of AI advances. Lee met with leaders at the 27th ASEAN-Republic of Korea Summit and a separate gathering at the Philippine International Convention Center. These meetings occurred as part of a four-day trip to the Philippines and China with first lady Kim Hea Kyung. The president emphasized the need for solidarity amid deepening geopolitical conflicts and growing economic uncertainty in the current international landscape.

The ASEAN-ROK AI Companionship Initiative and the ASEAN-ROK Cultural and Creative Industries Initiative aim to create new opportunities for young people. Lee proposed achieving annual bilateral trade of 300 billion US dollars by upgrading the ASEAN-Korea free trade agreement through proactive global responses. He pledged support for the ASEAN Community Vision 2045, a road map adopted in Malaysia in 2025 for a resilient, innovative ASEAN. Cooperation with Mekong nations, including Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, Laos, and Cambodia, will now include critical mineral supply chains and transnational crime. Bilateral trade between Korea and the Philippines reached 21.3 billion dollars as of September, surpassing the previous annual record.

President Lee stated that Korea is an ideal partner for Mekong countries because of its journey from aid recipient to donor. He claimed Korea possesses full-stack AI competitiveness, which includes infrastructure, models, applications, and services, to support safe and reliable AI development. Lee described ASEAN as a key partner for promoting lasting peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula and a regional cooperation pillar. He expressed firm support for ASEAN centrality, meaning Southeast Asian countries should drive the political and security architecture of the Indo-Pacific. The president promised that South Korea would serve as a reliable action partner to help realize the long-term ASEAN Community Vision.

Philippine President Ferdinand Romualdez Marcos Jr. said the partnership is relevant due to strategic uncertainty, rapid technological change, and various cross-border challenges. He noted that deep-rooted ties are reflected in shared strategic goals and vibrant people-to-people connections across the entire Southeast Asian region. Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul agreed with Lee to pursue cooperation in nuclear energy, the defense industry, and the protection of intellectual property. The East Timor president recommended that the Korean people receive the Nobel Peace Prize during a summit meeting with President Lee. Korean companies operating in Thailand and the Philippines are affected by Lee's requests for government support to expand their local operations.

The Mekong summit resumed after six years following the 2021 military coup in Myanmar, marking the 15th anniversary of Korea-Mekong ties. ASEAN and Korea established a comprehensive strategic partnership in 2024 to strengthen their existing diplomatic and economic relations across the region. Last year, Lee proposed a vision of being a contributor, springboard, and partner to deliver tangible benefits to the people of ASEAN. Korea and the Philippines signed a memorandum of understanding on science and technology cooperation to expand collaboration into the field of smart farming. They also signed a framework agreement on grant aid for projects run by the Korea International Cooperation Agency in the Philippines.

Lee and Prime Minister Anutin agreed to swiftly conclude a comprehensive economic partnership agreement to address uncertainty in the global trade environment. Korea and the Philippines committed to advancing future-oriented cooperation in aerospace, shipbuilding, disaster management, nuclear energy, and artificial intelligence technology. The two sides welcomed a plan to hold a special summit in Korea in 2029 for the 40th anniversary of dialogue relations. Lee will next attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, to continue his diplomatic meetings with various world leaders. The articles leave open the specific timeline for the industrial complexes and the final results of the free trade agreement negotiations.

stories.Headline: Korean man confesses to using AI to cheat on tax accountant exam as government investigates 528 national tests
stories.Summary:
Anonymous posters and a top exam scorer admitted to using AI to cheat on national exams in Korea around November 2026. A 34-year-old man surnamed Han confessed to cheating on the 63rd tax accountant certification exam. Other anonymous users claimed to have cheated on the civil service exam and the College Scholastic Ability Test. One user admitted to helping three other people pass an exam by lending them cheating devices. These admissions sparked a government investigation into AI-assisted cheating across various national tests.

The Ministry of Employment and Labor and HRDK will investigate 528 national certification exams administered this year. This review includes 37 professional qualifications like tax accountants and 491 technical qualifications like electrical engineers. Authorities will check for unusually high scores and large gaps in rankings compared to the last three years. For the 2027 CSAT, the government will assign dedicated personnel to test sites to identify smart glasses. A rapid-response system will link the Ministry of Education with metropolitan and provincial education offices.

The HRDK will establish a cheating tip-off center to analyze reports and online allegations. Grading experts will review answer sheets from first and second rounds for any flagged suspicious cases. If experts find clear grounds for suspicion, authorities plan to refer those cases to the police. A KRX spokesperson said they invalidated a June exam result and barred an applicant for five years. The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency is investigating Han after he submitted a written confession.

A medical student in the greater Seoul area claimed to achieve a 98.6 average percentile using a camera. A Grade 9 civil servant stated they felt no remorse because their job requires little specialized expertise. Singer Ateez's J-Hope encouraged students who worked hard while urging adults to strengthen safeguards. Other users criticized the anonymous posters for their lack of remorse regarding the alleged cheating. The identities and exam results of the anonymous posters have not been verified by authorities.

The controversy grew after Han admitted to using generative AI and electronic devices on his certification exam. HRDK already detected 12 cases of smart glasses cheating for fire protection and information processing engineers. A similar incident involving smart glasses occurred during a Korea Exchange recruitment exam in June. Training for smart glasses inspectors took place on November 11 at the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education. These events have led to increased worries about AI-assisted cheating across the country.

The government will refer confirmed cheating cases to the police or other investigative agencies for further action. Authorities are currently tightening anticheating measures ahead of the annual college entrance exam scheduled for Thursday. The police Provincial Special Detective Corps is leading the investigation into the tax accountant exam scandal. It remains open whether the anonymous online claims are true or contain false information. The articles do not state if any other specific exams will be reviewed.

stories.Headline: South Korea pushes a health data law that lets researchers use pseudonymized medical records without patient consent
stories.Summary:
The government is pushing the Digital Healthcare Act, which would let pseudonymized medical information be used broadly without individual consent to promote medical AI development and health research, and the plan has sparked controversy. The Ministry of Health and Welfare and the National Assembly are seeking to enact the law, with passage targeted within the year, according to the 16th report. The Lee Jae Myung government had presented as a national agenda the building of an AI expressway to leap into the top three AI powers. It stated that in the bio and healthcare sectors the government would collect and link data to create a data ecosystem. Critics say the bill lowers the threshold for data use without adequate personal information safeguards.

The core of the bill is to establish a legal basis for the secondary use of personal health and medical information and to build large-scale datasets on that basis. At present, pseudonymized medical data can be used for research when individuals are hard to identify, but data collection is restricted and external transfer must be approved by the medical institutions holding the data. Under the bill, the Minister of Health and Welfare may request data provision from the National Health Insurance Service, the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service, medical data-centered hospitals and participating medical institutions. Absent special reasons, institutions that receive requests must comply. For example, if the ministry requests from Hospital A the clinical information of patients who underwent cancer surgery in a given year, the hospital must provide it in pseudonymized form unless there are special reasons not to.

A Ministry of Health and Welfare official explained that a researcher who wishes to use health and medical data must undergo review at each individual institution. The official said review criteria and procedures differ across institutions, so it often takes more than a year just to collect the data. The official also said the government has no authority to oversee whether the reviews are being conducted properly. Lee Sang-yun, chief research fellow at Research Community Health and Alternatives and an occupational and environmental medicine specialist, said that if his medical information were to be used to advance the AI industry, many people would likely not agree.

He said there is currently no consent process in place that ensures individual autonomy. Civil society groups, labor circles and patient organizations are demanding supplements, saying protections for patient rights and personal information are lacking compared with the industrial use of medical information. The data provided may include genetic information or whether the patient has a rare disease, which can allow inferences about the patient and the family disease history. Information on rare diseases with only a few dozen patients may, when combined with other information, identify an individual.

Kim Sung-Ju, head of the Korea Severe Disease Alliance, said at a National Assembly forum held on the 2nd that if research achievements based on patient information come back as high-priced pharmaceuticals or treatment technologies, the costs will again be borne by patients and the public. The current bill does not specify a right for individuals to refuse the provision of their information. The UK and Germany institutionally guarantee a patient's right not to agree to the use of their health and medical information for research and similar purposes. In England, the National Health Service operates a National Data Opt-out system that allows patients to refuse the use of their medical information for research, policymaking and similar uses.

Patients can register or withdraw their refusal at any time via the website or by phone. Another issue raised is that even if particular researchers or companies obtain industrial benefits from research using medical information, there is no structure that allows the patients who provided the information or the public to share in those benefits. stories.Headline: Nvidia expects AI accelerator shortages to persist through fiscal 2028
stories.Summary:
Nvidia expects a shortage of its artificial intelligence accelerators to continue through the end of fiscal 2028, according to a report from Hanwha Investment & Securities on November 17. This prolonged supply constraint occurs despite a leadership transition and stricter United States restrictions on shipments to China. The company previously projected revenue growth of roughly 70 percent for that fiscal year, though former CEO Jensen Huang noted that demand could drive growth near 100 percent without supply limits.

The current market situation requires a shift in supply distribution, as unmet global demand from sovereign AI projects and model developers may absorb chips originally meant for China. Nvidia has committed 36 billion dollars to cloud capacity as of the second quarter of fiscal 2027 and seeks to mobilize over 500 billion dollars through an external financing platform. Additionally, proposed U.S. legislation like the MATCH Act, the Chip Security Act, and the AI OVERWATCH Act could restrict Chinese firms such as YMTC and CXMT from maintaining or expanding equipment. These changes are expected to benefit Samsung Electronics and SK hynix by reducing the risk of a global memory oversupply.

Interim CEO Colette Kress, who has served as chief financial officer since 2013, is now responsible for the company's capital allocation and investment strategies. Nvidia has stated that it intends to honor all existing customer commitments during this transition, although the terms for new financial support may become more stringent. Hanwha analyst Park Jun-young explained that while regulations might alter investment timing or customer mixes, they are unlikely to damage the structural demand for memory. He noted that limiting the growth of Chinese memory makers will likely provide a positive long-term outlook for the South Korean industry.

The broader customer base for GPUs now includes AI cloud providers and enterprises, which account for 45.3 percent of data center revenue compared to 54.7 percent from traditional hyperscalers. This diversification helps sustain demand even if some neocloud operators experience delays in their financing. Analysts will continue to monitor whether some demand from China is being met indirectly through operators in third countries. If these transactions are blocked, it could affect some sales, but the overall trajectory for AI infrastructure remains strong.

stories.Headline: KOSPI reclaims 5,000 mark as AI semiconductor stocks rally
stories.Summary:
The domestic stock market reclaimed the 5,000 mark on November 18, 2026. This strong rebound happened in just one day after a massive selling bomb. Global artificial intelligence semiconductor leaders provided tailwinds that boosted the morning opening. The KOSPI index opened at 5,098.82, which was up 130.34 points. This increase represented a 2.62 percent rise from the previous trading session.

The KOSPI index continued its bullish trend around 5,100 as of 9:50 a.m. The KOSDAQ opened at 664.93 and reached 666.71, recovering from a 650.06 close. Samsung Electronics rose around 4 percent to explore the 198,000 to 200,000 won range. SK hynix surged 5 to 6 percent to move above 1.1 million won. The won/dollar exchange rate started at 1,334 won, down 4.2 won from 1,338.2.

A financial investment industry official diagnosed the previous plunge as a complex interplay of factors. This person said the drop resulted from valuation burdens and deteriorated short-term supply and demand. The official described the current rebound as natural bargain hunting driven by global AI earnings. They noted that sustainability depends on the high bandwidth memory competitiveness of two major firms. This official suggested that foreign net buying must continue to settle at 5,000.

Foreign investors in the KOSPI recorded net purchases in the mid-100 billion won range. Institutional investors sold between 90 billion and 120 billion won for risk management. Retail investors in the KOSPI showed a mixed trend of 10 to 40 billion won. In the KOSDAQ, foreigners and institutions net bought 4.5 billion and 500 million won. Retail investors in the KOSDAQ market recorded net selling of 1.4 billion won.

The market had previously surrendered the 5,000 mark for the first time in nine months. New York markets underwent a correction due to hawkish Federal Reserve remarks and infrastructure concerns. Investors previously worried about the U.S.-China technological hegemony conflict and the so-called Jensen Huang risk. Retail investors had previously engaged in massive bargain hunting totaling 1.68 trillion won. The global dollar index had recently broken its highest level in 19 months.

Investors must now monitor the continuity of foreign supply and demand and exchange rates. They are required to watch changes in the policy stance of U.S. monetary authorities. The articles leave open whether this rebound will lead to a trending mainstream rise. It remains uncertain if Samsung Electronics and SK hynix will practically support the stock price. The volatility of the global exchange rate market remains a factor for careful monitoring.

stories.Headline: Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin admits Korea cannot guarantee detection of AI cheating before the CSAT
stories.Summary:
Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin admitted that authorities cannot guarantee the detection of AI cheating before the college entrance exam. This admission occurred on November 16 during a National Assembly Education Committee meeting held in Yeouido, Seoul. The minister spoke during a plenary meeting while answering questions from lawmakers about the security of the upcoming test. He acknowledged that countermeasures against miniature cameras and similar equipment would probably not be perfect for the examination. These statements were made just two days before the start of the College Scholastic Ability Test in Korea.

The government will now require candidates to surrender smart devices and block public Wi-Fi at all examination centers. Authorities also announced the formation of an interagency task force to handle the threat of AI assisted cheating. These new measures were announced on November 16 to protect the integrity of the largest annual national examination. The government is also ordering a retrospective review of 528 national exams following a major AI cheating scandal. These changes aim to prevent the use of sophisticated electronic devices during the high stakes university admission process.

Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin told People Power Party Rep. Park Jeong-hun that he could not identify every cheating case. He stated that he did not think the government could guarantee the detection of all AI assisted cheating attempts. The prime minister demanded vigorous effort to prevent violations and called for harsh punishment for those who cheat. He emphasized that the nation must prepare carefully as it approaches the biggest test day of the year. The minister's candid remarks have led some to describe his current position as irresponsible given the timing.

Some students and parents are demanding that the CSAT be postponed because of the intense fear of cheating. These groups worry that the fairness of university admissions will be undermined if the government cannot stop AI. Other affected parties include candidates in professional qualification exams, university essay tests, and various school based academic assessments. The public confidence in the system that determines educational opportunities for young people is now at serious risk. Many feel that the government responses lag far behind the rapidly evolving methods used by those who cheat.

AI cheating became more apparent after the top scorer on the certified tax accountant examination made several shocking revelations. In May, a candidate in Gwangju was caught using AI equipped glasses during a fire protection engineering certification exam. Prosecutors sought a summary judgment against that candidate for violating the National Technical Qualifications Act during the May test. Other cases have emerged in the Law School Admission Test, English proficiency tests, and various national professional qualification examinations. Online vendors have openly sold cheating kits, and button camera sets have reportedly sold out to prospective examinees.

The government must now procure and install additional equipment, which presents considerable practical difficulties with only two days remaining. Authorities must decide if they can comprehensively restrict communication between the examination rooms and all outside parties. Other countries have already revised professional exams, prohibited digital devices, or introduced measures to block all wireless communications. The articles leave open whether the current interagency task force can actually ensure a fair testing environment for students. It remains unclear if the government can restore public confidence before the College Scholastic Ability Test officially begins.

stories.Headline: South Korea forms emergency team to stop AI cheating in national exams
stories.Summary:
An anonymous user on the online community DC Inside claimed to have used artificial intelligence to cheat on the 2024 Suneung exam. This individual allegedly used a miniature camera disguised as a shirt button and a smartphone to obtain an average percentile score of 98.6. These claims surfaced shortly after Han Won-seok, the top scorer on this year's tax accountant qualification exam, confessed to using similar AI tools. Han admitted to using a miniature camera and generative AI during both rounds of the national exam in April and July. He scored 397.5 out of 400 points and achieved perfect scores in three of the four subjects.

The current situation requires the Education Ministry to implement strict measures to prevent the use of hidden cameras and smart glasses. YouTuber Kim Min-woo, known as Mimiminu, has urged the government to postpone the upcoming Suneung to ensure proper security. He noted that the exam was previously delayed in 2017 due to the Pohang earthquake and in 2020 because of the COVID-19 pandemic. To combat these threats, Prime Minister Han Seong-sook vowed on Tuesday to root out AI cheating by activating an interagency emergency response team. The government plans to ban smart devices and deploy additional staff at testing sites to maintain the integrity of the process.

Several education experts have expressed deep concern regarding the ability of authorities to detect modern cheating devices. Kim Min-woo explained that tiny devices hidden in bracelets or buttons can solve complex questions very quickly. Kang Sung-tae, the founder of Gongsin.com, argued that checking for thick-framed glasses is insufficient because many smart glasses from China have discreet designs. He stated that he has warned for years that AI-assisted cheating was inevitable and hoped his warnings would raise awareness. These experts believe that the current screening methods are outdated and cannot stop sophisticated technology.

The South Korean government is now racing to curb these technological breaches before the college entrance exam takes place this Thursday. Authorities are focusing on identifying a wide variety of smart glasses and other wearable electronics that students might smuggle into the rooms. The Education Ministry must now decide if the existing laws allow for a schedule change to better prepare for these threats. If the government cannot guarantee a fair environment, the pressure to delay the exam may increase. More to follow.

stories.Headline: SK hynix nearly doubles revenue from its largest customer to 35 trillion won
stories.Summary:
SK hynix generated nearly 35 trillion won in revenue from its largest customer, believed to be Nvidia, during the first three quarters of 2026. This figure of 34.98 trillion won, or about 26.17 billion dollars, nearly doubled the 17.36 trillion won recorded during the same period last year. The company reported these results on November 17, noting that the customer accounted for 14.79 percent of total revenue. Growth was particularly sharp in the third quarter, which added approximately 17.37 trillion won to the total.

The surge was driven by mass production of sixth-generation high-bandwidth memory, known as HBM4, and a 40 percent increase in server-grade DDR5 sales. Revenue from the United States reached 147.74 trillion won, while China contributed 56.14 trillion won, together making up 86.2 percent of total revenue. SK hynix spent 10.09 trillion won on research and development and 31.22 trillion won on capital expenditure through the third quarter. The company also paid 1.46 trillion won in cumulative cash dividends, including a third-quarter payout of 20,000 won per share.

Company representatives stated that their supply volumes for DRAM and HBM are effectively sold out through 2029. They noted that long-term supply agreements with 14 companies have already secured more than 50 percent of total production capacity for 2027 and 2028. The firm is also expanding its reach to other major clients, with a second customer believed to be Google or Microsoft contributing 23.85 trillion won. This trend indicates that demand for high-bandwidth memory is spreading as more technology companies develop their own artificial intelligence chips.

stories.Headline: Top tax exam scorer admits using AI to cheat as Korea plans glasses checks for national tests
stories.Summary:
The top scorer of this year's national tax accountant qualification exam admitted to using AI to cheat on the test. This examinee used a miniature camera to photograph questions and then checked the answers on a smartphone via an AI. Educators and exam boards now worry that traditional supervision cannot keep up with smaller and cheaper AI powered cheating tools. These tools are becoming harder to detect as methods for using them are shared on various online community platforms. The Human Resources Development Service of Korea administers the tax exam and prohibits all electronic and communication devices.

The Ministry of Education will visually inspect glasses before the College Scholastic Ability Test on Thursday, November 19, 2026. Proctors received training on November 11 at the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education building in Yongsan District, central Seoul. Some overseas platforms sell cheating sets with cameras, earphones, and batteries for around 60,000 won, which is about 45 dollars. Other available tools include AI pens that convert handwriting to digital text and smart rings that connect to AI glasses. Authorities will also investigate potential AI assisted cheating across 528 national exams and tighten checks for the 2027 CSAT.

The Human Resources Development Service of Korea failed to detect the cheating despite its strict ban on electronic devices. Professor Park Ju-hyung of Gyeongin National University of Education said miniature earphones could also be used to cheat during interviews. He warned that detecting cheating will be harder if communication devices are eventually integrated with parts of the human body. Professor Kim Byung-chan of Kyung Hee University stated that old testing methods can no longer effectively distinguish the abilities of candidates. He believes examinations should assess the thought process used to reach an answer rather than just the final result.

An 18 year old examinee surnamed Yoo worried that thick framed glasses might raise suspicion during the upcoming visual inspections. Yoo suggested that officials should use radio frequency detectors to thoroughly check whether students are carrying any forbidden electronic devices. Some online communities suggested using ultrasonic cleaners for glasses or installing electromagnetic pulse devices to block all wireless communications. Experts responded that ultrasonic cleaners may be ineffective and installing blocking devices at every national site would be impractical. Parents and students argue that technological measures are necessary because some cheating devices cannot be detected with the naked eye.

Equipment for cheating has been readily available for years on overseas online shopping platforms that provide detailed concealment instructions. Some users on the Blind community and other social media platforms share foolproof methods for using AI during exams. One method involves using a miniature camera and earphones to receive AI solved answers every five seconds during a test. Current AI glasses can be distinguished by physical features, but more sophisticated devices are making supervision increasingly difficult. These advances in technology challenge the security of traditional exams as detection methods struggle to keep pace with tools.

The government has vowed zero tolerance against cheating with AI glasses as it implements new visual inspection protocols for students. President Park Joo-ho of Daelim University suggested designing questions that AI cannot answer or evaluating how candidates use AI. Some experts believe the only solution is to allow AI use during examinations instead of trying to prohibit it. The articles leave open whether the government will adopt these fundamental changes to the design of national qualification exams. It remains unclear if radio frequency detectors or other technological tools will be deployed to replace simple visual inspections.

stories.Headline: Reporter uses AI glasses to solve difficult CSAT math questions in 22 minutes
stories.Summary:
On November 16, a Kyunghyang Shinmun reporter used AI glasses to solve 2026 College Scholastic Ability Test questions. The reporter tested the device on math and science sections to see if cheating was possible. This experiment showed that difficult math killer questions could be solved in one to two minutes. The reporter finished the entire math section in 22 minutes and scored 98 points. A tricky Korean language question was answered by the AI in only one second.

The reporter used Rokid Glass AI from the Chinese company Rokid, which was released last January. These glasses cost about 750 dollars, weigh 49 grams, and look like ordinary horn-rimmed glasses. The device used the Gemini AI model and required a 20 minute setup before starting. The reporter solved 30 math questions and 20 Life Science I questions using the device. The science section took 12 minutes and 44 seconds, resulting in a score of 34.

Senior Staff Reporter Jeong Ji-yun performed the test and found the AI produced answers very quickly. The reporter noted that the AI provided correct choices and explanations for each wrong option. It was observed that the display on the lens was not visible to nearby people. However, the reporter mentioned that unnatural head movements and touching the temple could look suspicious. The reporter also found that the battery drained from 75 percent to 30 percent quickly.

Education authorities are preparing to ban AI glasses from test sites because the CSAT is three days away. This follows cheating reports in national technical qualification tests and the certified tax accountant exam. A top scorer in the tax exam admitted to using an ultra-small camera for cheating. Other suspected methods include modified calculators, hidden vibrating devices, and wireless bone-conduction earphones. These technologies threaten the fairness of the CSAT, which is a key gateway in Korean society.

The Human Resources Development Service of Korea detected smart glasses in four of five cheating cases. Most of those cases involved the Rokid model used by the reporter in this experiment. General purpose AI models struggled with science subjects that require specific training like pedigree analysis. Major generative AIs gave conflicting wrong answers to the same Korean question only one year ago. This shows that AI progress has been steep and is becoming more sophisticated.

Authorities cannot deploy radio-frequency or metal detectors to every nationwide test site within three days. Current proctoring manuals have clear limits when policing these advanced AI devices. Professor Choi Kyung-jin stated that existing exam management rules make it difficult to detect AI cheating. He argued that new rules are needed because AI advancement is an unstoppable tide. The articles leave open how the government will effectively stop all future AI cheating.
