stories.Headline: South Korea plans to develop eight AI chips and two semiconductor IP assets by 2030
stories.Summary:
The South Korean government announced a plan on November 12, 2026, to develop eight domestic artificial intelligence chips and two semiconductor intellectual property assets by 2030. This initiative was finalized during the second-half 2026 AI Semiconductor M.AX Alliance General Assembly held at the Four Seasons Hotel in Seoul. The project aims to secure on-device AI semiconductors for critical sectors including defense, robotics, home appliances, and the automotive industry. These specialized chips will process data directly on devices rather than relying on external servers for processing. More than 150 participants from research institutions, academia, and industry attended the meeting to coordinate these efforts.

The K-On-Device AI Semiconductor Technology Development Project, launched in June, requires an investment of 800.2 billion won, which is approximately 600.53 million dollars. The government will develop one chip for autonomous vehicles, one for humanoid robots, one for collaborative robots, one for agricultural robots, and one for unmanned drones. Three chips will be created for smart home appliances, with one of these being accelerated for commercialization by more than a year. The two intellectual property assets will focus on chips for extreme environments and advanced manufacturing processes. Samsung Electronics will provide 21 prototype-production allocations in 2027, including three on the 2nm process, four on 4nm, three on 5nm, three on 8nm, three on 14nm, and five on 28nm.

Lee Min-woo, the director general of the Industrial Growth Office at the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, is responsible for overseeing the growth path. He stated that true cooperation in the semiconductor industry must be shown through the adoption of jointly developed technologies in actual products. Lee believes that the manufacturing competitiveness of customer companies should lead to commercial success and technological capabilities for domestic fabless companies. To manage the roadmap, a public-private strategic committee will be established and co-chaired by the vice minister of trade, industry and energy. Kim Jin-sang, the president of Kyung Hee University, will also serve as a co-chair for this strategic committee.

The committee will review annual development plans every year and coordinate technical challenges among the participating institutions and companies. Domestic and international semiconductor intellectual property providers have agreed to offer more flexible payment terms and common packages to lower design barriers. Customer companies will contribute by sharing technical requirements and providing testbeds in real-world operating environments to establish practical validation cases. Samsung Electronics plans to coordinate with existing production schedules and prioritize requests to ease bottlenecks in prototype manufacturing. This comprehensive approach integrates chip development with the driver software and modules used in final end products.

stories.Headline: SEMIFIVE uses 3D-IC platform for Preferred Networks AI inference chip and targets first quarter 2027 tape-out
stories.Summary:
The custom application-specific integrated circuit design company SEMIFIVE announced on November 17, 2026, that it is using a specialized 3D integrated circuit platform for a new artificial intelligence inference chip. This project is being developed for Preferred Networks, which is creating the MN-Core L2000 Series to enhance overall performance. The company is managing the entire process on a turnkey basis, which includes everything from the initial design implementation to the final supply of mass-produced wafers. This advanced semiconductor chip is currently scheduled to finish its design phase and enter the tape-out stage during the first quarter of 2027.

The new platform requires vertically stacking logic semiconductors and dynamic random-access memory to create hundreds of thousands of interconnects for faster data exchange. This specific architecture is designed to provide higher effective bandwidth than high-bandwidth memory while improving power efficiency through shorter data-transfer distances. By eliminating the need for an intermediate substrate known as an interposer, the company can simplify packaging processes and reduce total manufacturing costs. The vertical stacking also reduces the horizontal footprint of the chip, which makes the technology ideal for edge devices that require smaller form factors.

SEMIFIVE stated that they invested in this technology early to meet the anticipated demand for high-performance artificial intelligence chips. They explained that this platform could potentially address current supply constraints found within the high-bandwidth memory market. The company also noted that they plan to expand these applications into the fields of robotics, smart devices, and on-device artificial intelligence. To showcase this progress, SEMIFIVE and Preferred Networks are operating a joint exhibition booth at Supercomputing 2026 in Chicago from November 17 to 19.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: Prime Minister Han orders smart device checks and weighs Wi-Fi cutoff to stop AI cheating on national exams
stories.Summary:
Prime Minister Han Seong-sook directed eight ministries and agencies to prevent AI-assisted cheating during a meeting on Monday, November 16, 2026. The government will implement thorough smart device checks for students taking the College Scholastic Ability Test this Thursday. Officials are also considering a nationwide cutoff of public Wi-Fi at all testing sites to stop the use of wireless devices. These measures target advanced equipment that is difficult to detect, including AI glasses, ultrasmall cameras, and wireless earphones.

The Ministry of Education will lead a pangovernment emergency response team for the 2027 academic year CSAT to manage these screenings. Test-takers must hand in all smart devices, and the government will scrutinize results for implausibly high scores after the exam. Confirmed cheaters face stern penalties, including the nullification of their results, restrictions on future exams, and criminal investigations. Additionally, the Ministry of Employment and Labor and the Human Resources Development Service of Korea will overhaul national certification exams by installing smart screening gates.

Prime Minister Han stated that fairness in exams is a basic principle that upholds trust in society and must not be damaged. She urged officials to mobilize every capability to create a fair environment while ensuring that honest students do not suffer. Han also ordered the immediate voiding of results for the top scorer on this year's certified tax accountant exam who admitted to cheating. This individual will be barred from taking the exam for five years while the police conduct a rigorous investigation.

The government believes existing management is limited against new AI cheating techniques, leading to the creation of a pangovernment task force. This group will review how various ministries manage exams to establish common responses against smart device violations. Authorities will also operate a center for reporting cheating and investigate suspicious cases alongside the police. These broader efforts aim to protect the integrity of 528 national exams from the threats posed by advancing artificial intelligence.

stories.Headline: Foreign investors sell tech shares as Jensen Huang's Nvidia exit sinks Kospi 3.59 percent
stories.Summary:
Foreign investors sold off technology shares on Monday, November 16, 2026, causing the Kospi to tank. The main bourse lost 190.03 points to close at 5,100.5, which represents a 3.59 percent decline. This drop extended a losing streak to three sessions amid growing fears of an artificial intelligence bubble. The turmoil followed the ouster of Jensen Huang, who served as the chief executive officer of Nvidia. Investors remained cautious while awaiting an earnings report from Nvidia and the Nasdaq debut of Anthropic.

The market sell-off required significant adjustments for several major companies and financial instruments in South Korea. Samsung Electronics fell 4.47 percent to 196,800 won, while chipmaker SK hynix plunged 7.89 percent to 1.12 million won. Samsung Electro-Mechanics sank 8.19 percent to 785,000 won, and SK Square tumbled 9.71 percent to 688,000 won. Hyundai Motor slipped 1.48 percent to 265,500 won, and the local currency rose 1.9 won to 1,335.7 won against the dollar. Three-year Treasury yields shed 1.6 basis points to 3.743, and five-year government bond returns fell 1.1 basis points to 3.830.

Shinhan Securities analyst Kang Jin-hyuk explained that the market came under pressure from persistent concerns over Nvidia. He noted that these worries weighed heavily on semiconductor and other AI-related stocks during the trading day. Foreigners and institutions sold a net 1.38 trillion won and 451.26 billion won, respectively, while individuals bought a net 1.34 trillion won. Trade volume remained light at 209.27 million shares worth 15.8 trillion won, or approximately 11.8 billion dollars. Decliners far outnumbered advancers by a count of 612 to 263.

The broader context involves uncertainty regarding the global AI industry after the exit of a key figure like Jensen Huang. Investors are worried that the high-profile listing of Anthropic could divert necessary investment from other technology stocks. This environment has created a volatile atmosphere for AI infrastructure firms that previously grew using Nvidia cash. Market participants are now closely watching the upcoming earnings results to determine the future of AI spending. More to follow.

stories.Summary:
Prime Minister Han Seong-sook announced on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, that the government would take aggressive measures to stop artificial intelligence cheating. These actions come just before the College Scholastic Ability Test, which is scheduled to take place this Thursday. The government is reacting to a recent scandal where the top scorer of the certified tax accountant exam admitted to using AI to cheat. Prime Minister Han described the use of such technology during high-stakes examinations as a social evil that must be eliminated.

The new security plan requires the activation of an interagency emergency response team and the deployment of additional proctors to all test sites. Students are completely banned from possessing smart devices, meaning all smartphones must be powered off and turned in before the exam begins. Officials will conduct thorough inspections of clothing collars, sleeves, buttons, and accessories like glasses and watches to find hidden tech. All personal bags must be stored in hallways, where authorities will check for active devices and tighten the management of nearby Wi-Fi networks.

Prime Minister Han Seong-sook stated that the government will apply a zero-tolerance policy to strictly penalize any person caught cheating. She explained that suspected cases will lead to thorough investigations and stern actions, including the invalidation of the exam and the revocation of eligibility. The administration may also file criminal complaints or request formal police investigations for those who attempt to use AI. These strict measures are intended to ensure the integrity of the national entrance exam following the shocking tax accountant confession.

stories.Headline: PM calls for considering disabling Wi-Fi at CSAT test sites to prevent AI cheating
stories.Summary:
Prime Minister Han Seong-sook instructed government officials on Monday, November 16, 2026, to implement strict measures against artificial intelligence cheating. These urgent orders come just three days before the nationwide College Scholastic Ability Test, which is scheduled for this Thursday. The government is reacting to a shocking confession from the top scorer of this year's certified tax accountant exam. This individual admitted on Sunday to using a smartphone, a miniature camera, and generative AI to cheat on two rounds of that test. He further confessed to using these same sophisticated methods to cheat on a certified public accountant exam.

The new requirements involve the education ministry ensuring that all test takers turn in every smart device before the exam begins. Officials must conduct thorough checks to confirm that no smart devices are possessed by students during the testing period. Additionally, the science ministry has been asked to actively consider disabling all public Wi-Fi signals at the test sites. Prime Minister Han also announced the establishment of an interagency emergency response team for the 2027 CSAT to create comprehensive preventive measures. The government intends to investigate any abnormal signs that defy common sense after the exam using objective data.

Prime Minister Han stated that the government must concentrate all national capabilities to prepare against misconduct involving advanced AI technology. She explained that conventional exam management methods are now limited because AI technology is advancing so rapidly. The prime minister emphasized that upholding the fairness of examinations is a fundamental duty directly linked to public trust. She urged each government ministry to develop effective measures and ensure they are implemented thoroughly across all state-administered exams. Han called for the development of advanced detection technologies, including those leveraging AI, to counter ultra-small electronic devices and outside help.

The government is now scrambling to prevent similar AI-assisted cheating from occurring during the upcoming college entrance examinations. This concern follows reports of four separate cheating cases involving AI glasses at middle and high schools earlier this year. Authorities have indicated that they will pursue criminal punishment and a three-year exam ban for any CSAT cheaters using AI glasses. Officials are now tasked with creating a comprehensive government strategy to respond to increasingly diverse and sophisticated methods of cheating. They aim to create a fair testing environment that the public can trust through these new technical measures.

stories.Headline: Experts warn AI cheating detectors will not be ready for this Thursday's national college entrance exam
stories.Summary:
Experts warn that specialized detectors designed to stop AI cheating will not be ready for the national college entrance exam this Thursday. The urgency for these safeguards grew after a thirty four year old man surnamed Han confessed on YouTube to cheating on a tax accountant exam. Han admitted that he used a micro camera to send exam questions to an AI and then viewed the answers on a smartphone. This incident has forced education officials to seek ways to identify smart glasses and other wireless devices during high stakes testing.

The Korea Communications Agency issued a tender on November 2 to develop a handheld radio detector for AI smart glasses. This device would allow proctors to pick up Bluetooth and Wi-Fi signals, but the technology is still under development. Some suggest using thermal cameras or a method from a Duke University research team that identifies glowing lenses through filming. However, the Radio Waves Act prevents the use of signal jamming except for military or counterterrorism operations. Authorities now plan to investigate potential AI cheating across 528 national exams and tighten checks for the 2027 college entrance exam.

Ryu Dong kyu, a professor of optometry at Shinsung University, believes the most reliable method is detecting wireless signals. He suggests that proctors should inspect glasses in person and use professional opticians to attach certifying stickers to approved eyewear. Yoon Sang ho, a professor at the KAIST Graduate School of Culture Technology, argues that manufacturers should build safeguards into the devices. Yoon believes it is technically possible to block modified devices or stop them from working when the camera light is covered.

The current situation leaves proctors relying on manual inspections because signal blocking is illegal and thermal cameras are impractical for every classroom. Education officials recently held training sessions on November 11 at the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education to demonstrate smart glasses. These efforts aim to prevent a repeat of the tax accountant scandal before the nationwide exam begins. Future security will likely depend on the development of the handheld detectors and stricter manufacturing rules for smart wearables.

stories.Headline: South Korea and Philippines agree to deepen cooperation in AI and defense industry

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung and Philippine President Ferdinand Romualdez Marcos Jr. held a summit on Monday, November 16, 2026, in Manila. This meeting occurred on the sidelines of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit and marked the third time the two leaders have met. They previously held discussions in Gyeongju, South Korea, last year and again in the Philippine capital during March. The leaders focused on strengthening ties in traditional sectors and expanding their partnership into several emerging industries.

The agreement requires deeper cooperation in defense manufacturing, infrastructure, shipbuilding, artificial intelligence, nuclear power plants, aerospace, and disaster management. Bilateral trade between the two nations reached US$21.3 billion during the first nine months of this year, which already exceeds the previous annual record. The two countries signed a memorandum of understanding on science and technology to expand collaboration into smart farming. Additionally, they signed a grant aid agreement to help the Korea International Cooperation Agency implement various projects in the Philippines.

Spokesperson Kim Sung-wan stated that President Lee requested continued support from the Philippine government to help South Korean companies expand their operations. The spokesperson noted that both leaders pledged to foster mutually beneficial cooperation in areas where their bilateral ties are already strong. President Lee arrived in Manila on Monday for a four-day trip to engage with regional leaders. He is scheduled to travel to Shenzhen, China, next to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit.

stories.Headline: Cohesity expands into security and AI and grows South Korean customer base to about 1,000 clients
stories.Summary:
Cohesity expanded its business operations into the fields of security and artificial intelligence during a period ending in November 2026. The company announced these developments during a media roundtable held at the Westin Seoul Parnas hotel on November 17. This strategic shift helped the firm grow its South Korean customer base to approximately 1,000 local clients. These new customers include major businesses such as Lotte, Kolon, Ahn-Gook Pharmaceutical, Hyundai Mobis, and NongHyup Bank.

The company now organizes its offerings around three main pillars including DataProtect, FortKnox, and Gaia. Lotte Innovate adopted DataProtect early this year to manage backups for corporate servers and cloud systems using immutability technology. Ahn-Gook Pharmaceutical implemented FortKnox to isolate backup data from operating systems to protect against ransomware and natural disasters. Kolon Benit integrated the Gaia platform, which was developed with Nvidia, into its enterprise content management system for AI data analytics. These platforms utilize a scale-out architecture that increases processing capacity linearly by adding more servers or nodes.

Sanjay Poonen, the president and CEO of Cohesity, stated that South Korea is currently one of the top ten markets for the company. Lee Sang-hoon, the head of Cohesity Korea, noted that the security business is growing by more than 20 percent while AI is expanding explosively. Lee mentioned that the company handled business for ten of the largest firms in the country this year. He explained that Gaia improves productivity because most corporate data is unstructured and difficult for employees to search manually. Cohesity Korea previously reported revenue of 5.12 billion won during the last fiscal year.

The company concluded a series of regional events with the Catalyst on Tour: Seoul session on the afternoon of November 17. This event followed previous sessions held in the cities of Busan, Gwangju, and Daejeon. During the Seoul event, Sanjay Poonen and Chief Product Officer Mercy delivered keynote speeches to the attendees. Greg Statton, the chief technology officer for Asia Pacific and Japan, presented the future technical roadmap for the Gaia platform.

SK Innovation selected three artificial intelligence startups to receive commercialization support on November 17, 2026. The company hosted the AI Impact Solution Day 2026 event at the Startup Venture Campus Seoul in Mapo-gu. This selection followed a four month period of technology validation and expert mentoring for ten teams. These finalists were chosen from a total pool of 186 applicants who sought to solve energy and social challenges.

Each of the three winning teams will receive up to 20 million won in funding for commercialization. The grand prize was awarded to Peering for an AI tool that helps special education teachers manage administrative reports. Saemton earned the excellence award for its AI technology focused on dispatch and route optimization. PostAlign received the merit award for developing a medical AI system that supports clinical decisions for rare cancer treatments.

SK Innovation is responsible for the program and intends to provide further development support for these technologies. The company stated that it will help the winners with follow on commercialization efforts. Officials are also considering ways to connect these startups with various private investors. stories.Headline: DB GlobalChip expands its Nebula AI unit to develop edge AI and in-house power management chips
stories.Summary:
The fabless semiconductor company DB GlobalChip recently reorganized its research and development operations to support next-generation artificial intelligence display driver integrated circuits. On November 16, industry sources reported that the company expanded its existing power management integrated circuit business unit into the Nebula AI Business Unit. This new organization focuses on developing edge AI, mini red-green-blue LED drivers, mini LED controllers, and power management integrated circuits. The company also established a business development team to manage customer sales and identify new sales channels.

The Nebula AI brand integrates a microcontroller unit and a power management integrated circuit with proprietary display driver integrated circuits for mini LED televisions. This technology uses AI algorithms to maximize driving efficiency, which should reduce operating temperatures and power consumption. DB GlobalChip plans to test prototype modules by the end of this year and begin mass production next year. However, the company must still rely on external suppliers for microcontroller units and power management integrated circuits. Developing and commercializing its own proprietary power management integrated circuit technology is expected to take two to three years.

A company official stated that overall market conditions remain challenging because global demand for televisions and Samsung Electronics laptops has weakened. While smartphone display driver integrated circuit demand helped sustain the business this year, the company recorded an operating loss of approximately 5.9 billion won in the third quarter. To address the earnings slump that began last year, the company recently carried out restructuring that reduced its workforce by approximately 10 percent. Industry sources noted that focusing solely on display driver integrated circuits limits profitability in the growing mini LED market.

The company expects that earnings will not improve until after 2028 or 2029 when it secures its own power management integrated circuit technology. By developing these key components in-house, DB GlobalChip aims to lower production costs for television modules by reducing the need for heat dissipation components. This strategic shift allows the company to diversify into a favorable market while recovering from recent financial losses. The firm will continue to integrate these semiconductors to improve the overall efficiency of its next-generation products.

stories.Headline: Soros Fund Management reduces its stake in Nvidia
stories.Summary:
Soros Fund Management reduced its position in Nvidia during the quarter ending September 30. This move represented the largest disclosed reduction in the stock for the fund this year. The investment firm sold approximately 206,000 shares of the company. These shares were valued at as much as 47.4 million dollars. The action occurred as artificial intelligence hype began to cool.

The fund retained a stake worth just under 200 million dollars on September 30. This reduction of nearly a fifth followed earlier additions to the Nvidia position. At least a dozen family offices also reduced holdings, keeping combined positions above 1 billion dollars. Nvidia shares rose 22 percent through September 30, doubling the S&P 500 gain. The company is based in Santa Clara, California.

Dawn Fitzpatrick leads Soros Fund Management and previously served as an executive at UBS Group AG. George Soros is 96 years old and has an estimated worth of 9.7 billion dollars. The articles do not provide direct quotes from these individuals regarding the sale. They note that investors often reassess positions as new tools reshape their perspectives. These details came from required 13F reports for managers overseeing 100 million dollars.

Michael Platt of BlueCrest Capital Management also trimmed his stake in the company. President Donald Trump and some Silicon Valley backers are advocating for the return of the former CEO. Jensen Huang, age 63, was ousted on November 12 following disclosures of extramarital relationships. Some of these relationships were with Nvidia employees and a suspected Chinese spy. The Justice Department suspected the woman of being a spy.

Nvidia was a standout stock as investors chased the artificial intelligence boom. The market turned shakier after a late October New York Times report on Chinese espionage. That report suggested Jensen Huang might have been targeted in an espionage effort. Consequently, the stock has fallen more than 25 percent since that report. The company is now searching for a new chief executive officer.

Nvidia reports its third quarter results on Tuesday with Colette Kress stepping in. The articles leave open whether Jensen Huang will actually return to his role. They do not state if other family offices will further reduce their holdings. The future of the CEO search remains an open question for the company. It is unclear how the espionage allegations will affect future stock performance.

GITSN announced on November 17, 2026, that it has finished developing a new device to detect cheating during exams. This system uses artificial intelligence to identify signals from devices that candidates might use to commit fraud. The company created this technology after a high ranking tax accountant candidate recently used AI to cheat on an examination. GITSN now plans to begin mass production of the hardware after validating the system at various testing centers.

The new device is capable of detecting cellular signals in addition to Bluetooth and Wi-Fi transmissions. It specifically targets the cellular signals generated when candidates use miniature cameras to send test questions for answers. This technology provides an alternative to government detectors that will not be available until next year at the earliest. Furthermore, it avoids violating the Radio Waves Act, which currently prohibits blocking all communications inside examination centers.

A GITSN official explained that the core technology distinguishes signals inside a room from those of nearby base stations. The official stated that the system does not work by disrupting surrounding radio signals with powerful transmissions. Another representative noted that the company already possesses the underlying technologies needed for this specific application. They confirmed that the remaining tasks involve validating the system at centers before starting mass production.

GITSN has developed expertise in wireless signal detection since its establishment in 2000 through fighting illegal filming and hacking. The company manufactures the entire product lineup in house using proprietary Korean technology and signal analysis software. They intend to launch the device simultaneously in South Korea and various overseas markets. Specific product specifications and the official launch schedule will be announced by the company at a later date.

stories.Headline: Jensen Huang resigns from Nvidia amid spying scandal as AI sentiment and markets slide
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang quit Nvidia and admitted to an affair with a woman suspected of spying for China. These events, alongside high interest rates, rattled AI sentiment around November 18, 2026. Stocks, cryptocurrency, gold, and oil all declined together. Bitcoin fell 16 percent from the previous month to around 65,000 dollars. Gold plunged 6.36 percent in a single week.

The U.S. Commerce Department Bureau of Industry and Security implemented a 166-page rule on the 19th. It requires licenses for China to access U.S. AI semiconductor computing power through third-country data centers. Prior licenses are now required for advanced chip exports to Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield rose above 5 percent. The dollar index jumped to 103.695, its highest level since April last year.

Jensen Huang called himself a piece of shit before he resigned from his position. The U.S. government now requires approval for providing AI server performance to countries of security concern. China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs immediately signaled that it would retaliate against these new rules. The Federal Reserve may increase interest rates in December, which has frozen investor sentiment. The Remote Access Security Act in Congress is expected to move faster.

Retail investors bought 835.9 billion won of KODEX KOSDAQ150 Leverage ETFs while the KOSDAQ index fell 16.25 percent. These investors faced a 36.92 percent loss, while inverse ETFs returned between 19 and 21 percent. Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows of 1.1 billion dollars over one week. Domestic semiconductor materials, parts, and equipment makers face increased short-term share price volatility. The KOSPI index fell below 5,000.

South Korean business groups invested 413.3 billion won in AI equity stakes during the first half of this year. The LG Group invested 265.6 billion won, and the Kakao Group invested 156.2 billion won. Kakao placed a 150 billion won bet on the large language model startup Upstage. Total AI investment over two and a half years reached 1.0972 trillion won. This follows a drop to 145.3 billion won last year from 538.5 billion won in 2024.

The market awaits the results of regular shareholder meetings next year regarding corporate governance change. Analysts are watching for improvements in board independence and capital allocation efficiency. South Korea must determine if it can maintain its technology gap against Chinese 8.6-generation facilities. The impact of the new U.S. licensing system on the AI supply chain remains uncertain. Short-term volatility for related stocks is considered unavoidable.

stories.Headline: OpenAI adds computer-use agents and over 20 plugins to ChatGPT for Healthcare
stories.Summary:
OpenAI announced on November 16, 2026, that it is expanding ChatGPT for Healthcare with advances in computer-use agents, improved trusted clinical search, and more than 20 new healthcare plugins. The computer-use agents can navigate existing healthcare software by reading screens, clicking, typing, and moving between applications. OpenAI said it is working with healthcare organizations including Abridge, Ambience, Cigna Healthcare, and CVS Health to process referrals, move documents between systems, and bring together information care teams need. The announcement was reported by HCI Innovation Group on Nov. 17, 2026, in an article by Pietje Kobus-McAllister. The updates are intended to help healthcare organizations reduce time spent navigating disconnected software and streamline workflows from referral management and documentation to insurance verification and care coordination.

The computer-use agents include access controls and audit logs, and organizations can set which applications agents can access and which steps require human review. To support HIPAA-compliant workflows involving protected health information, organizations must use eligible services covered by their BAA with OpenAI, apply required security and retention settings, and extend protections to connected systems. Content shared with ChatGPT for Healthcare is not used to train models. In a blind evaluation, physicians reviewed responses to real-world clinical questions across multiple specialties, including multi-turn conversations, and in over 1300 reviews rated the updated experience more highly across all eight dimensions evaluated, including factual correctness, safety, actionability, and source authoritativeness. All of the more than 20 new plugins are available today in ChatGPT for Healthcare, including through ChartGPT, which brings ChatGPT into the EHR workflow.

The plugin list includes Aiva, Amion, Assort Health, Availity, Extend, Elation Health, Ferry, IMO Health, MCP Server, Infinitus, Relay, K Health, Luma Health, Metriport, Notable Integration Specs, Oracle HDI Overview, PenguinAI Medical Coding, Photon, Redox, Stedi, Subsalt, Trizetto, Turquoise, and UpToDate Expert AI. Elation Health's read-only beta plugin lets primary care practice managers use ChatGPT to identify patients scheduled for the following day who have gaps in insurance, registration, or contact information, and staff receive a list of issues to review and address in Elation's electronic health record before patients arrive. Kyna Fong, co-founder and CEO of Elation Health, said AI earns its place in primary care by helping the people who use it, and that the company earns it by being thoughtful about its use, maintaining control, and using it to make stronger systems. Infinitus is bringing its Relay agents into ChatGPT to support benefits verification and prior authorization workflows, and users can initiate a benefits verification, check the status of a prior authorization and identify next steps, or submit batch requests using a spreadsheet. Ankit Jain, CEO of Infinitus, said the next chapter of AI in healthcare won't be defined by how much information it can surface but by what it can actually accomplish.

The Elation beta is initially available to a limited group of Elation practices, and the company said the approach is designed to keep administrative work with AI while leaving clinical decisions and patient outreach under the control of practice teams. Relay is available to existing Infinitus customers using ChatGPT for Healthcare, and the integration is designed to let healthcare and life sciences organizations access Infinitus agents without leaving ChatGPT. Jain said healthcare is full of complex, interconnected workflows that require more than answering questions, requiring navigating systems, taking action, and following through, and that bringing Infinitus agents into ChatGPT combines frontier AI with specialized healthcare capabilities while maintaining the safeguards healthcare demands. The plugins let teams bring more of their work into the same conversation, including reviewing patient records and hospital protocols, preparing prescriptions for clinician review, coordinating patient outreach, checking insurance eligibility, and analyzing healthcare costs and operational performance. The new plugins join ChatGPT's broader ecosystem of plugins supporting work across industries, from healthcare data and research to documents, presentations, and software development.

OpenAI said healthcare teams need to piece together information from the EHR, hospital policies, scheduling systems, and payer portals to deliver care and manage operations. With ChatGPT for Healthcare, OpenAI is bringing the tools teams already use and the medical evidence they need into one platform to help them spend less time navigating systems and more time caring for patients. In a demo, a clinician uses Voice in the ChatGPT app to ask for help following up on an MRI request, and the agent reviews the chart and drafts an order and patient reply for review. The articles give examples including a care coordinator using Luma Health to find tomorrow's appointments that still need confirmation and TriZetto to check insurance eligibility, and a primary care physician using Metriport to find a discharge summary and UpToDate to check follow-up monitoring. Other examples include an inpatient nurse using AIVA for a hospital's inpatient pump policy and Amion to find the covering endocrinologist, a care navigator using IMO Health, Stedi, and Turquoise Health to compare MRI sites, and a referral manager using Assort Health and Ferry Health for referral review.

ChatGPT for Healthcare customers have computer-use agents in ChatGPT Work and Codex and improved trusted clinical search available today, subject to workspace settings, and workspace administrators can enable new healthcare plugins. Individual clinicians have computer-use agents in ChatGPT Work and Codex and improved trusted clinical search available today, and select plugins are also available. ChatGPT for Clinicians is free for eligible, verified clinicians in the U.S. to review medical evidence and prepare clinical documentation, and both products offer customers a Business Associate Agreement with OpenAI to support HIPAA-compliant workflows. Computer-use agent capability is available in the OpenAI API, ChatGPT Work, and Codex, and customers can purchase ChatGPT for Healthcare directly or through an AWS Marketplace private offer by contacting the sales team. OpenAI said it is continuing to invest in the plugin ecosystem and inviting more healthcare companies to build with it.

stories.Headline: Nvidia cuts its Nokia stake by 56% while Nokia expands its AI and cloud business
stories.Summary:
Nvidia disclosed late Monday that it had sold 93.53 million Nokia shares during the third quarter, cutting its position by 56% and leaving it with 72.86 million shares worth $738.8 million on Sept. 30, down from 166.39 million shares at the end of June. The chipmaker had agreed in October 2025 to invest $1 billion in Nokia at $6.01 a share for a 2.9% stake, alongside a partnership to run Nokia's 5G and future 6G network software on Nvidia chips. Nokia shares fell 5% on Monday to $7.69, a third consecutive session in the red, and slipped another 1% overnight after the stake sale became known. Nvidia also cut its Intel stake by 25% and its Synopsys stake by nearly 10% during the same quarter.

In the same quarter as the stake cut, Nokia's sales to AI and cloud customers rose 123% from a year earlier and orders from those customers grew 118%. On Monday, Nokia teamed up with Nscale, Skeleton, Telia and Verda to form AI Gigafactory Northern, which plans to bid for an EU contract to build and operate computing sites for European businesses, researchers and public agencies, with Nokia supplying the networking equipment. The partners have selected Oulu in Finland, Iru in Estonia and Valmiera in Latvia, and are still choosing a location in Sweden. Nokia also signed a multiyear agreement licensing its video technology for use in ASUS devices, resolving all related patent litigation between the companies, with financial terms kept confidential.

The partnership between the two companies continued after Nvidia reduced its holdings, and last month Nokia reported progress in using Nvidia chips to process radio signals and bring AI services closer to mobile users, citing work with European operators including BT, Deutsche Telekom, Elisa and Orange. On Stocktwits, Nokia retail sentiment has been bearish for a month amid a 1,250% surge in 24-hour message volumes, with several traders eyeing $5, about 35% below Monday's closing price and a dollar below what Nvidia originally paid per share. One user said $5 was their year-end target, another expects Nokia to fall back to $5 or lower, and a third flagged a possible slide to $6 and then $5 by year-end. Nokia's U.S.-listed stock has risen 20% year-to-date.

stories.Headline: Moritz assigns 90 percent of its workload to AI to handle complex cases within 24 hours
stories.Summary:
AI-native law firms are spreading across the United States to provide faster and cheaper legal services. These firms build their practices around artificial intelligence to improve overall efficiency. Nikkei reported on November 17 that these firms are growing rapidly. AI handles the legal work from the first draft through to the substance. Lawyers then verify and review the work produced by AI agents.

Moritz assigns 90 percent of its workload to AI to handle complex cases within 24 hours. Athena reduced a 20 hour complex case to two hours and 40 hour reviews to 40 minutes. Inside Practice notes pricing models include per-document rates, subscriptions, performance-based pricing, and flat fees. Norm AI raised 120 million dollars in a Series C round at a 1.2 billion dollar valuation. Norm Law is the firm associated with the parent company Norm AI.

Pamir Esas, chief executive of Moritz, said corporate fees are 80 to 90 percent lower than established firms. Richard Ferris, co-founder of Covenant, stated that every law firm will be AI-native in five years. Mike Schmidtberger joined Norm Law this year as chairman and partner. He was previously a chairman of the executive committee at Sidley Austin. These leaders emphasize that AI allows for much faster turnaround times.

Citigroup and Morgan Stanley are pressing large law firms to reduce fees due to AI efficiency. Junior associates are affected as their work is displaced and hiring for these roles is shrinking. A Citibank survey found 47 percent of firms saw summer internship hiring fall from a year earlier. Another 49 percent of firms expect next summer's internship hiring to fall further. Established law firms face pressure to cut rates to compete with AI-native firms.

The AI Firm Index showed 60 such firms worldwide as of September, doubling the number from six months prior. More than half of these firms are in the United States, Britain, Australia, and Germany. Crunchbase reported that legal-tech investment reached a record 4.586 billion dollars last year. GCVC is a venture fund for legal AI startups launched by current and former in-house counsel. Traditional firms previously relied on junior associates to prepare documents for senior lawyer sign-off.

Investment in legal-technology startups continues to increase as the use of AI widens in the legal field. The model of AI-native firms is currently spreading to Britain, Australia, and Germany. The articles do not state when the shift to AI-native firms will be complete. They do not specify which other countries might adopt this legal model. The reports leave open how traditional firms will adapt their hiring and billing.

stories.Headline: UNIST Finds Smaller Quantum AI Circuits That Resist Noise
stories.Summary:
Researchers developed a technique to identify essential regions of complex quantum artificial intelligence circuits on November 18, 2026. This method cuts computational load and noise induced errors at the same time. A team led by Professor Yoon Sung-hwan of UNIST developed the process. They worked with a team led by Professor Kim Joong-heon of Korea University. The researchers mathematically proved that high performing small circuits exist inside large quantum neural networks.

The team created an algorithm called Q-Edge-popup to find these circuits in practice. They established a quantum strong lottery ticket hypothesis to account for the characteristics of quantum computation. The findings were presented at the CIKM 2026 conference in Rome from November 7 to 11. The research used a quantum neural network made of 3,840 rotation gates for simulation. This process requires sufficient quantum gates and specific initial settings to produce results close to target outputs.

First author Kwon Hong-gyun said high performing small circuits are likely to exist when specific conditions are met. He noted that these circuits do not exist in every single quantum circuit. Professor Yoon stated the key is searching for circuits that cut gate numbers while maintaining performance. He added that this work helps develop quantum AI models combining efficiency with stability. The research received support from the National Research Foundation of Korea and the Institute of Information & Communications Technology Planning & Evaluation.

The study affected the way researchers approach the slimming of quantum neural network models. In conventional AI, the strong lottery ticket hypothesis allows for slimming without changing weights. This theory could not be applied directly to quantum networks because gate order and measurement affect outcomes. The new algorithm scores each gate based on task performance to build a small circuit. Performance is then pushed higher by fine tuning only the parameters of the remaining gates.

The researchers confirmed the slimming effect through a computer simulation involving handwritten digit image classification. Keeping half of the gates produced a classification accuracy of 75.2 percent without changing any parameters. Training the selected gates raised accuracy to 79.4 percent, which approached the 81.3 percent of the full circuit. In mixed noise environments, the full circuit accuracy plunged 71.3 percentage points from 81.3 percent down to 10.0 percent. A circuit with 25 percent of gates held accuracy at 74.7 percent, down only 1.5 points from 76.2 percent.

The next step involves using these findings to create more stable and efficient quantum AI models. The Q-Edge-popup algorithm allows for the practical location of these high performing small circuits. The researchers proved that keeping a subset of gates with fixed parameters can maintain high accuracy. The articles do not state when these circuits will be used in real hardware. They also leave open how this technique will scale to even larger quantum neural networks.

stories.Headline: US blocks Chinese companies from accessing AI chips through overseas data centers
stories.Summary:
The United States government blocked Chinese companies from indirectly accessing advanced artificial intelligence chips. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security released these export control rules on the 18th. This move extends controls beyond direct exports to cover indirect routes through overseas data centers. The decision has put Samsung Electronics and SK hynix on alert. These Korean chipmakers are watching the situation closely.

Rules apply to data centers providing AI services exceeding 12 million total processing performance to China and other controlled countries. Supplying chips to these centers requires U.S. government approval, and existing services must obtain licenses within 90 days. Licensing requirements tightened for exports to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, and Brazil. The U.S. found Chinese companies avoided restrictions by placing data centers in Southeast Asia and elsewhere. New rules require contract manufacturers and packaging firms to verify design companies and parent companies.

The Bureau of Industry and Security is responsible for these new export control rules. The U.S. government stated that Chinese companies were avoiding restrictions by using overseas data centers. The Federal Reserve released a financial stability report on the 13th regarding AI data center investment. The Fed warned that risk exposure at large U.S. banks is estimated at about 1 trillion dollars. This exposure includes loans and credit extended to technology companies and data center developers.

Samsung could see shrinking orders in its foundry business which manufactures chips for Chinese-affiliated companies. SK hynix faces weaker demand for high-bandwidth memory it supplies to Nvidia. Both companies could be affected if Chinese companies find it harder to use Nvidia graphics processing units. Industry estimates suggest GPUs accessed by China through indirect routes account for 20 percent of global usage. Some observers say the near-term hit to earnings will be limited.

New debt for advanced computing infrastructure exceeded 680 billion dollars from January through October this year. This amount is more than five times the 130 billion dollars raised during all of 2023. Seven large technology companies, including Nvidia, Microsoft, and Oracle, owe over 3 trillion dollars in obligations. Samsung said last month that its entire 2027 high-bandwidth memory supply was already sold. SK hynix has secured substantial volumes through long-term supply contracts with major customers.

Future business environments for Samsung and SK hynix may be affected over the medium to long term. Slower demand growth could weigh on pricing power and profitability as companies expand production capacity. Some buyers might forfeit advance payments if market conditions experience a rapid downturn. The articles leave open whether data center operators will scale back or delay their investments. It remains unclear if the near-term earnings hit will truly be limited.

stories.Headline: Penguin Solutions unveils photonics-based HBM-class memory appliance for agentic AI workloads
stories.Summary:
Penguin Solutions unveiled the MemoryAI Photonic Appliance on November 16, 2026, to help agentic AI workloads. This new system is the first photonics-based HBM-class memory appliance designed to overcome GPU memory capacity constraints. The company showcased the appliance and its MemoryAI Photonic Memory Module at SC26 in Chicago. This hardware uses silicon photonics to let CPUs and GPUs share memory at high bandwidth memory data rates. The underlying module is built on the Marvell Photonic Fabric technology platform to deliver HBM-class performance.

The appliance targets terabytes-per-second data rates across multi-rack AI infrastructure using CXL 3.0 and Marvell photonic network interface cards. It supports up to 16 TB of DDR5 RDIMM memory and 576 GB of HBM3E memory per appliance. Total appliance bandwidth targets 57.6 Tbps and offers HBM Direct, HBM-DDR5 Cached, and DDR5 Direct access modes. The system allows memory to be located meters from GPUs rather than millimeters to expand available capacity. It integrates with the MemoryAI KV Cache Server and SMART CXL add-in cards for scalable, tiered memory.

Andy Mills, VP of Advanced Product Development at Penguin Solutions, said photonics provides a step-function change for AI. He stated that GPUs will have a direct way to access scale memory without hopping to a CPU. Preet Virk from Marvell said integrating their Photonic Fabric technology creates a path to high-capacity memory sharing. Virk noted that this approach is designed to improve accelerator utilization and increase the quality of tokens. Both executives believe these advancements will relieve stress on HBM memory and improve economic efficiency for inference.

The technology affects customers running agentic AI workloads that require high-speed data access for essential token generation. These users often face data bottlenecks that leave GPUs underutilized and contribute to the growing AI memory wall. One commenter questioned if the system is just memory with fast fiber NICs that might hide memory locations. This person compared the transparent access to a previous GPU model where local and attached memory were blurred. The appliance aims to help these users scale inference workloads without needing a proportional increase in GPU resources.

Localized ultra-fast HBM technology must sit within millimeters of the GPU, which limits capacity by package size and silicon I/O. Silicon photonics consumes less power than traditional copper interconnects and extends memory access across a photonic memory fabric. The MemoryAI Platform Architecture allows applications to access appliance memory as if it were directly attached without specialized routines. Memory can be statically or dynamically allocated through Penguin management software to handle specific workload requirements. This system complements existing GPU-attached HBM rather than replacing it to reduce pressure on high-speed memory.

Penguin Solutions plans to start sampling the MemoryAI Photonic Appliance to select customers in the second half of 2027. The articles do not state the specific pricing for the appliance or the MemoryAI Photonic Memory Module. There is no information regarding which specific customers have been selected for the initial sampling phase in 2027. The text does not mention the exact power consumption figures compared to the traditional copper interconnects mentioned. It remains open whether the transparent memory access will face the driver issues suggested by the online commenter.

The production of these custom components will require the use of Samsung Foundry's 2nm process for the base die. This advanced manufacturing node allows for greater efficiency and performance in the memory architecture. The responsibility for the development of this hardware lies with the engineering teams at Samsung Electronics. While the provided text does not include direct quotes, it indicates that Samsung is the primary developer for the memory. The company is working to align its foundry capabilities with the design specifications provided by Meta. This partnership highlights the shift toward customized hardware for large-scale artificial intelligence infrastructure.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: Jastech wins South Korea world-class product status for its JFS humidity control solution
stories.Summary:
South Korean semiconductor humidity-control specialist Jastech said its second-generation humidity control solution, JFS, also called a Jet Flow Straightener, has been selected as a 2026 World-Class Product by South Korea's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency, known as KOTRA. The selection marks the second consecutive year the company has earned the certification, following its first-generation N2 LPM product last year. The World-Class Product designation is a certification program under which the ministry and KOTRA award domestic products after comprehensively evaluating their global market competitiveness, technological prowess and growth potential. With the latest selection, Jastech has received official recognition of its technological competitiveness in the semiconductor humidity-control field.

JFS manages humidity by precisely controlling airflow inside semiconductor manufacturing processes, and applying it alongside N2 LPM can reduce cleanroom humidity, typically around 45% in ambient air, to as little as 1%. The first-generation N2 LPM laid the groundwork for yield improvement with nitrogen purge technology and can lower humidity to below 5%, while JFS adds precision airflow control for a higher level of humidity control. Jastech developed JFS for the first time in the world after about three years of research and development, and is currently supplying it to major global integrated device manufacturers. According to industry sources, Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and U.S.-based Micron are known to have adopted Jastech's humidity-control solutions. Cumulative sales of N2 LPM have now surpassed 300 billion won, approximately $225.4 million, and the company has set a goal of achieving 300 billion won in total company revenue by 2030 through expanded JFS supply.

Ha Jung-min, director of Jastech's research institute and a vice president, said JFS is an optimal solution for improving yields in the increasingly ultra-fine and advanced HBM process environment. He said that as cumulative sales of the first-generation N2 LPM have comfortably exceeded 300 billion won, the company will make JFS a solid foundation for achieving 300 billion won in revenue by 2030. The certification is significant in that it comes as miniaturization of advanced memory processes such as HBM accelerates, and humidity management had been a relatively underappreciated process variable. As circuit linewidths shrink and stacking becomes more advanced, yield sensitivity is rising, raising the possibility that equipment demand will grow as well.

For Jastech, the certification amounts to securing a bridgehead to expand the global customer base built with its first-generation product to its second-generation product. However, the pace of capital investment by global semiconductor companies and the flow of equipment orders tied to HBM expansion plans are expected to act as variables before JFS translates into actual revenue contributions. As the company's 2030 revenue target of 300 billion won also exceeds the cumulative performance of its first-generation product, the speed at which the second-generation product penetrates the market is likely to be the key factor.

stories.Headline: Ted Theofrastous says Ohio organizations adopt AI tools before reading vendor terms and issue policies without owners
stories.Summary:
Ted Theofrastous, a partner at Kohrman Jackson & Krantz, said many Ohio organizations adopt an AI tool before reading the vendor’s terms and issue an AI policy without assigning anyone to own it. He chairs KJK’s AI, Risk Management & Compliance practice group, which the firm launched this year, and its IP, Technology & New Ventures practice group. He will speak at the Ohio AI Summit on Nov. 18. He said the group was formed to get in front of those issues, mastering the substantive law and understanding the business and operational impacts well enough to advise on both. He described two kinds of clients, some managing AI risk and opportunity inside their own organizations and others for whom AI is part of the product or solution they deliver.

The group includes newer and experienced attorneys from KJK’s corporate, labor and employment, intellectual property, privacy and data security, and litigation practices, and its clients include manufacturers, research organizations, high-technology providers and international businesses. The most common request is help setting up governance that balances productivity with sound management, and clients that build with AI also ask the firm to revise their terms and conditions, their customer-facing warranties and how they manage intellectual assets. He said many clients don’t fully understand the risks around confidentiality and discoverability and many lack tight control over how employees use these tools on proprietary information. He said some are taking unnecessary risks and others are missing opportunities by being overly conservative. Many employees treat AI as a more powerful Google when it could handle sustained research, triage and analysis, and others accept its answers without checking whether they are true in general and correct for the business question at hand.

He said companies often fail to manage prompts, outputs and other work product at the enterprise level, and employees often use consumer versions of these tools on company work. He described a generic, downloaded policy as a good starting point, and said a policy should omit provisions that do not apply and obligations the company has no need to undertake. He said a strong policy names the approved tools and says which ones may be used for which kinds of work, bars personal accounts for confidential work, and applies the company’s retention schedule and litigation hold procedures to prompts and outputs that count as business records. It also calls for periodic review of vendor terms, assigns responsibility for checking AI output and lists the uses that need advance review, and it has to match commitments the company has already made in employment agreements, vendor and customer contracts and privacy statements. He said the employee handbook should refer to it because employees read the handbook, and he recommended that legal and procurement choose tools together with IT, that human resources and the managers whose teams use the tools help write the policy, and that training reach executives and IT staff as well as employees.

His steps for getting started are to inventory which tools and accounts are in use and what information goes into them, read the vendor contracts and the company’s own obligations to customers and partners, identify repetitive, time-consuming work suited to AI support, assign ownership to a named person or small group, write the policy and train every employee on it, and review tools, contracts and the policy on a fixed schedule. He said not to assume that where AI is today is where it will be in three months. Ohio has no comprehensive AI law and the General Assembly’s session ends Dec. 31, and he pointed to three pending bills, all in House committees. Senate Bill 163 would require generative AI systems to watermark the images and videos they produce and would prohibit identity fraud using an AI replica of a person, House Bill 813 would require watermarks on AI-generated products and disclosure when an AI system acts as a human, and House Bill 828 would bar employers from basing an employment decision only on an automated tool and would require advance written notice to workers.

Any of them not passed by year-end would have to be reintroduced in 2027. Federal copyright law requires a human author, and in March the U.S. Supreme Court declined to review Thaler v. Perlmutter, which left that rule in place. Arkansas has a law assigning ownership of AI-generated content, but it doesn’t create copyright protection, and Ohio has no equivalent.

He advised Ohio businesses to assign ownership of prompts, outputs and trained models directly in their employment, contractor, vendor and customer agreements and to consider whether valuable output can be protected as a trade secret. Other states’ laws also reach Ohio companies that have customers or employees there, and Colorado’s automated decision-making law, Colorado’s chatbot law and New York’s law on AI companion features for minors all take effect Jan. 1, 2027. In Ohio, at least eight trial courts now require filers to disclose whether they used AI to prepare a filing. He said leaders should first know which of their information is confidential, private or proprietary, then make sure each use of AI leaves them just as able to manage that information.

He applies the same care to the reliability of AI output, to decisions about people and to tools that can take actions inside a company’s systems, and he said an organization that has done this work can move quickly. KJK trains all staff and attorneys at three levels: a general understanding of AI, its ethical use covering privilege, discoverability and confidentiality, and workflows specific to each practice. He noted the firm can also build a client’s own logic into its playbooks. He said he hopes attendees leave with a clearer view of the opportunities open to their businesses and of the practical steps for pursuing them responsibly.

stories.Headline: Anthropic's Claude outperforms Penn law students on spring 2026 final exams
stories.Summary:
Claude, an artificial intelligence model made by Anthropic, sat for eleven final exams given to students at the University of Pennsylvania's law school during the spring 2026 semester, and it outperformed many of the aspiring lawyers in the class. The experiment used Claude Opus 4.7, the latest version available at the time, and covered subjects that ranged from constitutional law to intellectual property. The tests were run twice, once with a version of the model that had been explicitly trained on the course materials and once with a version that had not been trained, so researchers could compare its baseline knowledge against its prepared performance. The AI-written answers were then slipped into the stack alongside regular student work, and the professors were told to grade everything according to their normal rubrics.

The results were mixed, but on multiple-choice sections the model did much better when it had been given the course materials, and in one case it improved its score substantially. One professor described an AI-generated submission as the best of the lot in a constitutional law class of 92 students. The findings suggest that law schools may need to radically rethink how they test students, especially since Penn already admits some of the country's brightest law students, with median LSAT scores in the mid-170s for its latest incoming class. The experiment also underscored a problem with outright bans on AI, because shadow use, meaning use in unauthorized ways, can be hard to detect.

The professors who graded the AI-generated exams sometimes had trouble detecting the bot's handiwork, and when they did spot it, they noticed tells such as punctuation quirks or formatting glitches. Penn is leaving it up to individual professors to decide how students can use the technology in their classrooms, while some other schools are banning AI to preserve traditional methods of legal reasoning. The study was reported by Axios Philadelphia in a story by Isaac Avilucea. The articles do not say what Penn or Anthropic plans to do next.

stories.Headline: PwC and Harvey launch a Pillar Two tax assistant spanning 21 countries
stories.Summary:
PwC and Harvey built the Pillar Two Tax AI Assistant, a specialist research tool within Harvey, the companies announced on November 17, 2026. The Harvey Team published the announcement. The tool covers the OECD Pillar Two rules alongside country-specific material supplied by PwC network firms. It currently spans 21 countries. It is PwC's go-to tool for Pillar Two technical research.

More than 8,000 multinational groups are in scope of Pillar Two, the OECD framework that sets a 15% global minimum effective tax rate for groups with consolidated revenue of €750 million or more. According to the OECD, 45 jurisdictions have already taken steps to introduce the Global Anti-Base Erosion (GloBE) rules. The assistant draws only on vetted public sources: enacted and draft local legislation, tax authority guidance, and other official publications such as government consultations. Online sources are refreshed weekly, new documents are added monthly, and the content is reviewed quarterly. Users select it as a source in Harvey, filter by the countries they need, and use it alongside Harvey's other platform features.

The assistant has been rolled out to more than 17,000 PwC users across 21 countries and has recorded more than 70,000 user activities across more than 24,000 conversation threads. Monthly use grew roughly 17x, from about 700 activities in October 2025 to more than 12,000 in September 2026. A PwC Senior Associate, International Tax, Japan, said the module significantly improves the efficiency of their day-to-day Pillar Two work by helping them quickly navigate filing obligations, deadlines, and jurisdiction-specific requirements. A PwC Manager, International Tax, Germany, noted the module provides quick, well-structured overviews and access to relevant guidance and legislation, making country-specific research more efficient and effective. A Head of Tax of a multi-national group said they had a very positive experience with the module and would certainly recommend it to other clients looking for additional support and guidance on Pillar 2.

GloBE calculations generally start from each entity's financial accounts, as prepared for the parent's consolidated statements, and then require jurisdiction-specific adjustments. Some domestic regimes may substitute consolidated statements with local accounts. The OECD rules don't settle every local nuance, so teams must read the global rulebook alongside each country's legislation. The framework is global, but implementation is local, and those local differences decide what a group files, when it files, and how much top-up tax it owes. Working out exactly what data each country's rules require, and whether a group's data supports it, is often the hardest part.

Harvey will demonstrate the Pillar Two Tax AI Assistant and the Pillar Two Agent live at the PwC Tax Evolution Summit on November 18 in Madrid, Spain. The custom Harvey Agent tests each jurisdiction in a group against the FY2025 transitional CbCR safe harbours: the de minimis test, the simplified ETR test, and the routine profits test. Where a jurisdiction fails all three tests, the agent calculates an indicative top-up tax and shows where it would be collected, either locally or at the parent. The output is an Excel workbook showing the ETR working with live formulas, along with a self-contained interactive HTML view of the results. PwC has also rolled it out to clients, with positive feedback.

stories.Headline: Richards, Layton & Finger lawyer pays $2,500 sanction for AI hallucinations in brief
stories.Summary:
A lawyer from the firm Richards, Layton & Finger was sanctioned for submitting a legal brief containing artificial intelligence hallucinations. This disciplinary action occurred because the attorney failed to correct the errors in the document before filing it with the Court of Chancery. The court issued this penalty on November 16, 2026, after discovering the inaccuracies in the filing. This case highlights the ongoing risks associated with using generative artificial intelligence in professional legal practice. The court ordered the attorney to pay a financial penalty of 2,500 dollars for the filing error.

This specific sanction was applied to the individual lawyer rather than the law firm as a whole. Vice Chancellor Lori Will presided over the matter and determined the appropriate amount for the fine. The ruling requires the attorney to take responsibility for the lack of oversight regarding the AI generated content. Vice Chancellor Lori Will explained that she declined to sanction the entire firm for this specific mistake.

She noted that the firm had made commendable efforts to prevent the misuse of generative artificial intelligence. The judge believed that the firm's internal policies were sufficient to avoid broader punishment. This decision emphasizes that the responsibility for the final accuracy of a brief rests with the signing attorney. More to follow.

KiteFishAI, an Indian artificial intelligence startup, launched a compact open-weight AI model called NanoI1 on November 18, 2026, according to a TechGig report published that morning. KiteFishAI described NanoI1 as a foundational element for purpose-built AI solutions rather than a direct competitor to large language models built for a wide range of general tasks. The official announcement did not include detailed benchmark results, specific model parameters, pricing information or hardware requirements for the new model.

The launch is meant to make AI adoption more accessible for businesses that need solutions tailored precisely to their own operational needs, including organisations in highly regulated industries where data security, compliance and deployment demands are paramount. According to KiteFishAI, smaller purpose-built models offer a practical alternative to relying on large general-purpose models for every application, and they give organisations greater control over their AI deployments. The company also said compact models enable applications built around specific business requirements, which fosters enhanced customisation and operational alignment. With NanoI1, KiteFishAI is looking to contribute to India's rapidly expanding AI development ecosystem by giving developers and businesses an accessible open-weight option for highly specialised solutions.

KiteFishAI positioned NanoI1 as a viable option for organisations whose most important requirements are customisation, security and specific operational considerations. The company stated that the model is intended to address specific operational needs rather than compete directly with large language models designed for a wide array of general tasks. stories.Headline: Chinese hacking group Vapor Panda uses AI tools to attack over 200 organizations worldwide
stories.Summary:
A Chinese-linked hacking organization known as Vapor Panda used artificial intelligence tools to attack over 200 organizations worldwide. These cyberattacks occurred between the 17th and 29th of last month, targeting government agencies and private companies. The group focused on diplomatic and security agencies across Asia, Europe, the Middle East, and Latin America. They also targeted various United States companies within the nuclear, defense, semiconductor, pharmaceutical, and financial sectors. South Korean organizations involved in foreign policy and think tanks were also identified as targets.

The attackers utilized an AI agent-based penetration tool called Artex, which was driven by the Chinese AI model DeepSeek. This tool allows hackers to repeatedly explore vulnerabilities in application programming interfaces and web applications to perform follow-up attacks. The organization also used paid subscription services from other state-of-the-art AI models to assist their operations. It is estimated that a single penetration process consumed approximately 1.4 billion input tokens. This automation significantly lowered the entry barrier for attacks and reduced the overall costs for the hackers.

Adam Myers, the general manager of attack response operations at CrowdStrike, confirmed that the attackers were successful. He stated that Vapor Panda is a sophisticated organization that seized the opportunity to attack hundreds of targets on a large scale. Myers explained that while the attacks are not completely new, the use of AI has increased their speed and scale. He noted that the firm has tracked this specific group since 2021 and has generated over 50 reports. The cybersecurity firm has already notified the relevant computer emergency response teams about the infringements.

CrowdStrike identified these activities by analyzing malicious code, web shells, attack infrastructure, and specific targets. This campaign is separate from another attack using Artex that targeted the South Korean financial sector last month. Myers observed that different hacking organizations have frequently used the Artex tool over the past six weeks. He believes that these AI-based attacks can be detected and defended with appropriate security technology and visibility. The firm recommends performing threat tracking twenty-four hours a day to maintain a strong defense.

stories.Headline: US, China and Russia leaders meet to discuss preventing AI from triggering nuclear war
stories.Summary:
Presidents Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin will meet for a trilateral summit. This meeting occurs alongside the APEC leaders meeting in Shenzhen, China. The leaders intend to discuss preventing artificial intelligence from triggering a nuclear war. They will also address the Ukraine War, trade, and tensions over Taiwan. This summit tests if great power diplomacy can build a safer international order.

The leaders could establish a standing trilateral dialogue on AI and nuclear strategic stability. This mechanism would include diplomatic, military, nuclear security, and technological officials with scientific experts. It would protect nuclear command and control systems against cyber interference and maintain reliable crisis communications. The group would preserve human authorization over nuclear use and report dangerous incidents involving autonomous systems. It builds on a 2024 commitment by America and China to maintain human control.

Jianli Yang proposes this dialogue to create a sustainable equilibrium in the distribution of power. He says the three powers must move beyond bargaining toward building a durable order. Yang believes no government should gamble with humanity's survival through dangerous technologies. He argues that human judgment and common rules must govern the most dangerous technologies. He states that limited progress could satisfy dimensions of international stability within a narrow field.

The United Kingdom, France, and India are other nuclear powers that would eventually need to participate. These nations and other countries are affected by the security of the international order. The author notes that the three leaders cannot grant themselves exclusive authority over humanity's security. He warns that mutual suspicion is profound and verification of any agreements would be difficult. Dialogue between these specific leaders could potentially become mere diplomatic theater.

The United States leads in frontier research, advanced computing, and technological entrepreneurship. China combines advancing AI capabilities with manufacturing capacity and affordable models distributed internationally. Russia possesses energy resources, nuclear energy expertise, and military experience with drones and electronic warfare. The New START treaty limiting American and Russian strategic nuclear forces expired in February 2026. China is also expanding its nuclear arsenal, which further complicates global strategic stability.

The leaders may eventually produce common definitions, confidence building measures, and limited reciprocal restraints. They must decide if they can cooperate against dangers that threaten their own existence. The articles leave open whether the three powers can actually move beyond simple bargaining. It remains uncertain if they can resolve underlying territorial disputes that threaten global peace. The success of this initial trilateral mechanism is described as far from guaranteed.
